attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes or comments regarding the investigational product record, such as special handling instructions, known stability issues, or interim regulatory communications. Captured by data management or regulatory affairs teams.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: packaging_description
attributes.description: Description of the primary and secondary packaging configuration for the investigational product (e.g., 'blister pack of 10 tablets in a carton', 'single-use vial 10 mL in a kit'). Referenced in supply chain, pharmacy, and RTSM kit configuration.
attributes.references: ICH Q8; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.94; EMA IMPD Guideline; Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investigational product by modality type (e.g., small molecule, biologic, gene therapy, medical device). Drives regulatory pathway selection, storage requirements, and supply chain handling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|gene_therapy|cell_therapy|medical_device|combination_product|vaccine|radiopharmaceutical — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Parts 312/812; EMA Guideline on IMP; ICH Q6A/Q6B

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_status
attributes.description: Current regulatory approval status of the investigational product (e.g., approved for a different indication, purely investigational, withdrawn from market). Informs regulatory strategy, labeling requirements, and comparator sourcing decisions.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: retest_period_months
attributes.description: Period in months after which the investigational product must be retested before continued use, applicable to active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and certain formulations. Distinct from shelf life; used in supply chain and QC planning.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; EMA IMPD Guideline

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Route by which the investigational product is administered to subjects (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical). Captured per CDISC SDTM EX domain EXROUTE variable and referenced in protocol and pharmacy instructions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|intrathecal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain (EXROUTE); FDA Route of Administration Terminology; ICH M5

attributes.name: shelf_life_months
attributes.description: Approved shelf life of the investigational product in months from the date of manufacture, as established by stability studies and documented in the IMPD/IND. Drives expiry date calculation, supply planning, and resupply triggers in Medidata Rave RTSM.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; EMA IMPD Guideline

attributes.name: sponsor_product_code
attributes.description: Sponsor's internal product or compound code used in portfolio management systems, distinct from the IMP code used in clinical operations. Enables cross-referencing between clinical development and commercial product pipelines.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Sponsor SOPs; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: storage_condition
attributes.description: Required storage conditions for the investigational product as specified in the IMPD/IND and product label (e.g., 'Store at 2–8°C, protected from light', 'Store below 25°C'). Critical for supply chain cold chain management and site pharmacy compliance.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; EMA IMPD Guideline

attributes.name: storage_temperature_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the investigational product. Used by supply chain and site pharmacy to configure cold chain monitoring alerts and validate storage compliance.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; WHO Technical Report Series

attributes.name: storage_temperature_min_c
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the investigational product. Used by supply chain and site pharmacy to configure cold chain monitoring alerts and validate storage compliance.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; WHO Technical Report Series

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: Nominal strength or concentration of the active substance in the investigational product as labeled (e.g., '10 mg', '100 mg/mL', '5 mg/kg'). Captured in the IMPD/IND and referenced in supply chain, pharmacy, and SDTM EX domain.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A; CDISC SDTM EX Domain (EXDOSE); FDA CMC Guidance

attributes.name: strength_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the investigational product strength (e.g., mg, mg/mL, IU). Standardized per CDISC controlled terminology to enable cross-study comparisons and SDTM dataset generation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg|mg/mL|mg/kg|mcg|mcg/mL|IU|IU/mL|g|% — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC Controlled Terminology (UNIT); ICH Q6A; FDA CMC Guidance

attributes.name: therapeutic_class
attributes.description: Therapeutic or pharmacological class of the investigational product (e.g., oncology, cardiovascular, CNS, anti-infective). Used for portfolio analytics, regulatory strategy, and study feasibility assessments.
attributes.references: WHO ATC; MedDRA SOC; FDA Pharmacologic Class

attributes.name: unit_of_dispensing
attributes.description: The unit in which the investigational product is dispensed to subjects at the investigational site (e.g., tablet, vial, kit, syringe). Used in RTSM dispensing records, drug accountability logs, and SDTM EX domain. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|vial|kit|syringe|patch|sachet|bottle|ampoule — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the investigational product master record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+ principles, and change management tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: who_dd_code
attributes.description: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) drug code assigned to the investigational product for standardized drug coding in adverse event reporting, SDTM datasets, and regulatory submissions. Enables cross-study signal detection in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: WHO-DD; CDISC SDTM CM/EX domains; ICH E2B(R3)

products.name: dosing_regimen
products.description: Defines the dosing regimen for each investigational product within a study arm. Records regimen name, dose level, dose unit, dosing frequency, dosing route, dosing duration, dose escalation scheme (for dose-escalation studies), dose modification rules, maximum tolerated dose (MTD) flag, and CDISC SDTM EX (Exposure) domain mapping. Supports PK/PD modeling and safety dose-response analysis.
products.reference: CDISC SDTM EX (Exposure) Domain / ICH E4

attributes.name: dosing_regimen_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the dosing regimen record within the Clinical Trials data platform. Primary key for the dosing_regimen product in the study domain.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: arm_id
attributes.description: Reference to the study arm (treatment group) to which this dosing regimen applies. A study may have multiple arms each with distinct regimens (e.g., active drug arm vs. placebo arm).
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM ARM; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: investigational_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational product (IP) being administered under this dosing regimen. Supports traceability from regimen to supply chain and accountability logs.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXTRT; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent clinical study for which this dosing regimen is defined. Links the regimen to the study protocol and all associated study-level metadata.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: study_protocol_amendment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to study.study_protocol_amendment. Business justification: dosing_regimen has amendment_number as a STRING but no FK to study_protocol_amendment. Dosing regimens are introduced or modified by protocol amendments — this FK formalizes that traceability. No bidi
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: adam_adex_mapping_notes
attributes.business_glossary_term: CDISC ADaM Exposure (ADEX) Domain Mapping Notes
attributes.description: Notes describing how this dosing regimen maps to the CDISC ADaM ADEX (Analysis Dataset for Exposure) domain, including derivation rules for cumulative dose, dose intensity, and relative dose intensity calculations used in biostatistical analysis.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM ADEX Implementation Guide; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA Statistical Review Guidance; SAP

attributes.name: blinding_type
attributes.description: Blinding level applied to this dosing regimen as defined in the study protocol (e.g., 'double-blind' where neither subject nor investigator knows the treatment assignment). Impacts RTSM/IRT dispensing logic and unblinding procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM TI Domain; FDA Guidance on Blinding

attributes.name: comparator_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this regimen represents an active investigational product, placebo, vehicle control, sham procedure, or no-treatment arm. Critical for ITT and PP population definitions and regulatory benefit-risk assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E10 Choice of Control Group; CDISC SDTM TA Domain; FDA Guidance on Placebo Controls

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this dosing regimen record was first created in the data platform, conforming to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: dose_escalation_step
attributes.description: Sequential step number within the dose escalation scheme (e.g., 1, 2, 3). Enables ordering of dose cohorts in escalation studies and supports dose-response curve construction in PK/PD modeling.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies; ICH E9

attributes.name: dose_form
attributes.description: Pharmaceutical form of the investigational product as administered (e.g., 'TABLET', 'CAPSULE', 'SOLUTION FOR INJECTION', 'PATCH'). Conforms to CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSFRM controlled terminology. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: TABLET|CAPSULE|SOLUTION FOR INJECTION|PATCH|POWDER|CREAM|SUPPOSITORY|INHALER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSFRM; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA NDA/BLA Labeling

attributes.name: dose_level
attributes.description: Numeric dose amount to be administered per dosing event as specified in the protocol (e.g., 10.0, 50.5, 100.0). Represents the planned dose per administration. Used in PK/PD modeling and dose-response analysis.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSE; ICH E9 Statistical Principles; FDA Guidance on PK Studies

attributes.name: dose_modification_rules
attributes.description: Narrative description of protocol-defined rules for dose modifications, reductions, interruptions, or discontinuations based on toxicity or adverse events (e.g., 'Reduce by 25% for Grade 2 AE; discontinue for Grade 3 SAE'). Supports safety monitoring and CTCAE-based dose management.
attributes.references: CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

attributes.name: dose_reduction_levels
attributes.description: Number of permitted dose reduction levels defined in the protocol (e.g., 2 levels: Level -1 and Level -2). Used in oncology studies to manage toxicity while maintaining therapeutic benefit. Supports safety dose-response analysis.
attributes.references: CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Oncology Drug Dosing

attributes.name: dose_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the dose level (e.g., 'mg', 'mg/kg', 'mg/m2', 'mcg/kg'). Conforms to CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSU controlled terminology. Essential for PK/PD modeling and regulatory submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg|mg/kg|mg/m2|mcg|mcg/kg|IU|mL|g — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSU; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH E9

attributes.name: dosing_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency of dose administration using standard clinical abbreviations (e.g., 'QD' = once daily, 'BID' = twice daily, 'QW' = once weekly, 'Q2W' = every two weeks). Conforms to CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSFRQ controlled terminology. Drives subject visit scheduling and PK sampling windows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: QD|BID|TID|QID|QW|BIW|TIW|Q2W|Q4W|ONCE|PRN — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSFRQ; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH E9

attributes.name: dosing_interval_days
attributes.description: Numeric interval between doses expressed in days (e.g., 1.0 for QD, 0.5 for BID, 7.0 for QW). Provides machine-readable precision for automated scheduling in RTSM/IRT systems and PK modeling when frequency alone is insufficient.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E9

attributes.name: dosing_route
attributes.description: Route by which the investigational product is administered (e.g., 'ORAL', 'INTRAVENOUS', 'SUBCUTANEOUS', 'INTRAMUSCULAR', 'TOPICAL', 'INHALATION'). Conforms to CDISC SDTM EX.EXROUTE controlled terminology. Critical for PK absorption modeling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ORAL|INTRAVENOUS|SUBCUTANEOUS|INTRAMUSCULAR|TOPICAL|INHALATION|INTRANASAL|TRANSDERMAL — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXROUTE; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH M9 Biopharmaceutics Classification

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this dosing regimen version ceased to be effective (e.g., superseded by an amendment). Null for currently active regimens. Supports temporal versioning and historical audit of regimen changes.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this dosing regimen version became effective in the study, typically aligned with protocol approval or amendment approval date. Supports temporal versioning of regimen changes across the study lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: escalation_scheme_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the dose escalation scheme applied in this regimen (e.g., '3+3 design', 'Accelerated Titration', 'BOIN design', 'mTPI-2'). Populated only when is_dose_escalation = True. Supports Phase I safety and PK/PD analysis.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies; ICH E9; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

attributes.name: food_effect_instruction
attributes.description: Protocol-defined instruction regarding food intake relative to dosing (e.g., 'fasted' = at least 8 hours fasting before dose, 'fed' = standard high-fat meal before dose). Impacts PK absorption and bioavailability. Conforms to FDA food effect guidance.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Food-Effect Bioavailability Studies; CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH M9

attributes.name: infusion_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration of intravenous or subcutaneous infusion in minutes, applicable when dosing_route is 'INTRAVENOUS' or similar. Null for non-infusion routes. Critical for PK modeling of IV drug exposure and site nursing procedure planning.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDUR; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies

attributes.name: is_dose_escalation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this regimen is part of a dose-escalation scheme (True) or a fixed-dose regimen (False). When True, the escalation_scheme_description and mtd_flag fields become operationally relevant. Common in Phase I oncology studies.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

attributes.name: is_mtd
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dose level has been designated as the Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD) by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or study team (True = MTD confirmed). Critical for Phase I dose-finding studies and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on MTD Determination; ICH E9; DSMB Charter; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

attributes.name: loading_dose_duration_days
attributes.description: Number of days the loading dose is administered before transitioning to the maintenance dose. Null if no loading dose is defined. Supports PK/PD modeling of drug accumulation and steady-state calculations.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies; DMPK principles

attributes.name: loading_dose_level
attributes.description: Initial higher dose administered to rapidly achieve therapeutic drug concentrations before transitioning to the maintenance dose level. Expressed in the same unit as dose_unit. Null if no loading dose is specified in the protocol.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies; DMPK principles

attributes.name: maximum_dose_level
attributes.description: Maximum allowable dose level for this regimen as defined in the protocol (e.g., dose cap for safety). Expressed in the same unit as dose_unit. Used in dose modification rules and safety monitoring.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation

attributes.name: pd_assessment_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether pharmacodynamic (PD) biomarker assessments are required for subjects on this dosing regimen (True = PD assessments mandated per protocol). Supports PK/PD modeling and dose-response analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PD Studies; CDISC SDTM CE/FA Domains; SAS Drug Development

attributes.name: pk_sampling_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether pharmacokinetic (PK) blood sampling is required for subjects on this dosing regimen (True = PK sampling mandated per protocol). Drives PK visit scheduling, sample collection logistics, and DMPK analysis planning.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies; CDISC SDTM PC/PP Domains; SAS Drug Development

attributes.name: planned_duration_days
attributes.description: Total planned duration of the dosing regimen expressed in days as specified in the study protocol (e.g., 84 days for a 12-week treatment period). Used for treatment period planning, supply forecasting, and CDISC SDTM EX.EXENDY derivation.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EXENDY; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: protocol_version
attributes.description: Version of the study protocol under which this dosing regimen was defined or last amended (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.1'). Enables traceability of regimen changes across protocol amendments. Supports TMF/eTMF document management and regulatory audit trails.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: randomization_ratio
attributes.description: Allocation ratio for randomization to this arm/regimen expressed as a colon-separated ratio (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'). Used in RTSM/IRT configuration and statistical analysis plan (SAP) for sample size and power calculations.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM TA Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One

attributes.name: regimen_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this dosing regimen within the study protocol (e.g., 'REG-001', 'ARM-A-DOSE-1'). Used in protocol documents, eCRFs, and CDISC SDTM EX submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: regimen_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the dosing regimen as defined in the study protocol (e.g., 'Low Dose QD', 'High Dose BID', 'Placebo TIW'). Used in protocol documents, SAP, and CSR narratives.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: regimen_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the dosing regimen within the study. 'draft' indicates protocol development; 'active' indicates currently administered; 'suspended' indicates temporarily halted (e.g., pending safety review); 'discontinued' indicates permanently stopped; 'completed' indicates all subjects have completed this regimen.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: sdtm_ex_mapping_notes
attributes.business_glossary_term: CDISC SDTM Exposure (EX) Domain Mapping Notes
attributes.description: Notes describing how this dosing regimen maps to the CDISC SDTM EX (Exposure) domain variables, including any derivation logic, controlled terminology mappings, or special handling required for regulatory submission datasets. Supports CDISC compliance and eCTD submission.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide EX Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this dosing regimen record was sourced or is managed (e.g., 'Oracle Clinical One' for study design, 'Medidata Rave' for EDC-captured exposure data). Supports data lineage and ETL traceability in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: starting_dose_level
attributes.description: Initial dose amount at the start of the regimen, particularly relevant for titration or escalation regimens where the dose changes over time. Expressed in the same unit as dose_unit. Supports PK/PD baseline modeling.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies

attributes.name: treatment_period_label
attributes.description: Label identifying the treatment period within the study to which this regimen applies (e.g., 'Period 1', 'Run-In', 'Maintenance', 'Extension'). Supports crossover and multi-period study designs. Maps to CDISC SDTM EX.EPOCH.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM EX.EPOCH; CDISC Study Design Model; ICH E9

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this dosing regimen record was last modified in the data platform, conforming to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: washout_period_days
attributes.description: Duration of the washout period in days required between treatment periods in crossover studies, or between prior therapy and study treatment. Null for parallel-group designs. Supports PK carryover analysis and crossover study scheduling.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM EX Domain; FDA Guidance on Crossover Studies

products.name: objective
products.description: Formally documents the primary, secondary, and exploratory objectives of a clinical study as stated in the protocol. Captures objective number, objective type (primary, secondary, exploratory), objective text, associated endpoint references, ICH E9(R1) estimand linkage, and protocol version in which the objective was introduced or modified. Provides the scientific rationale traceability from objective to endpoint to SAP.
products.reference: ICH E9(R1) / ICH E6(R2) Protocol Objectives

attributes.name: objective_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for a study objective record in the clinical trial data platform. Primary key for the study_objective entity.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM; ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary endpoint directly associated with this objective. Establishes the objective-to-endpoint traceability chain required by the SAP and regulatory submissions. Nullable for objectives that map to multiple endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent clinical study to which this objective belongs. Links the objective to its governing protocol and study master record.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM OI Domain; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: adam_dataset_reference
attributes.description: CDISC ADaM dataset name(s) used for the primary analysis supporting this objective (e.g., ADEFF, ADTTE, ADAE). Provides direct linkage from objective to analysis-ready datasets in SAS Drug Development.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Data Standards Catalog; PMDA Data Standards

attributes.name: alpha_level
attributes.description: Pre-specified Type I error rate (significance level) allocated to this objective in the SAP. Typically 0.05 for primary objectives or a fraction thereof when multiplicity adjustments are applied. Drives sample size calculations and hypothesis testing.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E9 Statistical Principles; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which this objective (as part of the protocol or amendment) received formal approval from the sponsor and/or IRB/IEC. Marks the transition from draft to active status and is required for regulatory audit trails.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.4; FDA 21 CFR Part 56; OHRP 45 CFR Part 46

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this study objective record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: csr_section_reference
attributes.description: Section number within the Clinical Study Report (CSR) where results for this objective are reported. Provides traceability from protocol objective through analysis to regulatory submission document per ICH E3 CSR structure.
attributes.references: ICH E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; eCTD

attributes.name: ctd_section_reference
attributes.description: Module and section reference within the Common Technical Document (CTD) / electronic CTD (eCTD) where this objective's results contribute to the regulatory dossier (e.g., Module 5.3.5.1). Supports regulatory submission traceability.
attributes.references: ICH M4E(R2) CTD Efficacy; eCTD Specification; FDA NDA/BLA Submission Requirements

attributes.name: dsmb_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether interim results for this objective are to be reviewed by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) during planned interim analyses. Drives interim analysis planning and unblinding procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this version of the objective ceased to be effective, typically due to a protocol amendment superseding it. Null for currently active objectives. Supports temporal versioning of protocol objectives.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.30; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this version of the objective became effective in the approved protocol. For original protocol objectives, this is the initial protocol approval date. For amended objectives, this is the amendment approval date.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.30; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: hypothesis_type
attributes.description: Statistical hypothesis framework associated with this objective. Superiority objectives aim to demonstrate a treatment effect greater than control; non-inferiority objectives aim to show the treatment is not worse by a defined margin; equivalence objectives test for no meaningful difference; descriptive objectives have no formal hypothesis.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials; EMA Guideline on the Choice of Non-Inferiority Margin

attributes.name: intercurrent_event_strategy
attributes.description: ICH E9(R1) estimand attribute specifying the strategy for handling intercurrent events (post-randomization events that affect interpretation of the outcome) for this objective. Strategies include while-on-treatment, hypothetical, composite, principal stratum, and treatment policy.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum; EMA Reflection Paper on Estimands; FDA Guidance on Estimands

attributes.name: irb_iec_review_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Review Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a change to this objective requires IRB/IEC review and approval (e.g., substantial protocol amendment). Drives the amendment workflow and site notification process.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.4; FDA 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 15; OHRP 45 CFR Part 46

attributes.name: last_amended_in_amendment_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Amended in Protocol Amendment Number
attributes.description: Protocol amendment number in which this objective was most recently modified. Null if the objective has never been amended. Used to track the amendment history of each objective for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.30; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: multiplicity_adjustment_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether statistical multiplicity adjustment (e.g., Bonferroni, Hochberg, hierarchical testing) is required for this objective due to multiple comparisons. Informs the SAP multiplicity control strategy.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Multiple Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, clarifications, or internal commentary related to this objective that does not fit structured fields. Used by data managers and biostatisticians during protocol development and SAP authoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: objective_number
attributes.description: Structured alphanumeric identifier for the objective within the protocol (e.g., P-1 for Primary Objective 1, S-2 for Secondary Objective 2). Used for cross-referencing in the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) and Clinical Study Report (CSR).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: objective_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the study objective. Draft objectives are under authoring review; active objectives are in the approved protocol; amended objectives have been modified by a protocol amendment; superseded objectives have been replaced; retired objectives have been removed from the protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: objective_text
attributes.description: Full verbatim text of the study objective as stated in the approved protocol. This is the authoritative scientific statement of what the study aims to demonstrate or evaluate, used verbatim in regulatory submissions and the CSR.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.23; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: objective_type
attributes.description: Classification of the study objective by its scientific hierarchy and regulatory weight. Primary objectives drive the primary endpoint and sample size calculation; secondary objectives provide supportive evidence; exploratory objectives generate hypotheses. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: primary|secondary|exploratory|safety|pharmacokinetic|pharmacodynamic — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints

attributes.name: population_description
attributes.description: Description of the analysis population to which this objective applies (e.g., Intent-to-Treat (ITT), Per Protocol (PP), Safety Population). Aligns with the estimand population attribute per ICH E9(R1).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: population_type
attributes.description: Standardized code for the analysis population associated with this objective. Intent-to-Treat (ITT), modified ITT (mITT), Per Protocol (PP), Safety, Pharmacokinetic (PK), or Pharmacodynamic (PD) population. Drives dataset selection in SAS Drug Development CDISC ADaM programming.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: protocol_section_reference
attributes.description: Section number within the study protocol document where this objective is formally stated (e.g., Section 2.1, Section 3.2). Enables direct navigation to the source text in the protocol and eTMF.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.23; CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: regulatory_commitment_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this objective is a formal regulatory commitment (e.g., a post-marketing commitment to FDA or EMA, or a condition of approval). Regulatory commitment objectives require heightened change control and reporting.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Post-Authorization Commitments; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: sap_section_reference
attributes.description: Section number or identifier within the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) that addresses the analysis corresponding to this objective. Provides direct traceability from protocol objective to statistical methodology, as required for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Statistical Guidance on Reporting Results; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: scientific_rationale
attributes.description: Narrative justification for why this objective is scientifically important and how it contributes to the overall study goals. Supports regulatory review, protocol synopsis, and investigator brochure alignment.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Design; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: sdtm_domain_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) Domain Reference
attributes.description: CDISC SDTM domain(s) that contain the data supporting this objective (e.g., ADAE, ADEFF, ADTTE). Enables automated linkage between protocol objectives and SDTM/ADaM datasets in SAS Drug Development.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Ordinal position of this objective within its objective type group (e.g., first primary objective = 1, second primary objective = 2). Governs display order in the protocol, SAP, and CSR sections.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: short_title
attributes.description: Concise human-readable label for the objective used in dashboards, reports, and CTMS displays where the full objective text is too lengthy. Typically 10–15 words summarizing the scientific intent.
attributes.references: CDISC Protocol Representation Model; Oracle Clinical One Study Design Module

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this objective record was sourced or authored (e.g., Oracle Clinical One study design module, Veeva Vault protocol document). Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the lakehouse.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: Native identifier of this objective record in the originating operational system (e.g., Oracle Clinical One objective GUID, Veeva Vault document section ID). Enables back-referencing and reconciliation with the system of record.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: summary_measure
attributes.description: Statistical summary measure used to quantify the treatment effect for this objective (e.g., difference in means, odds ratio, hazard ratio, response rate difference). Corresponds to the population-level summary attribute of the ICH E9(R1) estimand.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum; ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: testing_hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric level in the hierarchical testing procedure for this objective. Level 1 is tested first; subsequent levels are tested only if the preceding level achieves statistical significance. Implements the gatekeeping strategy defined in the SAP.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Multiple Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area or disease indication to which this objective is aligned (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology). Supports cross-study analytics and portfolio-level objective benchmarking.
attributes.references: MedDRA; CDISC Therapeutic Area Data Standards; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this study objective record in the data platform. Required for change tracking, data lineage, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: variable_description
attributes.description: Description of the variable (outcome measure) used to address this objective, as defined in the ICH E9(R1) estimand framework. Specifies what is measured on each subject to evaluate the treatment effect.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum; CDISC Protocol Representation Model

products.name: pk_sampling_schedule
products.description: Defines the pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) blood/urine/tissue sampling schedule for a clinical study. Records sample type, nominal sampling timepoint (pre-dose, 0.5h, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 24h post-dose, etc.), sampling window, visit association, analyte to be measured, bioanalytical method reference, sample volume, sample handling instructions, and CDISC SDTM PC (Pharmacokinetics Concentrations) domain mapping. Critical for DMPK studies.
products.reference: CDISC SDTM PC/PP Domains / FDA PK Guidance

attributes.name: pk_sampling_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each PK/PD sampling schedule record in the clinical study. Primary key for the pk_sampling_schedule data product.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; ICH E3

attributes.name: arm_id
attributes.description: Reference to the study arm or treatment group for which this sampling schedule applies. Enables arm-specific PK sampling designs.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM ARM; ICH E9

attributes.name: bioanalytical_assay_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the validated bioanalytical method used to quantify the analyte in the collected sample. Links to the bioanalytical method validation report per FDA/EMA guidance.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation 2011; ICH M10

attributes.name: epoch_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to study.study_epoch. Business justification: pk_sampling_schedule has epoch as a STRING but no FK to study_epoch. PK/PD sampling timepoints are associated with specific study epochs — this FK formalizes that structural relationship. No bidirecti
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this PK/PD sampling schedule is defined. Links the sampling schedule to the parent study protocol.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; ICH E3; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: study_protocol_amendment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the protocol amendment that introduced or last modified this sampling schedule entry. Supports audit trail and regulatory submission traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.30; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: study_visit_schedule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the scheduled study visit during which this PK/PD sample is to be collected. Associates the sampling timepoint with the visit schedule.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; Oracle Clinical One Visit Schedule

attributes.name: analyte_code
attributes.description: Standardized code for the analyte to be measured, aligned with WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) or internal compound coding. Maps to CDISC SDTM PC.PCTESTCD.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTESTCD; WHO-DD; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: analyte_name
attributes.description: Name of the drug compound, metabolite, or biomarker to be measured in the collected sample (e.g., parent drug, active metabolite, total drug). Maps to CDISC SDTM PC.PCTEST.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTEST; WHO-DD; FDA DMPK Guidance

attributes.name: backup_sample_volume_ml
attributes.description: Additional volume of biological sample to be collected as a backup or reserve aliquot, expressed in millilitres (mL). Supports re-analysis and incurred sample reanalysis (ISR) requirements.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation 2011

attributes.name: collection_tube_type
attributes.description: Type of collection tube or container required for sample collection (e.g., K2-EDTA, Li-Heparin, SST, urine cup). Critical for sample integrity and bioanalytical method compatibility.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this PK/PD sampling schedule record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: cycle_number
attributes.description: Treatment cycle number during which this PK/PD sample is collected, applicable for oncology and multi-cycle dosing studies. Null for single-dose or non-cyclic studies.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; ICH E3; FDA Oncology PK Guidance

attributes.name: day_in_cycle
attributes.description: Study day within the treatment cycle on which this PK/PD sample is to be collected. Used in conjunction with cycle_number for multi-cycle dosing regimens.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; ICH E3; FDA Oncology PK Guidance

attributes.name: dose_number
attributes.description: Sequential dose number relative to which this PK sample is collected (e.g., Dose 1, Dose 7 for steady-state). Supports single-dose vs. multiple-dose PK profiling.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; FDA DMPK Guidance; ICH E3

attributes.name: edc_field_oid
attributes.description: Object Identifier (OID) of the corresponding field in the EDC system (Medidata Rave eCRF) for this PK sampling timepoint. Enables direct mapping between protocol schedule and EDC data collection form.
attributes.references: CDISC ODM (Operational Data Model); Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this PK/PD sampling schedule entry ceases to be applicable (e.g., superseded by protocol amendment). Null if currently active.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this PK/PD sampling schedule entry is effective and applicable for subject data collection. Supports protocol amendment versioning and schedule lifecycle management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+

attributes.name: fasting_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject must be in a fasted state prior to sample collection at this timepoint. Relevant for food-effect PK studies and protocol compliance.
attributes.references: FDA Food-Effect Bioavailability and Fed Bioequivalence Studies Guidance; ICH E3

attributes.name: max_storage_duration_hours
attributes.description: Maximum allowable duration in hours that the sample may be stored at the specified storage temperature before shipment to the bioanalytical laboratory. Derived from bench-top and freeze-thaw stability data.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation 2011

attributes.name: nominal_timepoint_label
attributes.description: Descriptive label for the nominal PK sampling timepoint relative to dose administration (e.g., 'Pre-dose', '0.5h post-dose', '1h post-dose', '24h post-dose'). Maps to CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPT.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPT; ICH E3 Section 9.4.2

attributes.name: nominal_timepoint_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the nominal timepoint value (e.g., hours, minutes, days). Maps to CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTREF unit context.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTREF; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: nominal_timepoint_value
attributes.description: Numeric value of the nominal sampling timepoint relative to dose administration. Used for PK modeling and CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTNUM mapping. Expressed in the unit defined by nominal_timepoint_unit.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTNUM; FDA DMPK Guidance; ICH M3(R2)

attributes.name: number_of_aliquots
attributes.description: Number of aliquots into which the collected sample must be divided for analysis, backup, and archival purposes. Drives sample labelling and supply requirements.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: optional_sample
attributes.description: Indicates whether collection of this sample is optional (e.g., exploratory biomarker, sub-study) or mandatory per the study protocol. Affects protocol deviation assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ICH E3; CDISC SDTM PC Domain

attributes.name: pre_dose_sample
attributes.description: Indicates whether this sampling timepoint is a pre-dose (trough) sample collected before drug administration. Used to assess baseline concentrations and trough levels.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; FDA DMPK Guidance; ICH E3

attributes.name: processing_instructions
attributes.description: Detailed instructions for processing the collected sample at the clinical site (e.g., centrifugation speed, time, temperature, aliquoting steps). Ensures sample integrity per bioanalytical method requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; ALCOA+

attributes.name: protocol_version
attributes.description: Version of the study protocol under which this PK/PD sampling schedule was defined or last amended. Enables traceability of schedule changes across protocol amendments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: required_sample_volume_ml
attributes.description: Volume of biological sample required for bioanalytical analysis, expressed in millilitres (mL). Used for supply planning, patient burden assessment, and protocol feasibility.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: sample_type
attributes.description: Biological matrix type to be collected for PK/PD analysis (e.g., blood, plasma, serum, urine, tissue). Maps to CDISC SDTM PC.PCSPEC. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: blood|plasma|serum|urine|cerebrospinal_fluid|tissue|saliva|feces|dried_blood_spot|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCSPEC; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

attributes.name: sampling_category
attributes.description: Classification of the sampling purpose: Pharmacokinetic (PK), Pharmacodynamic (PD), combined PK/PD, biomarker, immunogenicity, or safety assessment. Drives CDISC domain assignment (PC for PK, PP for PD).
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC/PP Domains; ICH E3 Section 9.4; FDA DMPK Guidance

attributes.name: schedule_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code identifying this PK/PD sampling schedule entry within the study protocol. Used as the externally-known business identifier in CTMS and EDC systems such as Medidata Rave.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTNUM; ICH E3 Section 9.4

attributes.name: schedule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label for this sampling schedule entry (e.g., 'Pre-dose Day 1', '2h Post-dose Cycle 2'). Used in protocol documents and EDC eCRF annotations.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPT; ICH E3

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this PK/PD sampling schedule record. Tracks whether the schedule is in draft protocol design, active for data collection, amended via protocol amendment, retired, or cancelled.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM PC Domain

attributes.name: sdtm_domain
attributes.description: CDISC Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) domain to which this sampling record maps (e.g., PC for Pharmacokinetics Concentrations, PP for Pharmacokinetic Parameters). Required for regulatory submission datasets.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA CDISC Requirements

attributes.name: sdtm_pctptnum
attributes.description: Numeric representation of the planned timepoint as defined in CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTNUM. Used for sorting and PK modeling in SAS Drug Development and ADaM datasets.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTNUM; CDISC ADaM ADPC; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Ordinal sequence number defining the order of this sampling timepoint within the visit or study day PK profile. Used for display ordering in eCRF and SDTM datasets.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: shipping_condition
attributes.description: Required temperature or condition for shipping the sample from the clinical site to the central or bioanalytical laboratory (e.g., dry ice, refrigerated, ambient).
attributes.references: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

attributes.name: sparse_sampling
attributes.description: Indicates whether this timepoint is part of a sparse (population PK) sampling design rather than a full intensive PK profile. Drives population PK modeling strategy.
attributes.references: FDA Population Pharmacokinetics Guidance 2022; ICH E3; CDISC SDTM PC Domain

attributes.name: steady_state_sample
attributes.description: Indicates whether this sampling timepoint is intended to characterize drug concentrations at pharmacokinetic steady state. Relevant for multiple-dose PK studies.
attributes.references: FDA DMPK Guidance; ICH E3 Section 9.4; CDISC SDTM PC Domain

attributes.name: storage_temperature
attributes.description: Required storage temperature condition for the collected sample prior to shipment to the bioanalytical laboratory (e.g., ambient, refrigerated 2-8°C, frozen -20°C, frozen -70°C). Critical for sample stability.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018; EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation 2011; ICH Q1A

attributes.name: timepoint_reference
attributes.description: The reference event from which the nominal timepoint is measured (e.g., first dose, previous dose, start of infusion, end of infusion). Maps to CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTREF.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM PC.PCTPTREF; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this PK/PD sampling schedule record was last modified. Supports audit trail requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: window_lower_bound
attributes.description: Allowable lower deviation from the nominal timepoint for sample collection (expressed as a negative or zero offset in the same unit as nominal_timepoint_unit). Defines the acceptable collection window per protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

attributes.name: window_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the sampling window lower and upper bounds (e.g., minutes, hours, days).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM PC Domain

attributes.name: window_upper_bound
attributes.description: Allowable upper deviation from the nominal timepoint for sample collection (expressed as a positive offset in the same unit as nominal_timepoint_unit). Defines the acceptable collection window per protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

products.name: amendment_site_implementation
products.description: This association product represents the Event between study_protocol_amendment and study_site. It captures the formal process by which each protocol amendment is communicated to, acknowledged by, and operationally implemented at a specific investigational site. Each record links one protocol amendment to one study site and carries implementation-specific attributes — status, dates, reconsent completion, and EDC update confirmation — that exist only in the context of this amendment-site pairing and belong to neither entity alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, every protocol amendment must be formally implemented at each active investigational site — a site receives multiple amendments over a study's lifecycle, and each amendment must be tracked for implementation status, notification, and reconsent completion at every site independently. This is an operationally managed process: CRAs actively create, update, and close out amendment implementation records per site, making 'AmendmentSiteImplementation' a genuine business entity that clinical operations teams manage daily. The relationship carries its own rich data (implementation_status, implementation_date, notification_date, reconsent_completed_flag, edc_configuration_updated_flag, implementation_deadline) that belongs to neither the amendment nor the site alone.

products.name: ip_site_accountability
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory and operational contract between an investigational product and an investigational site. It captures the per-site authorization, storage compliance, dispensing status, and drug accountability obligations mandated by GCP and 21 CFR 312.62. Each record links one investigational_product to one investigational_site and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific IMP-site relationship — they cannot reside on the IMP master or site master alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, an investigational product (IMP) is shipped to and stored at multiple investigational sites simultaneously across a study, and each site handles multiple IMPs across different studies. The business actively manages per-site IMP authorization, storage compliance, dispensing authorization, and accountability — all of which are GCP and regulatory requirements (21 CFR 312.62) that constitute a named, operationally managed relationship. This is not an analytical correlation; clinical operations teams create, update, and audit these records throughout the trial lifecycle.

products.name: country_submission
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory filing event between a study_country and a regulatory submission. It captures the operational record of a specific submission being filed with or applicable to a specific country's regulatory authority within a clinical study. Each record links one study_country to one submission and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that country-submission pairing — such as the national sequence number, country-specific filing date, and national authority acknowledgement. Managed by regulatory affairs teams as part of the country-level dossier lifecycle.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single regulatory submission (e.g., a CTA package) can cover multiple countries simultaneously, and a single country's study activation requires multiple discrete submissions over time (initial CTA filing, substantial amendments, annual safety reports, responses to agency queries). The business actively manages and tracks each country-submission pairing as an operational record — regulatory affairs teams create, update, and close these records as part of the regulatory lifecycle. This is not an analytical correlation derivable from joins; it is a first-class operational entity that regulatory operations teams manage daily.

products.name: product_designation
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory designation grant relationship between an investigational_product and a special_designation. It captures the operational record of which special regulatory designation applies to which investigational product, under what indication scope, at what development phase, and as of what grant date. Each record links one investigational_product to one special_designation with attributes that exist only in the context of this product-designation pairing — such as the specific indication for which the designation was granted to that product and the applicable development phase.. Existence Justification: In clinical research, an investigational product (IMP) can receive multiple special regulatory designations simultaneously — e.g., a single drug may hold both Orphan Drug and Breakthrough Therapy designations from the FDA, plus a PRIME designation from the EMA, each for potentially different indications or scopes. Conversely, while a special designation is typically granted to a specific product-indication pair, a single designation record (e.g., an Orphan Drug designation for a rare disease) can in practice cover a product program that spans multiple formulations or related compounds. The business actively manages this relationship — regulatory affairs teams track which designations apply to which products, under what conditions, and for which indication scope, making this an operationally managed association with its own lifecycle data.

attributes.name: phone

attributes.name: specialty

products.name: principal_investigator
products.description: Master record for Principal Investigators (PIs) conducting clinical trials. Captures PI credentials, medical license numbers, specialty, board certifications, GCP training history, FDA Form 1572 submission status, financial disclosure status, debarment check results, and professional affiliations. Distinct from site_contact as PIs have regulatory accountability and their own lifecycle across multiple studies and sites.

attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Principal Investigator (PI) master record in the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS). Serves as the primary key for all downstream joins and regulatory traceability.

attributes.name: disqualification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the PI was disqualified from conducting clinical trials, either by a regulatory authority or by the sponsor. Nullable for active investigators.

attributes.name: disqualification_reason
attributes.description: Narrative description of the reason for PI disqualification, if applicable. Populated only when lifecycle_status is 'disqualified'. Required for regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.70; FDA Disqualified/Restricted Investigators List; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: email

attributes.name: eudract_investigator_number

attributes.name: fda_investigator_number
attributes.description: FDA-assigned investigator identifier, if applicable, used in IND applications and regulatory submissions to uniquely identify the PI in FDA systems.

attributes.name: financial_disclosure_date

attributes.name: financial_disclosure_status

attributes.name: first_name

attributes.name: form_1572_date

attributes.name: form_1572_status

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to program.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Site capacity assessments evaluate therapeutic area expertise as a primary dimension for program-level site selection and resource planning. The plain-text `therapeutic_area_expertise` column is a den

attributes.name: active_subject_count
attributes.description: Current number of subjects actively enrolled and on-study across all protocols at the site at the time of the capacity assessment. Used to calculate current capacity utilization.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: annual_patient_pool_size
attributes.description: Estimated number of patients seen annually at the site who could potentially qualify for clinical trial enrollment across therapeutic areas. A key input to enrollment feasibility planning and site selection scoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the sponsor or CRO representative who formally approved this capacity record for use in site selection and enrollment planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which this capacity record was formally approved by the authorized sponsor or CRO representative. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: assessment_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the site capacity was formally assessed or declared. Used to determine the currency of the capacity data for site selection scoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: available_exam_rooms
attributes.description: Number of examination rooms at the site that are available and dedicated or allocable to clinical trial activities. Directly constrains the number of concurrent subject visits that can be conducted.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ISO 14155

attributes.name: capacity_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this site capacity record. 'draft' indicates an initial assessment in progress; 'active' indicates the current approved capacity profile; 'under_review' indicates a reassessment is in progress; 'suspended' indicates the site is temporarily not accepting new trials; 'archived' indicates a superseded historical record.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: capacity_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the capacity figures were self-declared by the site (Principal Investigator or Site Coordinator), independently assessed by the CRA/CRO during a feasibility visit, or negotiated and agreed between the sponsor and site.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: competing_protocol_count
attributes.description: Number of active or pending clinical trial protocols currently running at the site that compete for the same patient population, staff resources, or infrastructure. A key input to site selection scoring and workload balancing.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: crc_count
attributes.description: Number of Clinical Research Coordinators (CRCs) currently assigned to or available at the site for trial coordination activities. Used in workload balancing and site selection scoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which this site capacity record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: dedicated_research_fte
attributes.description: Total full-time equivalent (FTE) headcount of staff dedicated to clinical research activities at the site, including Clinical Research Coordinators (CRCs), research nurses, and sub-investigators. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 2.5 FTE).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Workday HCM

attributes.name: dropout_rate_pct
attributes.description: Historical percentage of enrolled subjects who withdrew or were discontinued from trials at this site prior to study completion. Used in enrollment planning to account for subject attrition.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13

attributes.name: ecg_capability
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site has on-site 12-lead ECG capability for cardiac safety assessments required by many clinical trial protocols.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ICH E14 (QT/QTc Studies)

attributes.name: econsent_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site is equipped and approved to administer electronic Informed Consent Forms (eICF) using an eConsent platform such as Clinpal, in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; FDA eConsent Guidance 2016; Clinpal

attributes.name: edc_system_capable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Data Capture (EDC) System Capability Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site has the technical infrastructure and trained staff to use an Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system such as Medidata Rave for electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) data entry.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; Medidata Rave

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this capacity record is considered valid and applicable for site selection and enrollment planning purposes.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: effective_until_date
attributes.description: Date until which this capacity record remains valid. Null indicates the record is open-ended and currently active. Populated when a new version supersedes this record or the site closes.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: gcp_compliance_status
attributes.description: Current GCP compliance status of the site as determined by the most recent monitoring visit or audit. 'compliant' indicates no findings; 'minor_findings' indicates observations requiring corrective action; 'major_findings' indicates significant deviations; 'critical_findings' indicates critical GCP violations requiring immediate action; 'not_assessed' indicates no assessment has been completed.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR 312; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

attributes.name: imaging_capability
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site has on-site medical imaging capability (e.g., MRI, CT, PET, X-ray, ultrasound) relevant to clinical trial endpoint assessments. Sites without imaging may require referral to external imaging centers.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ISO 14155

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_capacity
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Approved Protocol Capacity
attributes.description: Maximum number of concurrent protocols for which the site's IRB/IEC has granted or is willing to grant approval. Regulatory constraint on the site's operational capacity.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 56; ICH E6(R2) Section 3; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

attributes.name: irt_rtsm_capable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Interactive Response Technology / Randomization and Trial Supply Management (IRT/RTSM) Capability Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site staff are trained and equipped to use an IRT/RTSM system (such as Medidata RTSM) for subject randomization and investigational product dispensing.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: lab_processing_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site has on-site laboratory processing capability for clinical trial samples (e.g., centrifugation, aliquoting, storage). Sites without this capability must rely on central or local reference laboratories.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; CLIA (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments); ISO 15189

attributes.name: lab_sample_processing_capacity
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Sample Processing Capacity (Samples per Day)
attributes.description: Maximum number of clinical trial samples the on-site laboratory can process per day. Null if the site does not have on-site laboratory processing capability. Used to assess feasibility for high-frequency sampling protocols.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ISO 15189; CLIA

attributes.name: last_monitoring_visit_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent on-site monitoring visit conducted by a Clinical Research Associate (CRA). Used to assess the currency of the GCP compliance status and schedule the next monitoring visit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: max_concurrent_protocols
attributes.description: Maximum number of distinct clinical trial protocols the site can run simultaneously without compromising GCP compliance or subject safety. Used for workload balancing across the site portfolio.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: max_concurrent_subjects
attributes.description: Maximum number of trial subjects the site can actively manage simultaneously across all concurrent protocols, as declared or assessed. This is the principal capacity metric used in site selection scoring and enrollment planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for CRA or site management notes regarding specific capacity constraints, caveats, or contextual information not captured in structured fields (e.g., planned staff changes, facility renovations, seasonal patient volume variations).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: pharmacy_cold_chain_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site pharmacy has validated cold chain storage capability (e.g., 2–8°C refrigeration or -20°C / -80°C freezer storage) for temperature-sensitive investigational medicinal products.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; EU GMP Annex 13; WHO Technical Report Series 961

attributes.name: pharmacy_storage_capacity_units
attributes.description: Number of discrete storage units (e.g., refrigerator slots, freezer compartments, or shelf units) available in the site pharmacy for investigational medicinal product (IMP) storage. Constrains the number of concurrent protocols requiring pharmacy support.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 312

attributes.name: pi_fte_allocation
attributes.description: Proportion of the Principal Investigator's time (expressed as FTE) allocated to clinical research activities at this site. A PI with 0.5 FTE allocation is available 50% of their working time for trial oversight.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.60

attributes.name: recruitment_rate_per_month
attributes.description: Historical average number of subjects recruited per month by this site across prior clinical trials, based on CTMS enrollment data. Used as a predictive input for enrollment planning and site selection scoring.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13

attributes.name: screen_failure_rate_pct
attributes.description: Historical percentage of screened subjects who failed to meet eligibility criteria and were not enrolled, based on prior trial data at this site. A high screen failure rate reduces effective enrollment capacity.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13

attributes.name: site_selection_score
attributes.description: Composite numeric score (typically 0–100) assigned to the site based on capacity, feasibility, and performance metrics for use in site selection ranking. Calculated by the CTMS or feasibility scoring model.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which this site capacity record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail and change tracking requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: utilization_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the site's maximum concurrent subject capacity currently in use, calculated as (active_subject_count / max_concurrent_subjects) * 100. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 75.50 for 75.5%). Used for workload balancing and site selection scoring.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Monotonically incrementing version number for this site capacity record, enabling historical tracking of capacity changes over time. Version 1 represents the initial assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

products.name: site_agreement

Complements the agreement domain which owns master service agreements at the sponsor level.

attributes.name: tmf_document_id

attributes.description: Reference identifier of the executed agreement document as stored in the Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) in Veeva Vault. Enables direct navigation from the CTMS record to the source document for inspection readiness.

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable reference number assigned to the site agreement (e.g., CTA-2024-0042). Used for cross-system tracking, regulatory correspondence, and audit trails. Sourced from Oracle Siebel CTMS or Veeva Vault contract management module.
