attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the site agreement. Tracks progression from initial drafting through negotiation, execution, and eventual expiry or termination. Drives workflow routing in Veeva Vault and Oracle Siebel CTMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Draft|Under Negotiation|Pending Execution|Executed|Expired|Terminated|Superseded — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault Contract Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the site-level agreement. CTA (Clinical Trial Agreement) is the primary investigational site contract; CDA (Confidential Disclosure Agreement) governs pre-trial information sharing; Budget Amendment captures renegotiated financial terms; Site Budget Agreement formalizes per-patient and overhead fee structures; Letter of Intent signals site commitment prior to full execution.
attributes.value_regex: CTA|CDA|Budget Amendment|Site Budget Agreement|Letter of Intent
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; FDA 21 CFR 312.53; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 46

attributes.name: amendment_number
attributes.description: Sequential amendment version number for this agreement record. A value of 0 indicates the original agreement; values ≥1 indicate successive amendments. Enables version tracking of negotiated changes over the study lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; Veeva Vault Document Management; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: closeout_fee
attributes.description: Fixed fee payable to the investigational site upon study close-out to cover archival, final monitoring visit support, and regulatory document finalization activities. Expressed in the currency defined by currency_code.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: confidentiality_term_years
attributes.description: Duration in years for which confidentiality obligations under the agreement remain in force after the agreement's expiration or termination. Particularly relevant for CDA (Confidential Disclosure Agreement) components.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; GDPR Article 5; HIPAA; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp indicating when this site agreement record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: cro_entity
attributes.description: Name of the Contract Research Organization (CRO) acting as the contracting party on behalf of the sponsor, if applicable. Captures the legal entity name when the CRO executes the agreement under delegated authority.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.2; FDA 21 CFR 312.52

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all financial terms within this site agreement (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Ensures consistent financial reporting across multi-country trials.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA Finance; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: data_privacy_addendum
attributes.description: Indicates whether a data privacy addendum (DPA) or data processing agreement is included as part of or annexed to this site agreement, addressing GDPR, HIPAA, or other applicable data protection obligations for patient data.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 28; HIPAA 45 CFR 164; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the site agreement becomes legally binding and operative. Marks the start of the contractual relationship between the sponsor/CRO and the investigational site. Aligns with MASTER_AGREEMENT EFFECTIVE_FROM category.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; FDA 21 CFR 312; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 46

attributes.name: execution_date
attributes.description: Date on which all required parties signed and fully executed the site agreement. May differ from the effective date when agreements are backdated or have a future effective date. Critical for regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the site agreement is scheduled to expire or cease to be operative. Nullable for open-ended agreements. Triggers renewal workflow alerts in Veeva Vault. Aligns with MASTER_AGREEMENT EFFECTIVE_UNTIL category.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; Veeva Vault Contract Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: governing_law_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the jurisdiction whose laws govern the interpretation and enforcement of this site agreement. Critical for multi-national trial legal compliance and dispute resolution.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; GDPR; HIPAA; ICH E6(R2); ISO 3166-1

attributes.name: indemnification_clause
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site agreement includes an indemnification clause protecting the investigational site and PI from third-party claims arising from the sponsor's negligence. Standard in CTA templates but may be absent in certain jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; FDA 21 CFR 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: insurance_coverage_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement mandates that the sponsor or CRO maintain clinical trial insurance coverage for the duration of the study at this site. Regulatory requirement in many jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.8; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 76; ISO 14155

attributes.name: insurance_policy_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the clinical trial insurance policy covering this site agreement. Populated when insurance_coverage_required is True. Used for regulatory inspection documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.8; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 76

attributes.name: ip_ownership_clause
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site agreement contains an intellectual property ownership clause specifying that all study data, inventions, and results generated at the site are owned by the sponsor. Standard in CTA templates.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; FDA 21 CFR 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Approval Required
attributes.description: Indicates whether IRB (Institutional Review Board) or IEC (Independent Ethics Committee) approval is a condition precedent to the agreement becoming operative. Relevant for agreements at sites in jurisdictions requiring ethics committee review prior to contract execution.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; FDA 21 CFR 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 4; OHRP

attributes.name: legal_review_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the sponsor's or CRO's legal team has completed their review and approved the final agreement text prior to execution. Part of the quality control workflow tracked in Veeva Vault.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; Veeva Vault Quality Management; SOX

attributes.name: legal_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the legal review of the site agreement was completed and sign-off was granted. Populated when legal_review_completed is True. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault

attributes.name: negotiation_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which formal contract negotiation commenced between the sponsor/CRO and the investigational site. Used to calculate cycle time KPIs for site activation performance reporting in CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing supplementary notes, special conditions, deviations from standard templates, or negotiation context relevant to this site agreement. Supports audit trail and institutional knowledge retention.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; ALCOA+; Veeva Vault

attributes.name: overhead_rate_pct
attributes.description: Institutional overhead or indirect cost rate (expressed as a percentage) applied on top of direct site costs as negotiated in the site budget agreement. Typically charged by academic medical centers or hospital institutions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; SAP S/4HANA Finance; OMB Circular A-21 (US academic institutions)

attributes.name: payment_schedule_type
attributes.description: Defines the payment trigger mechanism agreed upon in the site budget agreement. Determines how and when invoices are generated and processed in SAP S/4HANA Accounts Payable.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Number of days from invoice receipt within which payment must be remitted to the investigational site, as stipulated in the site agreement (e.g., Net 30, Net 45, Net 60). Drives accounts payable processing in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Accounts Payable; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6

attributes.name: per_patient_fee
attributes.description: Agreed fee payable to the investigational site for each evaluable patient who completes the study per protocol. Core financial term in the site budget agreement. Expressed in the currency defined by currency_code.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; SAP S/4HANA Project Accounting; FDA 21 CFR 312.53

attributes.name: publication_rights_clause
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site agreement includes a publication rights clause defining the investigator's right to publish study results and the sponsor's right to review manuscripts prior to submission. Relevant for academic site agreements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; ICMJE Publication Guidelines; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 37

attributes.name: site_signature_date
attributes.description: Date on which the authorized representative of the investigational site (e.g., PI or institutional official) signed the agreement. May differ from the sponsor/CRO signature date in multi-party execution workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: sponsor_signature_date
attributes.description: Date on which the authorized representative of the sponsor or CRO signed the agreement. The later of site_signature_date and sponsor_signature_date typically defines the execution_date.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: startup_fee
attributes.description: One-time fixed fee payable to the investigational site upon activation to cover site initiation activities such as staff training, IRB/IEC submission preparation, and regulatory document collection. Expressed in the currency defined by currency_code.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the site agreement was early-terminated prior to its scheduled expiration. Populated only when agreement_status is 'Terminated'. Supports regulatory close-out documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; FDA 21 CFR 312.64; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Categorized reason for early termination of the site agreement. Required for regulatory reporting and site performance analytics. Populated only when agreement_status is 'Terminated'.
attributes.value_regex: Mutual Consent|Sponsor Decision|Site Decision|Regulatory Action|Protocol Termination|For Cause

products.name: ib_site_distribution
products.description: This association product represents the IB Distribution Log event between investigational_site and investigator_brochure_safety. It captures the GCP-mandated record of each Investigator Brochure version distributed to each investigational site, including receipt confirmation, distribution method, and IRB/IEC notification tracking. Each record links one investigational_site to one investigator_brochure_safety version and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this site-specific distribution event.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, an Investigator Brochure (IB) version is distributed to every active investigational site participating in the relevant study — one IB version goes to many sites. Simultaneously, a single site receives multiple IB versions over the lifecycle of a study (initial version, safety amendments, annual updates). The business actively manages this distribution as a GCP-mandated essential document process called the 'IB Distribution Log', tracking per-site receipt confirmation, distribution method, and IRB/IEC notification obligations for each IB version delivered to each site.

products.name: sponsor_site_qualification
products.description: This association product represents the formal qualification and relationship contract between an investigational_site and a sponsor organization. It captures the operational record of a sponsor's qualification, rating, and preferred-network designation of a specific site — data that exists only in the context of this sponsor-site pairing. Each record links one investigational_site to one organization and tracks the qualification status, performance history, and preferred-site designation that the sponsor actively manages as part of their site network strategy.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials operations, investigational sites actively work with multiple sponsor organizations simultaneously across different studies, and each sponsor organization maintains relationships with dozens to hundreds of sites across their trial portfolio. This is not an analytical correlation — sponsors actively manage a 'qualified site roster' or 'preferred site network' as an operational business concept, tracking each site's qualification status, performance rating, and preferred-site designation per sponsor. The relationship itself carries meaningful data (qualification status, performance rating, relationship start date, historical study count) that belongs to neither the site nor the sponsor alone.

products.name: pi_qualification
products.description: This association product represents the Qualification relationship between a Principal Investigator and a Sponsor Organization. It captures the formal regulatory approval process by which a sponsor certifies a PI as eligible to conduct studies under their IND portfolio. Each record links one Principal Investigator to one Sponsor Organization and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific sponsor-PI qualification relationship, including approval status, therapeutic area scope, performance history, and compliance verification dates.. Existence Justification: In clinical research, a Principal Investigator is formally qualified and approved by each sponsor organization independently before being permitted to conduct studies for that sponsor. A single PI may be qualified by multiple sponsors (e.g., Pfizer, Roche, Novartis) simultaneously, and each sponsor maintains a roster of many qualified PIs. This is an actively managed regulatory process — sponsors track debarment status, GCP compliance, therapeutic area approvals, and performance ratings per PI, and the qualification must be renewed or revoked independently per sponsor.

products.name: signal_review
products.description: This association product represents the Site Signal Review event between study_site and safety_signal. It captures the operational process by which a medical monitor or safety team evaluates a specific safety signal in the context of a specific investigational site — recording site-level case counts, risk assessments, required actions, and review outcomes. Each record links one study_site to one safety_signal and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this site-specific signal evaluation. Supports regulatory traceability for site-level safety actions and DSMB/DMC reporting.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a safety signal is typically detected at the study level but must be evaluated across all participating sites — a single signal (e.g., hepatotoxicity) may implicate multiple study sites with differing case counts and require site-specific risk assessments and actions. Conversely, a single study site may be implicated in multiple safety signals over the course of a study's lifecycle. Medical monitors and safety teams actively manage per-site signal reviews, tracking site-specific case counts, risk assessments, and actions taken — this is an operational process, not an analytical derivation.

products.name: depot_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the supply assignment (role) between an investigational_site and a depot. It captures the formal clinical supply routing decision that designates which depot(s) serve each investigational site, including whether the depot is the primary or backup supply source, the logistics route type, and the effective date window of the assignment. Each record links one investigational_site to one depot and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this supply routing relationship. Clinical supply teams actively create, update, and close these records during study setup, supply chain re-routing, and site closeout.. Existence Justification: In clinical supply chain operations, an investigational site can receive IMPs from multiple depots (a primary depot plus one or more backup/regional depots), and a single depot services many investigational sites across multiple studies. This is a formally managed supply assignment relationship — clinical supply teams actively create, maintain, and expire these depot-to-site routing records as part of study setup and supply chain management. The relationship carries its own operational data (primary flag, route type, effective dates) that belongs to neither the site nor the depot alone.

products.name: authorization
products.description: This association product represents the Contract between investigational_site and clinical_trial_authorization. It captures the site-level regulatory authorization record that links a specific investigational site to a Clinical Trial Authorization issued by a national competent authority. Each record documents the authorization status, site-specific conditions, enrollment limits, and notification dates that apply uniquely to the site-CTA pairing — data that cannot reside on either the site master record or the CTA master record alone. Regulatory affairs teams create, update, and query these records throughout the trial lifecycle to demonstrate per-site regulatory compliance.. Existence Justification: In clinical research operations, a single Clinical Trial Authorization (CTA) issued by a national competent authority covers multiple investigational sites within that member state, and a given investigational site participates under multiple CTAs across different studies and countries. Regulatory operations teams actively manage site-specific CTA conditions, enrollment limits per site, and notification dates — data that belongs to the site-CTA pairing, not to either entity alone. This relationship is a recognized operational concept in EU CTR 536/2014 and national regulatory frameworks, where site-level authorization status must be tracked independently from the overall CTA.

attributes.name: enrollment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the subject within the enrollment process. Represents the subject's progression from initial screening through study completion or withdrawal. attributes.name: enrollment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the enrollment event type. attributes.name: first_dose_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject received the first dose of investigational product (IP). Defines the start of the treatment-emergent period for TEAE analysis. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RFXSTDTC; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CTCAE

attributes.name: icf_signed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject (or legally authorized representative) signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF), confirming voluntary agreement to participate. Must precede any study-specific procedures. Sourced from Clinpal eConsent.

attributes.name: icf_version

attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; OHRP; GDPR Article 7; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: itt_flag

attributes.name: last_dose_date

attributes.name: last_visit_date

attributes.name: pp_flag

attributes.name: randomization_date

attributes.name: safety_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject is included in the safety analysis population (typically all subjects who received at least one dose of study treatment). Used for adverse event and safety reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC ADaM ADSL; FDA Guidance; SAP

attributes.name: screen_failure_reason

attributes.name: randomization_method
attributes.description: The statistical randomization method used to generate this assignment (e.g., 'block' for permuted block randomization, 'minimization' for minimization/adaptive biased-coin, 'adaptive' for response-adaptive, 'simple' for simple randomization, 'stratified_block' for stratified block). attributes.name: randomization_number

This is the business identifier referenced in eCRFs, regulatory submissions, and audit trails. Corresponds to RNDMNO or equivalent field in RTSM.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RANDFL; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: randomization_ratio
attributes.description: The allocation ratio applied at randomization (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'). Represents the relative probability of assignment to each treatment arm as defined in the protocol and RTSM configuration.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 3.4; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: randomization_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the subject was randomized as recorded by the IRT/RTSM system. This is the authoritative business event timestamp for the randomization transaction. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM DM.RANDDT; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: re_randomization_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this assignment is a re-randomization event (True) rather than the initial randomization (False). Re-randomization may occur in crossover designs, adaptive trials, or following a protocol deviation that necessitates re-assignment.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: sdtm_randfl

attributes.description: CDISC SDTM-compliant randomization flag (Y/N) indicating whether the subject was randomized, as mapped to the DM.RANDFL variable. Populated during SDTM transformation to support regulatory submission datasets.

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: The native record identifier from the originating IRT/RTSM system (Medidata Rave RTSM or Oracle Clinical One IRT). Enables bidirectional traceability between the Silver layer lakehouse and the operational source system for reconciliation and audit purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: data_entry_status

attributes.name: days_from_planned

attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the visit in minutes from check-in to check-out as recorded in the CTMS or EDC. Used for site capacity planning, resource utilization analysis, and subject burden assessment.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: early_termination_reason
attributes.description: Reason for early termination of the visit or the subject's participation, applicable when visit_type is 'early_termination'. Captures clinical, safety, or administrative reasons per protocol requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM DS Domain

attributes.name: informed_consent_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether a valid, signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) was confirmed on file prior to this visit (True) or not (False). Critical GCP compliance requirement; absence may constitute a major protocol deviation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

attributes.name: is_scheduled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this visit was a protocol-scheduled visit (True) or an unscheduled/ad-hoc visit not defined in the protocol schedule of assessments (False). Unscheduled visits may indicate safety events or protocol deviations.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM SV Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: is_unblinded
attributes.description: Indicates whether the treatment assignment was unblinded at or prior to this visit (True) or the subject remained blinded (False). Relevant for double-blind studies and impacts data integrity assessments.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: missed_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded reason explaining why a scheduled visit was missed by the subject (e.g., subject unavailable, adverse event, travel, withdrew consent, site closure). Populated only when visit_status is 'missed'. Required for protocol deviation assessment and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM SV Domain

attributes.name: missed_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized coded value for the reason a scheduled visit was missed, aligned with sponsor or protocol-defined coding scheme. Complements missed_reason free text for structured analytics and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; MedDRA

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: planned_visit_date
attributes.description: The target date on which the visit was scheduled to occur per the protocol-defined visit schedule, calculated from the subject's reference date (e.g., randomization date or first dose date). Used to compute visit window compliance.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM SV.SVSTDTC; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this visit resulted in a protocol deviation (True), such as a visit outside the allowed window, missed required assessments, or procedural non-compliance. Triggers downstream protocol deviation record creation in the compliance domain.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: query_count
attributes.description: Number of open data discrepancy queries (DCFs) associated with this visit's eCRF data in the EDC system. Used for data quality monitoring and site performance tracking. Non-zero values may block database lock.
attributes.references: ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave EDC; CDISC CDASH

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this visit record was sourced (Medidata Rave EDC, Oracle Siebel CTMS, Oracle Clinical One, or manual entry). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; CDISC SDTM SV Domain

attributes.name: source_system_visit_key
attributes.description: The native primary key or unique identifier for this visit record in the originating source system (e.g., Medidata Rave visit OID, Siebel CTMS visit row ID). Enables traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and the system of record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; CDISC SDTM SV Domain

attributes.name: study_day
attributes.description: The relative study day on which the visit occurred, calculated from the subject's reference start date per CDISC convention (Day 1 = reference date; Day -1 = day before; no Day 0). Maps to SVSTDY in CDISC SDTM SV domain.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM SV.SVSTDY; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this subject visit record in the source system or Silver layer. Required for change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: visit_code
attributes.description: Protocol-defined alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the visit within the study schedule (e.g., SCR, BL, V01, V02, ET, EOS). Maps to VISITNUM/VISIT in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Used as the externally-known business identifier for the visit.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM SV.VISIT; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: visit_number
attributes.description: Sequential numeric identifier for the visit as defined in the study protocol schedule of assessments. Maps directly to VISITNUM in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Used for ordering visits chronologically within a subject's participation.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM SV.VISITNUM; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: visit_status
attributes.description: Current completion status of the visit indicating whether the subject attended and completed all required assessments, missed the visit entirely, partially completed assessments, had the visit rescheduled, or the visit was cancelled. Core lifecycle status field for monitoring trigger logic.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: visit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the visit by its role in the study protocol lifecycle. Drives SDTM SV domain population and visit compliance analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screening|baseline|treatment|follow_up|unscheduled|early_termination|end_of_study — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM SV Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: week

attributes.name: window_close_date

attributes.name: window_compliance_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the actual visit date fell within the protocol-defined visit window, occurred early (before window open), occurred late (after window close), was missed entirely, or is not applicable (e.g., unscheduled visits). Critical for protocol deviation identification and monitoring trigger logic.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM SV Domain

attributes.name: window_open_date
attributes.description: The earliest acceptable date for the visit to occur per the protocol-defined visit window (planned date minus the allowed early deviation in days). Used to determine visit window compliance status.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, clarifications, or contextual notes related to the deviation that do not fit into structured fields. May include reviewer notes, sponsor feedback, or monitoring observations.

attributes.description: The date and time when this deviation record was first created in the source system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2).

attributes.name: data_integrity_impact
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the deviation compromised the integrity of study data collected from the subject. Informs decisions on data exclusion, sensitivity analyses, and per-protocol (PP) population definitions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; FDA Data Integrity Guidance; CDISC

attributes.name: deviation_category
attributes.description: Classification of the deviation by severity and impact. 'Major' deviations significantly affect subject safety or data integrity; 'important' deviations may affect subject rights or study data; 'minor' deviations have minimal impact. Drives regulatory reportability and CAPA requirements per ICH E6(R2).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

attributes.name: deviation_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the specific deviation that occurred, including what protocol requirement was not met, the circumstances, and any relevant context. Captured by the Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) or Clinical Research Associate (CRA) in Oracle Siebel CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: deviation_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier for the deviation record as assigned by the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) or MasterControl. Used for cross-system referencing, regulatory submissions, and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; Oracle Siebel CTMS; MasterControl

attributes.name: deviation_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the deviation record. Tracks progression from initial identification through review, resolution, and closure. Drives operational dashboards and compliance monitoring in Oracle Siebel CTMS and MasterControl.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: identified_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the deviation was first identified or discovered, which may differ from the occurrence date. Used to calculate detection lag and assess monitoring effectiveness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: irb_iec_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Reportability Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this deviation must be reported to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) overseeing the study. Separate from regulatory authority reportability. True = must report to IRB/IEC.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.3; 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

attributes.name: occurrence_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the protocol deviation actually occurred. This is the principal real-world event date, distinct from the date the deviation was identified or reported. Critical for ALCOA+ compliance and regulatory timelines.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; CDISC SDTM DV Domain DVSTDTC

attributes.name: pi_aware_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Principal Investigator (PI) was informed of the deviation. Used to track compliance with site notification requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: pi_aware_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Principal Investigator (PI) at the site has been made aware of this deviation. True = PI has been informed. Required for GCP compliance as the PI bears ultimate responsibility for conduct of the trial at the site.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; FDA GCP Guidance

attributes.name: protocol_section_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific section, clause, or requirement number within the approved study protocol that was deviated from (e.g., 'Section 6.3.2 - Inclusion Criteria'). Enables precise traceability to the protocol document.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; FDA Protocol Deviation Guidance; CDISC SDTM DV Domain

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this deviation must be reported to a regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.), IRB/IEC, or sponsor per applicable regulations and the study protocol. True = reportable; False = not reportable. Drives regulatory submission workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5.2; 21 CFR Part 312.62; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA GCP Guidelines

attributes.name: reported_date
attributes.description: The date on which the deviation was formally reported to the sponsor, IRB/IEC, or regulatory authority as applicable. Used to track compliance with reporting timelines mandated by GCP and applicable regulations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5.2; 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the deviation was formally resolved and closed in the quality management system. Used to calculate time-to-resolution metrics and assess site responsiveness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: root_cause
attributes.description: Narrative description of the underlying root cause of the deviation as determined through investigation. Used to inform corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) and systemic quality improvement. Captured in MasterControl.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.20; MasterControl; FDA CAPA Guidance

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the root cause to enable trending and systemic analysis across deviations. Categories align with standard quality management frameworks used in MasterControl.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: sdtm_domain
attributes.description: The CDISC SDTM domain to which this deviation maps for regulatory submission. Protocol deviations are mapped to the DV (Protocol Deviations) domain per CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA eCTD Submission Standards; EMA Data Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this deviation record was sourced. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements. Primary sources are Oracle Siebel CTMS and MasterControl.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: The native record identifier from the originating source system (Oracle Siebel CTMS or MasterControl). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the operational system of record.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: sponsor_notified_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor was formally notified of the deviation. Used to verify compliance with contractual and regulatory notification timelines.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.4; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: sponsor_notified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the study sponsor has been formally notified of this deviation. True = sponsor has been notified. Required per GCP obligations for sponsor oversight of investigational sites.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.4; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: subject_continuation_decision
attributes.description: Decision regarding the subject's continued participation in the study following the deviation. Informs subject disposition tracking and intent-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) population assignments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.3; ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM DS Domain

attributes.name: subject_rights_impact
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the deviation affected the rights or well-being of the trial subject, including informed consent procedures, privacy protections, or voluntary participation rights.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 2; Declaration of Helsinki; OHRP; GDPR; HIPAA

attributes.name: subject_safety_impact
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the deviation had an impact on subject safety. 'None' indicates no safety impact; 'potential' indicates possible but unconfirmed impact; 'confirmed' indicates a verified safety impact. Critical for regulatory reporting decisions and DSMB/DMC review.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; FDA Safety Reporting Guidance; EMA GCP Guidelines

attributes.name: type_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the specific type of protocol deviation (e.g., eligibility criteria violation, missed visit, incorrect dosing, prohibited medication use, consent procedure deviation). Sourced from the MasterControl deviation classification taxonomy. attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl; CDISC SDTM DV Domain DVCAT/DVTERM

attributes.name: type_description
attributes.description: Human-readable label corresponding to the deviation_type_code, providing a plain-language description of the deviation type for reporting and review purposes.

attributes.description: Reference to the trial subject (participant) whose enrollment lifecycle status changed. Core party reference for this event log record.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the status transition was formally approved or electronically signed by the authorized user. Distinct from transition_timestamp (when the event occurred) and created_timestamp (when the record was created).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional clinical or administrative comments related to this status transition, entered by the site staff or sponsor. Supports contextual documentation for audit trail completeness per ALCOA+ standards.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this status history record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation requirements. Distinct from transition_timestamp (when the clinical event occurred).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: disposition_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the disposition event type associated with this status transition. Used for regulatory reporting in the CDISC SDTM DS domain and for subject flow summaries in Clinical Study Reports (CSRs). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screen-failure|early-termination|completion|randomization|enrollment|withdrawal|protocol-deviation — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DS.DSCAT; ICH E3 Section 10.2; FDA Guidance on CSR

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this status transition required prior approval from the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) (e.g., re-consent due to protocol amendment). True = IRB/IEC approval was required.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

attributes.name: is_blinded
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject's treatment assignment was blinded at the time of this status transition. True = blinded (treatment identity concealed); False = unblinded (treatment identity known). Critical for maintaining trial integrity and access control.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.7; FDA Guidance on Blinding

attributes.name: is_terminal_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the new_status represents a terminal (end-state) disposition for the subject in this study. True = the subject has reached a final state (completed, withdrawn, screen-failed, lost-to-follow-up) with no further expected transitions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DS domain; ICH E3; FDA Guidance on CSR

attributes.name: itt_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject was included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population at the time of this status transition. Supports biostatistical analysis population tracking per the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle; SAP

attributes.name: new_status
attributes.description: The subject's enrollment lifecycle status after this transition event. Represents the current state the subject entered as a result of this change. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pre-screened|screened|screen-failed|enrolled|randomized|on-treatment|completed|withdrawn|lost-to-follow-up|discontinued — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DS domain; ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical One Subject Status

attributes.name: pp_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject was included in the Per Protocol (PP) analysis population at the time of this status transition. Supports biostatistical analysis population tracking per the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance; SAP

attributes.name: prior_status
attributes.description: The subject's enrollment lifecycle status immediately before this transition event. Together with new_status, defines the state transition vector for longitudinal subject flow analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pre-screened|screened|screen-failed|enrolled|randomized|on-treatment|completed|withdrawn|lost-to-follow-up|discontinued — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DS domain; ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical One Subject Status

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a protocol deviation (PD) was associated with or triggered this status transition. True = a protocol deviation is linked to this transition event. Supports GCP compliance monitoring and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations; GCP

attributes.name: safety_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject was included in the safety analysis population at the time of this status transition (i.e., received at least one dose of investigational product). Supports safety reporting and TEAE analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting; CTCAE

attributes.name: screen_failure_reason
attributes.description: Specific reason why the subject failed screening and did not proceed to enrollment. Populated only when new_status = 'screen-failed'. Used for site feasibility analysis, protocol amendment decisions, and enrollment optimization.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM DS domain; Oracle Clinical One

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this status transition record was sourced. Either Oracle Clinical One (study design and subject management) or Medidata Rave (EDC and RTSM). Supports data lineage tracking in the Silver layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: source_system_record_key
attributes.description: The native primary key or unique identifier of this status transition record in the originating source system (Oracle Clinical One or Medidata Rave). Enables traceability back to the system of record for reconciliation and audit purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: study_day
attributes.description: The relative study day on which the status transition occurred, calculated from the subject's reference start date (typically first dose date). Negative values indicate pre-treatment days. Aligns with CDISC SDTM timing variable conventions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM General Observation Class; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: subject_number
attributes.description: The externally-known alphanumeric subject identifier assigned at enrollment (e.g., site-sequential number such as '001-001'). Used in regulatory submissions, eCRFs, and audit trails to identify the participant without revealing personal identity. Sourced from Oracle Clinical One and Medidata Rave.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM DM.SUBJID; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA §164.514

attributes.name: transition_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the subject's status transition occurred in the real-world clinical context. This is the principal business event date used for enrollment timelines, regulatory reporting, and subject flow analysis. Distinct from the system capture timestamp.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM DS.DSSTDTC; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: transition_reason
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the clinical or administrative reason for the subject status change (e.g., 'Subject met all inclusion/exclusion criteria', 'Subject withdrew consent', 'Adverse event led to discontinuation'). Supports regulatory audit trails and disposition analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM DS.DSDECOD; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.62

attributes.name: transition_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized coded value for the transition reason, aligned with CDISC SDTM DS domain disposition event codes (e.g., 'COMPLETED', 'WITHDRAWAL BY SUBJECT', 'ADVERSE EVENT', 'SCREEN FAILURE'). Enables structured analysis and regulatory submission mapping.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DS.DSDECOD; MedDRA; ICH E3

attributes.name: transition_sequence
attributes.description: Sequential ordinal number of this status transition within the subject's complete enrollment lifecycle history. Enables chronological ordering of all transitions for a given subject within a study. Starts at 1 for the first recorded transition.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DS domain; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: transition_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone) at which the subject status transition was recorded in the source system (Oracle Clinical One or Medidata Rave). Supports 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements and ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation standards.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; CDISC SDTM DS.DSSTDTC

attributes.name: triggered_by_system
attributes.description: Identifies whether the status transition was triggered by a human user or an automated system process, and which source system initiated it (Oracle Clinical One, Medidata Rave, IRT/RTSM). Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: triggered_by_user_role
attributes.description: The clinical role of the user who triggered this status transition (e.g., CRC - Clinical Research Coordinator, CRA - Clinical Research Associate, PI - Principal Investigator). Supports audit trail completeness and role-based accountability per GCP. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CRC|CRA|PI|sub-investigator|sponsor|system|data-manager — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this status history record was last modified in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports change tracking, audit trail completeness, and data quality monitoring per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ standards.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: withdrawal_reason
attributes.description: Specific reason for subject withdrawal or discontinuation from the study. Populated when new_status is 'withdrawn' or 'discontinued'. Categorized per CDISC SDTM DS domain controlled terminology (e.g., 'ADVERSE EVENT', 'WITHDRAWAL BY SUBJECT', 'LOST TO FOLLOW-UP').
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DS.DSDECOD; ICH E3 Section 10.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.62

products.name: subject_contact
products.description: Master entity storing contact and communication details for a trial subject, including primary phone, secondary phone, email address, preferred contact method, emergency contact name and relationship, home address (street, city, state, postal code, country), and privacy consent flags for contact. Supports patient recruitment follow-up, visit reminders, and safety follow-up communications. Governed by GDPR and HIPAA data privacy requirements. Sourced from Clinpal and Oracle Siebel CTMS.
products.reference: GDPR Article 5; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E6(R2) GCP subject identification

attributes.name: subject_contact_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the subject contact record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: consent_icf_version_id
attributes.description: Reference to the version of the Informed Consent Form (ICF) under which the subject's contact data privacy consent was obtained. Ensures traceability of consent to the specific ICF version approved by the IRB/IEC.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014; GDPR Article 7; Clinpal

attributes.name: investigational_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site where the subject is enrolled. Used to scope contact data to the correct site for monitoring and follow-up.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which this subject is enrolled. Scopes the contact record to a specific trial.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Reference to the trial subject (patient) whose contact information is stored in this record. Links to the subject master entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: address_line1
attributes.description: First line of the subject's home address (street number and street name). Used for postal communications, visit logistics, and safety follow-up mailings.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: address_line2
attributes.description: Second line of the subject's home address (apartment, suite, unit, floor, or building name). Supplements address_line1 for complete postal address.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: address_verified_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject's home address was last verified by site staff. Supports ALCOA+ data quality requirements and ensures contact information is current for safety follow-up.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: address_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject's home address has been verified by site staff or through an address validation service. True = address confirmed; False = address unverified or pending confirmation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality of the subject's home address. Used for geographic analysis of subject distribution and postal communications.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: consent_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject granted consent for contact communications. Required for GDPR and HIPAA audit trails to demonstrate lawful basis for processing contact data.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Clinpal

attributes.name: consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject has provided explicit consent to be contacted for study-related communications (visit reminders, follow-up calls). True = consent granted; False = consent not granted or withdrawn. Governed by GDPR and HIPAA privacy requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 & 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Clinpal

attributes.name: consent_withdrawn_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject withdrew consent for contact communications. Null if consent has not been withdrawn. Once populated, all non-safety-critical outreach must cease per GDPR right to withdraw.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 & 17; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: contact_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the subject contact record. 'active' indicates the contact details are current and in use; 'inactive' indicates superseded or no longer valid; 'withdrawn' indicates the subject has withdrawn consent for contact; 'pending_verification' indicates details awaiting confirmation; 'deceased' indicates the subject is deceased and contact is no longer applicable.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.526; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the subject's home address (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Determines applicable data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA) and communication rules.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this subject contact record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate) principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; GDPR Article 5(2)

attributes.name: do_not_contact_flag
attributes.description: Hard stop flag indicating the subject must not be contacted under any circumstances (excluding mandatory safety communications). True = do not contact; False = contact permitted per consent settings. Overrides all other contact preferences.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17 & 21; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.522; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this contact record is considered valid and active. Supports temporal versioning of contact information to maintain a history of address and phone changes over the course of a long-running trial.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; GDPR Article 5(1)(d) accuracy principle

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this contact record ceased to be valid (e.g., subject moved, changed phone number). Null for the currently active record. Enables Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) Type 2 history tracking of contact information.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; GDPR Article 5(1)(d) accuracy principle

attributes.name: email_address
attributes.description: Primary email address for the subject. Used for electronic communications including visit reminders, eConsent notifications, and patient engagement via Clinpal.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; 21 CFR Part 11; Clinpal

attributes.name: email_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject has specifically consented to receive communications via email. True = email contact permitted; False = email contact not permitted. Distinct from general contact consent as email may carry additional regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 & 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; CAN-SPAM Act; Clinpal

attributes.name: emergency_contact_name
attributes.description: Full name of the subject's designated emergency contact person. Used by site staff to reach a responsible party in the event of a serious adverse event (SAE) or medical emergency.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: emergency_contact_phone
attributes.description: Phone number for the subject's emergency contact. Used exclusively for safety-related communications and serious adverse event (SAE) follow-up.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: emergency_contact_relationship
attributes.description: Relationship of the emergency contact person to the subject (e.g., spouse, parent, legal guardian). Provides context for site staff when initiating emergency communications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spouse|parent|child|sibling|friend|caregiver|legal_guardian|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50

attributes.name: last_contact_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent successful contact with the subject. Used to track subject engagement, identify subjects at risk of dropout, and support visit compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; CTMS KPI reporting

attributes.name: last_contact_method
attributes.description: Communication channel used during the most recent successful contact with the subject. Supports analysis of effective outreach strategies and visit compliance improvement.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes recorded by site staff regarding the subject's contact preferences, special communication instructions, or relevant context (e.g., best time to call, language interpreter required). Classified as confidential due to potential inclusion of sensitive subject information.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code of the subject's home address. Used for geographic analysis, site feasibility, and postal communications.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification

attributes.name: preferred_contact_method
attributes.description: Subject's stated preference for how they wish to be contacted by the site or sponsor. Governs outreach channel selection for visit reminders and safety follow-up. 'no_contact' indicates the subject has requested no proactive outreach.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.522; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Clinpal

attributes.name: preferred_contact_time
attributes.description: Subject's preferred time of day to be contacted. Supports scheduling of outreach calls and reminders to maximize response rates and respect subject preferences.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Clinpal; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: preferred_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-1/639-2 language code representing the subject's preferred language for communications (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'zh-CN'). Ensures communications are delivered in the subject's native language to support informed participation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU CTR 536/2014; GDPR Article 7; Clinpal

attributes.name: primary_phone
attributes.description: Primary telephone number for contacting the subject. Used for visit reminders, recruitment follow-up, and safety follow-up communications. Stored in international format where possible.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: primary_phone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the primary phone number (e.g., mobile, home, work). Informs the appropriate time and method for outreach.
attributes.references: Clinpal; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: record_type
attributes.description: Classification of the contact record indicating the role of the contact in relation to the subject. 'primary' is the subject themselves; 'secondary' is an alternate contact; 'emergency' is for emergency use only; 'caregiver' is a designated caregiver; 'legal_representative' is a legally authorized representative.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: safety_contact_override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether safety-critical communications (e.g., SAE follow-up, urgent safety notifications) are permitted even when do_not_contact_flag is True. True = safety contact allowed regardless of general consent; False = all contact restricted. Supports regulatory obligation to notify subjects of safety findings.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.11; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 41

attributes.name: secondary_phone
attributes.description: Alternate telephone number for the subject, used when the primary phone is unreachable. Supports visit compliance and safety follow-up.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: secondary_phone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the secondary phone number (e.g., mobile, home, work).
attributes.references: Clinpal; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: sms_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject has specifically consented to receive communications via SMS/text message. True = SMS contact permitted; False = SMS contact not permitted.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 & 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act); Clinpal

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this contact record was sourced. Supports data lineage and reconciliation between Clinpal (eConsent/patient engagement) and Oracle Siebel CTMS (clinical trial management).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: withholding_amount
attributes.description: Amount withheld from the gross payment for tax purposes (e.g., backup withholding for US subjects who have not provided a valid TIN/SSN). Net payment to subject equals payment_amount minus withholding_amount.

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference

Required for regulatory submission datasets and cross-domain subject traceability. Classified as restricted PII as it can identify a trial participant.

attributes.name: age_at_screening
attributes.description: Subject's age in whole years at the time of the screening visit, derived from date of birth and screening date. Used for eligibility verification, stratification, and CDISC SDTM DM domain submission.

attributes.name: age_unit

attributes.name: birth_year
attributes.description: Subject's year of birth as a four-digit integer. Used when full date of birth is masked for privacy compliance but year-level granularity is required for age-cohort analyses and CDISC partial date handling.

attributes.name: bmi
attributes.description: Subject's body mass index calculated as weight (kg) divided by height squared (m²) at baseline. Stored as a baseline characteristic per CDISC ADaM ADSL convention; used in eligibility assessment and subgroup analyses.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes or clarifications related to the subject's demographic data, such as explanations for partial dates, data corrections, or special circumstances noted by the site or data manager.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code representing the country where the subject was enrolled. Used for geographic subgroup analyses, regulatory reporting by region, and CDISC SDTM DM domain.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.COUNTRY; ISO 3166-1 alpha-3

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the demographic record was first created in the silver layer lakehouse, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: data_entry_status
attributes.description: Current data entry and verification status of the demographic eCRF form in the EDC system. Tracks completeness and readiness for database lock (DBL) and SDTM submission.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave EDC; ICH E6(R2) GCP 5.18

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which the demographic data was sourced. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements across the lakehouse pipeline.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC Data Management Plan (DMP)

attributes.name: date_of_birth
attributes.description: Subject's date of birth in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd). Used to calculate age at key study milestones and to verify age-based eligibility criteria. May be partially masked (year only) per privacy regulations.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.BRTHDTC; GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR 164.514

attributes.name: dm_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential record number within the DM domain for a given subject, per CDISC SDTM convention. Used to uniquely identify each demographic record when multiple records exist per subject (e.g., re-screening scenarios).
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.DMSEQ

attributes.name: edc_subject_key
attributes.description: Source system record key for the subject's demographic record in the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Enables traceability from the silver layer back to the source EDC record for SDV and audit purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: epoch
attributes.description: The study epoch (e.g., SCREENING, TREATMENT, FOLLOW-UP) during which the demographic data was collected, per CDISC SDTM Trial Epochs dataset. Used for temporal context in multi-epoch study designs.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.EPOCH; CDISC Trial Epochs Dataset

attributes.name: ethnicity
attributes.description: Subject's self-reported ethnic origin, coded per FDA and CDISC controlled terminology. Distinguishes Hispanic/Latino origin from non-Hispanic/Latino. Required for FDA demographic subgroup reporting in NDA/BLA submissions.
attributes.value_regex: HISPANIC OR LATINO|NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO|NOT REPORTED|UNKNOWN
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.ETHNIC; FDA Guidance on Collection of Race and Ethnicity Data; ICH E5

attributes.name: first_exposure_date
attributes.description: Date of the subject's first exposure to the investigational product (IP). Defines the start of the treatment period and is the reference date for study day calculations in CDISC SDTM DM domain.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RFSTDTC; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: gender_identity
attributes.description: Subject's self-reported gender identity, distinct from biological sex. Collected per evolving FDA guidance on inclusion of gender identity in clinical trials. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MALE|FEMALE|TRANSGENDER MALE|TRANSGENDER FEMALE|NON-BINARY|PREFER NOT TO ANSWER|OTHER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Draft Guidance on Diversity Action Plans (2024); CDISC SDTM DM.GENDER

attributes.name: height_cm
attributes.description: Subject's height in centimeters measured at baseline/screening visit. Used for body surface area (BSA) calculations, dose determination, and baseline characteristic tables in the Clinical Study Report (CSR).
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM VS Domain (VSTEST=HEIGHT); CDISC ADaM ADSL HEIGHTBL

attributes.name: informed_consent_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject signed the informed consent form (ICF) prior to any study-related procedures. Anchors the CDISC SDTM DM.RFICDTC reference date and is required for regulatory compliance and ALCOA+ data integrity.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RFICDTC; ICH E6(R2) GCP 4.8; 21 CFR 50.25; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: last_exposure_date
attributes.description: Date of the subject's last exposure to the investigational product (IP). Used to define the end of the treatment period and calculate treatment duration for safety and efficacy analyses.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RFENDTC; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: lock_status
attributes.description: Lock status of the demographic eCRF record in the EDC system. LOCKED records cannot be modified without an audit-trailed unlock. FROZEN records are pending final database lock (DBL).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP 5.18; ALCOA+ Principles; FDA DBL Guidance

attributes.name: protocol_version
attributes.description: Version of the study protocol in effect at the time the demographic data was collected. Ensures traceability of demographic assessments to the applicable protocol amendment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP 8.2; CDISC SDTM; FDA 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: query_open_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more open data queries (discrepancies) exist against this demographic record in the EDC system. True = at least one unresolved query; False = no open queries. Used for data cleaning tracking.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP 5.18; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: race
attributes.description: Subject's self-reported racial category, coded per FDA and CDISC controlled terminology (e.g., WHITE, BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN, ASIAN, AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE, NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER, MULTIPLE, UNKNOWN, NOT REPORTED). Required for FDA demographic subgroup analyses. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WHITE|BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN|ASIAN|AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE|NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER|MULTIPLE|UNKNOWN|NOT REPORTED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RACE; FDA Guidance on Collection of Race and Ethnicity Data; 21 CFR 312.33

attributes.name: race_other_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of race when the subject selects 'OTHER' or 'MULTIPLE' as their racial category. Captures verbatim self-reported race for completeness in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RACEOTH; FDA Guidance on Collection of Race and Ethnicity Data

attributes.name: reference_start_date
attributes.description: The protocol-defined reference start date for the subject, used as the anchor for study day (STUDYDAY) calculations across all SDTM domains. May differ from first_exposure_date in some study designs (e.g., observational studies).
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.RFSTDTC; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: sdtm_domain
attributes.business_glossary_term: CDISC Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) Domain
attributes.description: CDISC SDTM domain code for this record. Always 'DM' for demographic records. Included to support automated SDTM dataset generation and regulatory submission pipelines.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM Domain; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: sdv_status
attributes.description: Status of source data verification (SDV) for the demographic record, indicating whether the EDC data has been verified against source documents by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) during site monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP 5.18.3; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; ALCOA+

attributes.name: sex
attributes.description: Biological sex of the subject as recorded at screening, coded per CDISC controlled terminology. M=Male, F=Female, U=Unknown, UNDIFFERENTIATED=Intersex or not classifiable. Used in safety analyses, PK/PD modeling, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.SEX; CDISC CT SDTM SEX; FDA Guidance on Sex as Biological Variable

attributes.name: subject_number
attributes.description: Site-assigned subject number used to identify the participant within the study site. Typically formatted as a numeric or alphanumeric code assigned at screening or enrollment.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.SUBJID; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: unique_subject_identifier
attributes.description: Globally unique identifier for the subject across the study, constructed per CDISC SDTM convention (typically STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID). Used as the primary cross-domain linkage key in SDTM submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM DM.USUBJID; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the demographic record in the silver layer lakehouse. Used for incremental data processing, change detection, and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: weight_kg
attributes.description: Subject's body weight in kilograms measured at baseline/screening visit. Used for dose calculations, PK/PD modeling, BMI derivation, and baseline characteristic tables in the CSR.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM VS Domain (VSTEST=WEIGHT); CDISC ADaM ADSL WEIGHTBL

attributes.name: concomitant_medication_flag
