attributes.name: condition_category
attributes.description: High-level category classifying the type of medical history entry. Corresponds to SDTM MHCAT variable. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MEDICAL HISTORY|SURGICAL HISTORY|FAMILY HISTORY|PSYCHIATRIC HISTORY|ALLERGY|OBSTETRIC HISTORY — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MHCAT; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: condition_status
attributes.description: Current clinical status of the pre-existing medical condition at the time of data collection. Supports safety profiling and eligibility determination.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MH Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: condition_subcategory
attributes.description: Optional secondary classification of the medical history condition providing further granularity within the category (e.g., CARDIOVASCULAR within MEDICAL HISTORY). Corresponds to SDTM MHSCAT.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MHSCAT; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: condition_verbatim
attributes.description: The verbatim (as-reported) text of the pre-existing medical condition or medical history event as entered by the investigator or CRC in the eCRF. This is the raw, uncoded term prior to MedDRA coding.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MHTERM; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this medical history record was first created in the EDC system or lakehouse. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: edc_record_reference
attributes.description: The unique record identifier assigned by the EDC system (Medidata Rave) for this medical history entry. Used for source data verification (SDV) and data reconciliation.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; Medidata Rave

attributes.name: eligibility_relevant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this medical history condition is relevant to the study's inclusion/exclusion eligibility criteria. Used by the medical monitor and data management team to assess protocol compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR 312; CDISC SDTM MH Domain

attributes.name: lock_status
attributes.description: Data lock status of this medical history record in the EDC system. Locked records cannot be modified without an authorized unlock procedure, supporting database lock (DBL) integrity.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM; ALCOA+

attributes.name: meddra_llt
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Lowest Level Term
attributes.description: The MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) that most closely maps to the verbatim condition text. Provides the most granular level of MedDRA coding hierarchy.
attributes.references: MedDRA; CDISC SDTM; ICH M1

attributes.name: meddra_pt
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term
attributes.description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) assigned to the verbatim medical history condition during medical coding. Used for standardized regulatory reporting and safety analysis.
attributes.references: MedDRA; CDISC SDTM MHDECOD; ICH M1; FDA; EMA

attributes.name: meddra_soc
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class
attributes.description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) associated with the coded medical history condition. Used for aggregate safety reporting and tabulation by body system.
attributes.references: MedDRA; CDISC SDTM MHSOC; ICH M1; FDA; EMA

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Version
attributes.description: The version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code this medical history condition (e.g., 26.0). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coding.
attributes.references: MedDRA; CDISC SDTM MHVERSION; ICH M1; FDA eCTD

attributes.name: mh_seq
attributes.description: Sequential number identifying each medical history record for a given subject within a study. Corresponds to the SDTM MHSEQ variable used in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MH Domain v3.3; FDA eCTD

attributes.name: ongoing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the medical history condition was ongoing at the time of the subject's screening or baseline assessment. True = condition is still active; False = condition has resolved. Corresponds to SDTM MHENRF or MHONGO.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MH Domain; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: The date on which the pre-existing medical condition first began or was first diagnosed. May be partial (year only or year-month) per CDISC partial date conventions. Corresponds to SDTM MHSTDTC.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MHSTDTC; ICH E6(R2); HIPAA; GDPR

attributes.name: pre_existing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the condition was present prior to the subject's first dose of investigational product. Distinguishes pre-existing conditions from treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in safety analysis.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM MH Domain; ICH E2A; FDA Safety Reporting Guidance; CTCAE

attributes.name: protocol_version
attributes.description: The version of the study protocol in effect at the time this medical history record was collected. Ensures traceability of data to the applicable protocol amendment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR 312; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: query_open_flag

attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC CDASH; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the pre-existing medical condition resolved or ended. Null if the condition is ongoing at the time of assessment. Corresponds to SDTM MHENDTC.

attributes.name: sdtm_domain

attributes.name: sdv_date

attributes.name: severity

attributes.name: source_system

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

products.name: visit_billing_reconciliation
products.description: This association product represents the billing reconciliation event between a subject_visit and an invoice_line in clinical trials sponsor invoicing. It captures the operational linkage used by finance teams to reconcile per-visit billing charges on sponsor invoices against actual subject visit completions. Each record links one subject_visit to one invoice_line and carries the billing period, quantity billed, completion date, and billing status that exist only in the context of this reconciliation relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials sponsor billing, invoice lines are aggregated billing records that cover multiple subject visits of a given type (e.g., all Week 4 visits at a site in a billing period), meaning one invoice_line maps to many subject_visits. Conversely, a given subject_visit type can be billed across multiple invoice lines in different billing periods or contract amendments, meaning one subject_visit can be referenced by multiple invoice_lines. The clinical trials finance team actively manages this reconciliation — tracking which visits have been billed, in which period, at what quantity — as a core operational process for sponsor invoicing accuracy and audit support.

products.name: sdv_review
products.description: This association product represents the Source Data Verification (SDV) Review event between a subject_visit and a monitoring_visit. It captures the operational record of a CRA reviewing a specific subject visit during a specific monitoring visit, including SDV outcome, coverage percentage, review date, and review status. Each record links one subject_visit to one monitoring_visit and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this review pairing — a subject visit may be reviewed across multiple monitoring visits (re-SDV, follow-up), and a monitoring visit covers many subject visits.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a CRA monitoring visit (monitoring_visit) covers SDV across multiple enrolled subjects and their corresponding subject visits — a single monitoring visit reviews many subject visits. Conversely, a single subject visit can be reviewed across multiple monitoring visits over the study lifecycle (initial SDV, re-SDV, follow-up verification after queries). The business actively tracks SDV outcome, coverage percentage, and review status per subject-visit/monitoring-visit pair as an operational record, not a derived analytical correlation.

products.name: subject_subject_consent
products.description: This association product represents the Informed Consent Event between a trial_subject and a document_icf_version. It captures the complete regulatory audit trail of every consent and re-consent signing event for each subject across all ICF versions applicable during their participation in the study. Each record links one trial_subject to one document_icf_version and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific signing event — including the date, method, status, and witness. Required for regulatory inspection readiness and TMF completeness.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a subject signs an ICF at initial enrollment and must re-consent whenever a protocol amendment produces a new ICF version — meaning one subject can sign multiple ICF versions over the life of a trial. Conversely, each ICF version is signed by many subjects (all those enrolled or re-consented under that version). The business actively manages these consent records as a regulatory and compliance obligation, tracking the date, method, and status of each individual consent event.

products.name: drug_lab_interaction
products.description: This association product represents the clinical assessment event linking a concomitant medication record to a laboratory result that triggered or informed a medication decision. It captures the pharmacovigilance and drug-lab interaction relationship between a specific medication action (initiation, dose change, or discontinuation) and the laboratory finding(s) that drove that clinical decision. Each record links one concomitant_medication to one lab_result with attributes that exist only in the context of this assessed relationship, supporting safety monitoring, regulatory reporting, and SDTM CM-LB linkage.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, concomitant medications are frequently initiated, modified, or discontinued in direct response to laboratory findings — a statin started after elevated LDL, a dose reduction triggered by elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST), or a medication stopped due to a critical creatinine value. One abnormal lab result can trigger multiple medication adjustments (e.g., both a diuretic dose reduction AND a potassium supplement initiation), and one medication change can be supported by multiple lab results reviewed together (e.g., a series of rising LFT values). This is an operationally managed relationship in pharmacovigilance and drug-lab interaction safety review workflows.

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Reference to the trial subject (patient) who experienced the adverse event. Core party reference linking the AE to the enrolled participant.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM AE Domain; HIPAA; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: action_taken
attributes.description: Action taken with the investigational product in response to the adverse event, as recorded by the investigator. Drives dose modification tracking and safety signal analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AEACN; Oracle Argus Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: ae_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the adverse event record, reflecting whether the event is still active, has resolved, or resulted in death. Drives workflow routing in Oracle Argus Safety and expedited reporting decisions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM AEOUT; Oracle Argus Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: ae_term_verbatim
attributes.description: The exact verbatim text of the adverse event as reported by the investigator or subject on the eCRF, prior to MedDRA coding. Preserved for ALCOA+ compliance and audit trail integrity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; CDISC SDTM AETERM; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known case identifier assigned by Oracle Argus Safety upon initial AE entry. This is the business-facing identifier used in regulatory submissions, safety narratives, and cross-system reconciliation with the source system of record.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: awareness_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor (or CRO acting on behalf of the sponsor) first became aware of the adverse event. This is the clock-start date for regulatory expedited reporting timelines per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014; Oracle Argus Safety; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: Investigator's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse event. Determines whether the event qualifies as a suspected adverse reaction and drives SUSAR classification and expedited reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment; CDISC SDTM AEREL; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: concomitant_medication_related
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event may be related to concomitant medications taken by the subject, as assessed by the investigator. Supports differential causality analysis and confounding factor assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM AERELCON; Oracle Argus Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this adverse event record was first created in the source system (Oracle Argus Safety). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; Oracle Argus Safety; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: ctcae_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade
attributes.description: Severity grade assigned per the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), ranging from 1 (mild) to 5 (death). The primary severity measure used in oncology and other therapeutic areas for safety reporting and DSMB/DMC reviews.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM AETOXGR; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on CTCAE

attributes.name: dsmb_reported
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reported Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse event has been reported to the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) for independent safety review. Supports DSMB/DMC meeting preparation and safety oversight documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on DSMB; EMA Guideline on DMC; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: edc_subject_sequence_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Data Capture (EDC) Subject Sequence Number
attributes.description: The AE sequence number assigned within the EDC system (Medidata Rave eCRF) for the subject, used to reconcile the safety database record with the source eCRF entry during SDV and data review.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC; CDISC SDTM AESEQ; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+

attributes.name: is_current_version
attributes.description: Indicates whether this record is the most current version of the adverse event. Used to filter the latest state of each AE without requiring a MAX(version_number) query, supporting efficient reporting and analytics.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer

attributes.name: is_expected
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event is listed in the current Investigator's Brochure (IB) or product labeling as an expected/anticipated reaction. Unexpected serious adverse reactions trigger SUSAR reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM AEEXP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: is_serious
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event meets the regulatory definition of a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) per ICH E2A criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or other medically important condition). Triggers expedited regulatory reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance; CDISC SDTM AESER

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse event has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited regulatory reporting to health authorities (FDA, EMA, MHRA, etc.) within defined timelines (7 or 15 calendar days).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA EudraVigilance; MHRA

attributes.name: is_teae
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event is treatment-emergent, defined as an event that first occurred or worsened in severity after the first dose of investigational product. Used in TEAE incidence tables in the CSR and SAP-defined safety analyses.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC ADaM ADAE; SAP; SAS Drug Development; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: meddra_llt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Lowest Level Term (LLT) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) numeric code assigned during medical coding, representing the most granular level of the MedDRA hierarchy closest to the verbatim term.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AELLTCD; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: meddra_llt_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Lowest Level Term (LLT) Name
attributes.description: MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) text description corresponding to the LLT code. Used in safety listings, narratives, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AELLT; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) numeric code, the primary level used for regulatory reporting, signal detection, and aggregate safety analysis.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEPTCD; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: meddra_pt_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Name
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) text description. The standardized medical term used in all regulatory submissions, DSMB/DMC reports, and safety narratives.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEDECOD; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) numeric code representing the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for aggregate safety tabulations by body system in CSRs and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AESOCCD; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: meddra_soc_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Name
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) text description. Used in safety tabulations, listings, and figures in the Clinical Study Report (CSR).
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AESOC; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Version
attributes.description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used for coding this adverse event (e.g., '26.0'). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coded terms across dictionary versions.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: medical_history_related
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event is considered related to or a continuation of a pre-existing medical history condition, as assessed by the investigator. Supports pre-existing condition confounding analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM AERELMH; Oracle Argus Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: narrative
attributes.description: Free-text medical narrative describing the clinical course of the adverse event, including relevant medical history, treatment, and outcome. Required for SAE/SUSAR regulatory submissions and DSMB/DMC safety reviews.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); Oracle Argus Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: The date on which the adverse event first began, as reported by the investigator. This is the principal real-world event date used for duration calculations, expedited reporting timelines, and TEAE determination.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM AESTDTC; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: outcome
attributes.description: Final or current outcome of the adverse event as assessed by the investigator. Used in safety listings, aggregate safety tables, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AEOUT; Oracle Argus Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: regulatory_report_due_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which an expedited safety report (e.g., SUSAR, IND Safety Report) must be submitted to the relevant health authority. Calculated from the date of first awareness per ICH E2A timelines (7-day for fatal/life-threatening, 15-day for other SUSARs).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA EudraVigilance; MHRA; PMDA

attributes.name: regulatory_report_submitted_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the expedited safety report was submitted to the health authority. Used to calculate compliance with regulatory reporting timelines and track submission performance KPIs.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA EudraVigilance; MHRA; PMDA

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this record represents the initial AE report, a follow-up update with new clinical information, or the final report upon event resolution. Supports version history tracking as the clinical picture evolves.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); Oracle Argus Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the adverse event resolved or returned to baseline. Null if the event is ongoing. Used to calculate AE duration and determine outcome status.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM AEENDTC; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: seriousness_criteria
attributes.description: Specific ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by this SAE (e.g., death, life-threatening, hospitalization required, persistent disability, congenital anomaly, medically significant). Multiple criteria may apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; CDISC SDTM AESDTH/AESHOSP/AESLIFE/AESDISAB/AESCONG/AESMIE; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Descriptive severity classification of the adverse event as assessed by the investigator (mild, moderate, severe, life-threatening, fatal). Distinct from CTCAE grade; used in non-oncology studies and as a complementary severity descriptor per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AESEV; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this adverse event record was sourced (Oracle Argus Safety, Medidata Rave EDC, Oracle Clinical One, or manual entry). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer; CDISC Data Management

attributes.name: study_day_onset
attributes.business_glossary_term: Study Day of Adverse Event (AE) Onset
attributes.description: The study day (relative to first dose date) on which the adverse event began. Calculated per CDISC convention (Day 1 = first dose date). Used in time-to-event analyses and safety exposure-adjusted incidence calculations.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM AESTDY; CDISC ADaM; ICH E9; SAS Drug Development

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this adverse event record was most recently modified in the source system. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; Oracle Argus Safety; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this AE record, incremented with each follow-up update. Version 1 is the initial report; subsequent versions capture evolving clinical information. Enables temporal evolution tracking across the AE lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); Oracle Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+

Captures SAE narrative, seriousness criteria met, initial and follow-up report dates, blinded/unblinded status, and regulatory reporting obligations. Linked to the parent adverse_event record. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.imp_master. Business justification: SAE expedited reporting to health authorities (FDA, EMA) requires precise IMP identification including formulation and strength. Direct FK to imp_master supports automated ICSR generation and regulato

attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site where the SAE was reported. Used for site-level safety monitoring and CRA follow-up.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to site.irb_iec_approval. Business justification: SAEs require IRB/IEC notification per ICH E6(R2) 4.11.1. The SAE record must reference the specific irb_iec_approval active at time of event to document which approval was notified and to drive notifi

Linking SAE to its regulatory filing replaces the denormalized regulatory_submission_date and enables SAE-to-submission tr

attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which the SAE occurred. Used for regulatory reporting and safety signal aggregation across the study.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.32; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Reference to the study subject (patient/participant) who experienced the SAE. Serves as the PARTY_REFERENCE for this transaction header per canonical attribute rules.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.32; CDISC SDTM DM Domain

attributes.name: action_taken
attributes.description: The action taken with the investigational product in response to the SAE (e.g., dose reduced, drug withdrawn, dose interrupted). This is a key regulatory field in ICSR submissions and clinical study reports.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Element G.k.8; CDISC SDTM AE.AEACN; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique case identifier assigned by Oracle Argus Safety upon SAE intake. This is the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER used for cross-system traceability, regulatory submissions, and sponsor communications.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: blinding_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE case is currently blinded (treatment assignment unknown) or unblinded (treatment assignment revealed for safety reporting purposes). Unblinding may be required for SUSAR reporting to regulatory authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 312.32; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: The investigator's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the SAE. This is a critical regulatory field used to determine whether the event qualifies as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR).
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CDISC SDTM AE.AEREL

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the SAE record was first created in Oracle Argus Safety. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field per canonical transaction header requirements. Conforms to 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ Principles; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: ctcae_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Severity Grade
attributes.description: The CTCAE severity grade assigned to the SAE, ranging from 1 (mild) to 5 (death). Grade 3 = severe, Grade 4 = life-threatening, Grade 5 = death. Used for oncology and other therapeutic area safety assessments.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM AE.AETOXGR; FDA Guidance on Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: dsmb_reported
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reported Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SAE was reported to the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) for independent safety review. Required for studies with an active DSMB/DMC charter.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EMA Reflection Paper on DMCs

attributes.name: expectedness
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE is expected (listed in the Investigator's Brochure or product labeling) or unexpected (not listed or differing in nature/severity). Unexpected + serious + related = SUSAR, triggering expedited regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: follow_up_number
attributes.description: Sequential number indicating which follow-up report this record represents (0 = initial report, 1 = first follow-up, 2 = second follow-up, etc.). Used to track the evolution of the SAE case over time as new information becomes available.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); Oracle Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: initial_report_date
attributes.description: The date on which the SAE was first reported to the sponsor or CRO by the investigational site. This is Day 0 for calculating regulatory reporting timelines (e.g., 7-day or 15-day expedited reporting clock).
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 5; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: irb_iec_notification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Notification Date
attributes.description: The date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was notified of the SAE. Required under GCP and local regulations to ensure ongoing ethical oversight of the study.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.3; 21 CFR Part 312.66; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP 45 CFR Part 46

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SAE has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited regulatory reporting to health authorities (e.g., FDA 7/15-day reporting, EMA reporting). Derived from causality, expectedness, and seriousness criteria but stored as a business flag.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: meddra_llt_code
attributes.description: The MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) code that most closely matches the verbatim SAE term. The LLT is the most granular level of MedDRA coding and is used to preserve the original reported term in a coded format.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AELLT

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code assigned to the SAE. The PT is the primary level of MedDRA used for regulatory reporting and is the standard coded term submitted in ICSRs and clinical study reports.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AEDECOD; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code assigned to the SAE during medical coding. Represents the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy, used for regulatory submissions and safety signal detection.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AESOC

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.description: The version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code this SAE (e.g., '26.0', '26.1'). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coding and compliance with current dictionary standards.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: narrative
attributes.description: The full medical narrative describing the SAE, including clinical course, relevant medical history, concomitant medications, investigational product details, and the investigator's assessment. This is the primary free-text field in the Argus Safety case and is included in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 6; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 312.32; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: The date on which the serious adverse event first began or was first observed by the subject or investigator. This is the principal BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date precision) for the SAE transaction.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; CDISC SDTM AE.AESTDTC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: outcome
attributes.description: The clinical outcome of the serious adverse event at the time of the most recent report. 'recovered_with_sequelae' indicates the subject recovered but with lasting effects. 'fatal' must align with seriousness_death = true.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) Element C.1.7; CDISC SDTM AE.AEOUT; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: regulatory_report_due_date
attributes.description: The calculated deadline by which the expedited regulatory report (e.g., IND Safety Report, SUSAR notification) must be submitted to the relevant health authority. Typically 7 calendar days for fatal/life-threatening SUSARs and 15 calendar days for other SUSARs.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 5; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Classifies the type of safety report generated for this SAE. 'expedited' = 7/15-day SUSAR or IND safety report; 'periodic' = included in DSUR/PSUR; 'spontaneous' = post-marketing spontaneous report; 'literature' = identified from published literature.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2C(R2) DSUR; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: reporting_authority
attributes.description: The health authority or regulatory body to which the SAE/SUSAR report was submitted (e.g., 'FDA', 'EMA', 'MHRA', 'PMDA', 'TGA', 'Health Canada'). May contain multiple authorities if reported to more than one. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|TGA|Health Canada|ANVISA|CDSCO — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA GVP Module VI; MHRA; PMDA

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the serious adverse event resolved, stabilized, or the subject died. Null if the event is ongoing at the time of reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AE.AEENDTC; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: sae_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the SAE case in Oracle Argus Safety. 'initial' = first report received; 'follow_up' = additional information received; 'closed' = case fully resolved and closed; 'nullified' = case determined not to meet SAE criteria and voided.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Oracle Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: sae_term
attributes.description: The verbatim (as-reported) description of the serious adverse event as recorded by the investigator or site staff in the source document or eCRF. This is the raw, uncoded term prior to MedDRA coding.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AE.AETERM; Oracle Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: seriousness_congenital_anomaly
attributes.business_glossary_term: Seriousness Criterion: Congenital Anomaly or Birth Defect
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in a congenital anomaly or birth defect in the offspring of the subject.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: seriousness_death
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in death of the subject. One of the six ICH E2A seriousness criteria that must be captured individually.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: seriousness_disability
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in persistent or significant disability or incapacity.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: seriousness_hospitalization
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of requiring inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: seriousness_life_threatening
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of being immediately life-threatening (i.e., the subject was at immediate risk of death at the time of the event).
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: seriousness_medically_important
attributes.business_glossary_term: Seriousness Criterion: Other Medically Important Condition
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of being an other medically important condition — events that may not be immediately life-threatening but may jeopardize the subject or require intervention to prevent one of the other serious outcomes.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: source_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the source document (e.g., hospital discharge summary, death certificate, medical records) that supports the SAE report. Used for SDV and audit trail purposes per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 1.52; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: sponsor_receipt_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor (or CRO acting on behalf of the sponsor) received the complete minimum information required to process the SAE. This date starts the regulatory reporting clock per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 5; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: subject_number
attributes.description: The protocol-assigned subject identifier (e.g., site-subject number) for the patient who experienced the SAE. Restricted as it can be used to identify an individual participant in combination with study data.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); HIPAA 45 CFR §164; GDPR Article 4; CDISC SDTM DM.SUBJID

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the SAE record was most recently modified in Oracle Argus Safety. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field per canonical transaction header requirements. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ Principles; Oracle Argus Safety

products.name: susar
products.description: Transactional record for Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) — SAEs that are both unexpected (not in the Investigator Brochure) and causally related to the investigational product. Captures expectedness assessment, causality determination, expedited reporting clock start date, 7-day and 15-day reporting deadlines, submission status to FDA/EMA/PMDA, and blind-break details. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety.
products.reference: ICH E2A; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 42; 21 CFR 312.32

Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete regulatory safety event with a defined lifecycle, expedited reporting obligations, and submission tracking.

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Reference to the study subject (patient) who experienced the SUSAR. Links to the subject master record for patient-level safety surveillance and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: ae_term
attributes.description: Verbatim description of the adverse event as reported by the investigator or subject, prior to MedDRA coding. Preserved for source data verification (SDV) and coding audit trail per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM AE domain; ICH E2A; MedDRA; ALCOA+

attributes.name: argus_case_reference
attributes.description: System-generated case identifier from Oracle Argus Safety, the operational system of record for adverse event and SUSAR management. Used to trace the SUSAR back to its source case in Argus.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; ICH E2A

attributes.name: awareness_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sponsor (or CRO acting on behalf of the sponsor) first became aware of the SUSAR. This date starts the regulatory reporting clock for 7-day and 15-day expedited reporting obligations under ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: blind_break_date
attributes.description: Date on which the treatment blind was broken for this subject. Populated only when blind_broken is True. Required for audit trail and regulatory documentation of unblinding events.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3.3; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: blind_broken
attributes.description: Indicates whether the treatment blind was broken for this subject in order to perform the causality assessment for this SUSAR. A blind break is a significant event requiring documentation and regulatory notification.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3.3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: blind_status
attributes.description: Blinding status of the study at the time of SUSAR reporting. Indicates whether the study was blinded, and if so, whether the blind was broken for this subject to determine treatment assignment for causality assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3.3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; ICH E9

attributes.name: case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric case number assigned by the sponsor or CRO for this SUSAR, used in all regulatory submissions and correspondence. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: Investigator's or sponsor's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the serious adverse reaction. A SUSAR requires a positive causality assessment (related or probably/possibly related) to the investigational product.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; WHO Causality Assessment; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the SUSAR record was first created in Oracle Argus Safety. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for this transaction header, supporting ALCOA+ data integrity requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: ctcae_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Severity Grade
attributes.description: CTCAE severity grade assigned to the adverse reaction (1=Mild, 2=Moderate, 3=Severe, 4=Life-threatening, 5=Death). Used for safety signal detection, DSMB/DMC reviews, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AE domain

attributes.name: deadline_15day
attributes.description: Calculated deadline for 15-day expedited reporting to regulatory authorities for non-fatal/non-life-threatening SUSARs. Derived from the reporting clock start date plus 15 calendar days per ICH E2A and FDA 21 CFR 312.32.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c)(2); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: deadline_7day
attributes.description: Calculated deadline for 7-day expedited reporting to regulatory authorities for fatal or life-threatening SUSARs. Derived from the reporting clock start date plus 7 calendar days per ICH E2A and FDA 21 CFR 312.32.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dose_at_onset
attributes.description: Dose of the investigational product administered to the subject at the time of the adverse reaction onset, including amount and unit (e.g., '100 mg'). Required for causality assessment and regulatory case narratives.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM EX domain; FDA 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: dsmb_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) was notified of this SUSAR. Populated only when dsmb_notified is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DSMB

attributes.name: dsmb_notified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Notification Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) was notified of this SUSAR. Required for studies with an active DSMB/DMC per ICH E6(R2) and study protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9

attributes.name: eudravigilance_number
attributes.description: Unique case identifier assigned by the EudraVigilance system upon submission of the SUSAR to the EMA. Used for tracking and referencing the case in EU regulatory correspondence and EudraVigilance database.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; EMA GVP Module VI; EudraVigilance

attributes.name: expectedness_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the serious adverse reaction is unexpected — i.e., not listed or not consistent with the nature, severity, or frequency described in the current Investigator's Brochure (IB). A SUSAR must be assessed as unexpected to qualify for expedited reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(a)(2); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: fatal_date
attributes.description: Date of subject death if the outcome of the SUSAR is fatal. Triggers the 7-day expedited reporting clock and is required for death narratives in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1); CDISC SDTM DS domain

attributes.name: follow_up_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of the follow-up report for this SUSAR case (e.g., 1 for first follow-up, 2 for second). Zero or null for initial reports. Tracks the version history of regulatory submissions for this case.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 5; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: irb_iec_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was notified of this SUSAR. Populated only when irb_iec_notified is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.11; FDA 21 CFR 312.66; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: irb_iec_notified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Notification Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was notified of this SUSAR as required by GCP and local regulations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.11; FDA 21 CFR 312.66; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: meddra_llt_code
attributes.description: MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) code that most closely matches the verbatim adverse event term. Used for granular coding traceability and verbatim-to-PT mapping audit.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE domain

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code assigned to this SUSAR. The PT is the primary level of MedDRA used for regulatory reporting, signal detection, and aggregate safety analysis in IND/NDA/BLA submissions.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE domain; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code assigned to this SUSAR during medical coding. Represents the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy and is required for regulatory submissions and aggregate safety reporting.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE domain; FDA 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used for coding this SUSAR (e.g., 26.0, 26.1). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coding and compliance with current MedDRA release requirements.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE domain; FDA 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: narrative
attributes.description: Medical narrative summarizing the SUSAR case, including patient demographics, event description, clinical course, causality assessment, and outcome. Required component of all expedited regulatory reports per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 6; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CIOMS I Form

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject first experienced the serious adverse reaction. This is the principal real-world event time (BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP) for the SUSAR and is the anchor for all regulatory reporting clocks per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; CDISC SDTM AE domain

attributes.name: outcome
attributes.description: Clinical outcome of the serious adverse reaction at the time of reporting. Required for regulatory submissions and DSMB/DMC safety reviews. Tracks resolution status of the event.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AE domain; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: reporting_clock_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which the regulatory reporting clock begins for this SUSAR. Typically the sponsor awareness date, but may be adjusted based on the date of unblinding or receipt of minimum reportable information per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: reporting_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the SUSAR regulatory reporting workflow. Tracks progression from initial draft through submission to regulatory authority acknowledgement and case closure. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this transaction.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Route by which the investigational product was administered (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous). Required for regulatory case narratives and pharmacovigilance signal assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM EX domain; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; WHO-DD

attributes.name: seriousness_criteria
attributes.description: ICH E2A seriousness criterion met by this adverse reaction that qualifies it as a Serious Adverse Event (SAE). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 1; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: submission_report_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SUSAR submission is an initial report, a follow-up report with additional information, or a final report closing the case. Regulatory authorities require tracking of report versions per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 5; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the SUSAR record in Oracle Argus Safety. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field for this transaction header, supporting audit trail and data integrity requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+
