attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC DM Best Practices; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: coding_method
attributes.description: Indicates how the MedDRA code was assigned: 'auto' for system-generated auto-coding by Oracle Argus Safety, 'manual' for coder-assigned coding, 'auto_confirmed' for auto-coded and confirmed by a coder, 'recoded' for a previously coded term that was revised. Drives QC workflows and audit requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC DM Best Practices; Oracle Argus Safety coding workflow; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: coding_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the MedDRA coding assignment. 'pending' indicates awaiting coding, 'coded' indicates a code has been assigned, 'confirmed' indicates QC-approved, 'rejected' indicates coding was rejected and requires rework, 'under_review' indicates currently in QC review. Drives coding workflow in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC DM Best Practices; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: confirmed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the MedDRA coding assignment was confirmed (QC-approved) by a second reviewer or coding supervisor. Null if coding has not yet been confirmed. Supports dual-coder QC workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC DM Best Practices; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: ctcae_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade
attributes.description: Severity grade assigned to the adverse event using the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) scale (1=Mild, 2=Moderate, 3=Severe, 4=Life-threatening, 5=Death). Used in oncology and other therapeutic areas for standardized severity grading alongside MedDRA coding.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM AETOXGR; FDA Oncology guidance; ICH E3

attributes.name: ctcae_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Version
attributes.description: Version of the NCI CTCAE grading scale used for severity assessment (e.g., '5.0', '4.03'). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure consistent severity grading interpretation across study sites and time periods.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE; FDA Oncology guidance; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: dictionary_language
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 639-2 language code of the MedDRA dictionary used for coding (e.g., 'ENG' for English, 'JPN' for Japanese). Relevant for multi-regional studies where local language MedDRA versions may be used (e.g., PMDA submissions in Japan).
attributes.references: ICH M1; PMDA MedDRA/J requirements; ISO 639-2

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this MedDRA coding record version is considered effective. Used in conjunction with is_current_version and effective_to_date to implement SCD Type 2 versioning for coding history tracking.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; CDISC DM Best Practices

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date until which this MedDRA coding record version is considered effective. Null for the current active record. Used with effective_from_date and is_current_version for SCD Type 2 coding history. Populated when a recoding event supersedes this record.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; CDISC DM Best Practices

attributes.name: hlgt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) Code
attributes.description: Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the High Level Group Term (HLGT), which sits between the HLT and SOC in the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for broad safety grouping in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEHLGTCD

attributes.name: hlgt_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) Name
attributes.description: Descriptive text of the MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) corresponding to hlgt_code. Supports broad-level safety grouping in aggregate analyses and CSR appendices.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEHLGT

attributes.name: hlt_code
attributes.description: Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the High Level Term (HLT) in the MedDRA hierarchy above the PT. Used for grouping related PTs in aggregate safety analyses and signal detection.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEHLTCD

attributes.name: hlt_name
attributes.description: Descriptive text of the MedDRA High Level Term (HLT) corresponding to hlt_code. Supports mid-level grouping in safety tabulations and DSMB/DMC review packages.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEHLT

attributes.name: is_current_version
attributes.description: Indicates whether this record represents the current (active) MedDRA coding assignment for the associated adverse event. Set to false for superseded coding records retained for historical audit trail. Supports slowly changing dimension (SCD Type 2) versioning in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; CDISC DM Best Practices

attributes.name: is_sae
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event associated with this MedDRA coding record meets the regulatory definition of a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) per ICH E2A criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or other medically important condition). Drives expedited reporting timelines.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CDISC SDTM AESER

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse event has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited regulatory reporting (7-day or 15-day) to health authorities. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety case classification.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: llt_code
attributes.description: Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the Lowest Level Term (LLT) assigned to the verbatim adverse event term. The LLT is the most granular level of the MedDRA hierarchy and is the primary coding target. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety MedDRA dictionary.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AELLTCD

attributes.name: llt_name
attributes.description: Descriptive text of the MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) corresponding to llt_code. Provides the human-readable label for the most granular MedDRA coding level. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety MedDRA dictionary.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AELLT

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used for this coding assignment (e.g., '26.0', '26.1'). Critical for regulatory submissions as coding must reference the specific MedDRA version in use at the time of the submission. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety dictionary configuration.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; FDA eCTD submission requirements; EMA MedDRA versioning policy

attributes.name: previous_pt_code
attributes.description: The MedDRA PT code that was previously assigned before a recoding event. Populated only when coding_method = 'recoded'. Enables before/after comparison for coding change impact analysis and regulatory audit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: previous_soc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Previous MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) Code
attributes.description: The MedDRA SOC code that was previously assigned before a recoding event. Populated only when coding_method = 'recoded'. Enables assessment of whether a recoding changed the SOC-level classification, which may affect regulatory safety tables.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: primary_soc_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SOC assignment is the primary (true) or secondary (false) SOC for the PT. MedDRA PTs may be linked to multiple SOCs; the primary SOC is used for standard regulatory safety tables. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AESOCCD primary SOC convention

attributes.name: pt_code
attributes.description: Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the Preferred Term (PT) to which the LLT maps. The PT is the primary level used for regulatory reporting, safety queries, and signal detection. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AEPTCD; FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: pt_name
attributes.description: Descriptive text of the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) corresponding to pt_code. Used as the standard term in regulatory submissions, CIOMS forms, and safety narratives.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEDECOD

attributes.name: recoding_reason
attributes.description: Free-text justification provided by the coder when a previously assigned MedDRA code is revised (coding_method = 'recoded'). Required for audit trail integrity and regulatory inspection readiness. Null when coding_method is not 'recoded'.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; CDISC DM Best Practices

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp at which this MedDRA coding record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp at which this MedDRA coding record was last modified in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Tracks the most recent update for change detection, incremental processing, and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: soc_code
attributes.description: Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the System Organ Class (SOC), the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy. SOC is the primary axis for organizing adverse events in regulatory safety tables (e.g., Table 14.3.1 in ICH E3 CSR).
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; ICH E3; CDISC SDTM AESOCCD; FDA NDA/BLA safety tables

attributes.name: soc_name
attributes.description: Descriptive text of the MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) corresponding to soc_code. Used as the primary grouping header in all regulatory safety tabulations, PSUR/PBRER narratives, and DSMB reports.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; ICH E3; CDISC SDTM AESOC

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system from which this MedDRA coding record was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer. Typically 'argus_safety' for records originating from Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC DM Best Practices; Data lineage governance

attributes.name: verbatim_term
attributes.description: The exact, unmodified adverse event term as reported by the investigator or subject in the source document or eCRF prior to MedDRA coding. Preserved for ALCOA+ compliance and audit trail. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety verbatim field.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AETERM; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

products.name: causality_assessment
products.description: Records the investigator and sponsor medical monitor causality assessments for each adverse event relative to the investigational product and concomitant medications. Captures assessor role, assessment date, causality category (unrelated, unlikely, possible, probable, definite), rationale narrative, and whether the assessment was revised. Supports regulatory reporting and signal detection workflows in Oracle Argus Safety.
products.reference: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Scale; CIOMS

attributes.name: causality_assessment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each causality assessment record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: adverse_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the adverse event record for which this causality assessment is being performed. Links the assessment to the parent AE in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dispensing_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.dispensing_record. Business justification: Causality assessment requires authoritative dispensing data (exact dose, formulation, timing) per ICH E2A guidelines. causality_assessment.dose_at_onset and dose_unit are denormalized; FK to dispensin
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the workforce member (PI, medical monitor, or independent reviewer) who performed this causality assessment, sourced from Workday HCM.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.11; GCP

attributes.name: investigational_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational product (drug, biologic, or device) being assessed for causal relationship to the adverse event.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM EX domain

attributes.name: lab_result_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_result. Business justification: Causality assessments evaluate AE-drug relationships using lab evidence (e.g., liver function tests, renal markers). Linking causality_assessment to the supporting lab_result formalizes the evidence c
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: prior_assessment_causality_assessment_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding causality assessment record that this revision supersedes. Null for original (first) assessments. Enables full revision chain reconstruction.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study protocol under which the adverse event occurred and this causality assessment was conducted.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM TS domain

attributes.name: study_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site where the subject was enrolled and the adverse event was reported.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: subject_randomization_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to randomization.subject_randomization. Business justification: Causality assessment explicitly evaluates temporal relationship between treatment and AE onset, requiring the authoritative randomization record. treatment_arm and blinding_status are denormalized fro
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: subject_visit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to subject.subject_visit. Business justification: Causality assessments are performed at specific visits (e.g., end-of-treatment, unscheduled safety visit). DSMB data packages and medical monitor reviews require visit-level causality tracking. No exi
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) for whom the adverse event and causality assessment applies.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM DM domain

attributes.name: alternative_explanation
attributes.description: Free-text description of alternative causes considered by the assessor (e.g., concomitant medications, underlying disease, concurrent procedures). Documents the differential diagnosis reasoning supporting the causality determination.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; CIOMS

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: The case number assigned by Oracle Argus Safety to the parent safety case containing this causality assessment. Enables direct traceability back to the source system for audit and regulatory purposes.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: argus_workflow_state
attributes.description: The workflow routing state of the causality assessment within Oracle Argus Safety at the time of data extraction (e.g., Open, Closed, Submitted, Archived). Supports reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and the source system. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|closed|submitted|archived|pending_review|locked — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: assessment_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the causality assessment was performed or last confirmed by the assessor. Used to track compliance with expedited reporting timelines (e.g., 7-day/15-day clock).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: assessment_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this causality assessment record, typically generated by Oracle Argus Safety (e.g., CA-2024-00123). Used for cross-system traceability and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Oracle Argus Safety case numbering conventions; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: assessment_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the causality assessment record within Oracle Argus Safety. Tracks progression from initial draft through regulatory submission. 'Superseded' indicates a newer revision exists.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Argus Safety workflow states

attributes.name: assessor_role
attributes.description: The professional role of the individual performing the causality assessment. Distinguishes between the Principal Investigator (PI) site-level assessment and the Sponsor Medical Monitor's independent assessment, as required by ICH E2A and GCP guidelines.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.11; FDA 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: causality_category
attributes.description: The assessor's determination of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse event. Standard WHO/ICH causality categories used in Oracle Argus Safety and regulatory submissions. 'Not assessable' applies when insufficient information is available.
attributes.references: WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; ICH E2A; CIOMS; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: causality_category_code
attributes.description: Standardized short code for the causality category used in CDISC SDTM AE domain submissions and Oracle Argus Safety exports (UN=Unrelated, UL=Unlikely, PO=Possible, PR=Probable, DE=Definite, NA=Not Assessable).
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM AE domain; ICH E2A; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: concomitant_medication_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this causality assessment pertains to a concomitant medication (True) rather than the primary investigational product (False). Enables differentiation of IP-related versus concomitant drug-related assessments within the same AE case.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM CM domain; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: concomitant_medication_name
attributes.description: Name of the concomitant medication being assessed for causal relationship when concomitant_medication_flag is True. Populated from WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) preferred drug name.
attributes.references: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM CM domain

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this causality assessment record was first created in the source system (Oracle Argus Safety). Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: dechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome observed when the investigational product was withdrawn (dechallenged) following the adverse event. A positive dechallenge (AE resolved or improved upon withdrawal) supports a causal relationship. Captured per ICH E2A causality criteria.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; CIOMS

attributes.name: dsmb_review_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Review Date
attributes.description: The date on which the DSMB/DMC formally reviewed this causality assessment during a scheduled or ad hoc safety review meeting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DMC

attributes.name: dsmb_reviewed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reviewed Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this causality assessment was reviewed by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) as part of a formal safety review. Supports DSMB/DMC meeting documentation and regulatory oversight.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DMC; EMA Reflection Paper on DMC

attributes.name: expectedness
attributes.description: Determination of whether the adverse event is listed in the current Investigator's Brochure (IB) or Reference Safety Information (RSI) as a known effect of the investigational product. Drives SUSAR classification and expedited reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: expedited_report_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this causality assessment triggers an obligation for expedited regulatory reporting (7-day or 15-day report) to health authorities such as FDA, EMA, or PMDA based on SUSAR classification.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: is_revised
attributes.description: Indicates whether this causality assessment is a revision of a previously submitted assessment. True when the assessor has changed their causality determination after initial submission, triggering regulatory follow-up reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: rationale_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text clinical narrative provided by the assessor explaining the reasoning behind the causality determination. Includes consideration of temporal relationship, biological plausibility, dechallenge/rechallenge results, and alternative explanations. Required for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: rechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome observed when the investigational product was re-administered (rechallenged) after the adverse event resolved. A positive rechallenge (AE recurred) provides strong evidence of causal relationship. Captured per ICH E2A causality criteria.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; CIOMS

attributes.name: report_due_date
attributes.description: Calculated deadline date by which the expedited regulatory report (SUSAR/IND safety report) must be submitted to health authorities. Derived from the date of first awareness plus the applicable reporting timeline.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: reporting_timeline_days
attributes.description: The applicable expedited reporting timeline in calendar days from the date of first awareness of the SUSAR (typically 7 days for fatal/life-threatening or 15 days for other serious unexpected reactions). Drives compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential revision version number for this causality assessment. Starts at 1 for the original assessment and increments with each revision. Enables audit trail tracking of assessment changes over the case lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Argus Safety versioning

attributes.name: signal_detection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this causality assessment has been flagged for inclusion in pharmacovigilance signal detection analysis within Oracle Argus Safety. Supports aggregate safety review and cumulative causality trend monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E2E; EMA GVP Module IX; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

attributes.name: source_record_reference
attributes.description: The native record identifier from the source system (Oracle Argus Safety case assessment ID or Medidata Rave record ID) for this causality assessment. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational system.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this causality assessment record was extracted. Primarily Oracle Argus Safety; may include Medidata Rave for EDC-sourced assessments or 'manual' for paper-based entries.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: sponsor_causality_category
attributes.description: The Sponsor Medical Monitor's independent causality determination, captured separately from the investigator's assessment. When sponsor_causality_override is True, this field holds the sponsor's differing conclusion used for regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: sponsor_causality_override
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Sponsor Medical Monitor's causality determination differs from (overrides) the Investigator's assessment. When True, both assessments are retained and the sponsor's determination governs regulatory reporting obligations per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: susar_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse event has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) based on the combination of seriousness, causality (at least possible), and unexpectedness criteria. Triggers mandatory expedited regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: temporal_relationship
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the timing between investigational product administration and adverse event onset is consistent with a causal relationship. A key criterion in WHO and ICH causality assessment frameworks.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; CIOMS

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this causality assessment record was most recently modified in the source system. Tracks the latest change for audit trail compliance and Silver layer incremental load processing.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: who_dd_drug_code
attributes.description: WHO Drug Dictionary standardized drug code for the product (investigational or concomitant) being assessed. Enables cross-study signal detection and regulatory pharmacovigilance reporting.
attributes.references: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

products.name: narrative
products.description: Stores the structured clinical narrative for SAEs and SUSARs, including case summary, patient description, event description, treatment details, outcome, and medical monitor commentary. Tracks narrative version, authoring date, review status, and approval by the medical monitor. Used in expedited regulatory reports (ICSRs) submitted via Oracle Argus Safety in eCTD/E2B(R3) format.

attributes.name: narrative_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the safety narrative record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this data product.

attributes.name: trial_subject_id

attributes.name: ae_onset_date

attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.8; CDISC SDTM AE.AEOUT; FDA MedWatch 3500A

attributes.name: ae_resolution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the adverse event resolved or stabilized. Null if the event is ongoing at the time of narrative authoring. Used to determine event duration and outcome status.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.8; CDISC SDTM AE.AEENDTC; ICH E2A

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the medical monitor formally approved the final version of the safety narrative for regulatory submission. Represents the final lifecycle milestone before submission.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: The externally-known case number assigned by Oracle Argus Safety to the adverse event case. Used as the primary business identifier for cross-system traceability and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch

attributes.name: authoring_date
attributes.description: Date on which the safety narrative was initially authored or drafted. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and version history tracking.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: case_summary
attributes.description: High-level executive summary of the safety case, synthesizing the patient description, event, treatment, and outcome into a concise paragraph suitable for inclusion in the ICSR narrative field of E2B(R3) submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section H.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: case_type
attributes.description: Classification of the safety case for which this narrative is written. SAE = Serious Adverse Event; SUSAR = Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction; AE = Adverse Event; AESI = Adverse Event of Special Interest.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: Medical monitor's or investigator's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse event. Used in regulatory reporting and signal detection.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.4; WHO-UMC causality categories; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this safety narrative record was first created in the system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record requirements.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: ctcae_grade
attributes.description: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) severity grade assigned to the adverse event (1=Mild, 2=Moderate, 3=Severe, 4=Life-threatening, 5=Death). Used for safety signal detection and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM AE.AETOXGR; FDA Guidance on Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: ctcae_version
attributes.description: Version of the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events used for severity grading in this narrative (e.g., '5.0'). Ensures consistency in grading across study sites and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE; CDISC SDTM; FDA Guidance on Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: dsmb_review_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Review Date
attributes.description: Date on which the DSMB or DMC reviewed this safety case. Populated only when dsmb_reviewed is True. Used to track safety oversight compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees

attributes.name: dsmb_reviewed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reviewed Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this safety case and its narrative have been reviewed by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC). True if reviewed; False if not yet presented to the DSMB/DMC.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees; EMA Reflection Paper on DMCs

attributes.name: e2b_message_reference
attributes.description: Unique message identifier assigned to the ICSR transmission in E2B(R3) XML format as submitted via eCTD to health authorities. Enables traceability between the narrative record and the regulatory submission artifact.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway; EMA EVWEB; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: event_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the onset, nature, severity, and clinical course of the adverse event or serious adverse event, including signs, symptoms, and diagnostic findings. Core narrative section for ICSR submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2; ICH E2A; FDA MedWatch 3500A; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: expedited_report_due_date
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which the expedited safety report (ICSR) must be submitted to health authorities. Calculated from the date of first awareness per ICH E2A (7-day for fatal/life-threatening; 15-day for other serious unexpected).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: expedited_report_submitted_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the expedited safety report (ICSR) was submitted to the relevant health authority via eCTD/E2B(R3) format. Used to verify compliance with regulatory reporting timelines.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: is_blinded
attributes.description: Indicates whether the narrative was authored under blinded conditions (True) or after unblinding of treatment assignment (False). Critical for maintaining study integrity in double-blind trials; blinded narratives must not reveal treatment allocation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Blinding; EMA Reflection Paper on Blinding

attributes.name: meddra_llt_code
attributes.description: MedDRA Lowest Level Term code representing the verbatim adverse event term as coded. Provides the most granular level of MedDRA coding for source data traceability.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AELLT

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term code for the primary adverse event. Eight-digit numeric code at the PT level of the MedDRA hierarchy, used as the standard coding for regulatory submissions and pharmacovigilance.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AEPTCD

attributes.name: meddra_pt_term
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term text (e.g., 'Atrial fibrillation') for the primary adverse event. Human-readable label used in narrative text and regulatory reports.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AEDECOD

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class code for the primary adverse event term. Eight-digit numeric code representing the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy used for regulatory reporting and signal detection.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AESOCCD

attributes.name: meddra_soc_term
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class term (e.g., 'Cardiac disorders') corresponding to the SOC code. Used for narrative labeling and regulatory submission display.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AESOC

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used for coding the adverse event terms in this narrative (e.g., '26.1'). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coding.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AEMEDDRA

attributes.name: medical_monitor_commentary
attributes.description: Clinical commentary and causality assessment provided by the medical monitor, including their opinion on the relationship between the investigational product and the adverse event, and any recommendations for protocol amendments or safety actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: medical_monitor_name
attributes.description: Full name of the medical monitor or safety physician who reviewed and approved the safety narrative. Required for regulatory audit trail and ICSR submission accountability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: narrative_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the safety narrative document. Tracks progression from initial authoring through medical monitor review and approval to regulatory submission. 'superseded' indicates a newer version has replaced this record.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Argus Safety workflow; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: outcome_description
attributes.description: Narrative section describing the resolution or current status of the adverse event, including recovery details, sequelae, or death information. Corresponds to the outcome field in E2B(R3) regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.8; ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM AE.AEOUT

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_notified
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of regulatory authorities to which this safety report was submitted (e.g., FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA). Supports multi-jurisdictional compliance tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|TGA|Health_Canada|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014; PMDA regulations

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this narrative supports an initial expedited report, a follow-up report with updated information, or a final report closing the case. Drives regulatory submission timelines under ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the medical monitor or safety physician completed their clinical review of the narrative. Distinct from the authoring date; marks the transition from draft to reviewed status.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Argus Safety workflow; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: seriousness_criteria
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of ICH E2A seriousness criteria met by the adverse event (e.g., death|life_threatening|hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant). Determines expedited reporting obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: source_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or path to the source documents (e.g., hospital records, lab reports, investigator notes) used to author this narrative, as stored in Veeva Vault eTMF. Supports SDV and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ principles; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: subject_description
attributes.description: Structured narrative section describing the patient's relevant medical history, demographics (age, sex, weight), concomitant medications, and pre-existing conditions relevant to the adverse event. Contains protected health information (PHI).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.1; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; GDPR Article 9; CDISC SDTM DM/MH domains

attributes.name: treatment_description
attributes.description: Narrative section describing the investigational product(s) and concomitant medications administered, including dose, route, frequency, start and stop dates, and any dose modifications or interruptions relevant to the adverse event.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section B.4; CDISC SDTM EX/CM domains; ICH E2A

attributes.name: unblinding_date
attributes.description: Date on which the treatment assignment was unblinded for this subject in the context of this safety case. Populated only when is_blinded transitions to False. Relevant for causality re-assessment post-unblinding.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Blinding; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this safety narrative record was most recently modified. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail, version control, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record requirements.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the safety narrative document, incremented each time the narrative is revised. Version 1 is the initial draft; subsequent versions reflect amendments or follow-up updates.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11

products.name: icsr
products.description: Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) — the formal regulatory submission record for expedited safety reporting to health authorities (FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA). Captures report type (initial, follow-up, nullification), submission date, acknowledgement receipt, regulatory agency, submission method (E2B XML, MedWatch, CIOMS), report version, submission status, clock start date (date of first awareness), calculated 7-day and 15-day deadline dates, actual submission date, days-to-submission, on-time compliance flag, and reason for delay if late. Enables compliance monitoring against ICH E2A and regional reporting requirements. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety case submission module.
products.reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) who experienced the adverse event triggering this ICSR.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA

attributes.name: acknowledgement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory agency formally acknowledged receipt of the ICSR submission. For electronic submissions via EudraVigilance or FDA gateway, this is the date of the automated acknowledgement message (ACK).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance; FDA ESG (Electronic Submissions Gateway)

attributes.name: acknowledgement_number
attributes.description: The unique reference number or message ID returned by the regulatory agency in the acknowledgement (ACK) message confirming receipt of the ICSR. Used for reconciliation and proof of submission.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance ACK; FDA ESG

attributes.name: applicable_deadline_date
attributes.description: The operative regulatory deadline date for this specific ICSR, reflecting the applicable reporting window (7-day or 15-day) based on the seriousness criteria and expectedness of the adverse event. Used for compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: The unique case identifier assigned by Oracle Argus Safety to the source safety case from which this ICSR was generated. Used for traceability back to the system of record.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety case submission module; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: awareness_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clock Start Date (Date of First Awareness)
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor or CRO first became aware of the adverse event that triggered this ICSR. This is the regulatory clock start date (Day 0) from which all expedited reporting deadlines (7-day and 15-day) are calculated per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this ICSR record was first created in Oracle Argus Safety and ingested into the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports audit trail and ALCOA+ data integrity requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 8

attributes.name: days_to_submission
attributes.description: The number of calendar days elapsed between the awareness_date (clock start) and the actual submission_date. Used to assess compliance with 7-day and 15-day expedited reporting requirements. Negative values indicate early submission.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: deadline_15day_date
attributes.description: The calculated calendar date by which a serious unexpected adverse reaction (non-fatal/non-life-threatening SUSAR) must be submitted to the regulatory agency, computed as awareness_date + 15 calendar days per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)(1)(ii); EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: deadline_7day_date
attributes.description: The calculated calendar date by which a fatal or life-threatening unexpected SUSAR must be submitted to the regulatory agency, computed as awareness_date + 7 calendar days per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)(1)(i); EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: delay_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation documenting the reason why the ICSR was not submitted within the applicable regulatory deadline. Required for late submissions to support CAPA processes and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; GCP ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; CAPA requirements

attributes.name: dsmb_notified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Notified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) was notified of this ICSR. Required for studies with an active DSMB charter.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DSMB; EMA DSMB guidance

attributes.name: irb_iec_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was formally notified of this ICSR. Used for compliance tracking against GCP notification requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.11; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.66; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: irb_iec_notified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Notified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) overseeing the study was notified of this ICSR, as required by GCP and applicable regulations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.11; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.66; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

attributes.name: is_current_version
attributes.description: Indicates whether this record represents the most current version of the ICSR. True for the latest version; False for superseded versions retained for audit history.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); ALCOA+ data integrity principles; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: is_fatal
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event associated with this ICSR resulted in the death of the subject. Fatal cases trigger the 7-day expedited reporting clock per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)(1)(i); EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: is_life_threatening
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event associated with this ICSR was life-threatening (i.e., the subject was at immediate risk of death). Life-threatening cases trigger the 7-day expedited reporting clock per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 3.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)(1)(i); EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: is_on_time
attributes.description: Indicates whether the ICSR was submitted to the regulatory agency on or before the applicable regulatory deadline date. True = compliant submission; False = late submission. Key KPI for regulatory compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance; ISO 14155

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ICSR relates to a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR). SUSARs require expedited reporting to regulatory authorities and ethics committees under ICH E2A and EU CTR 536/2014.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; EMA EudraVigilance; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
attributes.description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code for the primary adverse event reported in this ICSR. Used for standardized coding across regulatory submissions and signal detection.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2; CDISC SDTM AE domain

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
attributes.description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code for the primary adverse event in this ICSR. Used for aggregate safety analysis and signal detection by body system.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM AE domain

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.description: The version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code the adverse event in this ICSR (e.g., '26.1'). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coding.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2a; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: narrative
attributes.description: The structured free-text clinical narrative summarizing the adverse event, patient information, treatment details, and outcome as included in the ICSR submission. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) H.1 narrative section.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) H.1; FDA MedWatch 3500A Section G; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: The reason provided by the regulatory agency when an ICSR submission is rejected (e.g., data validation failure, duplicate case, missing mandatory fields). Populated only when submission_status = 'rejected'.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance; FDA ESG validation rules

attributes.name: report_number
attributes.description: The externally-known, unique regulatory report identifier assigned to this ICSR submission (e.g., the E2B message identifier or MedWatch report number). Used by health authorities to track and acknowledge the submission.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.0.1; FDA MedWatch 3500A; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ICSR is an initial submission, a follow-up update with new information, or a nullification (withdrawal) of a previously submitted report. Aligns with ICH E2B(R3) A.1.6.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.6; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: report_version
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this ICSR record. Version 1 is the initial report; subsequent versions represent follow-up or amended submissions for the same case.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); Oracle Argus Safety case versioning

attributes.name: sender_identifier
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the organization or individual sending the ICSR to the regulatory agency, as defined in ICH E2B(R3) A.3.1. Typically the sponsor or CRO EudraVigilance/FDA sender ID.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.3.1; EMA EudraVigilance; FDA ESG

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this ICSR record was sourced. Primarily Oracle Argus Safety case submission module; 'Manual' for records entered outside the system.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ data integrity principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The actual calendar date on which the ICSR was transmitted to the regulatory agency. Used to calculate days-to-submission and determine on-time compliance against the applicable deadline.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance; ALCOA+

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: The technical format or channel used to transmit the ICSR to the regulatory agency. E2B XML is the standard electronic format per ICH E2B(R3); MedWatch and CIOMS I are paper/PDF formats used for specific agencies or fallback scenarios.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch 3500A; CIOMS I Form; EMA EudraVigilance gateway

attributes.name: submission_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the ICSR submission lifecycle. Tracks progression from internal drafting through regulatory acknowledgement or rejection.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: submission_timestamp

attributes.name: awareness_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Date of First Awareness (Clock Start Date)
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor or CRO first became aware of the adverse event meeting expedited reporting criteria. This is the regulatory clock start date (Day 0) from which all reporting deadlines are calculated, per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: The investigator's or sponsor's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse event. Causality is a key determinant of SUSAR classification and expedited reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); WHO Causality Assessment; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this expedited report deadline tracking record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: days_overdue
attributes.description: Number of calendar days by which the submission exceeded the applicable regulatory deadline. Positive value indicates late submission; zero or null indicates on-time or not yet due. Used for CAPA tracking and regulatory risk assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CAPA — MasterControl

attributes.name: days_to_submission
attributes.description: The number of calendar days elapsed between the awareness_date (clock start) and the actual submission_date. Populated only after submission. Used for compliance KPI reporting and trend analysis against ICH E2A timelines.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: deadline_15_day
attributes.description: Calculated deadline date for 15-day expedited reporting, applicable to non-fatal/non-life-threatening unexpected SUSARs and other serious unexpected adverse reactions. Computed as awareness_date + 15 calendar days per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: deadline_7_day
attributes.description: Calculated deadline date for 7-day expedited reporting, applicable to fatal or life-threatening unexpected SUSARs. Computed as awareness_date + 7 calendar days per ICH E2A and FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: deadline_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the expedited report deadline. Pending = report not yet submitted and deadline not passed; Submitted_on_time = submitted within required days; Submitted_late = submitted after deadline; Overdue = deadline passed without submission; Waived = regulatory waiver granted; Not_applicable = reporting exemption applies.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: delay_reason_code
attributes.description: Coded reason explaining why the expedited report was submitted after the applicable regulatory deadline. Required for CAPA documentation and regulatory inspection readiness. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: incomplete_clinical_info|pending_causality_assessment|medical_review_delay|translation_required|system_outage|sponsor_approval_delay|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CAPA — MasterControl; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: delay_reason_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the specific circumstances that caused the expedited report to be submitted after the regulatory deadline. Supports CAPA documentation and regulatory inspection responses.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; GCP ICH E6(R2); CAPA — MasterControl; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: dsmb_notification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Notification Date
attributes.description: The date on which the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) was formally notified of this expedited safety report.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9

attributes.name: dsmb_notified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Notified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) was notified of this expedited safety report. Required for studies with an active DSMB/DMC per the study protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9

attributes.name: follow_up_due_date
attributes.description: The target date by which a follow-up expedited safety report must be submitted to the regulatory agency with updated case information. Applicable when follow_up_required is True.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: follow_up_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a follow-up expedited safety report is required to provide additional or updated information to the regulatory agency after the initial submission, per ICH E2A guidance.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: investigator_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Principal Investigator (PI) was notified of the SUSAR or expedited safety report submission, as required by ICH E2A and GCP guidelines. Supports site-level compliance tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: irb_iec_notification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Notification Date
attributes.description: The date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was notified of the SUSAR or expedited safety report, as required by GCP and applicable regulations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.66; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

attributes.name: is_fatal_or_life_threatening
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event is classified as fatal or life-threatening, which triggers the 7-day expedited reporting requirement rather than the standard 15-day timeline per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: is_on_time
attributes.description: Indicates whether the expedited safety report was submitted on or before the applicable regulatory deadline. True = submitted within the required timeframe; False = submitted late or not yet submitted past deadline. Core compliance KPI.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: is_unexpected
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event is unexpected (not consistent with the Investigator Brochure or current labeling), which is a key criterion for SUSAR classification and expedited reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: regulatory_agency
attributes.description: The regulatory authority to which the expedited safety report must be submitted (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, TGA, Health Canada). Determines the applicable reporting timeline and format requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|TGA|Health_Canada|ANVISA|Other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014; MHRA; PMDA; TGA; Health Canada

attributes.name: report_category
attributes.description: Indicates whether this deadline record pertains to an initial expedited report submission, a follow-up report with updated information, or a final report closing the case.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Classification of the expedited safety report type. SAE = Serious Adverse Event report; SUSAR = Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction; USADE = Unexpected Serious Adverse Device Effect; IND_Safety = IND Safety Report; BLA_Safety = Biologics License Application Safety Report.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: reporting_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the jurisdiction in which the expedited report must be filed. Drives country-specific regulatory timeline requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; ICH E2A; EU CTR 536/2014; GDPR

attributes.name: sponsor_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor was formally notified of the adverse event by the investigator or CRO. May differ from awareness_date if the CRO received information before the sponsor. Relevant for sponsor-level clock start determination.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the expedited safety report was submitted to the regulatory agency. Null if the report has not yet been submitted. Used to calculate days-to-submission and determine on-time compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: The electronic or paper-based method used to transmit the expedited safety report to the regulatory agency (e.g., eCTD via FDA ESG, E2B(R3) via EMA EVWEB, MedWatch 3500A, paper submission).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA ESG; EMA EVWEB; 21 CFR Part 11; eCTD

attributes.name: submission_reference_number
attributes.description: The acknowledgement or tracking number returned by the regulatory agency upon receipt of the expedited safety report submission (e.g., FDA ESG acknowledgement number, EMA EVWEB submission ID). Confirms successful receipt.
attributes.references: FDA ESG; EMA EVWEB; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the expedited safety report was electronically transmitted to the regulatory agency, including timezone offset. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2A; FDA ESG (Electronic Submissions Gateway); EMA EVWEB

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this expedited report deadline tracking record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: waiver_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal regulatory waiver or exemption has been granted for this expedited report, allowing submission outside the standard 7- or 15-day timeline. When True, waiver_reference must be populated.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2A

attributes.name: waiver_reference
attributes.description: The reference number or description of the regulatory waiver or exemption granted for this expedited report submission. Populated only when waiver_granted is True.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2A

products.name: dsur
products.description: Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) — the annual periodic safety report submitted to health authorities summarizing cumulative safety data for an investigational product across all ongoing studies. Captures reporting period, data lock date, cumulative subject exposure, SAE line listing summary, benefit-risk conclusion, and submission dates per agency. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety periodic reporting module.
products.reference: ICH E2F; FDA Annual IND Safety Report; EMA DSUR
