attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this DSUR was formally approved by the sponsor's qualified medical officer or pharmacovigilance responsible person, as recorded in the document management system.
attributes.references: ICH E2F; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; Veeva Vault Quality Management; MasterControl

attributes.name: argus_periodic_report_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Oracle Argus Safety Periodic Report ID
attributes.description: The internal report identifier assigned by Oracle Argus Safety periodic reporting module, used to trace this DSUR back to its source system record.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety Periodic Reporting Module; ICH E2F

attributes.name: benefit_risk_conclusion
attributes.description: The sponsor's overall benefit-risk conclusion for the investigational product based on the cumulative safety data reviewed in this DSUR, as required by ICH E2F.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 16; ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.33; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: benefit_risk_summary
attributes.description: Narrative text summarizing the sponsor's benefit-risk assessment for the reporting period, including key safety findings, emerging signals, and overall conclusions as documented in the DSUR.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 16; ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.33

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this DSUR record was first created in the system, providing the audit trail creation anchor per ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 8; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: cumulative_sae_count
attributes.description: Total number of serious adverse events (SAEs) reported for the investigational product from program inception through the end of the reporting period, as captured in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 10; ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: cumulative_subject_exposure_count
attributes.description: Total number of subjects exposed to the investigational product from the inception of the development program through the end of the reporting period, representing the cumulative safety exposure denominator.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 9; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.33; EMA DSUR Guideline

attributes.name: cumulative_subject_exposure_days
attributes.description: Total patient-days of exposure to the investigational product accumulated across all studies from program inception through the reporting period end date, used as the denominator for incidence rate calculations.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 9; ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: cumulative_susar_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Count
attributes.description: Total number of SUSARs (Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions) reported from program inception through the reporting period end date, a key regulatory safety metric.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 10; ICH E2A; EMA EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: data_lock_date
attributes.description: The database lock date on which safety data was frozen for inclusion in this DSUR. No new safety data is incorporated after this date for the current reporting period.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 4; CDISC SDTM; Oracle Argus Safety DBL Process

attributes.name: development_phase
attributes.description: The clinical development phase of the investigational product at the time of this DSUR (e.g., Phase I, Phase II, Phase III), which contextualizes the safety data and benefit-risk assessment.
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase II|Phase III|Phase IV|Phase I/II|Phase II/III
attributes.references: ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Trials; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: dibd
attributes.description: The Development International Birth Date — the date of first approval of a Clinical Trial Application (CTA) or equivalent in any country, used as the anchor date for annual DSUR reporting cycles.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 4.1; EMA Guideline on DSUR

attributes.name: dsmb_review_conducted
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Review Conducted Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) review was conducted during the reporting period, with findings incorporated into this DSUR.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 15; FDA Guidance for Clinical Trial Sponsors on DSMB; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: fatal_sae_count
attributes.description: Number of serious adverse events with a fatal outcome reported during the reporting period, a critical safety metric for benefit-risk assessment and DSMB/DMC review.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 10; ICH E2A; CTCAE v5.0 Grade 5; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: health_authority_acknowledgement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the health authority formally acknowledged receipt of the DSUR submission, used for regulatory compliance tracking and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: ICH E2F; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; Veeva Vault Regulatory Submissions

attributes.name: health_authority_query_received
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority issued a query or request for additional information in response to this DSUR submission, triggering a response workflow.
attributes.references: ICH E2F; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; Veeva Vault Regulatory Submissions

attributes.name: medical_reviewer
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the qualified medical officer or pharmacovigilance physician who performed the medical review and sign-off of this DSUR prior to submission.
attributes.references: ICH E2F; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: new_safety_signal_identified
attributes.description: Indicates whether a new safety signal for the investigational product was identified during the reporting period, triggering additional signal management activities and potential regulatory notifications.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 14; ICH E2C(R2); EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module IX

attributes.name: ongoing_study_count
attributes.description: Number of clinical studies with the investigational product that were ongoing during the reporting period, providing context for the scope of the safety data.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 6; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; WHO ICTRP

attributes.name: period_sae_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reporting Period Serious Adverse Event (SAE) Count
attributes.description: Number of serious adverse events (SAEs) reported during the current annual reporting period, used to assess period-over-period safety trends.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 10; ICH E2A; Oracle Argus Safety Periodic Reporting Module

attributes.name: period_subject_exposure_count
attributes.description: Number of subjects exposed to the investigational product during the current annual reporting period only, used to assess period-specific safety signal rates.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 9; Oracle Argus Safety Periodic Reporting Module

attributes.name: period_susar_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reporting Period Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Count
attributes.description: Number of SUSARs reported during the current annual reporting period, used for expedited reporting compliance monitoring and signal detection.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 10; ICH E2A; EMA EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42

attributes.name: reference_safety_document_type
attributes.description: Type of reference safety information document used to assess expectedness of adverse reactions in this DSUR (e.g., IB = Investigator's Brochure, CCSI = Company Core Safety Information, SmPC = Summary of Product Characteristics, USPI = US Prescribing Information, RSI = Reference Safety Information).
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 7; ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.23

attributes.name: reference_safety_document_version
attributes.description: Version number or edition of the reference safety document (e.g., Investigator's Brochure edition) used as the basis for expectedness assessment in this DSUR.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 7; ICH E2C(R2); Veeva Vault eTMF Document Management

attributes.name: regulatory_action_taken
attributes.description: Significant regulatory or safety action taken during the reporting period as a result of safety findings (e.g., protocol amendment, Investigator's Brochure update, study suspension). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|protocol_amendment|ibr_update|study_suspension|study_termination|rmp_update|label_update|dhcp_letter — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 15; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EU CTR 536/2014 Article 54

attributes.name: report_number
attributes.description: Externally-known sequential report number assigned to this DSUR (e.g., DSUR-2024-001), used for regulatory tracking and cross-referencing across submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 3; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the DSUR document, tracking its progression from authoring through regulatory acceptance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|under_review|approved|submitted|accepted|rejected|withdrawn — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2F; Veeva Vault Quality Management; MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: report_version
attributes.description: Version number of the DSUR document (e.g., 1.0, 2.0), incremented upon amendments or corrections to a previously submitted report.
attributes.references: ICH E2F; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the annual reporting period covered by this DSUR, marking the data cut-off for safety data included in the report.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 4; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.33; EMA EU CTR 536/2014 Article 43

attributes.name: reporting_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the annual reporting period covered by this DSUR, typically the Development International Birth Date (DIBD) anniversary.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 4; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.33; EMA EU CTR 536/2014 Article 43

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which this DSUR was submitted to the primary health authority, used for regulatory compliance tracking and on-time submission KPI monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E2F; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.33; EMA EU CTR 536/2014 Article 43; Veeva Vault Regulatory Submissions

attributes.name: submission_due_date
attributes.description: The regulatory deadline by which this DSUR must be submitted to health authorities, typically 60 days after the reporting period end date per ICH E2F.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 4; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.33; EMA EU CTR 536/2014 Article 43

attributes.name: submission_format
attributes.description: The electronic or paper format used for the DSUR submission to health authorities (e.g., eCTD = Electronic Common Technical Document, NeeS = Non-eCTD Electronic Submission).
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Guideline; FDA eCTD Technical Specifications; EMA eCTD Guidance; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The clinical therapeutic area or disease indication for which the investigational product is being developed (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology), used for safety signal contextualization.
attributes.references: ICH E2F; MedDRA SOC Classification; FDA CDER Therapeutic Area Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this DSUR record was last modified in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage tracking per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 8; GDPR Article 5

products.name: ctcae_grade
products.description: Reference table for CTCAE (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events) severity grading definitions. Captures CTCAE version, SOC category, adverse event term, grade (1–5), grade description, and clinical criteria. Used to standardize severity grading across all AE records. Infrequently updated when new CTCAE versions are released by NCI.
products.reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CTCAE v4.03

attributes.name: ctcae_grade_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade ID
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each CTCAE grade definition record in the reference table. This is the primary key for the ctcae_grade product. [_canonical_skip_reason: Entity role is REFERENCE_LOOKUP — a controlled NCI-published code list of severity grades; per-role minimum categories are exempt.]
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: meddra_term_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.meddra_term. Business justification: ctcae_grade stores meddra_pt_code, meddra_pt_name, meddra_soc_code, meddra_version as strings representing the MedDRA mapping for each CTCAE grade. Adding meddra_term_id FK to the meddra_term referenc
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: ae_term
attributes.description: The official CTCAE adverse event term name as published by NCI (e.g., 'Atrial fibrillation', 'Nausea', 'Peripheral neuropathy'). This is the standardized clinical term used to classify and report adverse events across all clinical trials. Corresponds to the AETERM or AEDECOD field in CDISC SDTM AE domain and is the primary human-readable label for this grading record.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM IG v3.3 AE Domain; ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

attributes.name: applicable_population
attributes.description: Specifies the patient population for which this CTCAE grade definition is applicable (e.g., 'All', 'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Oncology'). Some CTCAE terms and grade criteria differ by population (e.g., pediatric-specific grading criteria). Used to filter applicable grade definitions when assigning severity in studies with specific population constraints.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E11 Clinical Investigation of Medicinal Products in the Pediatric Population; FDA Pediatric Study Requirements

attributes.name: cdisc_codelist_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Codelist Code
attributes.description: The CDISC controlled terminology codelist code associated with this CTCAE grade entry (e.g., the AETOXGR codelist code). Enables direct mapping to CDISC SDTM submission datasets and ADaM analysis datasets produced in SAS Drug Development. Required for eCTD regulatory submissions to FDA, EMA, and PMDA.
attributes.references: CDISC Controlled Terminology; CDISC SDTM IG v3.3; CDISC ADaM IG; FDA eCTD Technical Specifications

attributes.name: change_summary
attributes.description: A brief description of what changed in this grade definition relative to the prior CTCAE version (e.g., 'Grade 3 criteria updated to include specific lab threshold', 'New term added in v5.0', 'Grade description clarified'). Supports data managers and regulatory affairs teams in assessing the impact of CTCAE version upgrades on ongoing studies and in preparing regulatory submission change justifications.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE Version History; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Protocol Amendments; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: clinical_criteria
attributes.description: Supplementary clinical criteria, laboratory thresholds, or objective measurement parameters that define the boundary conditions for assigning this specific grade to the AE term (e.g., specific lab value ranges, vital sign thresholds, functional impairment descriptors). Distinct from the grade_description in that it captures the measurable/objective criteria rather than the narrative description. Used by clinical staff for precise grade assignment and by biostatisticians for consistency validation.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CTCAE Grading Guidelines; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this CTCAE grade reference record was first loaded into the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+ principles, and GDPR Article 5 data integrity obligations. Used by data management teams to track when new CTCAE version data was ingested.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: ctcae_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Term Code
attributes.description: Official NCI-assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the CTCAE adverse event term within a given version. Used as the primary business identifier for cross-system referencing and CDISC SDTM mapping (AETOXGR domain). Enables unambiguous linkage between AE records and the reference grading criteria.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM IG v3.3 AE Domain; NCI Thesaurus (NCIt)

attributes.name: ctcae_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Version
attributes.description: Version number of the CTCAE publication from which this grade definition originates (e.g., 'v5.0', 'v4.03'). Critical for ensuring AE severity grading is applied against the correct version mandated by the study protocol. New CTCAE versions are released by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and may alter grade descriptions or add/remove terms.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on AE Reporting

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this CTCAE grade definition was superseded, retired, or replaced by a newer version (nullable for currently active records). Used in conjunction with effective_start_date to implement bi-temporal versioning of the reference table, ensuring that AE records can always be validated against the grade criteria that were in effect at the time of the adverse event.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE Publication History; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5 (data accuracy)

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this CTCAE grade definition became effective and available for use in clinical trial AE grading (typically the official NCI publication date of the CTCAE version). Used to determine which version of a grade definition was applicable at the time of an AE occurrence, supporting retrospective audit and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE Publication History; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: grade
attributes.description: Numeric severity grade (1 through 5) as defined by CTCAE. Grade 1 = Mild; Grade 2 = Moderate; Grade 3 = Severe; Grade 4 = Life-threatening or disabling; Grade 5 = Death related to AE. This is the core grading dimension of the reference table and is used to populate the AETOXGR field in CDISC SDTM submissions and to trigger SAE/SUSAR reporting workflows in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain

attributes.name: grade_description
attributes.description: Full verbatim clinical description of the severity grade for the specific AE term as published in the CTCAE by NCI (e.g., for 'Nausea' Grade 2: 'Moderate nausea; oral intake decreased without significant weight loss, dehydration or malnutrition'). This is the authoritative clinical criteria text used by investigators and CRAs to assign the correct grade during AE assessment. Stored verbatim to preserve regulatory integrity.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: grade_label
attributes.description: Standardized textual label corresponding to the numeric CTCAE grade (e.g., 'Mild' for Grade 1, 'Moderate' for Grade 2, 'Severe' for Grade 3, 'Life-Threatening' for Grade 4, 'Death' for Grade 5). Provides a human-readable severity descriptor for use in clinical reports, DSMB/DMC safety narratives, and regulatory submissions without requiring a lookup of the numeric grade.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E2A; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: grading_notes
attributes.description: Additional clinical notes, caveats, or guidance provided by NCI for applying this specific grade to the AE term (e.g., 'Also consider Anemia', 'See also Cardiac disorders: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction'). Captures the 'Also consider' and 'Navigational Note' annotations present in the CTCAE publication that guide investigators in differential grading decisions.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on AE Assessment

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether this CTCAE grade definition record is currently active and available for use in new AE grading assignments. Set to False when a term or grade is retired, superseded by a newer CTCAE version, or deprecated. Enables version-controlled filtering so that active studies use only current, approved grading criteria while historical records remain accessible for audit.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: is_oncology_specific
attributes.description: Indicates whether this CTCAE adverse event term and grade definition is specific to oncology/cancer treatment contexts. CTCAE was originally developed for oncology trials; some terms are exclusively relevant to chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy adverse effects. Used to filter applicable grading criteria for oncology versus non-oncology study protocols.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; NCI Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP); FDA Oncology Guidance

attributes.name: is_serious_by_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Serious Adverse Event (SAE) Flag by Grade
attributes.description: Indicates whether this CTCAE grade level is inherently classified as a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) based on regulatory definitions (typically Grade 3 and above may trigger SAE criteria, Grade 4–5 are always serious). Used to automate SAE flagging logic in Oracle Argus Safety and EDC systems (Medidata Rave) when a grade is recorded, supporting expedited reporting timelines under ICH E2A and FDA 21 CFR 312.32.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; NCI CTCAE v5.0

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
attributes.description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code that most closely corresponds to this CTCAE adverse event term, enabling cross-coding between CTCAE and MedDRA terminologies. Used for regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA) that require MedDRA coding, and for signal detection in Oracle Argus Safety. Alignment maintained per current MedDRA version used in the study.
attributes.references: ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology; MedDRA Introductory Guide; CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain; FDA MedDRA Requirements

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
attributes.description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) numeric code corresponding to the primary SOC classification of this CTCAE term's MedDRA PT cross-reference. Enables integrated safety tabulations that span both CTCAE-graded AE data and MedDRA-coded data in regulatory submissions and DSMB/DMC reports.
attributes.references: ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology; CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain; FDA MedDRA Requirements; EMA MedDRA Requirements

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Version
attributes.description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used for the cross-reference mapping between this CTCAE term and its corresponding MedDRA PT/SOC codes (e.g., '26.0', '25.1'). MedDRA is updated biannually; version tracking ensures regulatory submissions reference the correct dictionary version as required by FDA, EMA, and PMDA.
attributes.references: ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology; MedDRA Release Notes; FDA MedDRA Requirements; EMA MedDRA Requirements

attributes.name: nci_concept_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Cancer Institute (NCI) Thesaurus Concept ID
attributes.description: The NCI Thesaurus (NCIt) concept identifier (e.g., 'C54767') for this CTCAE adverse event term. Provides a stable, version-independent identifier from the NCI controlled vocabulary that persists across CTCAE versions. Used for ontology-based data integration, CDISC terminology alignment, and cross-study analytics in SAS Drug Development and AI/ML safety signal detection pipelines.
attributes.references: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt); CDISC Controlled Terminology; NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: nci_publication_date
attributes.description: The official publication date of the CTCAE version from which this grade definition originates, as released by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP). Provides the authoritative reference date for regulatory submissions and audit trails, distinct from the effective_start_date which may reflect internal adoption timing.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; NCI Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP); FDA Guidance on AE Reporting

attributes.name: prior_version_code
attributes.description: The CTCAE term code from the immediately preceding CTCAE version that this record supersedes or corresponds to, enabling version-to-version lineage tracking. Used by data managers and biostatisticians to reconcile AE grading data collected under different CTCAE versions within the same study or across studies in integrated safety analyses.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE Version History; CDISC SDTM IG; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: reporting_timeline_days
attributes.description: The maximum number of calendar days within which an AE at this grade must be reported to regulatory authorities upon sponsor awareness (e.g., 7 days for fatal/life-threatening unexpected SUSARs, 15 days for other serious unexpected reactions, null for non-expedited grades). Drives automated due-date calculation in Oracle Argus Safety and regulatory_report_due_date population on the adverse_event product.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR 312.32; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014; PMDA Safety Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: requires_expedited_reporting
attributes.description: Indicates whether an AE recorded at this CTCAE grade level triggers mandatory expedited regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., 7-day or 15-day IND safety reports to FDA, EMA, PMDA). Derived from regulatory guidance but stored as a reference attribute to drive automated reporting workflow triggers in Oracle Argus Safety and CTMS. Supports compliance with FDA 21 CFR 312.32, EMA GVP Module VI, and ICH E2A timelines.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR 312.32; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI; PMDA Safety Reporting Guidelines; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: sdtm_domain
attributes.description: The two-letter CDISC SDTM domain code to which this CTCAE grade reference applies (e.g., 'AE' for Adverse Events domain). Supports SDTM dataset construction in SAS Drug Development and ensures correct domain-level mapping during regulatory submission preparation.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM IG v3.3; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA CDISC Requirements

attributes.name: sdtm_variable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) Variable Name
attributes.description: The CDISC SDTM variable name to which this CTCAE grade value maps in regulatory submission datasets (e.g., 'AETOXGR' for the AE domain toxicity grade). Used by SAS Drug Development programmers and CDISC data managers to ensure correct SDTM dataset population and FDA/EMA submission compliance.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM IG v3.3; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide AE Domain; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA CDISC Requirements

attributes.name: soc_code
attributes.description: NCI-assigned code for the System Organ Class (SOC) category within the CTCAE hierarchy. Enables programmatic grouping and filtering of adverse event terms by organ system for safety tabulations, DSMB/DMC reports, and regulatory submissions. Distinct from MedDRA SOC codes but may be cross-referenced.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; NCI Thesaurus (NCIt); CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain

attributes.name: soc_name
attributes.description: The System Organ Class (SOC) category name as defined in the CTCAE, representing the highest-level anatomical or physiological grouping of adverse event terms (e.g., 'Cardiac disorders', 'Gastrointestinal disorders', 'Nervous system disorders'). Aligns with MedDRA SOC hierarchy for cross-coding purposes. Used for safety signal detection and aggregate reporting by organ system.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology

attributes.name: source_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific section, page, or table in the official NCI CTCAE publication document from which this grade definition was extracted (e.g., 'CTCAE v5.0, Section 2, Table: Cardiac Disorders, p.12'). Supports regulatory inspection readiness and audit trail requirements by providing a direct link to the authoritative source document stored in Veeva Vault eTMF.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system or authoritative source from which this CTCAE grade reference record was loaded (e.g., 'Oracle Argus Safety' where CTCAE codes are maintained, 'SAS Drug Development' for CDISC-aligned reference data, 'NCI CTCAE' for direct NCI publication ingestion). Supports data lineage tracking and Silver layer provenance requirements.
attributes.value_regex: Oracle Argus Safety|SAS Drug Development|NCI CTCAE|Manual
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC Data Management Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent update to this CTCAE grade reference record in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Tracks corrections, enrichments, or metadata updates applied after initial load. Required for audit trail completeness under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: veeva_document_reference
attributes.description: The document identifier in Veeva Vault eTMF for the official NCI CTCAE source document associated with this version. Enables direct navigation from the reference record to the controlled source document in the electronic Trial Master File, supporting audit trail completeness and regulatory inspection readiness per 21 CFR Part 11 and EU CTR 536/2014.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault eTMF System

products.name: meddra_term
products.description: Reference master for the MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) terminology hierarchy, storing all active terms across all five levels: LLT (Lowest Level Term), PT (Preferred Term), HLT (High Level Term), HLGT (High Level Group Term), and SOC (System Organ Class). Captures term code, term name, level, primary SOC flag, MedDRA version, and active/retired status. Updated with each biannual MedDRA release.
products.reference: MedDRA v27.0; MSSO MedDRA Browser; ICH M1

attributes.name: meddra_term_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each MedDRA term record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key. [REFERENCE_LOOKUP role — _canonical_skip_reason: This entity is a standardized regulatory reference code list (MedDRA hierarchy) maintained by MSSO/ICH; per-role minimums for REFERENCE_LOOKUP are exempt.]
attributes.references: MedDRA Maintenance and Support Services Organization (MSSO); ICH M1 Guideline

attributes.name: argus_dict_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Oracle Argus Safety Dictionary Record ID
attributes.description: The internal dictionary record identifier assigned by Oracle Argus Safety when this MedDRA term is loaded into the Argus dictionary module. Enables direct cross-reference between the lakehouse silver layer and the Oracle Argus Safety system of record for adverse event coding reconciliation and audit.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety Dictionary Management Guide; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: change_type
attributes.description: Describes the nature of the change applied to this term in the current MedDRA version: 'new' (first introduced), 'modified' (name or hierarchy changed), 'retired' (removed from active use), 'split' (one term divided into multiple), 'merged' (multiple terms combined), or 'reinstated' (previously retired term reactivated). Critical for managing dictionary upgrade impacts in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Change Documentation; ICH E2B(R3); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this MedDRA term record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Supports data lineage, audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles for the clinical data management platform.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: ctcae_grade_mapping
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade Mapping
attributes.description: The CTCAE v5.0 term name that corresponds to this MedDRA PT, where a direct mapping exists. Enables cross-referencing between MedDRA coding and CTCAE severity grading used in oncology and other therapeutic area studies. Null where no CTCAE mapping exists for this term.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; MedDRA-CTCAE Mapping Table; CDISC SDTM IG; FDA Oncology Guidance

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this MedDRA term is officially effective and available for use in adverse event coding and regulatory submissions, corresponding to the MSSO release date of the version in which it was introduced. Supports version-gating logic in Oracle Argus Safety and study-level coding version controls.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Release Schedule; ICH E2B(R3); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: The level within the five-tier MedDRA hierarchy to which this term belongs: LLT (Lowest Level Term), PT (Preferred Term), HLT (High Level Term), HLGT (High Level Group Term), or SOC (System Organ Class). Determines how the term is used in adverse event coding, CTCAE mapping, and regulatory aggregate reporting.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1 Guideline; CDISC SDTM IG (AEDECOD, AEBODSYS); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: hlgt_code
attributes.description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the High Level Group Term (HLGT) in the primary SOC path for this term. Populated for LLT, PT, HLT, and HLGT level terms to support aggregate safety analysis and regulatory tabulations at the HLGT level.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: hlgt_name
attributes.description: The official MedDRA name of the High Level Group Term (HLGT) in the primary SOC path. Denormalized for direct use in safety tabulations and signal detection analytics without requiring a hierarchy traversal.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: hlt_code
attributes.description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the High Level Term (HLT) in the primary SOC path for this term. Populated for LLT, PT, and HLT level terms to support aggregate safety analysis at the HLT level in regulatory submissions and DSMB/DMC reports.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: hlt_name
attributes.description: The official MedDRA name of the High Level Term (HLT) in the primary SOC path. Denormalized for direct use in safety tabulations and signal detection analytics.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: introduced_version
attributes.description: The MedDRA version in which this term was first introduced into the dictionary. Supports historical analysis of term availability across study timelines and ensures correct version-gating when coding adverse events from legacy studies.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term History Documentation

attributes.name: is_llt_current
attributes.description: Applicable to LLT-level terms only. Indicates whether the LLT is a 'current' LLT (true) — meaning it maps to a PT with the same name — or a 'non-current' LLT (false) that maps to a PT with a different name. Current LLTs are preferred for new coding; non-current LLTs are retained for historical traceability per MSSO policy.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO LLT Currency Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: is_primary_soc
attributes.description: Indicates whether this term's association to a System Organ Class (SOC) is the primary (true) or secondary (false) SOC linkage. MedDRA allows a PT to be linked to multiple SOCs; the primary SOC is used for regulatory aggregate safety tabulations, DSMB/DMC safety reviews, and CTCAE-aligned reporting.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG (AEBODSYS); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: ISO 639-1/639-2 language code for the language of this term record (e.g., 'en' for English, 'ja' for Japanese, 'de' for German). MedDRA is published in multiple languages; this field supports multi-language implementations required for submissions to PMDA (Japanese), EMA (EU languages), and Health Canada (French/English).
attributes.references: ISO 639-1; MedDRA Multi-Language Guide; PMDA Submission Requirements; EMA MedDRA Policy; Health Canada Guidance

attributes.name: llt_code
attributes.description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the Lowest Level Term (LLT). For LLT-level records this equals term_code. For higher-level terms this field is null. LLTs capture verbatim-level medical concepts and are the entry point for verbatim-to-MedDRA coding in Oracle Argus Safety and EDC systems.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG; FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: llt_name
attributes.description: The official MedDRA name of the Lowest Level Term (LLT). For LLT-level records this equals term_name. Null for higher-level terms. Used in verbatim coding workflows and auto-coding dictionaries in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: load_date
attributes.description: The date on which this MedDRA term record was loaded into the lakehouse silver layer from the MSSO distribution files. Used to track the effective date of each biannual dictionary update and to support audit trails required under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; MSSO Release Schedule; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.description: The biannual MedDRA release version in which this term was introduced or last updated (e.g., '27.0', '26.1'). Critical for regulatory submissions requiring version-specific coding, database lock (DBL) documentation, and CDISC SDTM dataset compliance. MedDRA releases occur twice yearly (March and September).
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Release Schedule; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: pt_code
attributes.description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the Preferred Term (PT) to which this term maps. For PT-level records this equals term_code. For LLT-level records this is the parent PT code. Used as the primary coding level in Oracle Argus Safety adverse event records, CDISC SDTM (AEDECOD), and regulatory case submissions (ICH E2B).
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG (AEDECOD); FDA Adverse Event Reporting; EMA MedDRA Policy

attributes.name: pt_name
attributes.description: The official MedDRA name of the Preferred Term (PT) to which this term maps. Denormalized for direct use in adverse event coding displays, safety narratives, CDISC SDTM datasets, and regulatory submissions without requiring a hierarchy join.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG (AEDECOD); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: rave_dict_entry_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medidata Rave EDC Dictionary Entry ID
attributes.description: The dictionary entry identifier assigned by Medidata Rave EDC when this MedDRA term is configured in the Rave coding dictionary for eCRF verbatim-to-MedDRA auto-coding. Supports reconciliation between EDC-coded adverse events and the master MedDRA reference in the lakehouse.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave Coding Module Documentation; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: replacement_term_code
attributes.description: The 8-digit MedDRA code of the term that replaces this term when it has been retired, split, or merged. Null for active terms and retired terms with no direct replacement. Supports automated re-coding workflows in Oracle Argus Safety during biannual MedDRA version upgrades.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement and Replacement Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: retired_version
attributes.description: The MedDRA version in which this term was retired, if applicable. Null for active terms. Used to enforce coding rules in Oracle Argus Safety and to flag terms that should not be applied to new adverse event records after the specified version.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: The date on which this MedDRA term was officially retired by MSSO, corresponding to the release date of the version in which it was retired. Null for active terms. Used to enforce coding restrictions in Oracle Argus Safety and to flag terms in legacy study datasets.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: smq_membership
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of Standardised MedDRA Query (SMQ) names to which this PT belongs. SMQs are validated, topic-focused groupings of MedDRA terms used for signal detection, aggregate safety analysis, and regulatory queries (e.g., 'Anaphylactic reaction', 'Drug-induced liver injury'). Populated for PT-level terms only.
attributes.references: MedDRA SMQ Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO SMQ Documentation; ICH E2B(R3); EMA Signal Detection Guidance

attributes.name: smq_scope
attributes.description: Indicates whether this term's SMQ membership is classified as 'broad' (higher sensitivity, more inclusive) or 'narrow' (higher specificity, more restrictive) within the associated SMQ. Used to configure signal detection algorithms in Oracle Argus Safety and to define the scope of safety queries in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: MedDRA SMQ Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO SMQ Documentation; EMA Signal Detection Guidance; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: soc_abbreviation
attributes.description: The standardized two-to-four letter abbreviation for the System Organ Class (SOC) as defined by MSSO (e.g., 'CARD' for Cardiac disorders, 'NERV' for Nervous system disorders). Used in safety tabulation headers, DSMB/DMC slide decks, and abbreviated regulatory reports.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO SOC Abbreviation List; ICH M1

attributes.name: soc_code
attributes.description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the System Organ Class (SOC) to which this term is linked (primary or secondary). Populated for all hierarchy levels to enable direct SOC-level filtering in safety tabulations, signal detection, and regulatory submissions without requiring a hierarchy traversal join.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG (AEBODSYS); EMA MedDRA Policy

attributes.name: soc_name
attributes.description: The official MedDRA name of the System Organ Class (SOC) associated with this term. Denormalized for direct use in safety tabulations, DSMB/DMC reports, and CDISC SDTM datasets (AEBODSYS variable) without requiring a hierarchy join.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; CDISC SDTM IG; ICH E2B(R3); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

attributes.name: source_file_name
attributes.description: The name of the MSSO-distributed MedDRA ASCII flat file from which this term record was loaded (e.g., 'llt.asc', 'pt.asc', 'hlt.asc', 'hlgt.asc', 'soc.asc'). Supports data lineage traceability and ETL audit for the biannual MedDRA dictionary update process in the Databricks lakehouse.
attributes.references: MSSO MedDRA Distribution File Format Guide; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: term_code
attributes.description: The official 8-digit numeric MedDRA term code assigned by the Maintenance and Support Services Organization (MSSO) uniquely identifying this term within the MedDRA hierarchy. Used as the primary lookup key in Oracle Argus Safety for adverse event coding and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1 Guideline; FDA MedDRA Requirements; EMA MedDRA Policy

attributes.name: term_name
attributes.description: The official MedDRA term label as published by MSSO for this term code. Represents the standardized medical concept name used in adverse event coding, regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA), and safety signal detection across all five hierarchy levels.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1 Guideline; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: term_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the MedDRA term is currently active and available for coding or has been retired in a subsequent MedDRA version release. Retired terms are retained for historical traceability of previously coded adverse events but must not be used for new coding in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement Policy; ICH E2B(R3) Guideline

attributes.name: term_type
attributes.description: Classifies the term as 'standard' (fully endorsed MedDRA term) or 'non-standard' (a term that has been superseded, split, or merged and retained for backward compatibility). Drives coding validation rules in Oracle Argus Safety and Medidata Rave auto-coding configurations.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Classification Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this MedDRA term record was last updated in the lakehouse silver layer, typically triggered by a biannual MedDRA version release load. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: who_art_mapping
attributes.description: The corresponding WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology (WHO-ART) preferred term code or name for this MedDRA term, where a legacy mapping exists. Supports legacy study migration and cross-dictionary reconciliation for studies coded under WHO-ART prior to MedDRA adoption.
attributes.references: WHO-ART to MedDRA Mapping Guide; MSSO Cross-Dictionary Mapping; ICH M1

products.name: review_committee
products.description: Master record for internal sponsor Safety Review Committees (SRCs) and external Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs) overseeing study safety. Captures committee name, type (internal SRC, DSMB, DMC, IDMC), charter version, meeting frequency, member roster, independence status, and associated studies. Distinct from the dsmb_review entity which captures individual meeting records.
products.reference: ICH E9; FDA DSMB Guidance; EMA DMC Reflection Paper

attributes.name: review_committee_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the safety review committee record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: health_authority_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Safety review committees (DSMBs) report to specific regulatory authorities per their charter. Linking to health_authority normalizes the regulatory_authority_notified field and enables governance trac
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: organization_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sponsor.organization. Business justification: Safety review committees (DSMBs/DMCs) are established by and report to a specific sponsor organization. The charter, independence requirements, and reporting authority are sponsor-specific governance
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: tmf_document_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier of the charter document as stored in Veeva Vault eTMF. Enables direct retrieval of the governing charter for audit and regulatory inspection purposes.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: argus_committee_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for this committee as configured in Oracle Argus Safety for routing SAE/SUSAR reports and safety data packages to the committee. Enables traceability between safety case management and committee oversight.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: associated_study_count
attributes.description: Number of clinical studies currently under the oversight of this committee. A single DMC/DSMB may oversee multiple studies within a development program. Used for workload assessment and committee capacity planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: charter_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current version of the committee charter was formally approved by the sponsor or designated authority. Establishes the effective date of the committee's operating mandate.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: charter_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current charter version expires and requires renewal or amendment. Null if the charter is open-ended and tied to study completion. Used for compliance tracking in MasterControl.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: charter_title
attributes.description: Official title of the committee's governing charter document as stored in Veeva Vault eTMF. The charter defines the committee's mandate, operating procedures, decision-making authority, and confidentiality obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; Veeva Vault eTMF; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: charter_version
attributes.description: Version number of the currently approved committee charter document (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.1'). Tracks charter amendments over the committee lifecycle. Linked to the document in Veeva Vault eTMF.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: closed_session_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the committee charter mandates a closed/executive session restricted to independent committee members and the unblinded statistician, excluding sponsor representatives. Required for independent DMC/DSMB per FDA guidance.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19

attributes.name: committee_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric business identifier for the committee used in Oracle Siebel CTMS and Oracle Argus Safety for cross-system referencing and reporting (e.g., 'DMC-2024-001', 'SRC-ONCOLOGY-01').
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: committee_name
attributes.description: Official full name of the safety review committee as defined in its charter (e.g., 'Study XYZ Data Monitoring Committee', 'Global Safety Review Committee'). Used as the primary human-readable identifier across CTMS and safety systems.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: committee_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the committee. 'active' = operational and conducting reviews; 'inactive' = temporarily not meeting; 'dissolved' = formally disbanded at study close-out; 'suspended' = operations halted pending investigation; 'pending_charter' = established but charter not yet approved.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: committee_type
attributes.description: Classification of the committee by its regulatory and operational role. SRC = internal Safety Review Committee; DSMB = Data Safety Monitoring Board; DMC = Data Monitoring Committee; IDMC = Independent Data Monitoring Committee; ISMC = Independent Safety Monitoring Committee. Drives applicable regulatory obligations and independence requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees (EMA/CHMP/EWP/5872/03)

attributes.name: confidentiality_agreement_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether all committee members are required to execute a confidentiality agreement prior to receiving unblinded study data. Mandatory for independent committees with unblinded access per GCP and sponsor SOPs.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 28; HIPAA; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: conflict_of_interest_policy
attributes.description: Identifies the conflict-of-interest (COI) policy framework governing committee member disclosures and recusal procedures. 'sponsor_policy' = governed by sponsor's COI SOP; 'charter_defined' = COI rules embedded in the committee charter; 'external_standard' = governed by an external professional body standard.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees; OHRP

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this committee record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Supports ALCOA+ data integrity principles and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: ctms_committee_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Committee ID
attributes.description: Identifier for this committee record in Oracle Siebel CTMS, used for meeting scheduling, site notification workflows, and cross-system reconciliation between the CTMS and the lakehouse.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: dissolution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the committee was formally dissolved, typically at study close-out or database lock (DBL). Null if the committee is still active. Required for TMF completeness at study archival.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault eTMF; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: establishment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the committee was formally established and constituted by the sponsor. Marks the start of the committee's operational lifecycle and is recorded in the Trial Master File (TMF).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: governing_regulation
attributes.description: Primary regulatory framework or guideline under which the committee operates (e.g., '21 CFR Part 312', 'EU CTR 536/2014', 'ICH E6(R2)', 'ISO 14155'). Determines reporting obligations and procedural requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 21_CFR_312|EU_CTR_536_2014|ICH_E6R2|ISO_14155|PMDA_GCP|TGA_GCP — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); ISO 14155; PMDA; TGA

attributes.name: independent_statistician_assigned
attributes.description: Indicates whether an independent (unblinded) statistician has been formally assigned to support the committee with unblinded data analysis. Required for DSMB/DMC operations per ICH E9(R1) and FDA guidance.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees

attributes.name: is_independent
attributes.description: Indicates whether the committee operates independently from the sponsor and investigators (True) or is an internal sponsor committee (False). Independence is a regulatory requirement for DMC/DSMB/IDMC roles per ICH E6(R2) and FDA guidance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees

attributes.name: last_meeting_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recently completed committee meeting. Used for monitoring meeting cadence compliance against the charter-defined frequency and for DSMB/DMC oversight tracking in Oracle Siebel CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: meeting_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency at which the committee convenes for safety reviews as defined in the charter. 'per_protocol' indicates frequency is defined by study protocol milestones (e.g., after every N subjects enrolled). Drives meeting scheduling in Oracle Siebel CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: meeting_minutes_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether formal written minutes are required for each committee meeting per the charter. Minutes are a GCP requirement for DMC/DSMB meetings and must be archived in the eTMF.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: next_meeting_date
attributes.description: Date of the next scheduled committee meeting as planned in Oracle Siebel CTMS. Used for advance preparation of safety data packages and member notification workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: open_session_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the committee charter mandates an open session (attended by sponsor representatives) in addition to the closed/executive session (independent members only). Standard DMC practice per FDA guidance.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19

attributes.name: outstanding_recommendations_count
attributes.description: Number of committee recommendations that have been issued but not yet formally resolved or closed by the sponsor. A non-zero value triggers escalation workflows in Oracle Siebel CTMS and MasterControl CAPA tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; MasterControl CAPA; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: primary_therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The primary therapeutic area or disease indication for which the committee provides safety oversight (e.g., 'Oncology', 'Cardiovascular', 'Neurology'). Used for committee expertise matching and portfolio-level safety analytics.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM TA domain

attributes.name: quorum_requirement
attributes.description: Minimum number of committee members required to be present for a meeting to be valid and for decisions to be binding, as specified in the charter. Enforced during meeting scheduling and minutes review.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_notified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA) has been formally notified of the committee's establishment and composition, as required for certain study types and jurisdictions.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EU CTR 536/2014; EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: reporting_authority
attributes.description: Name or role of the organizational body or individual to whom the committee formally reports its recommendations (e.g., 'Sponsor Medical Officer', 'Executive Steering Committee', 'IRB/IEC'). Defines the escalation path for safety recommendations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: safety_data_package_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the unblinded safety data package is prepared and distributed to committee members prior to meetings. Governs data preparation schedules in SAS Drug Development and Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: sponsor_liaison_name
attributes.description: Full name of the sponsor's designated liaison or medical monitor who serves as the primary point of contact between the sponsor organization and the committee. This individual typically attends open sessions but is excluded from closed sessions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: statistical_charter_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether the committee charter includes a statistical analysis plan (SAP) or statistical charter defining interim analysis rules, stopping boundaries (e.g., O'Brien-Fleming, Lan-DeMets), and alpha-spending functions. Critical for DSMB/DMC oversight of adaptive trials.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; SAP per CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: stopping_rules_defined
attributes.description: Indicates whether the charter defines pre-specified stopping rules for efficacy, futility, or safety that the committee is empowered to invoke. Presence of stopping rules is a key regulatory expectation for DSMB/DMC charters.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees

attributes.name: tmf_section_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the TMF section or zone in Veeva Vault eTMF where committee-related documents (charter, member CVs, meeting minutes, recommendations) are filed. Aligns with the DIA Reference Model for TMF structure.
attributes.references: DIA TMF Reference Model; Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: total_meetings_held
attributes.description: Cumulative count of formal committee meetings held since the committee's establishment. Used for lifecycle tracking, regulatory inspection readiness, and TMF completeness verification.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault eTMF; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006)

attributes.name: unblinded_access
attributes.description: Indicates whether the committee has access to unblinded (treatment-arm-identified) safety and efficacy data during its reviews. Unblinded access is standard for independent DMC/DSMB; internal SRCs may operate on blinded data. Governs data preparation workflows in SAS Drug Development.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this committee record in the lakehouse silver layer. Required for change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

products.name: investigator_brochure_safety
products.description: Master record tracking the safety-relevant sections of the Investigator Brochure (IB) for each investigational product, including the Reference Safety Information (RSI) used to assess expectedness of adverse reactions. Captures IB version, RSI section content, listed adverse reactions, update date, and whether a SUSAR triggered an IB amendment. Drives expectedness determination in Oracle Argus Safety.
products.reference: ICH E2F; ICH E6(R2) Section 7; 21 CFR 312.23(a)(5)

attributes.name: investigator_brochure_safety_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Investigator Brochure safety record in the silver layer. Primary key for this data product. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — represents a versioned document resource (the safety-relevant section of the IB) owned and managed by the sponsor/CRO.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; ICH E2F Development Safety Update Report

attributes.name: clinical_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to program.clinical_program. Business justification: The Investigator Brochure is a program-level regulatory document covering the investigational product across all studies in the development program. IB version management, annual review tracking, and
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: clinical_trial_authorization_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.clinical_trial_authorization. Business justification: IB updates in EU trials are filed as substantial modifications to CTAs. Linking investigator_brochure_safety to clinical_trial_authorization enables EU CTA substantial modification tracking for IB saf
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: ind_application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.ind_application. Business justification: IB updates are filed as IND amendments under specific IND applications per FDA requirements. Linking investigator_brochure_safety to ind_application enables IND amendment tracking for IB updates and s
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: labeling_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.labeling_document. Business justification: The IB safety section constitutes the Reference Safety Information (RSI) used in labeling. Linking investigator_brochure_safety to its corresponding regulatory labeling_document enables RSI alignment
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sponsor.organization. Business justification: The IB is a sponsor-owned document; sponsor identity drives IB version distribution, regulatory notification workflows, and investigator notification tracking. sponsor_name is denormalized from organi
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: prepared_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: IB preparation is a named regulatory document control role under ICH E6(R2) and FDA 21 CFR 312.23 requiring employee traceability for TMF completeness and inspection readiness. prepared_by is a denorm
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: primary_investigator_product_investigational_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational product (drug, biologic, or device) for which this Investigator Brochure safety record applies. Links to the master investigational product entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.23; IND Application

attributes.name: prior_version_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding version of this IB record. Enables version chain traversal for audit, regulatory inspection, and historical RSI reconstruction.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; MasterControl Document Control; 21 CFR Part 11 Audit Trail

attributes.name: study_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agreement.study_contract. Business justification: IB updates triggered by SUSARs are a contracted CRO obligation — the study contract/SOW defines responsibility for IB revision and distribution timelines. This link enables tracking of IB update deliv
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: IB safety updates triggered by SUSARs or signals are filed as regulatory submissions (IND amendments, CTA substantial modifications). Linking IB safety record to its submission enables IB lifecycle ma
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: template_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document_template. Business justification: IB safety sections are authored using standardized document templates that define structure, required content, and formatting per ICH M4 and sponsor standards. Linking to the template ensures version-
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: tmf_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: The Investigator Brochure is a core TMF essential document (DIA TMF Zone 4). The IB safety section record must link to the filed TMF document to support TMF completeness tracking, version control, and
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: amendment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of update that produced this IB version. 'safety_amendment' indicates the update was driven by new safety information (e.g., a SUSAR). 'full_revision' indicates a comprehensive annual or periodic update. Critical for regulatory reporting and TMF classification.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; ICH E2F; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.55; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 54

attributes.name: annual_review_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigator Brochure (IB) Annual Review Due Date
attributes.description: Date by which the next annual review and update of the IB is due, as required by ICH E6(R2). Sponsors must review and update the IB at least annually. Drives compliance calendar in Oracle Siebel CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.55; GCP

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this IB version received final approval from the authorized signatory. Distinct from effective_date (distribution date). Captured from MasterControl electronic approval workflow.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; MasterControl Document Control; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authorized signatory who approved this IB version (typically the Sponsor Medical Officer or Chief Medical Officer). Captured from MasterControl electronic signature records per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; MasterControl Document Control; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Signatures; ALCOA+

attributes.name: argus_rsi_config_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Oracle Argus Safety Reference Safety Information (RSI) Configuration ID
attributes.description: Identifier of the RSI configuration record in Oracle Argus Safety that corresponds to this IB version. Used to synchronize expectedness determination logic in Argus with the approved IB version. Source system cross-reference key.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety RSI Configuration; ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: change_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the key changes made in this IB version compared to the prior version, including new safety information added, adverse reactions added or removed from the RSI, and labeling changes. Required for investigator notification letters.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; ICH E2F; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.55; GCP

attributes.name: compound_code
attributes.description: Internal sponsor compound code or development code for the investigational product (e.g., ABC-123). Used to cross-reference the IB with IND/CTA filings and internal development program records.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; IND Application; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.23

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this IB safety record was first created in the silver layer data product. Represents the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for the MASTER_RESOURCE role. Populated by the ingestion pipeline from Oracle Argus Safety or Veeva Vault source.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ (Attributable Legible Contemporaneous Original Accurate); ICH E6(R2) Section 8

attributes.name: dsmb_review_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) / Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) Review Date
attributes.description: Date on which the DSMB/DMC reviewed the safety content of this IB version. Provides audit trail for DSMB oversight activities.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9

attributes.name: dsmb_reviewed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) / Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) Reviewed Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DSMB/DMC has reviewed the safety information in this IB version. Relevant for ongoing studies where the DSMB/DMC monitors accumulating safety data and may recommend IB updates.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: edition_number
attributes.description: Sequential integer edition number of the IB (e.g., Edition 1, Edition 2). Distinct from version_number in that edition represents a full rewrite, while version may capture minor amendments within an edition.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; ICH E2F Development Safety Update Report

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this IB version became effective and was distributed to investigators and sites. This is the MASTER_RESOURCE EFFECTIVE_FROM date — the date from which the RSI in this version governs expectedness determinations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7.1; ICH E2A Expedited Reporting; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: ib_document_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique document control number assigned to this Investigator Brochure, as registered in Veeva Vault eTMF or MasterControl. Serves as the business identifier for the IB document across systems.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 7; Veeva Vault eTMF; MasterControl Document Control; TMF Reference Model

attributes.name: ib_status

products.name: signal_case_contribution
products.description: This association product represents the Signal Case Contribution event between adverse_event and safety_signal. It captures the formal pharmacovigilance process by which individual adverse event case reports are linked to safety signals as contributing evidence, tracking when each case was included, its statistical weight, and its inclusion status across evaluation cycles. Each record links one adverse_event to one safety_signal with attributes that exist only in the context of this case-to-signal contribution relationship, as governed by ICH E2E and implemented in Oracle Argus Safety.. Existence Justification: In clinical pharmacovigilance, safety signal detection is explicitly an aggregation process where multiple individual adverse event cases (ICSRs) contribute evidence to a single safety signal, and a single adverse event case can contribute to multiple signals (e.g., a hepatotoxicity AE may contribute to both a 'liver injury' signal and a 'drug-induced liver disease' signal). This is a formally recognized operational process governed by ICH E2E and implemented in Oracle Argus Safety, where pharmacovigilance teams actively manage which cases are included in each signal evaluation cycle. The relationship itself carries operationally meaningful data: when the case was included, whether it was flagged as contributing, which detection cycle it belongs to, and its statistical weight — none of which belong on the AE record or the signal record alone.

products.name: dsur_line_listing
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory inclusion of a SUSAR within a specific Development Safety Update Report (DSUR). It captures the ICH E2F-mandated line listing relationship between a periodic safety report and individual SUSAR cases, recording whether each case is new in the reporting period or a cumulative carry-forward, which line listing section it appears in, and how it contributes to the DSUR's aggregate counts. Each record links one DSUR to one SUSAR with attributes that exist only in the context of this regulatory inclusion decision. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety periodic reporting module line listing outputs.. Existence Justification: ICH E2F guidelines mandate that DSURs include explicit line listings of all SUSARs occurring during the reporting period AND cumulative summaries across all periods. A single DSUR covers multiple SUSARs (all cases in the reporting period), and a single SUSAR can appear in multiple DSURs (e.g., initial report in one DSUR, follow-up in the next annual period). This is an operationally managed regulatory artifact — safety teams actively curate which SUSARs are included in each DSUR, whether they are new in the period or carry over cumulatively, and in which line listing section they appear.
