attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study under which this laboratory query was raised. Links the query to the parent protocol and sponsor context.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IG; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: study_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site associated with the subject whose laboratory result triggered this query. Used for site-level query metrics and monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: subject_visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the scheduled or unscheduled study visit during which the specimen was collected and the lab result was generated, providing temporal context for the query.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM TV/SE domains; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: tertiary_lab_responded_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who submitted the query response on behalf of the site or laboratory. Supports ALCOA+ attributability and electronic signature audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Signatures; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Reference to the trial subject (patient) whose laboratory result is the subject of this query. Supports subject-level data quality tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM DM domain; HIPAA; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: assigned_to_party_type
attributes.description: Type of organizational party to whom the query is assigned for response — investigational site, central laboratory, local laboratory, sponsor, or CRO (Contract Research Organization). Determines routing and accountability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave EDC; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of why the query was cancelled, if applicable (e.g., query raised in error, duplicate query, data issue resolved through another mechanism). Required for cancelled queries to maintain ALCOA+ audit trail integrity.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: corrected_value
attributes.description: The laboratory result value after correction, if a data change was made as a result of this query. Null if no correction was applied. Provides after-state for audit trail per ALCOA+ and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this lab_query record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer. Audit trail field for data lineage and ALCOA+ compliance. Distinct from raised_datetime which captures the business event time.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: data_correction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the resolution of this query resulted in a data value change in the source EDC or LIMS record. True = a data correction was made; False = original data confirmed or query cancelled without change. Key metric for data quality reporting.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: dbl_blocking_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this open query is blocking the Database Lock (DBL) for the study or subject. True = must be resolved before DBL can proceed; False = non-blocking. Critical for study close-out planning and timeline management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC CDASH; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; DBL SOP

attributes.name: ecrf_field_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) Field Name
attributes.description: Specific field name within the eCRF form that contains the queried laboratory data value (e.g., 'LBORRES', 'LBORRESU'). Enables precise identification of the data point in question for site response and EDC correction.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC; CDISC CDASH; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18

attributes.name: ecrf_form_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) Form Name
attributes.description: Name of the eCRF form in the EDC (Medidata Rave) on which the queried laboratory data field resides (e.g., 'Laboratory Results', 'Hematology'). Supports EDC navigation and query routing to the correct data entry form.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC; CDISC CDASH; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18

attributes.name: edc_query_code
attributes.description: Native query identifier assigned by the source EDC system (Medidata Rave) or LIMS. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer record and the operational system of record for reconciliation and audit.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC Query Management; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18.4

attributes.name: escalation_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the query was formally escalated. Null if no escalation has occurred. Used for escalation cycle time analytics and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this query has been formally escalated to a higher authority (e.g., from CRA to Clinical Lead, or from site to sponsor medical monitor) due to non-response, SLA breach, or data criticality. Triggers escalation workflow in CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Sponsor-CRO escalation SOPs

attributes.name: original_value
attributes.description: The laboratory result value as it existed at the time the query was raised, captured as a string to accommodate numeric, text, and coded values. Provides before-state for audit trail and data lineage per ALCOA+ requirements.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: query_category
attributes.description: Functional category indicating which business process or team initiated the query — data management programmatic check, medical monitor review, safety review, statistical review, or site-initiated clarification. Supports workload analytics and process improvement.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC CDASH; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: query_iteration_count
attributes.description: Number of times this query has been re-opened or re-issued against the same laboratory result field, indicating the number of response-review cycles. A high iteration count signals persistent data quality issues at the site or lab.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; Medidata Rave EDC Query Management

attributes.name: query_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally visible query identifier assigned by the EDC (Medidata Rave) or LIMS system at the time of query creation. Used for cross-system tracking and communication with sites and labs (e.g., QRY-2024-00123).
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC Query Management; CDISC CDASH; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18

attributes.name: query_priority
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to the query indicating urgency of resolution. Critical queries (e.g., those linked to SAE data or DBL-blocking issues) require immediate attention. Drives escalation and SLA enforcement.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC CDASH; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: query_source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record in which this query originated — EDC (Medidata Rave), a Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), Oracle Clinical One, or a manually entered query. Supports multi-system data quality governance.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: query_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the laboratory data query. Drives workflow routing, SLA monitoring, and DBL readiness assessment. Open = awaiting response; Answered = response received, pending DM review; Closed = resolved and accepted; Cancelled = withdrawn.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC Query Lifecycle; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: query_text
attributes.description: Full narrative text of the query as raised by the data manager or medical monitor, describing the data issue, the specific concern, and the action requested from the site or laboratory. Core ALCOA+ documentation field.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: query_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reason the query was raised against the laboratory result. Drives triage, routing, and resolution workflows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missing_value|implausible_result|unit_mismatch|collection_time_deviation|reference_range_deviation|transcription_error|duplicate_entry|method_deviation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC CDASH; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: raised_by_role
attributes.description: Functional role of the person or process that raised the query (e.g., Data Manager, Medical Monitor, Clinical Research Associate (CRA), Statistician, or automated system check). Denormalized for reporting without requiring a user-role join.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC CDASH; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: raised_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone) when the query was formally raised and entered into the EDC or LIMS. Principal business event timestamp for the query lifecycle. Required for SLA calculation and ALCOA+ contemporaneity compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC CDASH

attributes.name: resolution_action
attributes.description: Outcome action taken to resolve the query: data value was corrected in the EDC/LIMS, original data was confirmed as correct, query was withdrawn by the raiser, or no action was required. Critical for data audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: resolution_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone) when the query was formally closed or cancelled by the data manager after reviewing the site/lab response. Marks the end of the query lifecycle. Used for cycle time analytics and DBL readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: response_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone) when the site or laboratory submitted their response to the query. Used for SLA compliance measurement and ALCOA+ contemporaneity tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC CDASH

attributes.name: response_text
attributes.description: Full narrative response provided by the site or laboratory in reply to the query, explaining the data discrepancy, confirming the value, or documenting a correction. Core ALCOA+ documentation field for audit trail.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018

attributes.name: safety_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the queried laboratory result is associated with a safety event (SAE, AE, or SUSAR) or a critical value, requiring expedited resolution. True = safety-relevant; False = routine data quality query. Drives prioritization and safety reporting workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CTCAE

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the query response or resolution exceeded the defined SLA target days. True = SLA was breached; False = responded within SLA. Drives escalation workflows and site performance KPI reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Sponsor-CRO Agreement SLA terms

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this lab_query record was last modified in the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports incremental data processing, change detection, and audit trail requirements per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GLP|GCP_LAB_QUALIFICATION|CAP_PROFICIENCY|CLIA_SPECIALTY|EQA_SCHEME|ISO_15189|OTHER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP Accreditation; FDA 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; OECD GLP Principles

attributes.name: eqa_participation_cycle
attributes.description: Identifier for the specific EQA participation cycle or survey period (e.g., '2024-Q1', '2024-CYCLE-2'). Applicable when certification_type = EQA_SCHEME. Supports tracking of periodic proficiency testing compliance.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP Proficiency Testing; ISO 15189

attributes.name: eqa_scheme_name
attributes.description: Name of the External Quality Assurance scheme in which the laboratory participates under this certification (e.g., UKNEQAS, RIQAS, EQAS, CAP PT). Applicable only when certification_type = EQA_SCHEME.
attributes.references: ISO 15189; WHO Laboratory Quality Standards; CAP Proficiency Testing; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the certification expires and is no longer valid unless renewed. Null for certifications with indefinite validity. Critical for renewal workflow triggering and regulatory compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; CAP Accreditation

attributes.name: glp_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this certification specifically confers or requires Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) compliance as defined by FDA 21 CFR Part 58 or OECD GLP Principles. True = GLP-compliant certification; False = non-GLP certification.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: is_primary_certification
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the primary or principal certification for the laboratory's participation in clinical trials. True = primary certification; False = supplementary or specialty certification. Supports lab qualification assessments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: Date on which the certification was formally issued or granted by the issuing authority. Represents the effective start date of the certification's validity period.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189

attributes.name: issuing_authority
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory body, accreditation organization, or competent authority that issued the certification (e.g., CMS/CLIA, College of American Pathologists, FDA, EMA, MHRA, COFRAC, DAKKS, UKAS, INAB).
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; EMA GLP Compliance; OECD GLP Principles; ISO 15189

attributes.name: issuing_authority_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction under which the certification was issued (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU, JPN, AUS). Supports multi-jurisdictional regulatory compliance tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; EMA GLP; PMDA; TGA; Health Canada

attributes.name: lab_director_name
attributes.description: Full name of the laboratory director or responsible person named on the certification at the time of issuance. Required for regulatory submissions and GCP/GLP compliance documentation.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493.1441; FDA 21 CFR Part 58.29; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: mutual_recognition_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this certification is recognized under a mutual recognition agreement between regulatory authorities (e.g., FDA-EMA, OECD GLP MAD). True = recognized under MRA; False = jurisdiction-specific only. Relevant for multi-regional clinical trials.
attributes.references: OECD GLP Mutual Acceptance of Data (MAD); FDA-EMA Mutual Recognition Agreement; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: notification_lead_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days before the expiry date at which automated renewal notifications should be triggered. Configurable per certification type and issuing authority requirements (e.g., 90 days for CLIA, 180 days for GLP).
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2); MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: previous_certificate_number
attributes.description: Certificate number of the immediately preceding certification record that this record renews or supersedes. Enables chain-of-custody traceability across certification renewal cycles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: proficiency_test_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the most recent proficiency testing or EQA survey associated with this certification. SATISFACTORY = passed; UNSATISFACTORY = failed one or more analytes; UNSUCCESSFUL = failed to meet minimum passing threshold; PENDING = results not yet received; NOT_APPLICABLE = no proficiency testing required for this certification type.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 Subpart H; CAP Proficiency Testing; ISO 15189

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this certification record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this certification record in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data currency monitoring per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or dossier identifier for any regulatory submission (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, CTD/eCTD) in which this laboratory certification was included as supporting documentation.
attributes.references: FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; FDA NDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA MAA; ICH CTD; eCTD

attributes.name: reinstatement_date
attributes.description: Date on which a previously suspended certification was reinstated by the issuing authority following successful corrective action. Null if the certification has never been suspended or has not yet been reinstated.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: renewal_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the renewal application must be submitted to the issuing authority to maintain uninterrupted certification status. Typically calculated as a fixed lead time before the expiry date per issuing authority requirements.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; CAP Accreditation; ISO 15189

attributes.name: renewal_status
attributes.description: Current status of the certification renewal process. Tracks the renewal workflow from initiation through approval or rejection. NOT_REQUIRED applies to certifications that do not have a periodic renewal cycle.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2); MasterControl CAPA/Document Control

attributes.name: renewal_submitted_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the renewal application was submitted to the issuing authority. Used to confirm timely submission and support audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: signatory_name
attributes.description: Name of the authorized signatory from the issuing authority who signed or approved the certificate. Supports audit trail and certificate authenticity verification.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this certification record was sourced or ingested (e.g., MasterControl document control, Veeva Vault eTMF, Oracle Siebel CTMS, or manually entered). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the originating operational system (MasterControl, Veeva Vault, CTMS). Enables traceability back to the source system for reconciliation and audit purposes per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: specialty_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the laboratory specialty or discipline covered by this certification, aligned with CLIA specialty categories or equivalent regulatory classification (e.g., HEMATOLOGY, CHEMISTRY, MICROBIOLOGY, IMMUNOLOGY, TOXICOLOGY, MOLECULAR_PATHOLOGY).
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 Subpart C; CAP Accreditation Checklists; ISO 15189

attributes.name: suspension_date
attributes.description: Date on which the certification was suspended, revoked, or withdrawn. Populated only when certification_status is SUSPENDED, REVOKED, or WITHDRAWN. Supports regulatory compliance and audit trail.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: suspension_reason
attributes.description: Reason provided by the issuing authority or the laboratory for suspension, revocation, or withdrawal of the certification. Populated only when certification_status is SUSPENDED, REVOKED, or WITHDRAWN.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2)

products.name: lab_analyte
products.description: Reference master for individual laboratory analytes (measurable substances or properties) used across all lab panels and assays. Captures analyte name, LOINC code, MedDRA PT mapping, CDISC LBTESTCD/LBTEST standardized code and label, default unit of measure, specimen type compatibility, analyte category (hematology/chemistry/coagulation/urinalysis/immunology/PK/biomarker), and SDTM domain assignment. Serves as the controlled vocabulary for analyte standardization across the enterprise.
products.reference: CDISC SDTM LB LBTESTCD; LOINC; MedDRA

attributes.name: lab_analyte_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for a laboratory analyte record in the enterprise reference master. Primary key for the lab_analyte entity. [_canonical_skip_reason: Role classified as MASTER_RESOURCE — a controlled vocabulary reference entity representing a measurable substance or property used across lab panels and assays.]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: meddra_term_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.meddra_term. Business justification: Lab analytes are mapped to MedDRA preferred terms for AE coding when lab abnormalities are reported as adverse events. This mapping is standard in CDISC SDTM LB domain and is required for MedDRA-coded
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: adam_param_code
attributes.description: CDISC ADaM PARAMCD value for this analyte used in analysis datasets (BDS — Basic Data Structure). Maximum 8 uppercase alphanumeric characters per CDISC ADaM controlled terminology. Used in SAS Drug Development to build ADLB, ADPC, and other analysis datasets for statistical analysis and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; CDISC ADaM BDS Structure; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

attributes.name: adam_param_label
attributes.description: CDISC ADaM PARAM value — the full descriptive label for this analyte in analysis datasets. Corresponds to the PARAM variable in ADLB and ADPC datasets. Used in SAS Drug Development outputs, TLFs (Tables, Listings, and Figures), and the Clinical Study Report (CSR).
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; CDISC ADaM BDS Structure; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: analyte_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the analyte by laboratory discipline or scientific domain. Corresponds to CDISC LBCAT variable. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HEMATOLOGY|CHEMISTRY|COAGULATION|URINALYSIS|IMMUNOLOGY|PHARMACOKINETICS|BIOMARKER|MICROBIOLOGY|SEROLOGY|ENDOCRINOLOGY|TOXICOLOGY|GENOMICS — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LB Domain LBCAT; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: analyte_code
attributes.description: Internal enterprise-assigned short code uniquely identifying the analyte within the controlled vocabulary. Used as the primary business key for cross-system referencing and data integration. Follows CDISC LBTESTCD conventions (max 8 uppercase alphanumeric characters).
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LB Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: analyte_name
attributes.description: Full human-readable name of the laboratory analyte (e.g., 'Hemoglobin', 'Alanine Aminotransferase', 'Creatinine'). Serves as the display label in reports, eCRFs, and regulatory submissions. Corresponds to CDISC LBTEST label.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LB Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: analyte_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the analyte in the enterprise reference master. ACTIVE: approved for use in studies; INACTIVE: no longer used in new studies; DEPRECATED: superseded by another analyte code; PENDING_VALIDATION: under review for addition; RESTRICTED: use requires special authorization (e.g., exploratory biomarkers).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC Controlled Terminology Governance; FDA Data Standards Catalog; MasterControl Document Control SOP

attributes.name: analyte_subcategory
attributes.description: More granular classification within the analyte category. Corresponds to CDISC LBSCAT variable (e.g., 'LIVER FUNCTION', 'RENAL FUNCTION', 'LIPID PANEL', 'COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT' within CHEMISTRY or HEMATOLOGY). Used for panel grouping, report organization, and SDTM dataset population.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LB Domain LBSCAT; CDISC Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: analyte_type
attributes.description: Classification of the analyte result type: QUANTITATIVE (numeric value with unit), QUALITATIVE (categorical result such as Positive/Negative), SEMI_QUANTITATIVE (e.g., 1+/2+/3+), or ORDINAL (ranked scale). Determines result entry validation rules in Medidata Rave eCRF and SDTM LBORRES handling logic.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LB Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: analyte_version
attributes.description: Version number of the analyte definition record (e.g., '1.0', '2.3'). Incremented when material changes are made to the analyte specification (unit, LOINC code, CDISC mapping, reference ranges). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles; CDISC Controlled Terminology Governance

attributes.name: assay_method
attributes.description: The analytical method or technology platform used to measure this analyte (e.g., 'ELISA', 'LC-MS/MS', 'Flow Cytometry', 'Immunoturbidimetry', 'Colorimetric', 'PCR', 'Electrochemiluminescence'). Documented for bioanalytical method validation traceability and regulatory submission in the CSR and eCTD.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guideline (2011); ICH M10; ISO 15189:2022

attributes.name: biomarker_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this analyte is classified as a biomarker (safety, efficacy, predictive, prognostic, or pharmacodynamic). Biomarker analytes require additional regulatory documentation per FDA Biomarker Qualification Program and EMA qualification opinions, and may trigger special handling in the TMF and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: FDA Biomarker Qualification Program; EMA Qualification of Novel Methodologies; ICH E16; BEST (Biomarkers, EndpointS, and other Tools) Resource

attributes.name: biomarker_type
attributes.description: When biomarker_flag is true, classifies the biomarker by its regulatory and scientific role per FDA BEST framework: SAFETY (organ toxicity monitoring), EFFICACY (treatment response), PREDICTIVE (patient selection), PROGNOSTIC (disease outcome), PHARMACODYNAMIC (drug effect), SUSCEPTIBILITY, RESPONSE, or DIAGNOSTIC. Drives regulatory submission strategy and SAP content. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SAFETY|EFFICACY|PREDICTIVE|PROGNOSTIC|PHARMACODYNAMIC|SUSCEPTIBILITY|RESPONSE|DIAGNOSTIC — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA BEST (Biomarkers, EndpointS, and other Tools) Resource; EMA Reflection Paper on Biomarkers; ICH E16; FDA Biomarker Qualification Program

attributes.name: collection_tube_type
attributes.description: Required blood collection tube type or container for this analyte (e.g., 'EDTA', 'SST', 'LITHIUM HEPARIN', 'CITRATE', 'FLUORIDE OXALATE'). Drives specimen collection kit configuration in RTSM and lab manuals. Critical for pre-analytical quality and result validity per ISO 15189 and CLSI guidelines.
attributes.references: ISO 15189:2022 Medical Laboratories; CLSI GP41-A6; CAP Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this analyte record was first created in the enterprise reference master. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+ data integrity principles, and GDPR data governance. Populated automatically by the system at record creation.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: critical_value_lower
attributes.description: The lower critical (panic) value threshold for this analyte below which an immediate clinical notification is required per laboratory protocol. Results below this threshold trigger critical_value_flag in lab_result and require expedited reporting to the investigator per GCP and CTCAE grading requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.17; CTCAE v5.0; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ISO 15189:2022

attributes.name: critical_value_upper
attributes.description: The upper critical (panic) value threshold for this analyte above which an immediate clinical notification is required per laboratory protocol. Results above this threshold trigger critical_value_flag in lab_result and require expedited reporting to the investigator per GCP and CTCAE grading requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.17; CTCAE v5.0; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ISO 15189:2022

attributes.name: ctcae_grade_mapping
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade Mapping Rule
attributes.description: Describes the CTCAE grading rule or reference for this analyte (e.g., 'CTCAE v5.0 — Anemia: Grade 1 <LLN–10.0 g/dL; Grade 2 8.0–<10.0 g/dL; Grade 3 <8.0 g/dL'). Used by the safety data management team to auto-assign CTCAE grades to lab results in Medidata Rave and Oracle Argus Safety for AE/SAE reporting.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Safety Reporting Requirements 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: ctcae_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Version
attributes.description: Version of the NCI CTCAE grading criteria applied to this analyte for adverse event severity grading (e.g., 'CTCAE v5.0'). Ensures consistency between lab result grading and safety reporting across the study lifecycle.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2); FDA Safety Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: default_unit
attributes.description: The standard unit of measure in which this analyte result is reported by default (e.g., 'g/dL', 'mmol/L', 'U/L', 'ng/mL', '%'). Aligns with CDISC LBORRESU (original unit) and LBSTRESU (standard unit) conventions. Used to pre-populate EDC fields in Medidata Rave and validate incoming lab data.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LBORRESU/LBSTRESU; UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure); ISO 11240

attributes.name: detection_limit_lower
attributes.description: The lowest concentration or value that can be reliably detected by the analytical method for this analyte (Lower Limit of Detection, LLOD). Values below this threshold are reported as '<LLOD'. Critical for PK/DMPK bioanalytical assay validation and SDTM LBSTRESC handling of below-detection results per FDA and EMA bioanalytical guidance.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guideline (2011); ICH M10; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: detection_limit_upper
attributes.description: The highest concentration or value that can be reliably quantified by the analytical method for this analyte (Upper Limit of Quantitation, ULOQ). Values above this threshold require dilution or are reported as '>ULOQ'. Essential for PK/DMPK bioanalytical assay validation and concentration-time profile analysis.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guideline (2011); ICH M10

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this analyte definition was retired or superseded. Null indicates the analyte is currently active. Used to enforce temporal validity checks when mapping historical study data and to prevent use of deprecated analytes in new study builds.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC Controlled Terminology Governance; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this analyte definition became effective and approved for use in clinical trial data collection. Supports temporal versioning of the controlled vocabulary and ensures studies use the correct analyte definition at the time of data collection.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC Controlled Terminology Governance; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records

attributes.name: lbtest
attributes.description: CDISC SDTM standardized long name for the laboratory test (LBTEST variable). The decode value corresponding to LBTESTCD. Used in SDTM LB domain submissions and must match CDISC Controlled Terminology. Enables regulatory reviewers to interpret analyte identity without code lookup.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LB Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology NCI Thesaurus

attributes.name: lbtestcd
attributes.description: CDISC SDTM standardized short name for the laboratory test (LBTESTCD variable). Maximum 8 uppercase alphanumeric characters per CDISC controlled terminology. Used for SDTM dataset submission to FDA, EMA, and PMDA. Must align with CDISC Controlled Terminology for the LB domain.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LB Domain; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

attributes.name: loinc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC) Code
attributes.description: Internationally recognized LOINC code identifying the specific laboratory observation. Enables interoperability with external laboratory information systems (LIMS), electronic health records, and health data exchanges. Required for HL7 FHIR-based data exchange and increasingly expected by FDA and EMA for lab data standardization.
attributes.references: Regenstrief Institute LOINC Standard; HL7 FHIR R4; FDA Data Standards Catalog; CDISC SDTM Supplemental Qualifiers

attributes.name: max_freeze_thaw_cycles
attributes.description: Maximum number of freeze-thaw cycles permitted for specimens used to measure this analyte before result validity is compromised. Enforced during specimen chain-of-custody tracking to flag specimens that have exceeded the allowable cycle count, particularly critical for PK/DMPK and biomarker analytes.
attributes.references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guideline (2011); ICH M10; ISO 15189:2022

attributes.name: minimum_volume_ml
attributes.description: Minimum volume of specimen in milliliters required to perform the assay for this analyte. Used to validate specimen adequacy upon receipt at the central laboratory and to configure collection volume requirements in the lab manual and RTSM kit specifications.
attributes.references: ISO 15189:2022 Medical Laboratories; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLSI GP41-A6 Venipuncture

attributes.name: pk_pd_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this analyte is used in pharmacokinetic (PK) or pharmacodynamic (PD) analyses. When true, the analyte is subject to DMPK bioanalytical method validation requirements and results are processed through the PC/PP SDTM domains and NCA/population PK workflows in SAS Drug Development.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — PC/PP Domains; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guideline (2011); ICH M10

attributes.name: preferred_volume_ml
attributes.description: Optimal/preferred volume of specimen in milliliters for reliable analyte measurement, accounting for repeat testing and QC requirements. Drives collection kit tube size selection and subject blood volume burden calculations in protocol feasibility assessments.
attributes.references: ISO 15189:2022 Medical Laboratories; CLSI GP41-A6; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Study Protocol Design Standards

attributes.name: reporting_precision
attributes.description: Number of decimal places to which results for this analyte should be reported and stored. Ensures consistent numeric precision across EDC data entry in Medidata Rave, SDTM dataset generation, and statistical analysis outputs in SAS Drug Development. Prevents spurious precision in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: requires_fasting
attributes.description: Indicates whether specimen collection for this analyte requires the subject to be in a fasting state. When true, the eCRF in Medidata Rave will prompt collection of fasting status (LBFAST in SDTM) and the collection instructions in the lab manual will specify fasting duration requirements.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LBFAST; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Study Protocol Design Standards

attributes.name: sdtm_domain
attributes.business_glossary_term: Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) Domain Assignment
attributes.description: CDISC SDTM domain to which this analyte is assigned for regulatory submission datasets. LB=Laboratory Test Results, PC=Pharmacokinetics Concentrations, PP=Pharmacokinetics Parameters, FA=Findings About, MB=Microbiology Specimen, MS=Microbiology Susceptibility. Drives SDTM dataset generation in SAS Drug Development.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: specimen_type
attributes.description: Primary specimen type required or accepted for this analyte (e.g., 'BLOOD', 'SERUM', 'PLASMA', 'URINE', 'CSF', 'TISSUE'). Corresponds to CDISC LBSPEC variable. Used to validate specimen collection against analyte requirements and drive collection kit selection in RTSM/IRT systems. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BLOOD|SERUM|PLASMA|URINE|CSF|TISSUE|SALIVA|STOOL|BONE MARROW|SYNOVIAL FLUID|BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LBSPEC; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ISO 15189

attributes.name: stability_hours_ambient
attributes.description: Maximum number of hours the collected specimen remains stable for this analyte at ambient (room) temperature before processing or refrigeration is required. Critical for pre-analytical quality management, shipment planning, and chain-of-custody compliance per ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation standards.
attributes.references: ISO 15189:2022 Medical Laboratories; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLSI EP25-A Specimen Stability

attributes.name: stability_hours_frozen
attributes.description: Maximum number of hours (or equivalent duration) the collected specimen remains stable for this analyte when stored frozen (typically -20°C or -80°C). Governs long-term biobanking, re-analysis eligibility, and sample expiry management in the specimen repository.
attributes.references: ISO 15189:2022 Medical Laboratories; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLSI EP25-A Specimen Stability; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

attributes.name: stability_hours_refrigerated
attributes.description: Maximum number of hours the collected specimen remains stable for this analyte when stored refrigerated (2–8°C). Used to define specimen handling windows in the lab manual, RTSM kit instructions, and central lab processing SOPs.
attributes.references: ISO 15189:2022 Medical Laboratories; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLSI EP25-A Specimen Stability

attributes.name: standard_unit
attributes.description: The SI (International System of Units) or CDISC-standardized unit to which all results for this analyte are converted for cross-study analysis and regulatory submission. Corresponds to CDISC LBSTRESU. Enables unit-harmonized pooled analyses and ADaM dataset derivations in SAS Drug Development.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4 — LBSTRESU; UCUM; ISO 80000-1; ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles

attributes.name: unit_conversion_factor
attributes.description: Numeric multiplier applied to convert a result from the default_unit to the standard_unit (e.g., 0.0555 to convert glucose from mg/dL to mmol/L). Used by the data transformation layer in SAS Drug Development and Medidata Rave to auto-standardize incoming lab values for SDTM and ADaM datasets.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; UCUM; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this analyte record was most recently modified. Used for change detection in downstream ETL pipelines, audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles

attributes.name: who_dd_code
attributes.description: WHO Drug Dictionary code associated with this analyte when the analyte represents a drug concentration measurement (e.g., for PK analytes measuring parent drug or metabolite levels). Enables linkage between PK analyte results and the study drug coding in safety and efficacy analyses.
attributes.references: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM PC Domain; FDA Pharmacokinetics Guidance

products.name: lab_qualification
products.description: This association product represents the formal qualification and engagement contract between a lab_facility and a clinical_program. It captures the sponsor-approved, program-specific qualification of a laboratory facility to perform defined specimen analyses for a clinical development program. Each record links one lab_facility to one clinical_program and carries attributes — qualification status, approval dates, scope of services, and contract reference — that exist only in the context of this program-facility relationship and cannot reside on either master entity alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials operations, a clinical program selects and qualifies multiple laboratory facilities (central lab, PK lab, biomarker lab, etc.) to support its studies, and each lab facility simultaneously serves multiple clinical programs across different sponsors and therapeutic areas. This is an actively managed vendor oversight relationship — sponsors and CROs formally qualify labs per program, track approval status, define scope of services, and maintain contract references for each program-facility pairing. The relationship is a recognized operational business concept in clinical procurement and vendor management.

products.name: panel_composition
products.description: This association product represents the formal composition contract between a lab_panel and its constituent lab_analytes. It captures the version-controlled membership of each analyte within a panel as actively managed by lab directors and protocol teams. Each record links one lab_panel to one lab_analyte and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this panel-analyte relationship: the analyte's position in the panel, its required/optional status, its specimen volume contribution, its reporting inclusion, and the effective date range of its membership. This is the authoritative source for panel composition used in LIMS configuration, SDTM LB domain mapping, and protocol amendment tracking.. Existence Justification: In clinical laboratory operations, a test panel is formally defined as a named collection of specific analytes — a CBC panel contains hemoglobin, hematocrit, WBC, platelets, etc., while a CMP panel contains glucose, BUN, creatinine, electrolytes, etc. This composition is actively managed by lab directors and protocol teams, is version-controlled per protocol amendment, and is a recognized concept in LIMS systems and CDISC SDTM LB domain modeling. One panel contains many analytes, and one analyte (e.g., Sodium) appears in many panels (CMP, BMP, Electrolyte Panel) — this is a genuine operational M:N with full reciprocity. The relationship carries its own data: sequence order within the panel, whether the analyte is required vs. optional, minimum volume contribution, reporting flags, and effective dates for version control.

products.name: sow_lab_panel_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the Contract between scope_of_work and lab_panel in clinical research operations. It captures the formal contractual inclusion of a specific laboratory test panel within a Scope of Work, recording the negotiated terms (unit price, turnaround commitment, visit applicability) that govern how the CRO will deliver that panel for the study. Each record links one scope_of_work to one lab_panel with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual relationship — they are neither properties of the panel catalog nor of the SOW document alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical research operations, a Scope of Work (SOW) contractually specifies which laboratory panels the CRO will perform for a given study, and a single lab panel (e.g., a CBC safety panel or PK panel) can appear across many different SOWs for different studies or sponsors. The business actively manages this relationship as a 'contracted lab panel requirement' — negotiating unit pricing, turnaround commitments, and visit applicability per panel per SOW. This is not derivable from transactional data; it is a contractual record created during SOW authoring and updated during amendments.

products.name: lab_service_contract
products.description: This association product represents the Contract between lab_facility and study_budget. It captures the facility-specific financial and operational terms under which a laboratory facility is engaged to perform specimen analysis services for a specific study budget. Each record links one lab_facility to one study_budget with attributes — contracted rate, service scope, effective dates, and amendment tracking — that exist only in the context of this study-facility contractual relationship. Serves as the operational record for lab vendor cost management, sponsor invoicing reconciliation, and budget variance analysis at the facility level.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials operations, a lab facility (e.g., a central lab or bioanalytical lab) is contracted to serve multiple studies — each with its own budget, contracted rates, service scope, and amendment history. Conversely, a single study budget allocates funds across multiple lab facilities (central lab, local labs, PK lab), each under distinct contractual terms. This relationship is actively managed by finance and lab operations teams as a 'Lab Service Contract' or 'Lab Budget Allocation', carrying facility-specific contracted rates, service scope, effective dates, and amendment numbers that belong to neither the facility master record nor the budget master record alone.

attributes.name: min_storage_temp_c
attributes.description: Minimum permissible storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the IMP. Used to define temperature excursion thresholds, configure temperature monitoring devices, and assess cold-chain compliance at depots and sites.

attributes.name: packaging_configuration

attributes.name: product_code
attributes.description: Sponsor-assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the IMP within the sponsor's product catalogue. Used as the externally-known business identifier across RTSM, EDC, and regulatory submissions. Maps to the product code field in Medidata Rave RTSM.

attributes.name: product_name

attributes.name: product_status

attributes.name: product_type

attributes.name: regulatory_classification

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|IMPD|CTA|NDA|BLA|MAA|exempt — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: retest_period_months

attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability Guidelines; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; EMA IMPD Guideline

attributes.name: route_of_administration

attributes.name: rtsm_product_code

attributes.name: shelf_life_months

attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability Guidelines; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; EMA IMPD Guideline

attributes.name: sourcing_strategy
attributes.description: Indicates how the IMP is obtained for the clinical trial: manufactured (custom GMP production), commercially procured (purchased from market), over-the-counter, or imported. Drives procurement workflows, GMP documentation requirements, and supply chain planning.
attributes.references: EMA IMPD Guideline; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ICH Q7

attributes.name: sponsor_product_code
attributes.description: The sponsor's internal product code or compound number for the IMP (e.g., development compound identifier such as 'ABC-123'). Distinct from the CRO's product_code; used for sponsor-facing reporting, cross-study portfolio analytics, and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA IMPD Guideline

attributes.name: storage_condition
attributes.description: Required storage conditions for the IMP as specified in the product dossier and labelling (e.g., 'Store at 2–8°C', 'Store below 25°C, protect from light'). Drives cold-chain logistics, depot and site storage compliance, and temperature excursion management.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability Guidelines; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; EMA IMPD Guideline

attributes.name: strength_unit

attributes.name: strength_value
attributes.description: Numeric quantity of the active substance per dosage unit (e.g., 10, 500, 1.5). Must be interpreted in conjunction with strength_unit. Serves as the template from which physical kits are manufactured and assigned. Distinct from kit_inventory which tracks physical instances.
