attributes.description: Reason provided by the regulatory authority for revoking a previously approved import permit. Populated when permit_status is 'revoked'. Triggers regulatory notification and supply chain hold.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: storage_condition
attributes.description: Required storage condition for the IMP as specified on the import permit and in the IMP dossier. Drives cold-chain logistics requirements during import and customs clearance. Must align with kit_definition storage conditions.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; EU CTR 536/2014; 21 CFR Part 312; GDP guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the import permit record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: utilized_quantity
attributes.description: Cumulative quantity of IMP actually imported against this permit to date. Used to track permit utilization, remaining authorized quantity, and accountability reconciliation. Expressed in the same unit as permitted_quantity_unit.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ICH Q10; ALCOA+

attributes.name: utilized_shipment_count
attributes.description: Number of shipments that have been made against this permit to date. Used to track permit utilization and determine remaining shipment capacity for multi_shipment permits.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ICH Q10; ALCOA+

attributes.name: valid_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which the import permit is legally effective and shipments may be made under its authority. Typically coincides with or follows the approval date.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; 21 CFR Part 312; ICH Q10

attributes.name: valid_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which the import permit expires and is no longer valid for authorizing IMP shipments. Critical for preventing shipment delays due to expired permits. Null for open-ended permits.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; 21 CFR Part 312; ICH Q10

products.name: comparator_drug
products.description: Master record for comparator drugs and placebo products used in controlled clinical trials. Captures comparator drug name, manufacturer, regulatory approval status in applicable countries, sourcing strategy (commercial purchase vs. sponsor-supplied), storage requirements, and blinding configuration. Distinct from IMP master as comparators are commercially sourced and subject to different procurement and regulatory rules.
products.reference: Comparator Drug / Active Control

attributes.name: comparator_drug_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the comparator drug or placebo master record in the clinical supply system.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: clinical_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to program.clinical_program. Business justification: Comparator drugs are procured and governed at the program level. IMPD comparator sections and program-level supply agreements require linking comparator drug records to the clinical program. Supply ex
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: imp_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.imp_master. Business justification: comparator_drug is a specialization of imp_master — imp_master explicitly covers comparator products. Linking comparator_drug to its corresponding imp_master record establishes the product hierarchy a
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.purchase_order. Business justification: Comparator drugs are commercially sourced via purchase orders — a significant and separately tracked cost line in clinical trial budgets. Finance tracks comparator procurement costs per PO for budget
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: qualified_person_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Comparator drugs used in clinical trials require QP certification under EU GMP Annex 13. Linking to employee enables QP qualification verification and GMP compliance reporting for comparator IMP. qual
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.approval. Business justification: Comparator drugs are approved marketed products — supply teams must verify the regulatory approval status and conditions before procurement and use in trials. `marketing_authorisation_number` is a den
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: study_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agreement.study_contract. Business justification: Comparator drug sourcing, over-labelling obligations, and supply terms are governed by the study contract. Comparator supply contract management is a distinct clinical supply process; regulatory inspe
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to program.therapeutic_area. Business justification: comparator_drug carries a plain-text 'therapeutic_area' column that is a denormalized reference to the therapeutic_area reference entity. Normalizing this FK ensures consistent therapeutic area classi
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: tmf_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Comparator drug sourcing documentation, marketing authorization certificates, and GMP certificates are ICH GCP essential TMF documents. Each comparator drug record must link to its regulatory document
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: approved_countries
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes where the comparator drug holds a valid marketing authorisation or regulatory approval. Used to validate site-level dispensing eligibility and import compliance.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; FDA 21 CFR 314; ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: atc_code
attributes.description: WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for the comparator drug active substance. Used for therapeutic area alignment, WHO-DD coding, and pharmacovigilance signal detection.
attributes.references: WHO ATC/DDD Index; WHO-DD; CDISC SDTM CM Domain

attributes.name: blinding_type
attributes.description: Blinding configuration applied to the comparator drug in the trial context: open_label (no blinding), single_blind (subject blinded), double_blind (subject and investigator blinded), triple_blind (subject, investigator, and sponsor blinded). Drives kit labelling and RTSM configuration.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Blinding; CDISC SDTM TA Domain

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this comparator drug master record was first created in the system. RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Supports ALCOA+ data integrity requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: destruction_method
attributes.description: Approved method for destruction of unused or returned comparator drug stock. Used in drug accountability reconciliation and environmental compliance documentation.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 312.59; ICH Q3C; GDPR (for destruction records)

attributes.name: discontinuation_date
attributes.description: Date on which this comparator drug master record was discontinued or retired from active clinical supply use. Null if the record is still active. Used for lifecycle management and historical reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 312

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Pharmaceutical dosage form of the comparator drug (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, oral solution, patch). MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE proxy for MASTER_RESOURCE role — the principal physical characteristic of the drug product. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|injection|oral_solution|patch|powder|cream|inhaler|suppository|gel — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM CM Domain; WHO Pharmaceutical Dosage Forms; FDA 21 CFR 211

attributes.name: drug_code
attributes.description: Internally assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this comparator drug or placebo within the clinical supply catalogue. Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL / BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for cross-system reference.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM CM Domain; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: drug_name
attributes.description: Full proprietary or International Non-proprietary Name (INN) of the comparator drug or placebo product as it appears on the commercial label or sponsor documentation.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM CM Domain

attributes.name: drug_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the comparator drug master record. LIFECYCLE_STATUS for MASTER_RESOURCE role. 'quarantined' indicates the product is on hold pending quality investigation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 211

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this comparator drug master record is valid and approved for use in clinical supply operations. Supports version-controlled master data management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: formulation_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the comparator drug formulation including excipients, vehicle, and any special formulation characteristics relevant to blinding, matching, or stability. Sourced from the product SmPC or Certificate of Analysis.
attributes.references: ICH Q8(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 314

attributes.name: gmp_certificate_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the current Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificate issued by the relevant regulatory authority for the manufacturing site producing the comparator drug. Required for import authorisation and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: EU GMP Directive 2003/94/EC; FDA 21 CFR 211; ICH Q7; EMA GMP Database

attributes.name: import_licence_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether an import licence or import authorisation is required to ship the comparator drug into the trial countries. True triggers the regulatory affairs team to obtain the necessary import documentation prior to shipment.
attributes.references: EU Directive 2001/20/EC; FDA 21 CFR 312.110; ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: inn_name
attributes.description: WHO-assigned International Non-proprietary Name (INN) for the active substance of the comparator drug, used for regulatory submissions and MedDRA/WHO-DD coding alignment.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; WHO-DD; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: is_biological
attributes.description: Indicates whether the comparator drug is a biological product (e.g., monoclonal antibody, vaccine, blood-derived product). Biological products are subject to additional regulatory requirements including BLA/MAA pathways and cold-chain mandates.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR 600; EMA Directive 2001/83/EC Annex I Part II; ICH Q5A-Q5E

attributes.name: is_cold_chain
attributes.description: Indicates whether the comparator drug requires cold-chain logistics (temperature-controlled storage and transport). True triggers cold-chain monitoring, qualified packaging, and GDP-compliant distribution documentation.
attributes.references: EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 68/01; WHO Technical Report Series No. 961; ICH Q1A

attributes.name: is_controlled_substance
attributes.description: Indicates whether the comparator drug is classified as a controlled substance under applicable national legislation (e.g., DEA Schedule in the US, UK Misuse of Drugs Act). Triggers additional accountability and chain-of-custody requirements.
attributes.references: US DEA Controlled Substances Act; UK Misuse of Drugs Act 1971; EU Directive 2001/83/EC

attributes.name: is_placebo_matched
attributes.description: Indicates whether a matching placebo has been manufactured or sourced to maintain blinding integrity for this comparator drug. True = matching placebo exists; False = no matching placebo required.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: manufacturer_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the comparator drug is manufactured. Used for import/export compliance and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; FDA 21 CFR 312; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the pharmaceutical manufacturer or marketing authorisation holder responsible for producing the comparator drug. Used for procurement, GMP verification, and regulatory documentation.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 211; ICH Q7

attributes.name: max_storage_temp_c
attributes.description: Maximum permissible storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the comparator drug, as specified in the product SmPC or Certificate of Analysis. Used for cold-chain excursion monitoring and depot qualification.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 68/01; WHO Technical Report Series No. 961

attributes.name: min_storage_temp_c
attributes.description: Minimum permissible storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the comparator drug, as specified in the product SmPC or Certificate of Analysis. Used for cold-chain excursion monitoring and depot qualification.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 68/01; WHO Technical Report Series No. 961

attributes.name: ndc_code
attributes.description: FDA-assigned National Drug Code (NDC) for the comparator drug product, used for US-based procurement, dispensing records, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR 207; FDA NDC Directory

attributes.name: over_labelling_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the commercial comparator drug packaging must be over-labelled with clinical trial-specific information (e.g., protocol number, sponsor name, 'For Clinical Trial Use Only') to meet GMP Annex 13 and local regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 312.6; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: packaging_configuration
attributes.description: Description of the primary and secondary packaging configuration for the comparator drug (e.g., blister pack of 28 tablets, vial in carton). Used for kit definition alignment and label design.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 211.94; ICH Q6A

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Classification of the product role in the trial: comparator (active reference drug), placebo (inert matching product), active_control (approved drug used as benchmark), or rescue_medication (permitted concomitant therapy). CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE for MASTER_RESOURCE role.
attributes.references: ICH E10; FDA 21 CFR 312; EMA Guideline on the Choice of the Non-Inferiority Margin

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_status
attributes.description: Regulatory approval status of the comparator drug in the primary trial country. Indicates whether the product holds a valid marketing authorisation (MA) or equivalent approval. Distinct from IMP regulatory classification.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: retest_period_months
attributes.description: Period in months after which the comparator drug must be retested to confirm continued compliance with specification before further use. Applicable where a formal expiry date is not assigned.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); ICH Q1E; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Standardised route by which the comparator drug is administered to the subject (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical). Aligned with CDISC SDTM controlled terminology. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|intrathecal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Controlled Terminology (ROUTE); FDA 21 CFR 201; ICH M4

attributes.name: rtsm_product_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) Product ID
attributes.description: Product identifier assigned to the comparator drug within the RTSM system (Medidata Rave RTSM). Used to link supply planning, kit assignment, and dispensing records in the RTSM to this master record.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: shelf_life_months
attributes.description: Total approved shelf life of the comparator drug in months from the date of manufacture, as stated on the Certificate of Analysis or product SmPC. Used for expiry management, resupply planning, and RTSM expiry configuration.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR 211.137

attributes.name: sourcing_strategy
attributes.description: Strategy used to procure the comparator drug: commercial_purchase (bought from open market), sponsor_supplied (provided directly by sponsor), comparator_sourcing_service (via specialist CRO sourcing vendor), or donated (provided at no cost by manufacturer).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; FDA Guidance on Comparator Drug Sourcing

attributes.name: sponsor_product_code
attributes.description: Sponsor-assigned product code for the comparator drug, used in sponsor-facing documentation, supply agreements, and financial reconciliation with the sponsor.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: storage_condition
attributes.description: Prescribed storage condition category for the comparator drug as specified in the product SmPC or Certificate of Analysis. Drives depot and site storage configuration and cold-chain logistics planning.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GDP Guidelines; WHO Technical Report Series No. 961; FDA 21 CFR 211.142

attributes.name: strength_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the dose strength value (e.g., mg, mcg, g, mg/mL, IU). Combined with strength_value to express the full dose strength. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg|mcg|g|mg/mL|IU|%|mmol — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Controlled Terminology (UNIT); ICH Q6A; WHO Pharmaceutical Dosage Forms

attributes.name: strength_value
attributes.description: Numeric dose strength of the comparator drug per dosage unit (e.g., 500 for 500 mg). Used in conjunction with strength_unit for full dose characterisation.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM CM Domain; ICH Q6A; FDA 21 CFR 201

attributes.name: units_per_pack
attributes.description: Number of individual dosage units (e.g., tablets, capsules, vials) contained in one commercial or clinical pack of the comparator drug. Used for inventory planning and dispensing quantity calculations.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; CDISC SDTM EX Domain; FDA 21 CFR 211

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this comparator drug master record. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

products.name: ancillary_supply
products.description: Tracks non-IMP clinical supplies required at investigational sites, including syringes, diluents, infusion sets, patient diaries, lab kits, and other protocol-required materials. Captures supply type, unit of measure, site stock levels, reorder thresholds, and shipment history. Distinct from IMP/kit inventory as ancillary supplies follow different procurement, labeling, and accountability rules.
products.reference: Ancillary Clinical Supply

attributes.name: ancillary_supply_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each ancillary supply record in the clinical trial supply chain. Primary key for the ancillary_supply data product.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: depot_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.depot. Business justification: Ancillary supplies are stored at and distributed from clinical supply depots before being shipped to investigational sites. Adding depot_id to ancillary_supply establishes the storage/sourcing depot f
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: protocol_version_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific protocol version that mandates the use of this ancillary supply. Ensures supply requirements are aligned with the current approved protocol amendment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; FDA 21 CFR 312.23

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.purchase_order. Business justification: Ancillary supplies (lab kits, eDiaries, devices, PPE) are procured via purchase orders. Finance tracks ancillary supply costs against POs for budget reconciliation and sponsor pass-through billing. Cl
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: scope_of_work_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agreement.scope_of_work. Business justification: Ancillary supplies (lab kits, patient diaries, devices) are specified in the SOW as protocol-required materials with defined quantities and accountability requirements. SOW-driven ancillary supply pro
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this ancillary supply is required. Links the supply item to the protocol-defined study context.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS Study Object

attributes.name: study_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site at which this ancillary supply stock is held or required. Enables site-level inventory tracking and reorder management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4; Oracle Siebel CTMS Site Object

attributes.name: study_visit_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to study.study_visit_schedule. Business justification: Ancillary supplies (lab kits, patient diaries, eDiary devices) are required at specific protocol-defined visits. Linking ancillary_supply to study_visit_schedule enables visit-level supply planning an
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: accountability_status
attributes.description: Current reconciliation status of the ancillary supply accountability record. Indicates whether the received, dispensed, returned, and destroyed quantities have been fully reconciled per GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ALCOA+; 21 CFR 312.62; FDA Guidance on Drug Accountability

attributes.name: ancillary_supply_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the ancillary supply item at the site or study level. Drives reorder triggers, site communications, and supply chain planning actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: country_of_origin
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the country where the ancillary supply was manufactured. Required for import/export regulatory compliance and customs documentation.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; EU CTR 536/2014; FDA Import Regulations

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this ancillary supply record was first created in the system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: ctms_supply_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Supply Reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for this ancillary supply record in Oracle Siebel CTMS. Supports cross-system traceability between supply chain operations and site management activities.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: current_stock_quantity
attributes.description: Current on-hand inventory quantity of the ancillary supply at the assigned site, expressed in the defined unit of measure. Updated upon receipt of shipments and dispensing events.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Medidata Rave RTSM Inventory

attributes.name: destroyed_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of ancillary supply that has been destroyed at the site or depot due to expiry, damage, or protocol requirements. Supports accountability reconciliation and destruction certificate documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: destruction_method
attributes.description: Method used to destroy expired or unused ancillary supply stock. Required for environmental compliance, regulatory inspection readiness, and accountability documentation.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62; EPA Regulations

attributes.name: dispensed_quantity
attributes.description: Cumulative quantity of this ancillary supply dispensed to subjects or consumed in study procedures since last receipt. Used for accountability reconciliation and waste analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ALCOA+; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this ancillary supply record is valid and active for the study and site. Supports protocol amendment tracking and supply version management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this ancillary supply record ceases to be valid for the study and site. Null indicates the record is currently active. Supports supply lifecycle management and study close-out.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current stock of this ancillary supply expires and must no longer be used. Critical for expiry management, destruction scheduling, and GCP compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 211.137

attributes.name: is_cold_chain
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ancillary supply requires cold-chain logistics management during storage and shipment. When true, temperature-controlled packaging and monitoring are mandatory.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); WHO Technical Report Series 961; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: is_patient_facing
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ancillary supply is directly used by or administered to study subjects (e.g., patient diaries, injection devices). Patient-facing supplies may require additional labeling and consent documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR 164

attributes.name: is_protocol_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ancillary supply is explicitly mandated by the study protocol. Protocol-required supplies must be tracked for accountability and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; FDA 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: label_language_code
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) of the ancillary supply label (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de-DE'). Ensures site-appropriate labeling for multi-national trials.
attributes.references: ISO 639-1; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: label_text
attributes.description: Full text content of the label applied to the ancillary supply packaging as required by the protocol and applicable regulations. Supports label review, audit, and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.6; CDISC CDASH

attributes.name: last_dispensed_date
attributes.description: Date on which this ancillary supply was most recently dispensed to a study subject or used in a study procedure. Supports usage tracking and expiry risk assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: last_shipment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent shipment of this ancillary supply to the site. Used to monitor supply chain activity, identify sites with stale stock, and support resupply planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; SAP S/4HANA

attributes.name: lot_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer's lot or batch number for the current stock of ancillary supply. Essential for traceability, recall management, and ALCOA+ compliance in clinical trial accountability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; 21 CFR 211.184; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the manufacturer or supplier of the ancillary supply. Required for traceability, quality event investigations, and regulatory inspection documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ISO 14155; 21 CFR 820

attributes.name: manufacturer_part_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer's own catalogue or part number for the ancillary supply. Used for procurement ordering, quality investigations, and cross-referencing with supplier documentation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Procurement; ISO 14155

attributes.name: max_storage_temp_c
attributes.description: Maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this ancillary supply. Paired with min_storage_temp_c to define the acceptable temperature range for storage and transport.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 211.142

attributes.name: maximum_stock_quantity
attributes.description: Upper inventory limit for this ancillary supply at the site. Prevents overstocking, reduces waste from expiry, and supports cold-chain capacity planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; SAP S/4HANA

attributes.name: min_storage_temp_c
attributes.description: Minimum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this ancillary supply. Used for cold-chain monitoring, excursion detection, and GCP compliance reporting.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 211.142

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, handling instructions, or special requirements associated with this ancillary supply record. Supports site communications and CRA monitoring activities.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: pack_size
attributes.description: Number of individual units contained within one ordering/shipping pack of the ancillary supply. Used to convert between pack-level and unit-level inventory quantities.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Material Master; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: procurement_lead_time_days
attributes.description: Number of days required from placement of a purchase order to receipt of the ancillary supply at the site or depot. Used for reorder planning and supply continuity risk management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Procurement; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: receipt_date
attributes.description: Date on which the ancillary supply was received at the investigational site or depot. Used for inventory reconciliation, shelf-life calculation, and shipment confirmation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ALCOA+; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: regulatory_classification
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the ancillary supply under applicable medical device or in-vitro diagnostic regulations (e.g., FDA Class I/II/III device, EU MDR class). Determines labeling, CE marking, and accountability requirements.
attributes.references: EU MDR 2017/745; 21 CFR Part 820; ISO 14155; PMDA

attributes.name: reorder_quantity
attributes.description: Standard quantity to be ordered when the reorder threshold is reached. Represents the economic order quantity agreed with the supplier or depot for this ancillary supply.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Procurement; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: reorder_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum stock quantity level at which a replenishment order must be triggered for this ancillary supply at the site. Supports automated reorder alerts and supply continuity planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: returned_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of ancillary supply returned from the site to the depot or sponsor for destruction or reuse. Required for accountability reconciliation and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: rtsm_supply_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) Supply ID

attributes.name: shelf_life_days
attributes.description: Total shelf life of the ancillary supply in days from the date of manufacture or receipt. Used to calculate expiry dates and plan supply replenishment schedules.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: storage_condition
attributes.description: Required storage condition for the ancillary supply as specified by the manufacturer or protocol (e.g., room_temperature, refrigerated). Drives cold-chain logistics and site storage compliance checks.

attributes.name: supply_category

attributes.name: supply_code

attributes.name: supply_name

attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM EX Domain

attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; CDISC CDASH

attributes.name: unit_of_measure

attributes.name: certificate_of_analysis_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the Certificate of Analysis (CoA) issued by the manufacturer for this batch. The CoA confirms the batch meets specification and is required for QP release and regulatory inspection readiness.

attributes.name: destruction_certificate_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the destruction certificate issued when qty_destroyed units were disposed of. Required for drug accountability reconciliation and regulatory submission documentation.

attributes.name: erp_material_document_number

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Expiration date assigned to this IMP batch by the manufacturer. Inventory with expiry_date in the past must be quarantined or destroyed per GMP requirements. Drives automated expiry alerts in RTSM.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.137; ICH Q1A(R2); Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: import_permit_number
attributes.description: Regulatory import permit or customs clearance number associated with this batch's receipt at the depot. Required for cross-border IMP shipments and regulatory inspection documentation.

attributes.name: inventory_record_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable identifier for this depot inventory record as assigned by the RTSM or CTMS system (e.g., INV-2024-00123). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: inventory_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this depot inventory record. Drives supply availability calculations, RTSM allocation logic, and GMP disposition decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Available|Allocated|Quarantined|Expired|Destroyed|Returned|On_Hold — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211; ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: is_cold_chain
attributes.description: Indicates whether this IMP batch requires continuous cold-chain management throughout storage and distribution. Drives cold-chain logistics planning, temperature monitoring requirements, and qualified carrier selection.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; WHO TRS 961; ICH Q1A(R2); GDP Guidelines 2013/C 343/01

attributes.name: is_controlled_substance
attributes.description: Indicates whether this IMP batch is classified as a controlled substance requiring enhanced security, dual-custody handling, and DEA/national narcotics authority reporting for inventory accountability.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 1301 (DEA); EU Directive 2011/62/EU; UN Convention on Psychotropic Substances

attributes.name: kit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the kit contents held in this inventory record. Distinguishes IMP, comparator, placebo, rescue medication, ancillary supplies, and open-label kits for supply planning and accountability.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM EX domain

attributes.name: last_physical_count_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent physical inventory count was conducted at the depot for this batch/kit type. Supports GMP compliance scheduling and audit readiness.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.192; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this depot inventory record, whether from an RTSM transaction, physical count, or manual adjustment. Supports audit trail and data lineage per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: manufacture_date
attributes.description: Date on which the IMP batch was manufactured. Used alongside expiry date to calculate remaining shelf life and support GMP batch traceability.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.137; ICH Q7

attributes.name: min_stock_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum quantity of available stock that must be maintained at this depot for this IMP/kit type before a replenishment order is triggered. Supports proactive supply planning and prevents stockouts.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave RTSM supply planning; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for supply chain staff to record observations, discrepancy explanations, QP comments, or other contextual information relevant to this depot inventory record. Supports audit trail documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: physical_count_discrepancy
attributes.description: Difference between qty_last_physical_count and the system-recorded qty_on_hand at the time of the physical count. A non-zero value triggers a discrepancy investigation per GMP requirements.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.192; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: qp_release_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Qualified Person formally released this batch for clinical use. Null if release is pending or the batch has been rejected.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; EU Directive 2001/83/EC; EMA GMP guidelines

attributes.name: qp_release_status
attributes.description: Status of the Qualified Person (QP) batch release decision for this inventory. Only QP-released stock may be dispensed to clinical sites per EU GMP Annex 13 requirements.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; EU Directive 2001/83/EC; EMA GMP guidelines

attributes.name: qty_allocated
attributes.description: Number of kits or units reserved for pending outbound shipments or site replenishment orders that have been confirmed but not yet physically dispatched. Prevents double-allocation in RTSM.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave RTSM; EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: qty_available
attributes.description: Number of kits or units available for new allocation or shipment. Calculated as qty_on_hand minus qty_allocated minus qty_quarantined minus qty_expired. Represents the net usable stock for RTSM dispensing decisions.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave RTSM; EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: qty_destroyed
attributes.description: Cumulative number of kits or units destroyed at this depot for this batch. Supports drug accountability reconciliation and regulatory destruction certificate documentation.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 312.62; ICH E6(R2); DEA regulations (controlled substances)

attributes.name: qty_expired
attributes.description: Number of kits or units that have passed their expiry date and are no longer eligible for dispensing. Tracked separately to support destruction reconciliation and regulatory accountability reporting.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.137; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: qty_last_physical_count
attributes.description: Actual kit or unit count recorded during the most recent physical inventory count at the depot. Used to reconcile system-recorded quantities against physical stock and identify discrepancies.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.192; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: qty_on_hand
attributes.description: Total number of kits or units of this IMP batch currently physically present at the depot, regardless of allocation status. The gross stock figure before netting allocated, quarantined, or expired quantities.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave RTSM inventory module

attributes.name: qty_quarantined
attributes.description: Number of kits or units placed under quarantine status due to quality investigations, temperature excursions, damaged packaging, or pending QP release. Quarantined stock is excluded from available supply.
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.192; ICH Q10; MasterControl QMS

attributes.name: qty_returned
attributes.description: Number of kits or units returned from clinical sites to this depot. Returned stock is typically quarantined pending QP review before any disposition decision (reuse, destruction, or reconciliation).
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; 21 CFR Part 312.62

attributes.name: quarantine_reason
attributes.description: Reason code explaining why stock was placed in quarantine status. Required for GMP deviation documentation and QP disposition decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Temperature_Excursion|Damaged_Packaging|QP_Hold|Recall|Stability_Failure|Pending_Release|Investigation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.192; ICH Q10; MasterControl CAPA

attributes.name: receipt_date
attributes.description: Date on which this batch/kit stock was physically received at the depot. Used for FIFO/FEFO inventory management, shelf-life calculations, and GMP receipt documentation.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp

attributes.name: reorder_quantity

attributes.references: Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: retest_date

attributes.name: rtsm_inventory_code

attributes.name: storage_condition_zone

attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH Q1A(R2) Stability; USP <1079>; WHO TRS 961

attributes.name: temperature_excursion_flag

attributes.references: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH Q1A(R2); WHO TRS 961; 21 CFR Part 211.68

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The dispensing or counting unit used for all quantity fields in this inventory record (e.g., Kit, Vial, Tablet). Ensures consistent quantity interpretation across RTSM, ERP, and accountability reports. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Kit|Vial|Tablet|Capsule|Syringe|Bottle|Blister_Pack — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

products.name: budget_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the Contract between supply_plan and budget_line. It captures the operational mapping maintained by clinical supply finance teams that links specific supply plan versions to granular budget line items, tracking the quantity, unit cost, cost category, time period, and variance for each allocation. Each record links one supply_plan to one budget_line with attributes that exist only in the context of this financial-operational reconciliation relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical trial operations, a supply plan covers multiple cost categories (manufacturing, packaging, distribution, destruction) each represented as distinct budget lines, while a single budget line (e.g., IMP manufacturing) is informed by and allocated across multiple supply plan versions as the study evolves through amendments and planning cycles. Clinical supply finance teams actively maintain and manage this supply plan-to-budget line mapping as a recognized operational artifact, tracking quantity allocations, unit costs, and variances per pairing. This is not an analytical derivation — it is an actively managed financial-operational reconciliation record that bridges supply planning and study budgeting.

products.name: contracted_supply_item
products.description: This association product represents the Contract between imp_master and study_contract. It captures the specific terms under which a given investigational medicinal product is included in the supply scope of a Clinical Trial Agreement — recording the supply role, contracted quantity, unit price, and validity window for each IMP-contract pairing. Each record links one imp_master to one study_contract with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual supply relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single IMP (e.g., a novel oncology compound) is routinely supplied across multiple study contracts — different studies, different sponsors, different CROs — while a single study contract (CTA) almost always covers multiple IMPs: the investigational product, an active comparator, and a placebo. The business actively manages this relationship as a 'contracted supply item' or 'IMP supply scope' within each CTA, tracking contracted quantities, unit pricing, and the supply role (IMP vs. comparator vs. placebo) per IMP per contract. This is not derivable from transactional data; it is an operational record that procurement and supply chain teams create, negotiate, and update throughout the contract lifecycle.

products.name: imp_authorization
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory authorization contract between an investigational medicinal product (imp_master) and a Clinical Trial Authorization (clinical_trial_authorization). It captures the specific terms under which a given IMP is authorized for use within a given CTA in a given EU member state jurisdiction, including authorized quantities, effective dates, and authorization status at the IMP level. Each record links one imp_master to one clinical_trial_authorization with attributes that exist only in the context of this IMP-CTA regulatory pairing, supporting EU CTR 536/2014 compliance and multi-country supply planning.. Existence Justification: In EU clinical trial operations, a single IMP (e.g., a monoclonal antibody) requires separate CTAs filed in each EU member state where the trial runs, meaning one IMP is covered by many CTAs. Conversely, a single CTA for a combination product or multi-arm trial can authorize multiple IMPs simultaneously. The business actively manages this relationship as a regulatory compliance record — tracking authorized quantities, effective dates, and authorization status per IMP-per-CTA combination — which is a named concept in EU CTR 536/2014 regulatory practice.

products.name: depot_sla_coverage
products.description: This association product represents the Contract/Assignment between a clinical supply depot and a Service Level Agreement. It captures which SLAs are actively governing each depot in the supply network, along with the operational details of that coverage — effective date, scope of activities covered, current performance status, and last review date. Each record links one depot to one SLA and holds attributes that exist only in the context of that specific depot-SLA assignment, enabling supply chain managers to audit compliance and manage SLA coverage across the depot network.. Existence Justification: In clinical trial supply operations, a depot (warehouse node) can be governed by multiple SLAs simultaneously — e.g., a temperature monitoring SLA, a dispatch turnaround SLA, and a receipt confirmation SLA — while a single SLA (e.g., 'dispatch within 24 hours') can apply to multiple depots across the supply network. This is an operationally managed relationship: supply chain managers actively assign, activate, and review which SLAs govern each depot, and the assignment itself carries meaningful data (effective date, scope, performance status, last review date) that belongs to neither the depot nor the SLA alone. Business stakeholders in clinical supply would recognize this as 'Depot SLA Coverage' or a 'Depot SLA Assignment' — a governed, auditable record of which performance commitments apply to which supply nodes.

products.name: imp_indication_track
products.description: This association product represents the Development Track between imp_master and indication. It captures the operational record of a specific investigational medicinal product being developed for a specific therapeutic indication, including the development phase, regulatory filing status, line of therapy, and biomarker strategy applicable to that specific IMP-indication pairing. Each record links one imp_master to one indication with attributes that exist only in the context of this development relationship and cannot be attributed to either the IMP or the indication alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical drug development, a single IMP (investigational medicinal product) is routinely developed across multiple therapeutic indications simultaneously — e.g., a PD-1 inhibitor studied in NSCLC, breast cancer, and colorectal cancer at the same time. Conversely, a given indication (e.g., NSCLC) will have multiple IMPs under active development within a program, including combination regimens. The business actively manages each IMP-indication pairing as a distinct development program track, tracking its own development phase, regulatory status, line of therapy, and biomarker strategy — data that belongs to neither the IMP master nor the indication record alone.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

products.name: imp_sop_applicability
products.description: This association product represents the formal applicability relationship between an investigational medicinal product (IMP) and a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) within the quality management system. It captures which SOPs govern each IMP, in what operational capacity (storage, dispensing, destruction, cold-chain), and for what period. Each record links one imp_master to one sop with attributes that exist only in the context of this IMP-SOP governance relationship, supporting GMP compliance, audit readiness, and training management.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single IMP (e.g., a cold-chain biological IMP) is governed by multiple SOPs simultaneously — a storage SOP, a dispensing SOP, a destruction SOP, and a cold-chain SOP — each applying to that product in a distinct capacity. Conversely, a single SOP (e.g., a GMP dispensing SOP) applies to multiple IMPs across different studies. The business actively manages this applicability relationship through document control processes, tracking when each SOP became applicable to each IMP, in what role, and whether training is required for that specific IMP-SOP pairing.

attributes.name: amber_threshold
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value at which the KRI triggers an amber (warning) alert, indicating elevated risk requiring heightened monitoring attention. Defined in the RBM monitoring plan.

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Formal description or formula specifying how the KRI value is computed (e.g., 'Number of screen failures / Number of subjects screened × 100'). Ensures reproducibility and auditability of centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) outputs.

attributes.name: capa_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) must be initiated in response to the KRI breach. Drives workflow integration with MasterControl CAPA tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; MasterControl CAPA; ISO 9001

attributes.name: computation_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the KRI value was most recently computed for the site. Used to assess data currency and trigger recomputation schedules in the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: computation_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency at which the KRI is recomputed for each site (e.g., weekly for enrollment KRIs, monthly for data quality KRIs). Defined in the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: computation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time at which the KRI value was computed, including timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: computed_value
attributes.description: Current computed numeric value of the KRI for the associated site, derived from the source system data as of the last computation run. This is the principal quantitative fact of the risk indicator record.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: consecutive_breach_count
attributes.description: Number of consecutive computation cycles during which the KRI has remained at or above the amber or red threshold. Used to trigger escalation workflows and CAPA initiation per the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; MasterControl CAPA

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this KRI record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which the KRI input data is extracted for computation (e.g., Medidata Rave EDC for data quality KRIs, Oracle Argus Safety for safety KRIs, Oracle Siebel CTMS for enrollment KRIs).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: denominator_value
attributes.description: Raw denominator component of the KRI computation (e.g., total subjects screened, total expected data points, total SAEs reported). Stored alongside the numerator to enable independent verification of the computed value.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: Date from which this KRI definition became active and applicable to the study and site. Supports versioning of KRI definitions when monitoring plan amendments are issued.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: Date on which this KRI definition was superseded or retired. Null for currently active KRI definitions. Supports historical analysis and monitoring plan amendment tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: escalation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the current KRI alert status and breach history require formal escalation to the sponsor, Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB), or senior management per the RBM escalation procedure.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: indicator_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of what the KRI measures, its business rationale, and how it supports risk detection within the RBM framework.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: indicator_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the KRI as defined in the RBM monitoring plan (e.g., 'Screen Failure Rate', 'Missing Data Rate', 'SAE Reporting Timeliness'). Used in dashboards, monitoring visit reports, and sponsor communications.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: indicator_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the KRI definition within the monitoring plan. Active KRIs are computed and monitored; draft KRIs are under review; retired KRIs are no longer in use.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; MasterControl Document Control; Veeva Vault

attributes.name: indicator_type
attributes.description: Quantitative type of the KRI value, indicating whether the computed metric is a rate, absolute count, percentage, ratio, or duration in days. Governs how the value is interpreted against thresholds.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; TransCelerate RBM Framework; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: is_centralized_monitoring
attributes.description: Indicates whether this KRI is part of the Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) program, as opposed to a site-level operational indicator. Supports differentiation of CSM KRIs from operational monitoring metrics.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for CRA or data manager annotations regarding the KRI computation, alert status, or remediation context. Supports monitoring visit report narrative and sponsor communication.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: numerator_value
attributes.description: Raw numerator component of the KRI computation (e.g., number of screen failures, number of missing data points, number of overdue SAE reports). Stored to support audit and recomputation validation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: prior_computed_value
attributes.description: KRI computed value from the immediately preceding computation cycle for the same site. Enables trend analysis and detection of rapid deterioration or improvement in site risk profile.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: red_threshold
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value at which the KRI triggers a red (critical) alert, indicating a significant risk requiring immediate escalation and corrective action per the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: reference_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the data window used to compute the KRI value. Together with reference_period_start, defines the exact temporal scope of the KRI computation for reproducibility and audit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: reference_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the data window used to compute the KRI value (e.g., rolling 30-day window start, or study start date for cumulative KRIs). Defines the temporal scope of the computation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: risk_indicator_category
attributes.description: Business category classifying the domain of risk the KRI monitors. Supports stratified risk reporting across enrollment, data quality, safety, protocol compliance, and Investigational Product (IP) accountability domains.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: risk_score_contribution
attributes.description: Weighted contribution of this KRI to the overall site risk score, expressed as a percentage (0–100). Reflects the KRI's relative importance in the composite site risk scoring model.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; TransCelerate RBM Framework; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: sdv_impact
attributes.description: Defines the impact of this KRI's alert status on the Source Data Verification (SDV) strategy for the site. A red alert may trigger targeted or increased SDV; a green status may support reduced SDV per the risk-adaptive monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: sponsor_defined
attributes.description: Indicates whether this KRI was defined by the sponsor (True) or by the CRO as part of its standard RBM methodology (False). Supports differentiation of sponsor-mandated versus CRO-standard risk indicators.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: threshold_direction
attributes.description: Indicates whether the KRI alert is triggered when the computed value exceeds (above) or falls below (below) the defined amber/red thresholds. Critical for correct alert logic in centralized statistical monitoring (CSM).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: trend_direction
attributes.description: Directional trend of the KRI value compared to the prior computation cycle. Supports proactive risk management by identifying sites where risk is worsening before threshold breach.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit in which the KRI value and thresholds are expressed (e.g., '%', 'days', 'count', 'ratio'). Ensures consistent interpretation of computed values across sites and studies.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM Controlled Terminology

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this KRI record, supporting change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier of the KRI definition (e.g., v1.0, v2.1), incremented when the calculation method, thresholds, or data source is amended. Supports audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault Document Control

attributes.name: weight
attributes.description: Numeric weight assigned to this KRI in the composite site risk scoring model, reflecting its relative importance compared to other KRIs in the monitoring plan. Used in weighted risk score calculations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: notification_sent_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the visit notification was sent to the investigational site. Used to verify compliance with advance notice requirements in the monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.1; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: planned_duration_days
attributes.description: The expected duration of the monitoring visit in days as planned in the monitoring schedule. Used for CRA capacity planning and resource allocation.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: planned_visit_date
attributes.description: The target calendar date on which the monitoring visit is planned to occur, representing the principal business event date for scheduling and CRA workload forecasting.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: The priority assigned to this planned monitoring visit for CRA workload management and scheduling. Critical visits (e.g., for-cause, safety-triggered) take precedence over routine interim visits.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring (2023); ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: rescheduling_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation for why the planned monitoring visit was rescheduled. Required when schedule_status is 'Rescheduled'. Supports audit and compliance review.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: schedule_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this visit schedule record as assigned in Oracle Siebel CTMS (e.g., VS-2024-0042). Used for cross-system reference and audit trail.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the planned monitoring visit schedule record within Oracle Siebel CTMS.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: scheduling_basis
attributes.description: The basis or rationale used to determine when this visit should occur: Calendar-Based (fixed interval), Risk-Based Trigger (driven by KRI/risk indicator breach), Milestone-Based (linked to study milestone such as first patient enrolled), Enrollment-Based (triggered by subject enrollment count), or Regulatory-Required (mandated by regulatory authority).
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring (2023); ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3

attributes.name: sdv_scope
attributes.description: The Source Data Verification (SDV) scope category for this planned visit: 100% SDV (all data points), Risk-Based SDV (targeted by risk), Critical Data Only (primary endpoints and safety data), or No SDV (remote/centralized monitoring only).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring (2023)

attributes.name: sdv_target_percentage
attributes.description: The planned percentage of source data to be verified during this monitoring visit as defined in the monitoring plan. Reflects the risk-based SDV strategy for this visit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; CDISC

attributes.name: sponsor_approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor approved this planned monitoring visit schedule. Populated only when sponsor_approved is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: sponsor_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the sponsor has reviewed and approved this planned monitoring visit schedule, particularly relevant for risk-based or for-cause visits requiring sponsor authorization.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.description: The username or system account identifier of the user who last modified this visit schedule record in Oracle Siebel CTMS. Required for audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ (Attributable).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this visit schedule record was most recently modified in Oracle Siebel CTMS. Supports audit trail requirements per ALCOA+ and 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Incremental version number of this visit schedule record, incremented each time the schedule is modified (e.g., rescheduled, scope changed). Supports audit trail and change history per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: visit_mode
attributes.description: Indicates whether the planned monitoring visit will be conducted on-site at the investigational site, remotely (e.g., via EDC review), or as a hybrid combining both approaches.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring (2023); EMA Reflection Paper on Risk-Based Quality Management

attributes.name: visit_objectives
attributes.description: Free-text description of the specific objectives and scope of work planned for this monitoring visit, as defined in the monitoring plan or visit notification (e.g., ICF review, IP accountability, protocol deviation follow-up).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: visit_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordinal number of this planned visit within the site's monitoring schedule for the study (e.g., 1 = first interim visit, 2 = second interim visit). Used for ordering and CRA workload planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: visit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the planned monitoring visit by its purpose within the study lifecycle: Site Initiation Visit (SIV), Interim Monitoring Visit, Close-Out Visit, Remote Monitoring Visit, For-Cause Visit, or Pre-Study Visit.
attributes.value_regex: Site Initiation Visit|Interim Monitoring Visit|Close-Out Visit|Remote Monitoring Visit|For-Cause Visit|Pre-Study Visit
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: window_earliest_date
attributes.description: The earliest acceptable date on which the monitoring visit may be conducted while still satisfying the monitoring plan window requirements. Used to define the permissible scheduling window.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: window_latest_date
attributes.description: The latest acceptable date on which the monitoring visit may be conducted while still satisfying the monitoring plan window requirements. Visits beyond this date are considered overdue.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: window_tolerance_days
attributes.description: The number of days of allowable deviation on either side of the planned visit date that defines the acceptable scheduling window (e.g., ±14 days). Used to compute window_earliest_date and window_latest_date.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: The username or system account identifier of the user who created this visit schedule record in Oracle Siebel CTMS. Required for audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ (Attributable).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2)

products.name: ip_accountability_log
products.description: Investigational Product (IP) accountability verification record captured during monitoring visits. Records CRA verification of IP receipt, dispensing, return, and destruction records at the site level. Captures IP batch/lot number, quantity reconciliation (received vs dispensed vs returned vs destroyed), reconciliation status, temperature excursion checks, discrepancy notes, and CRA verification date. Supports GCP compliance for IP accountability under ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3 and 21 CFR 312.62.
products.reference: IP Accountability Log (ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3, GCP, 21 CFR 312)

attributes.name: ip_accountability_log_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Investigational Product (IP) accountability verification record captured during a monitoring visit. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: accountability_reconciliation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.accountability_reconciliation. Business justification: The CRA's ip_accountability_log (on-site verification record) and supply's accountability_reconciliation (formal IMP balance record) are complementary GCP documents for the same IP accountability proc

attributes.name: compliance_capa_id
attributes.description: Reference to the CAPA record initiated in MasterControl as a result of IP accountability findings. Populated when capa_required is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; MasterControl; GCP

attributes.name: destruction_record_id

attributes.description: Reference to the monitoring visit during which this IP accountability verification was conducted by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to randomization.kit_assignment. CRAs verify ip_accountability_log against kit_assi
