attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.approval. Business justification: IP accountability verification must confirm the dispensed investigational product matches the approved formulation, dose, and labeling per the regulatory approval. This is a GCP/GMP compliance require
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this IP accountability log record applies.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR 312.62; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: study_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site at which the IP accountability verification was performed.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; 21 CFR 312.62; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: tmf_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: IP accountability logs are GCP-required records filed in eTMF Zone 7 (Investigational Product). CRAs and QA teams must trace each IP accountability verification to its TMF-filed document for inspectio
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: accountability_finding_severity
attributes.description: The severity classification of any IP accountability finding identified during the CRA verification. 'None' indicates full compliance; 'Critical' indicates a finding that may impact subject safety or data integrity and requires immediate escalation to the sponsor.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; GCP

attributes.name: batch_lot_number
attributes.description: The manufacturing batch or lot number of the investigational product as recorded on the IP label and dispensing records. Critical for traceability and recall management under GCP and GMP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.3; 21 CFR 312.62; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: capa_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) is required as a result of IP accountability findings identified during this monitoring visit. When True, a CAPA record must be initiated in MasterControl.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; MasterControl; GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: cra_comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments entered by the CRA regarding the overall IP accountability verification, including observations about site practices, documentation quality, and any additional context not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; Oracle Siebel CTMS; ALCOA+

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this IP accountability log record was first created in the system, including timezone offset. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: destruction_records_reviewed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Destruction Records Reviewed Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the CRA reviewed IP destruction certificates or records during the monitoring visit to confirm that destroyed IP quantities are properly documented and authorized.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: discrepancy_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the nature of any IP accountability discrepancy identified during the CRA verification, including potential explanations, site staff comments, and initial investigation findings. Required when reconciliation_status is 'discrepancy_identified'.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; ALCOA+

attributes.name: discrepancy_quantity
attributes.description: The numeric difference between the calculated IP balance (received minus dispensed minus returned minus destroyed) and the physical quantity on hand. A non-zero value indicates an accountability discrepancy requiring investigation and documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: dispensing_log_reviewed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Dispensing Log Reviewed Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the CRA reviewed the site's IP dispensing log during the monitoring visit to verify accuracy and completeness of dispensing records against subject randomization and dosing data.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; GCP

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The expiration date of the investigational product batch/lot as printed on the label. CRA verifies that no expired IP has been dispensed to subjects. Non-compliance is a critical GCP finding.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.3; 21 CFR 312.62; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: ip_form
attributes.description: The pharmaceutical dosage form of the investigational product (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection). Relevant for storage condition verification and dispensing record review. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|injection|infusion|topical|inhaler|powder|solution|suspension|patch|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: ip_label_compliance_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Label Compliance Verified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the CRA verified that IP labels comply with applicable regulatory requirements (e.g., correct language, required statements, batch/lot number, expiry date, storage conditions) per the approved labeling.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.3; 21 CFR 312.6; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: ip_storage_location
attributes.description: The physical location identifier or description of where the investigational product is stored at the site (e.g., pharmacy refrigerator unit ID, locked cabinet reference). Verified by the CRA during the monitoring visit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.2; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: ip_strength
attributes.description: The dose strength of the investigational product as labeled (e.g., '100 mg', '5 mg/mL'). Used to verify that the correct strength was dispensed per the protocol and randomization assignment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: log_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this IP accountability log record, typically assigned by the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) or Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system (e.g., 'IPAL-2024-00123'). Used for cross-system referencing and audit trail.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; Oracle Siebel CTMS; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: quantity_destroyed
attributes.description: The total quantity of investigational product units destroyed at the site or returned to sponsor for destruction, as documented in the destruction records. Required for full IP accountability reconciliation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: quantity_dispensed
attributes.description: The total quantity of investigational product units dispensed to study subjects at the site, as recorded in the dispensing log. Used in the IP accountability reconciliation calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: quantity_on_hand
attributes.description: The physical count of investigational product units remaining in site inventory at the time of the CRA verification visit. Compared against the calculated balance (received minus dispensed minus returned minus destroyed) to identify discrepancies.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: quantity_received
attributes.description: The total quantity of investigational product units received at the site from the sponsor or depot, as recorded in the site's IP receipt log. Expressed in the unit of dispensing (e.g., number of tablets, vials, kits). Used as the starting balance for reconciliation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; Medidata Rave RTSM

attributes.name: quantity_returned
attributes.description: The total quantity of investigational product units returned by subjects to the site (unused or partially used), as recorded in the return log. Included in the reconciliation to account for all IP.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: quantity_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Quantity Unit of Measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure used for all IP quantity fields (received, dispensed, returned, destroyed, on hand) in this record (e.g., 'tablet', 'vial', 'kit'). Ensures consistent interpretation of quantity values across reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|vial|kit|syringe|patch|unit|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: reconciliation_status
attributes.description: The outcome status of the IP quantity reconciliation performed by the CRA. 'Balanced' indicates quantities account for all IP; 'Discrepancy Identified' indicates a mismatch requiring investigation. Drives CAPA and escalation workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; GCP

attributes.name: return_log_reviewed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Return Log Reviewed Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the CRA reviewed the site's IP return log during the monitoring visit to verify that all returned IP units are documented with subject ID, return date, and quantity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; GCP

attributes.name: review_period_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Accountability Review Period End Date
attributes.description: The end date of the period covered by this IP accountability review (i.e., the date up to which IP transactions are being reconciled). Typically corresponds to the current monitoring visit date.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; GCP

attributes.name: review_period_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Accountability Review Period Start Date
attributes.description: The start date of the period covered by this IP accountability review (i.e., the date from which IP transactions are being reconciled). Typically corresponds to the date of the previous monitoring visit or last accountability check.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; 21 CFR 312.62; GCP

attributes.name: rtsm_irt_reconciled
attributes.business_glossary_term: Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) / Interactive Response Technology (IRT) Reconciled Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site's physical IP accountability records have been reconciled against the RTSM/IRT system (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM) dispensing and randomization data. Discrepancies between physical records and RTSM/IRT are a critical GCP finding.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.4; Medidata Rave RTSM; GCP

attributes.name: sponsor_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor was notified of IP accountability findings or discrepancies. Populated when sponsor_notified is True. Used to track timeliness of sponsor communication per GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; 21 CFR 312.62; GCP

attributes.name: sponsor_notified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the sponsor has been notified of IP accountability discrepancies, temperature excursions, or critical findings identified during this verification. Required for critical and major findings under GCP.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; 21 CFR 312.62; GCP

attributes.name: storage_condition_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Storage Condition Verified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the CRA verified that the investigational product was stored under the protocol-specified conditions (e.g., temperature range, light protection, humidity) at the time of the monitoring visit. A value of True confirms compliance; False triggers a finding.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.2; 21 CFR 312.62; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: storage_temperature_max_c
attributes.description: The maximum temperature (in degrees Celsius) recorded in the IP storage area during the period under review, as verified by the CRA from temperature monitoring logs or data loggers. Used to assess compliance with protocol-specified storage conditions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.2; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: storage_temperature_min_c
attributes.description: The minimum temperature (in degrees Celsius) recorded in the IP storage area during the period under review, as verified by the CRA from temperature monitoring logs or data loggers. Used to assess compliance with protocol-specified storage conditions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.2; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62

attributes.name: temperature_excursion_details
attributes.description: Free-text description of any temperature excursion identified, including the duration, magnitude, affected IP units, and any corrective actions taken by site staff. Populated only when temperature_excursion_occurred is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.2; 21 CFR 312.62; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: temperature_excursion_occurred
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational Product (IP) Temperature Excursion Occurred Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a temperature excursion (storage outside the protocol-specified temperature range) was identified during the CRA review of temperature monitoring records. True triggers mandatory sponsor notification and potential IP quarantine.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13.2; 21 CFR 312.62; EU GMP Annex 13

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this IP accountability log record was most recently modified, including timezone offset. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records audit trail and change tracking requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the CRA performed the IP accountability verification at the site. This is the principal real-world event date for this record, distinct from the record creation timestamp. Required for GCP compliance documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; 21 CFR 312.62; ALCOA+

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: The current workflow status of this IP accountability log record. 'Draft' indicates the CRA has initiated but not finalized the record; 'Completed' indicates CRA sign-off; 'Reviewed' indicates supervisor review; 'Approved' indicates final approval; 'Closed' indicates all findings resolved.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; Oracle Siebel CTMS; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: verification_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time at which the CRA completed the IP accountability verification, including timezone offset. Supports ALCOA+ (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate) audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; ALCOA+

Managed in Oracle Siebel CTMS.

attributes.description: Reference to the CRA (Clinical Research Associate) who initiated and raised this escalation record.

Linking alerts to the s

attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this central monitoring alert was generated. Links the alert to the study protocol context.

attributes.name: study_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site at which the anomaly or Key Risk Indicator (KRI) threshold breach was detected. Core contextual dimension for risk-based monitoring (RBM) triage.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: alert_category
attributes.description: Broad business domain category of the alert, used for routing, reporting, and escalation prioritization. DATA_QUALITY: data entry or consistency issues. SAFETY: adverse event or safety reporting concerns. ENROLLMENT: subject recruitment or screen failure anomalies. PROTOCOL_COMPLIANCE: protocol deviation patterns. REGULATORY: regulatory document or submission concerns. OPERATIONAL: site operational performance issues.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; CDISC RBM Reference Model

attributes.name: alert_generated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the alert was generated by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) system or manually created by a central monitor. This is the principal real-world business event time. BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: alert_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-known business identifier for the alert, formatted as CMA-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used in communications, reports, and audit trails to uniquely reference an alert across systems. Sourced from Oracle Siebel CTMS. BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; CDISC RBM Reference Model

attributes.name: alert_severity
attributes.description: Risk-stratified severity level of the alert, driving escalation urgency and response timelines. CRITICAL: immediate action required, potential patient safety or data integrity risk. HIGH: significant risk requiring prompt review within defined SLA. MEDIUM: moderate risk requiring scheduled review. LOW: informational, monitor for trend.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: alert_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the alert within the review and disposition workflow. OPEN: generated and awaiting assignment. UNDER_REVIEW: assigned reviewer is actively assessing. ESCALATED: elevated to on-site visit or senior oversight. CLOSED: reviewed and dispositioned. CANCELLED: determined to be erroneous or duplicate. LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: alert_type
attributes.description: Classification of the alert by the nature of the triggering condition. KRI_THRESHOLD_BREACH: a Key Risk Indicator exceeded its amber or red threshold. DATA_ANOMALY: a data pattern inconsistency detected by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) system. STATISTICAL_OUTLIER: site-level metric is a statistical outlier relative to the study population. MANUAL: alert raised by a central monitor without an automated trigger. ENROLLMENT_SIGNAL: enrollment rate deviation. SAFETY_SIGNAL: potential safety concern flagged centrally. CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category.
attributes.references: TransCelerate RBM Initiative; CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the alert was assigned to a reviewer for investigation. Used to measure assignment SLA compliance from alert generation to assignment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: capa_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) must be initiated as a result of this alert. Set to True when disposition is CAPA_INITIATED or when a confirmed critical finding requires systematic remediation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl CAPA; FDA 21 CFR Part 820; ISO 14155

attributes.name: consecutive_breach_count
attributes.description: Number of consecutive computation cycles in which the triggering KRI has breached its threshold at this site prior to and including this alert. A higher count indicates a persistent risk pattern and informs escalation urgency.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this alert record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer. Distinct from alert_generated_timestamp which captures the business event time. RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: disposition
attributes.description: Action decision made following review of the alert. ESCALATE_ONSITE_VISIT: alert severity warrants an unscheduled or triggered on-site monitoring visit. REMOTE_FOLLOW_UP: issue to be addressed via remote monitoring or site communication. NO_ACTION_REQUIRED: alert reviewed and no further action needed. CAPA_INITIATED: a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) has been opened. PROTOCOL_DEVIATION_RAISED: a protocol deviation record has been created. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ESCALATE_ONSITE_VISIT|REMOTE_FOLLOW_UP|NO_ACTION_REQUIRED|CAPA_INITIATED|PROTOCOL_DEVIATION_RAISED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the alert was formally escalated to a higher oversight level. Null when escalation_required is False. Used to track escalation timeliness and compliance with monitoring plan escalation SLAs.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: escalation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this alert has been escalated to a higher level of oversight (e.g., sponsor, Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB), or senior management). True when disposition is ESCALATE_ONSITE_VISIT or when severity is CRITICAL.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: is_repeat_alert
attributes.description: Indicates whether this alert is a recurrence of a previously closed alert for the same KRI and site within the current study. True when a prior alert for the same KRI-site combination was closed and the KRI has breached again, signaling unresolved systemic issues.
attributes.references: TransCelerate RBM Initiative; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: kri_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the specific Key Risk Indicator (KRI) that breached its threshold and triggered this alert (e.g., KRI-AE-001 for adverse event reporting timeliness). Denormalized from the risk_indicator product for alert-level reporting without requiring a join. Null for manually triggered alerts.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: kri_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the Key Risk Indicator (KRI) that triggered the alert (e.g., 'Adverse Event Reporting Timeliness', 'Query Resolution Rate'). Denormalized for alert reporting and dashboard display without requiring a join to the risk_indicator product.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: observed_value
attributes.description: The actual computed value of the Key Risk Indicator (KRI) or data signal at the time the alert was generated. Compared against threshold_value to confirm the breach. QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category per TRANSACTION_HEADER non-monetary role.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: reference_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the data analysis window used by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) system to compute the KRI value that triggered this alert. Together with reference_period_start, defines the exact data window under review.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: reference_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the data analysis window used by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) system to compute the KRI value that triggered this alert. Defines the temporal scope of the anomaly.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: review_completed_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the reviewer completed the assessment and recorded a disposition for the alert. Used to calculate review cycle time and SLA compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: review_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the assigned reviewer must complete the review and disposition of the alert, as defined by the monitoring plan SLA for the given alert severity level.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: review_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text narrative entered by the reviewer documenting the findings, rationale for the review outcome, and justification for the chosen disposition. Supports audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: review_outcome
attributes.description: Conclusion reached by the reviewer after investigating the alert. CONFIRMED: the anomaly or KRI breach is genuine and requires action. FALSE_POSITIVE: the alert was triggered in error or the signal is not clinically meaningful. INCONCLUSIVE: insufficient data to determine; requires further monitoring. PENDING: review not yet completed.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); TransCelerate RBM Initiative; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the originating operational system (Oracle Siebel CTMS or CSM engine) for this alert. Enables lineage tracing and reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the system of record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: sponsor_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sponsor was formally notified of this alert. Null when sponsor_notified is False. Used to verify compliance with sponsor notification SLAs defined in the monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: sponsor_notified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the study sponsor has been formally notified of this alert, as required for critical or high-severity alerts under the monitoring plan and sponsor oversight obligations per ICH E6(R2).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

attributes.name: threshold_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the breached threshold was the amber (warning) or red (action-required) threshold level as defined in the monitoring plan. Drives escalation logic and response SLA.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: The amber or red threshold value that was breached at the time the alert was generated. Captured at alert generation time to preserve the threshold configuration in effect, as thresholds may be revised over the study lifecycle.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2); TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: trigger_source
attributes.description: System or process that generated the alert. AUTOMATED_CSM: centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) engine. MANUAL_ENTRY: entered directly by a central monitor. EDC_INTEGRATION: triggered by Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system data feed (e.g., Medidata Rave). CTMS_RULE: rule-based trigger from Oracle Siebel CTMS. SAFETY_SYSTEM: triggered from Oracle Argus Safety integration.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Medidata Rave

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit in which the observed_value and threshold_value are expressed (e.g., 'percent', 'days', 'count', 'ratio'). Required for correct interpretation of the KRI metric values in alert review and reporting.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this alert record was last modified in the Databricks Silver Layer, capturing status changes, review updates, and disposition entries. RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2)

products.name: checklist_item
products.description: Master reference table for checklist_item. Referenced by checklist_item_id.

attributes.name: checklist_item_id
attributes.description: Primary key for checklist_item

attributes.name: checklist_template_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the checklist template to which this item belongs, linking items to their parent monitoring checklist definition.

attributes.name: parent_item_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to a parent checklist item, enabling hierarchical checklist structures with sub-items.

attributes.name: applicable_phase
attributes.description: The clinical trial phase(s) for which this checklist item is applicable, as different phases may have varying monitoring requirements.

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date when this checklist item was formally approved for use in monitoring activities, per quality management review processes.

attributes.name: capa_trigger
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether non-compliance on this item automatically initiates a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) workflow.

attributes.name: category
attributes.description: High-level classification category grouping the checklist item by monitoring focus area such as regulatory compliance, patient safety, or data quality.

attributes.name: code
attributes.description: Unique business code assigned to the checklist item for identification in monitoring workflows and CTMS systems.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this checklist item record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements for GCP compliance.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the checklist item explaining the monitoring task, verification requirement, or assessment criteria.

attributes.name: deviation_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the type of deviation that would be recorded if this checklist item is found non-compliant during monitoring.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this checklist item version becomes effective and available for inclusion in monitoring visit checklists.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date until which this checklist item version remains effective. Null indicates the item is currently active with no planned retirement.

attributes.name: escalation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a non-compliant finding on this checklist item automatically triggers an escalation workflow or CAPA initiation.

attributes.name: expected_response
attributes.description: The expected or compliant response value for this checklist item, used to auto-flag deviations when actual responses differ.

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.description: How frequently this checklist item should be assessed during the course of monitoring a clinical trial site.

attributes.name: guidance_text
attributes.description: Instructional guidance or help text provided to CRAs explaining how to properly assess or complete this checklist item during monitoring.

attributes.name: is_critical_to_quality
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this checklist item is designated as Critical to Quality (CtQ) per the study risk assessment, requiring heightened monitoring attention.

attributes.name: is_mandatory
attributes.description: Indicates whether this checklist item must be completed during every applicable monitoring visit or if it can be optionally skipped by the CRA.

attributes.name: item_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of monitoring action required: verification (source data check), assessment (judgment-based), confirmation (yes/no), collection (document retrieval), or observation (visual inspection).

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this checklist item definition, supporting change tracking and version control.

attributes.name: monitoring_method
attributes.description: The monitoring method for which this checklist item is applicable, supporting risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategies that combine on-site, remote, and centralized approaches.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or title of the checklist item as displayed to Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) during monitoring visits.

attributes.name: region_applicability
attributes.description: Geographic region or country codes where this checklist item is applicable, supporting multi-regional trial monitoring with jurisdiction-specific requirements.

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation to the specific regulatory requirement, guideline section, or standard operating procedure (SOP) that mandates this checklist item.

attributes.name: requires_documentation
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether completion of this checklist item requires supporting documentation or evidence to be attached to the monitoring visit report.

attributes.name: response_type
attributes.description: Defines the expected response format when a CRA completes this checklist item during a monitoring visit.

attributes.name: retired_date
attributes.description: Date when this checklist item was retired from active use, maintaining historical reference while preventing inclusion in new monitoring checklists.

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: Risk classification of the checklist item indicating the severity level if the item is found non-compliant, aligned with risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategy.

attributes.name: sdv_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this checklist item requires source data verification against original patient records or source documents.

attributes.name: section_name
attributes.description: The section or sub-grouping within the monitoring checklist where this item is organized, enabling structured checklist navigation.

attributes.name: sort_order
attributes.description: Numeric sequence defining the display order of this checklist item within its parent checklist or category grouping.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this checklist item definition originates, such as Oracle Siebel CTMS or other clinical trial management systems.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the checklist item in the master reference table, controlling its availability for use in monitoring visit checklists.

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The therapeutic area or disease indication for which this checklist item is specifically relevant, if not universally applicable across all studies.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for the checklist item definition, supporting version control as monitoring requirements evolve across protocol amendments.

attributes.name: visit_type_applicability
attributes.description: Indicates which type of monitoring visit this checklist item applies to: site initiation visit (SIV), interim monitoring visit (IMV), close-out visit (COV), or all visit types.

attributes.name: weight_score
attributes.description: Numeric weighting factor assigned to this checklist item for calculating overall site compliance scores in risk-based monitoring analytics.

attributes.name: parent_checklist_item_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on checklist_item (parent_checklist_item_id)

attributes.name: analysis_type

attributes.name: approval_date

attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 4; FDA Statistical Guidance; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: authoring_system

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: blinding_status

'blinded' means the SAP was finalized before unblinding; 'unblinded' means finalized post-unblinding (e.g., for final CSR); 'partially_unblinded' applies to interim analyses with limited unblinding. Critical for regulatory integrity.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 4.1; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; EMA Reflection Paper on Methodological Issues

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this SAP record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: dbl_date
attributes.description: Date on which the clinical database was locked (DBL) for the analysis covered by this SAP. The SAP must be approved prior to or on this date for confirmatory analyses. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Database Lock; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: dsmb_review_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Review Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SAP includes or supports interim analyses to be reviewed by a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC). Drives interim analysis planning and blinding procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees; EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: Date from which this SAP version is considered effective and binding for statistical analyses. Typically the approval date. Supports version history and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: Date on which this SAP version was superseded by a newer version or retired. Null for the currently active version. Supports version history management and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: estimand_description
attributes.description: Description of the treatment effect estimand(s) as defined per ICH E9(R1), including the population, variable (endpoint), intercurrent events handling strategy, and summary measure. Mandatory for SAPs submitted to FDA and EMA under ICH E9(R1) framework.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis; EMA Reflection Paper on Estimands

attributes.name: interim_analysis_count
attributes.description: Number of pre-specified interim analyses planned for this study as defined in the SAP. Zero if no interim analyses are planned. Drives alpha spending function selection and DSMB/DMC meeting scheduling.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees

attributes.name: is_current_version
attributes.description: Indicates whether this record represents the currently active and approved version of the SAP for the study. Only one version per study should have this flag set to True at any given time.
attributes.references: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records

attributes.name: itt_population_definition
attributes.description: Formal definition of the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population as specified in the SAP, including inclusion/exclusion criteria for subjects in this population. The ITT population is the primary analysis population for most confirmatory trials per ICH E9.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.2.2; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle; EMA Guideline on Missing Data

attributes.name: missing_data_strategy
attributes.description: Pre-specified strategy for handling missing data in the primary and key secondary analyses (e.g., multiple imputation, LOCF (Last Observation Carried Forward), MMRM, tipping point analysis). Regulatory agencies require explicit pre-specification of missing data approaches.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; EMA Guideline on Missing Data; FDA Guidance on Missing Data

attributes.name: multiplicity_adjustment_method
attributes.description: Statistical method used to control the family-wise error rate (FWER) or false discovery rate (FDR) when testing multiple hypotheses (e.g., Bonferroni, Holm, Hochberg, Dunnett, hierarchical testing, Benjamini-Hochberg). Required for confirmatory trials with multiple endpoints or doses.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.6; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues in Clinical Trials; FDA Multiple Endpoints Guidance

attributes.name: power_percent
attributes.description: Pre-specified statistical power (1 - beta) expressed as a percentage (e.g., 80.00, 90.00) used in the sample size calculation. Represents the probability of detecting a true treatment effect of the assumed magnitude.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 3.5; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: pp_population_definition
attributes.description: Formal definition of the Per Protocol (PP) analysis population as specified in the SAP, including criteria for protocol deviations that would exclude subjects. Used as a sensitivity analysis population alongside ITT.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.2.3; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Populations

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_description
attributes.description: Full narrative definition of the primary efficacy or safety endpoint as specified in the SAP, including the outcome measure, timepoint, and measurement scale. Aligned with the study protocol and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 2.2; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

attributes.name: primary_statistical_method
attributes.description: Description of the primary statistical methodology applied to the primary endpoint analysis (e.g., ANCOVA, mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM), Cox proportional hazards, logistic regression). Sourced from SAS Drug Development SAP authoring.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.3; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Missing Data

attributes.name: regulatory_impact
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory impact of this SAP version or amendment. 'none' for administrative changes; 'minor' for non-material updates; 'major' for changes affecting primary analysis; 'requires_submission' for changes requiring regulatory notification or submission.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_alignment
attributes.description: Identifies the regulatory submission type(s) this SAP is aligned to support (e.g., IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, eCTD). Ensures the SAP meets the statistical requirements of the target regulatory agency. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|NDA|BLA|MAA|CTD|eCTD|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); FDA 21 CFR Part 601 (BLA); EMA MAA Guidelines; ICH CTD M4S

attributes.name: safety_population_definition
attributes.description: Formal definition of the safety analysis population as specified in the SAP, typically all randomized subjects who received at least one dose of study treatment. Used for all safety and adverse event analyses.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E6(R2); CTCAE v5.0

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Total number of subjects planned for enrollment as specified in the SAP sample size calculation section. Derived from power calculations and protocol-specified assumptions. Used for enrollment tracking and regulatory review.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 3.5; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; EMA Guideline on Sample Size

attributes.name: sap_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable identifier for the SAP document, typically assigned by the sponsor or CRO (e.g., SAP-STUDY001-001). Used for regulatory submissions and cross-system referencing in Veeva Vault and SAS Drug Development.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance on Reporting Results from Studies Evaluating Psychiatric Drugs

attributes.name: secondary_endpoint_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of all pre-specified secondary endpoints as defined in the SAP. May include multiple endpoints listed in priority order. Supports regulatory review and CSR statistical sections.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 2.2; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints

attributes.name: sections_modified
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or narrative description of SAP sections that were modified in this amendment (e.g., 'Section 3.1 Primary Endpoint, Section 5.2 Multiplicity Adjustment'). Supports change impact assessment and regulatory review.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: sensitivity_analysis_description
attributes.description: Description of pre-specified sensitivity analyses designed to assess the robustness of primary analysis conclusions to key assumptions (e.g., missing data assumptions, outlier handling, covariate selection). Required per ICH E9(R1).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 5; FDA Guidance on Sensitivity Analysis; EMA Guideline on Missing Data

attributes.name: significance_level
attributes.description: Pre-specified two-sided alpha level for hypothesis testing (e.g., 0.0500 for 5%). Defines the threshold for declaring statistical significance. May be adjusted for multiplicity. Stored as a decimal fraction.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.6; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Full descriptive title of the Statistical Analysis Plan document, typically including the study name, indication, and phase (e.g., 'Statistical Analysis Plan for a Phase III Randomized Controlled Trial of Drug X in Indication Y').
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SAP Template

attributes.name: tlf_specifications
attributes.description: Reference to or summary of the Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLF) shells or specifications associated with this SAP. Defines the outputs to be produced by the statistical programming team in SAS Drug Development for the CSR.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E3 Structure of Clinical Study Reports

attributes.name: unblinding_date
attributes.description: Date on which the study blind was broken for the analysis covered by this SAP version. Null if the SAP was finalized while the study remained blinded. Supports regulatory audit trail for pre-specification of analyses.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 4.1; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this SAP record. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles. Used for change detection in ETL pipelines.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier of the SAP document following semantic versioning convention (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0). Incremented with each amendment. Supports version history tracking and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: version_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this SAP version. 'draft' indicates authoring in progress; 'in_review' indicates under biostatistics or sponsor review; 'approved' indicates final sign-off obtained; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer version; 'retired' indicates withdrawn.

attributes.name: amendment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the SAP amendment document. Tracks progression from authoring through approval and eventual supersession by a later amendment.

attributes.name: amendment_title
attributes.description: Descriptive title of the SAP amendment summarizing the primary change (e.g., 'Amendment 1: Revised Primary Endpoint Analysis Population'). Used in document headers and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance

attributes.name: amendment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the amendment scope: major (changes to primary/key secondary endpoints, analysis populations, or statistical methods), minor (clarifications or secondary analysis changes), or administrative (formatting, typo corrections, contact updates).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity

attributes.name: amendment_version_code
attributes.description: Human-readable version label for the amended SAP document (e.g., v1.1, v2.0, v3.1). Aligns with document management versioning conventions in Veeva Vault eTMF.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault Document Management; ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: analysis_population_changed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this amendment modifies the definition of any analysis population (e.g., Intent-to-Treat (ITT), Per Protocol (PP), Safety population). Population changes affect the integrity of the statistical inference.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance; CDISC ADaM ADSL

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the SAP amendment received final approval from the responsible statistician and sponsor. This is the effective date from which the amended analysis plan governs study conduct.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; MasterControl

attributes.name: approver_name
attributes.description: Full name of the responsible statistician or biostatistics director who approved this SAP amendment. Captured at time of approval for regulatory audit trail integrity.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: author_name
attributes.description: Full name of the biostatistician or statistical programmer who authored this SAP amendment. Captured at time of authorship for audit trail integrity per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: authored_date
attributes.description: Date on which the SAP amendment was completed by the author and submitted for review. Establishes the contemporaneous authorship timestamp per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E9

attributes.name: blinding_impact
attributes.description: Assessment of whether this amendment has any impact on study blinding integrity. Amendments that require access to unblinded data must be documented and controlled to prevent bias.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; EMA Reflection Paper on Methodological Issues

attributes.name: change_summary
attributes.description: Concise executive summary of all changes introduced by this amendment, suitable for inclusion in the Clinical Study Report (CSR) statistical section and regulatory submission cover letter.
attributes.references: ICH E3 CSR Structure; ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: dbl_date
attributes.description: Date on which the clinical database was locked at the time this amendment was classified. Used to determine pre- vs. post-DBL status and regulatory impact.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on DBL; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: dsmb_notification_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Notification Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DSMB/DMC must be notified of this SAP amendment, particularly when interim analysis plans or stopping rules are modified.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this SAP amendment becomes operationally effective and supersedes the prior version. May differ from approval date if a transition period is required.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance; Veeva Vault Document Management

attributes.name: interim_analysis_changed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this amendment modifies the interim analysis plan, including timing, stopping rules, alpha spending, or DSMB/DMC charter alignment.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: irb_iec_notification_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Notification Required Flag

attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 56; ICH E6(R2) Section 3; OHRP Regulations; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: missing_data_method_changed

attributes.name: pre_dbl_flag

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_changed

attributes.name: randomization_scheme_changed

attributes.name: regulatory_impact_assessment

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_required

attributes.name: review_completed_date

attributes.name: sample_size_changed

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The date from which this version of the analysis population definition became effective, supporting SAP amendment versioning. Enables temporal tracking of population definition changes across SAP versions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The date on which this version of the analysis population definition was superseded or retired, supporting SAP amendment versioning. Null if this is the current active version.
attributes.references: ICH E9; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: exclusion_criteria_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the criteria that would exclude a subject from this analysis population despite meeting inclusion criteria (e.g., major protocol deviations, missing primary endpoint data). Defined in the SAP.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; ICH E3

attributes.name: inclusion_criteria_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the criteria a subject must meet to be included in this analysis population, as defined in the SAP. Captures the logical rules (e.g., randomized and received at least one dose of study drug).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: missing_endpoint_handling
attributes.description: The pre-specified method for handling missing primary endpoint data for subjects in this population, as defined in the SAP (e.g., LOCF - Last Observation Carried Forward, multiple imputation, observed cases only). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: locf|bocf|wocf|multiple_imputation|observed_cases|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.4; FDA Guidance on Missing Data; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for biostatistician notes, clarifications, or amendments related to this analysis population definition. May capture DSMB/DMC recommendations, protocol amendment impacts, or sponsor queries.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: planned_sample_size
attributes.description: The pre-specified planned number of subjects for this analysis population as determined by the sample size calculation in the SAP. Serves as the denominator benchmark for enrollment tracking and power calculations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; FDA Guidance on Sample Size; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: population_code
attributes.description: Short, unique alphanumeric code identifying the analysis population within the study (e.g., ITT, PP, SAF, MITT, PK). Used as the CDISC ADaM ADSL flag variable name prefix and in TLF shell headers.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; CDISC ADSL

attributes.name: population_finalized_date
attributes.description: The date on which the analysis population definition was formally finalized and approved in the SAP, prior to unblinding. Supports pre-specification audit trail for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Pre-specification

attributes.name: population_logic_summary
attributes.description: Concise programmatic or pseudo-code summary of the population derivation logic used in SAS Drug Development ADaM programming (e.g., RANDFL='Y' AND DOSEFL='Y'). Bridges the narrative SAP definition and the SAS implementation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development Best Practices

attributes.name: population_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the analysis population as defined in the SAP (e.g., Intent-to-Treat Population, Per Protocol Population, Safety Population, Modified Intent-to-Treat Population, Pharmacokinetic Population).
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: population_rationale
attributes.description: Scientific and regulatory rationale for defining this analysis population, as documented in the SAP. Explains why this population is appropriate for the associated analysis objectives and how it aligns with regulatory guidance.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E3 Section 9.7; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: population_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the analysis population definition. Tracks progression from initial SAP drafting through biostatistics review, approval, and potential supersession by an amended SAP version.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: population_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the analysis population by its primary analytical purpose. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: efficacy|safety|pharmacokinetic|pharmacodynamic|per_protocol|modified_itt|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: primary_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this population is designated as the primary analysis population for the study as specified in the SAP. The primary population drives the primary efficacy endpoint analysis and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.2; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_exclusion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether subjects with major protocol deviations are excluded from this analysis population. Typically True for Per Protocol (PP) populations and False for ITT populations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2); CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: randomization_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether randomization is a mandatory inclusion criterion for subjects in this analysis population. True for ITT and most efficacy populations; may be False for screening failure or safety populations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: regulatory_primary_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this population is the pre-specified primary population for regulatory submission purposes (NDA/BLA/MAA). Distinct from internal primary flag; reflects the population declared in the IND/protocol.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: sap_section_reference
attributes.description: The specific section number or identifier within the SAP document that formally defines this analysis population (e.g., Section 5.2.1). Enables direct traceability from the data product to the governing statistical document.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E3; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: sap_version
attributes.description: Version number of the SAP document in which this analysis population definition was introduced or last amended (e.g., v1.0, v2.1). Supports version-controlled traceability for regulatory audit.
attributes.references: ICH E9; Veeva Vault eTMF versioning; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: sas_program_name
attributes.description: Name of the SAS Drug Development program used to derive and validate the ADSL flag variable for this analysis population (e.g., adsl.sas). Enables traceability from population definition to the validated SAS code.
attributes.references: SAS Drug Development; CDISC ADaM; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: sensitivity_analysis_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this population is designated as a sensitivity analysis population (as opposed to a primary or secondary analysis population). Sensitivity populations test the robustness of primary analysis conclusions.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.8; FDA Guidance on Sensitivity Analyses

attributes.name: subject_count_at_dbl
attributes.description: The number of subjects assigned to this analysis population at the time of Database Lock (DBL). This is the final, locked count used in the Clinical Study Report (CSR) and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH E3 Section 10.1; CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on DBL

attributes.name: subject_count_interim
attributes.description: Number of subjects assigned to this analysis population at the most recent interim analysis cut, if applicable. Used by the DSMB/DMC for interim review and blinded/unblinded reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; DSMB Charter

attributes.name: submission_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this analysis population is included in the regulatory submission package (NDA/BLA/MAA/eCTD). Populations marked True must have fully validated ADaM datasets and TLF outputs.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4E (CTD Module 5)

attributes.name: tlf_shell_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLF) Shell Reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier(s) for the TLF shells that use this analysis population as their denominator or subject set. Links the population definition to the output specifications in the SAP/TLF shell document.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM; ICH E3; SAS Drug Development TLF Specifications

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this analysis population record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Current validation status of the SAS programming for this analysis population's ADSL flag variable in SAS Drug Development. Tracks QC progress from initial programming through double-programming validation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; GCP ICH E6(R2)

Captures study phase, primary endpoint type, assumed effect size, standard deviation, alpha level, power, dropout rate, allocation ratio, calculated sample size per arm, total enrollment target, software used (e.g., PASS, nQuery), and version. Supports regulatory submission and protocol amendments.
products.reference: Sample Size Calculation — ICH E9, FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: sample_size_calc_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each sample size calculation record within the biostatistics domain.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: analysis_population_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to biostatistics.analysis_population. Business justification: sample_size_calc has analysis_population (STRING) indicating which population the sample size calculation targets. Normalizing to a FK to analysis_population.analysis_population_id enforces referentia
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: approved_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Sample size calculations require a named approving statistician for protocol and regulatory submission documentation. Linking to workforce.employee enables GCP training verification and inspection-rea
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: pipeline_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sponsor.pipeline_asset. Business justification: Sample size assumptions (effect_size, dropout_rate, event_rate_control) are derived from the pipeline asset's prior clinical data and development phase. Sponsors review sample size calculations at por
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific protocol version under which this sample size calculation was conducted, supporting traceability to protocol amendments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: rand_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to randomization.rand_scheme. Business justification: Sample size calculations depend directly on the randomization scheme's allocation_ratio, block structure, and stratification. Regulatory submissions require sample size justification to reference the
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: sap_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) document that governs or references this sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this sample size calculation was performed.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: accrual_period_months
attributes.description: The assumed patient accrual (enrollment) period in months, used in time-to-event sample size calculations to determine the number of events required.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: allocation_ratio
attributes.description: The randomization allocation ratio between treatment arms (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'), specifying the relative number of subjects assigned to each arm.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM Randomization Standards

attributes.name: alpha_level
attributes.description: The pre-specified Type I error rate (significance level, alpha) used in the sample size calculation, typically 0.05 for two-sided or 0.025 for one-sided tests.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity

attributes.name: alpha_spending_method
attributes.description: The alpha-spending function applied to control Type I error across planned interim analyses (e.g., O'Brien-Fleming, Pocock, Lan-DeMets). Null or 'none' if no interim analysis is planned.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Narrative justification for revising a prior version of the sample size calculation, such as updated assumptions from interim data, protocol amendment, or regulatory feedback.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Protocol Amendment Guidance; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sample size calculation was formally approved by the responsible biostatistician, marking readiness for inclusion in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: calc_date
attributes.description: The date on which this sample size calculation was performed or finalized, serving as the principal business event date for regulatory traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: calc_identifier
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code or reference number assigned to this sample size calculation, used in regulatory submissions and protocol documentation (e.g., SSC-2024-001).
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Sample Size Calculations

attributes.name: calc_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sample size calculation record, from initial draft through regulatory approval to archival.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: calc_version
attributes.description: Version number of this sample size calculation (e.g., v1.0, v2.1), enabling tracking of revisions driven by protocol amendments or updated assumptions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this sample size calculation record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: dropout_rate
attributes.description: The assumed proportion of enrolled subjects expected to discontinue or be lost to follow-up, used to inflate the calculated sample size to ensure adequate evaluable subjects.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Missing Data in Clinical Trials

attributes.name: effect_size
attributes.description: The clinically meaningful difference or effect size assumed between treatment arms (e.g., mean difference, odds ratio, hazard ratio) used as the basis for the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Sample Size Calculations

attributes.name: effect_size_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the assumed effect size (e.g., mmHg, %, hazard ratio, odds ratio, mean difference), providing dimensional context for regulatory interpretation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM Unit Standards

attributes.name: event_rate_control
attributes.description: The assumed event rate or response rate in the control arm, applicable for binary or time-to-event endpoints. Null for continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: event_rate_treatment
attributes.description: The assumed event rate or response rate in the treatment arm, applicable for binary or time-to-event endpoints. Null for continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: follow_up_period_months
attributes.description: The assumed minimum follow-up period in months after the last patient enrolled, used in time-to-event calculations to ensure sufficient events are observed.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance

attributes.name: hypothesis_type
attributes.description: The statistical hypothesis framework applied (superiority, non-inferiority, equivalence), which determines the directionality and margin used in the sample size formula.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10 Choice of Control Group; FDA Non-Inferiority Guidance

attributes.name: interim_analysis_planned
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more interim analyses are planned for this study, which may require alpha-spending adjustments to the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: median_survival_control
attributes.description: The assumed median survival time in the control arm for time-to-event endpoints, used in log-rank or exponential model-based sample size calculations. Null for non-survival endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance

attributes.name: non_inferiority_margin
attributes.description: The pre-specified non-inferiority or equivalence margin (delta) used in the hypothesis test, applicable when hypothesis_type is non_inferiority or equivalence. Null for superiority designs.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10; FDA Non-Inferiority Guidance 2016

attributes.name: number_of_arms
attributes.description: Total number of treatment arms (including control) in the study design, used to determine the allocation structure and multiplicity adjustments.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10

attributes.name: number_of_events_required
attributes.description: The minimum number of primary endpoint events (e.g., deaths, progressions) required to achieve the specified power for time-to-event analyses. Null for non-event-driven endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance; EMA Guideline on Survival Analysis

attributes.name: power
attributes.description: The pre-specified statistical power (1 minus Type II error rate, beta) used in the calculation, representing the probability of detecting the assumed effect size. Typically 0.80 or 0.90.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the primary endpoint used in the sample size calculation (e.g., 'Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24'), providing clinical context for regulatory reviewers.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_type
attributes.description: Statistical nature of the primary efficacy endpoint (e.g., continuous, binary, time-to-event, ordinal, count) that drives the choice of sample size formula.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1) Estimands Addendum; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: reference_source
attributes.description: Citation or reference for the data source used to derive the assumed effect size, standard deviation, or event rate (e.g., published literature citation, prior Phase II study identifier, internal pilot data).
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: sample_size_per_arm
attributes.description: The calculated number of subjects required per treatment arm to achieve the specified power at the given alpha level, accounting for the assumed effect size and standard deviation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: software_name
attributes.description: Name of the validated statistical software used to perform the sample size calculation (e.g., PASS, nQuery Advisor, SAS PROC POWER, R), required for regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E9; CDISC Validation Standards

attributes.name: software_version
attributes.description: Version number of the statistical software used (e.g., PASS 2023, nQuery 9.1), required for reproducibility and regulatory validation documentation.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 820 (software validation)

attributes.name: standard_deviation
attributes.description: The assumed population standard deviation for continuous endpoints, derived from prior studies or literature, used in the sample size formula. Null for non-continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: statistical_method
attributes.description: The specific statistical formula or method used for the calculation (e.g., two-sample t-test, log-rank test, chi-square test, Kaplan-Meier), providing methodological traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: study_design_type
attributes.description: The clinical trial design type (e.g., parallel group, crossover, factorial, adaptive) that determines the statistical methodology applied in the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

attributes.name: study_phase
attributes.description: Clinical development phase of the study (Phase I through Phase IV) for which the sample size is being calculated, influencing regulatory expectations and statistical rigor.
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase II|Phase IIa|Phase IIb|Phase III|Phase IV
attributes.references: ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Trials; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: test_sidedness
attributes.description: Specifies whether the statistical test is one-sided or two-sided, directly affecting the critical value and resulting sample size.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: total_enrollment_target
attributes.description: The total number of subjects to be enrolled (randomized) after inflating the total sample size by the assumed dropout rate, representing the actual recruitment target submitted in the protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: total_sample_size
attributes.description: The total number of subjects required across all treatment arms before applying the dropout inflation, representing the minimum evaluable sample.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this sample size calculation record was most recently modified, supporting version control and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: change_reason

attributes.name: codelist_name
