attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context about the sponsor organization including strategic relationship notes, special handling instructions, or historical background not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: org_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sponsor organization record. Controls whether new studies can be initiated with this sponsor and whether existing engagements remain operationally active.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: org_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the sponsor organization by entity type. Drives regulatory pathway selection, contract templates, and reporting obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pharmaceutical|biotech|academic|government|non_profit|medical_device — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: preferred_edc_system
attributes.description: Sponsor's preferred Electronic Data Capture (EDC) platform for clinical data collection. Informs technology stack decisions for study setup in Medidata Rave or Oracle Clinical One and impacts eCRF build timelines.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC; Oracle Clinical One; CDISC CDASH; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: preferred_etmf_system
attributes.business_glossary_term: Preferred Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) System
attributes.description: Sponsor's preferred Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) platform for document management and regulatory archival. Determines integration requirements with Veeva Vault eTMF and document exchange protocols.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; TMF Reference Model; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: Primary operational email address for the sponsor organization used for study-related communications, regulatory notifications, and CRO engagement. Classified as confidential organizational contact data.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; GDPR Article 4; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary telephone number for the sponsor organization's main point of contact. Used for urgent safety communications, regulatory escalations, and operational coordination.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: regulatory_strategy_region
attributes.description: Geographic regulatory strategy scope for the sponsor's clinical development program. Determines which regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA, PMDA, TGA, Health Canada) are engaged and which submission pathways apply.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); PMDA; TGA; Health Canada

attributes.name: safety_reporting_contact_email
attributes.description: Designated email address for the sponsor's pharmacovigilance or drug safety unit. Used for Serious Adverse Event (SAE), Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), and expedited safety report submissions to Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E2A; Oracle Argus Safety

attributes.name: sap_vendor_code
attributes.description: SAP S/4HANA vendor master record identifier for the sponsor organization. Links the sponsor to financial transactions including accounts receivable (AR), invoicing, and project accounting in the ERP system.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Vendor Master; SOX

attributes.name: stock_exchange
attributes.description: Primary stock exchange on which the sponsor organization's shares are listed. Relevant for SOX compliance scope and financial reporting obligations.
attributes.references: SOX; SEC; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: stock_ticker
attributes.description: Exchange-listed stock ticker symbol for publicly traded sponsor organizations. Used for financial monitoring, SOX compliance tracking, and market intelligence.
attributes.references: SOX; SEC; NYSE/NASDAQ listing standards

attributes.name: tax_number
attributes.description: Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) or equivalent national tax identifier for the sponsor organization. Required for SAP S/4HANA financial transactions, contract execution, and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA; IRS EIN; SOX; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: trade_name
attributes.description: Operating or brand name of the sponsor organization, which may differ from the legal name. Used in commercial communications, CTMS records, and sponsor-facing correspondence.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the sponsor organization record. Supports change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: website_url
attributes.description: Official public website URL of the sponsor organization. Used for due diligence, pipeline research, and sponsor profile enrichment.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: who_universal_trial_number_prefix
attributes.business_glossary_term: World Health Organization (WHO) Universal Trial Number Prefix
attributes.description: WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) assigned prefix for the sponsor organization, used to construct Universal Trial Numbers (UTN) for WHO-registered studies.
attributes.references: WHO ICTRP; ICMJE Clinical Trial Registration Policy

products.name: org_hierarchy
products.description: Defines parent-child corporate hierarchy relationships among sponsor organizations, capturing subsidiary, affiliate, and division structures. Tracks relationship type (parent, subsidiary, affiliate, division, joint-venture), effective dates, ownership percentage, controlling entity flag, and hierarchy depth level. Enables roll-up reporting across sponsor corporate families and supports multi-national sponsor structures where regional entities contract independently.
products.reference: Corporate Hierarchy / Sponsor Affiliate Structure

attributes.name: org_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each parent-child corporate hierarchy relationship record within the sponsor organization structure.
attributes.references: ISO 11179 Data Element Naming Convention

attributes.name: child_org_organization_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the child sponsor organization in this hierarchy relationship. References the subordinate entity (e.g., subsidiary, affiliate, regional division, or joint-venture partner).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: primary_organization_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent sponsor organization in this hierarchy relationship. References the superior entity in the corporate structure (e.g., ultimate parent, holding company, or intermediate parent).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: tertiary_workday_org_organization_id
attributes.description: Organization identifier in Workday HCM corresponding to the child entity. Enables workforce planning, headcount roll-up, and talent management data to be aligned with the sponsor corporate hierarchy.
attributes.references: Workday HCM; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the organizational hierarchy relationship was formally approved by the designated authority. Distinct from the effective start date, which reflects when the relationship became operationally active.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual or governance body that approved the establishment or modification of this organizational hierarchy relationship (e.g., Chief Legal Officer, Corporate Governance Committee). Supports SOX and GCP audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: change_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the business reason for creating or modifying this hierarchy relationship record (e.g., 'Acquisition of regional affiliate', 'Corporate restructuring post-merger', 'Divestiture of oncology division'). Supports audit trail requirements under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: consolidation_scope
attributes.description: Indicates how the child organization's financials are consolidated into the parent's financial statements per IFRS 10 / US GAAP ASC 810. Full = 100% consolidation; Proportional = pro-rata by ownership; Equity method = single-line investment; Excluded = not consolidated (e.g., held-for-sale).
attributes.references: IFRS 10; US GAAP ASC 810; SOX Section 302; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: contracting_entity_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the child organization is authorized to independently execute clinical trial contracts and CRO agreements on behalf of the sponsor corporate family. True = can contract independently; False = contracts flow through parent entity. Critical for multi-national sponsor structures.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the child organization's primary jurisdiction of incorporation or operation. Supports multi-national sponsor structure analysis and regulatory jurisdiction mapping (FDA, EMA, PMDA, TGA, Health Canada, MHRA).
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH E6(R2); EMA EU CTR 536/2014; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this organizational hierarchy relationship record was first created in the Silver Layer data product. Supports audit trail requirements under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: ctms_org_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Organization Code
attributes.description: Organization identifier assigned to the child entity within Oracle Siebel CTMS. Used for cross-referencing sponsor hierarchy records with study portfolio, site management, and monitoring visit data in the CTMS.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: data_sharing_agreement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal data sharing agreement exists between the parent and child organization governing the exchange of clinical trial data, safety data, and regulatory submissions. Relevant for GDPR, HIPAA, and ICH E6(R2) data governance compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 26 (Joint Controllers); HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the parent-child organizational relationship ceased to be effective. Null indicates an open-ended, currently active relationship. Supports bi-temporal modeling and historical hierarchy queries.
attributes.references: IFRS 10; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the parent-child organizational relationship became legally or operationally effective. Used for temporal filtering and historical hierarchy reconstruction.
attributes.references: IFRS 10; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: gdpr_data_controller_role
attributes.description: Defines the GDPR data controller/processor role of the child organization relative to the parent for clinical trial subject data. Controller = determines purposes and means; Joint Controller = shared determination; Processor = processes on behalf of controller. Drives data processing agreement requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4, 26, 28; ICH E6(R2); EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth level of the child organization within the corporate hierarchy tree. Level 1 represents a direct subsidiary of the ultimate parent; higher values indicate deeper nesting. Enables efficient tree traversal and roll-up aggregation across sponsor corporate families.
attributes.references: ISO 15926 Industrial Data; IFRS 10

attributes.name: hierarchy_path
attributes.description: Materialized path string representing the full ancestry chain from the ultimate parent to the child organization, using a delimiter-separated list of organization IDs (e.g., '1001/1045/1078'). Enables efficient subtree queries and hierarchy visualization without recursive joins.
attributes.references: ISO 15926; IFRS 10

attributes.name: hierarchy_version
attributes.description: Monotonically incrementing version number for this hierarchy relationship record, supporting optimistic concurrency control and change history tracking. Incremented each time the relationship attributes are updated.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 (Audit Trail); ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+

attributes.name: ind_holder_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the child organization holds or co-holds an Investigational New Drug (IND) application or equivalent regulatory authorization (e.g., CTA in EU) in its own name. Relevant for regulatory accountability and submission ownership tracking.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: is_controlling_entity
attributes.description: Indicates whether the parent organization exercises control over the child organization as defined by IFRS 10 (power over investee, exposure to variable returns, ability to use power to affect returns). True = controlling; False = non-controlling interest.
attributes.references: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: is_primary_path
attributes.description: Indicates whether this relationship represents the primary (canonical) reporting path for the child organization when multiple parent relationships exist (e.g., matrix structures or dual-reporting affiliates). True = primary path used for standard roll-up; False = secondary or alternate path.
attributes.references: IFRS 10; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional contextual information about the organizational hierarchy relationship not captured in structured fields (e.g., special contractual arrangements, regulatory carve-outs, transition notes during M&A activity).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: ownership_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of equity ownership held by the parent organization in the child organization, expressed as a decimal value between 0.00 and 100.00. Critical for determining consolidation thresholds under IFRS 10 and for sponsor financial roll-up reporting. Classified confidential as it reflects proprietary corporate financial structure.
attributes.references: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SEC Regulation S-K Item 601; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: pipeline_scope
attributes.description: Defines the breadth of the sponsor's drug development pipeline that the child organization is responsible for managing or contracting. Supports portfolio analytics and CRO engagement planning across the sponsor corporate family.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Primary regulatory authority governing the child organization's clinical trial activities (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA, TGA, MHRA, Health Canada). Determines applicable regulatory submission requirements and GCP compliance frameworks for studies contracted through this entity.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); PMDA; TGA; MHRA; Health Canada

attributes.name: relationship_basis
attributes.description: The legal or operational basis underpinning the parent-child relationship. Equity = share ownership; Contractual = agreement-based control without equity; Regulatory = regulatory-mandated grouping; Operational = functional reporting without legal ownership; Statutory = legally mandated structure.
attributes.references: IFRS 10; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: relationship_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this hierarchy relationship, used for cross-system referencing in Oracle Siebel CTMS, SAP S/4HANA, and regulatory submissions. Follows the sponsor organization's internal coding convention.
attributes.references: ISO 11179; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: relationship_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the parent-child organizational relationship. Drives whether the relationship is included in active roll-up reporting and sponsor portfolio consolidation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; IFRS 10

attributes.name: relationship_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the corporate relationship between the parent and child organization. Drives roll-up logic and reporting scope. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: parent|subsidiary|affiliate|division|joint_venture|licensee|branch|representative_office — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
attributes.references: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SEC Regulation S-K; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: sap_company_code
attributes.description: Four-character SAP S/4HANA company code assigned to the child organization for financial accounting, accounts payable/receivable, and project accounting. Enables direct linkage between the organizational hierarchy and financial ledger entries in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; SOX Section 302; IFRS 10

attributes.name: source_record_reference
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the source operational system (e.g., Siebel CTMS account relationship ID, SAP company code pairing key). Enables reverse traceability from the Silver Layer back to the originating system record for reconciliation and audit.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this hierarchy relationship record was sourced or last updated. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across Oracle Siebel CTMS, SAP S/4HANA, Workday HCM, and Veeva Vault.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_alignment
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area(s) for which the child organization is responsible within the sponsor corporate family (e.g., Oncology, Cardiovascular, Neuroscience, Immunology). Supports portfolio roll-up reporting and pipeline analysis by therapeutic area across the sponsor hierarchy.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; MedDRA SOC classification

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this organizational hierarchy relationship record was most recently modified in the Silver Layer data product. Supports change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: veeva_account_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the child organization's account record in Veeva Vault, used for eTMF document ownership, regulatory submission tracking, and quality management linkage. Supports traceability between the corporate hierarchy and document management.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: voting_rights_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of voting rights held by the parent organization in the child organization. May differ from ownership percentage in cases of dual-class share structures or contractual voting arrangements. Relevant for regulatory filings and control determination under IFRS 10.
attributes.references: IFRS 10; SEC Regulation S-K; SOX Section 302

products.name: sponsor_contact
products.description: Master record for individual sponsor contacts including medical monitors, project managers, regulatory affairs leads, clinical operations directors, and business development representatives. Captures full name, title, department, role type, primary and secondary email, phone numbers, preferred communication channel, LinkedIn profile, contact status (active, inactive, departed), and the sponsor organization they represent. SSOT for sponsor personnel identity within the CRO relationship.
products.reference: Sponsor Contact / CTMS Contact Record

attributes.name: sponsor_contact_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the sponsor contact record within the CRO's Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS). Primary key for the sponsor_contact master data product.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: organization_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor organization that this contact represents. Links the individual to their parent sponsor entity in the CRO relationship.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: academic_degree
attributes.description: Highest academic or professional degree held by the sponsor contact (e.g., MD, PhD, PharmD, MBA). Relevant for medical monitor qualification verification and regulatory submission authorship.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: contact_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sponsor contact record within the CRO system. 'Active' indicates current engagement; 'inactive' indicates temporarily disengaged; 'departed' indicates the individual has left the sponsor organization; 'on_leave' indicates temporary absence.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country where the sponsor contact is primarily based. Used for regulatory jurisdiction mapping, time zone inference, and regional CRA assignment.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; GDPR; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the sponsor contact record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: ctms_contact_ref
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Contact Reference
attributes.description: The native contact record identifier from Oracle Siebel CTMS, the operational system of record for sponsor contact management. Used for system reconciliation and data lineage tracing.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the originating operational system from which this sponsor contact record was sourced or last updated. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across the CRO's system landscape.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: department
attributes.description: Organizational department within the sponsor company to which this contact belongs (e.g., Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, Business Development). Used for organizational mapping and escalation routing.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: do_not_contact
attributes.description: Indicates that this sponsor contact has requested to not be contacted directly, or has been flagged by the CRO as off-limits for direct outreach. Enforces communication suppression in CTMS and marketing workflows.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17; HIPAA; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: first_name
attributes.description: Given (first) name of the sponsor contact individual. Used for formal correspondence, system display, and CRO-sponsor relationship management.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: gdpr_consent_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Consent Date
attributes.description: Date on which GDPR data processing consent was last obtained or updated for this sponsor contact. Required for audit trail compliance under GDPR Article 7.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: gdpr_consent_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Consent Status
attributes.description: Records the GDPR data processing consent status for this sponsor contact's personal data. Required for contacts based in EU/EEA jurisdictions. 'not_applicable' for contacts outside GDPR scope.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6; GDPR Article 7; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: is_financial_contact
attributes.description: Indicates whether this contact is authorized to receive financial communications including invoices, budget amendments, and payment notifications from SAP S/4HANA finance workflows.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA; SOX; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: is_primary_contact
attributes.description: Indicates whether this individual is the designated primary point of contact for the sponsor organization in the CRO relationship. Only one contact per sponsor should hold this flag as True at any given time.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: is_regulatory_contact
attributes.description: Indicates whether this contact is designated to receive regulatory submission notifications, IND/NDA/BLA/MAA correspondence, and Health Authority query routing. Used by the regulatory affairs team for submission workflow management.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: is_safety_contact
attributes.description: Indicates whether this contact is designated to receive Serious Adverse Event (SAE) and Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) notifications. Drives automated safety reporting distribution in Oracle Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: language_preference
attributes.description: Preferred language for communications with this sponsor contact, expressed as an IETF BCP 47 language tag (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'ja'). Used for localized document delivery and meeting facilitation.
attributes.references: IETF BCP 47; ICH E6(R2); GDPR

attributes.name: last_interaction_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent documented interaction between the CRO and this sponsor contact (e.g., meeting, email exchange, call). Used for relationship health monitoring and CRA engagement tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: last_name
attributes.description: Family (last) name of the sponsor contact individual. Used in combination with first_name for full identity resolution and formal communications.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: linkedin_profile_url
attributes.description: URL to the sponsor contact's LinkedIn professional profile. Used by business development and CRA teams for relationship intelligence, background verification, and professional network mapping.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: middle_name
attributes.description: Middle name or initial of the sponsor contact, used for disambiguation when multiple contacts share the same first and last name within a sponsor organization.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for CRA or CRO staff to record relationship context, communication preferences, background information, or other relevant notes about the sponsor contact. Not for clinical or safety data.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: office_location
attributes.description: Physical office location or site name where the sponsor contact is based (e.g., 'Pfizer - New York HQ', 'Roche - Basel Campus'). Used for logistics, visit planning, and organizational mapping.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: preferred_communication_channel
attributes.description: The sponsor contact's preferred method for receiving communications from the CRO. Drives automated notification routing and meeting scheduling preferences within the CTMS.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: primary_email
attributes.description: Primary business email address for the sponsor contact. Used as the principal digital identifier for all CRO-sponsor communications, system notifications, and regulatory correspondence. SSOT for sponsor personnel identity.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: primary_phone
attributes.description: Primary business telephone number for the sponsor contact in E.164 international format. Used for direct voice communication, urgent safety escalations, and regulatory notifications.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; ITU-T E.164

attributes.name: professional_title
attributes.description: Job title or professional designation of the sponsor contact (e.g., Medical Monitor, Clinical Operations Director, Regulatory Affairs Lead, Project Manager). Reflects the contact's formal role within the sponsor organization.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: role_type
attributes.description: Functional role classification of the sponsor contact within the CRO engagement. Determines communication routing, escalation paths, and system access permissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medical_monitor|project_manager|regulatory_affairs|clinical_operations|business_development|pharmacovigilance|data_management|biostatistics|quality_assurance|finance — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: salutation
attributes.description: Formal salutation or honorific prefix for the sponsor contact (e.g., Dr., Mr., Ms., Prof.). Used in formal written correspondence, regulatory submissions, and meeting invitations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: secondary_email
attributes.description: Alternate email address for the sponsor contact, used when the primary email is unavailable or for routing specific communication types (e.g., personal email for urgent safety notifications).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: secondary_phone
attributes.description: Alternate telephone number (e.g., mobile, home office) for the sponsor contact. Used as a backup contact channel when the primary phone is unreachable.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; ITU-T E.164

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_expertise
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area(s) of expertise for this sponsor contact (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology, Rare Disease). Used for study assignment matching, medical monitor qualification, and business development targeting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; MedDRA; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the sponsor contact's primary work location (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Used to schedule meetings, set notification delivery windows, and coordinate cross-regional communications.
attributes.references: IANA Time Zone Database; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the sponsor contact record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for data lineage, change tracking, and ALCOA+ compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: veeva_contact_ref
attributes.description: The contact record identifier from Veeva Vault, used when the sponsor contact is associated with eTMF document approvals, regulatory submissions, or quality management workflows.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

products.name: pipeline_asset
products.description: Master record for investigational drug, biologic, or device assets in a sponsor's development pipeline. Captures compound/molecule name, INN (International Nonproprietary Name), brand name candidate, drug class, mechanism of action, modality (small molecule, biologic, gene therapy, cell therapy, medical device), development phase (preclinical, Phase I-IV), therapeutic area, target indication, IND/CTA number, NDA/BLA/MAA filing status, patent expiry date, and orphan drug designation. Enables pipeline portfolio management and study-to-asset linkage.
products.reference: Investigational Product / IND Asset / Pipeline Compound

attributes.name: pipeline_asset_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the investigational pipeline asset record in the Clinical Trials lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this master resource entity.
attributes.references: CDISC, ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.application. Business justification: Pipeline asset management requires linking to the master regulatory application record (which spans IND through NDA/BLA) for application status, clinical hold tracking, and lifecycle phase reporting —
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: ind_application_id

products.name: engagement_contact_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the formal Role assignment between a sponsor_contact and an engagement. It captures the operational record of which sponsor personnel are assigned to a CRO commercial engagement, in what functional capacity, and for what period. Each record links one sponsor_contact to one engagement with attributes — role, effective dates, primary flag, and status — that exist only in the context of this specific assignment and cannot correctly reside on either the contact or the engagement alone.. Existence Justification: In CRO operations, sponsor contacts are formally assigned to commercial engagements in specific roles (medical monitor, project manager, regulatory lead, financial approver). A single contact — such as a VP of Clinical Operations — routinely spans multiple engagements simultaneously, and each engagement requires multiple contacts across different functional roles. The business actively manages these assignments as named records with effective dates, role designations, and primary-contact flags that belong to neither the contact nor the engagement alone.

products.name: engagement_scope
products.description: This association product represents the Contract/Scope between a sponsor engagement and a health authority. It captures the formal designation of which health authorities are in scope for a given CRO-sponsor engagement, along with submission volume targets, regional scope, and designated regulatory contacts agreed for that pairing. Each record links one engagement to one health authority with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific engagement-HA relationship and cannot reside on either entity alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical research CRO operations, a single sponsor engagement spans multiple regulatory jurisdictions simultaneously — a global Phase III trial under one engagement may require FDA, EMA, PMDA, and MHRA submissions concurrently. Conversely, a major health authority like the FDA is relevant to dozens of active sponsor engagements at any given time. The CRO actively manages which health authorities are in scope per engagement, tracks submission volume targets per HA per engagement, and assigns primary regulatory contacts — this is an operationally managed relationship, not a derived analytical correlation.

products.name: obligation_fulfillment
products.description: This association product represents the fulfillment event between a contractual deliverable and a contract obligation. It captures the operational record of how and to what degree a specific deliverable satisfies a specific contractual obligation, serving as the system of record for GCP audit trails, contract compliance reporting, and dispute resolution. Each record links one deliverable to one contract_obligation with attributes that exist only in the context of this fulfillment relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical research contract management, a single deliverable (e.g., a Clinical Study Report) can fulfill multiple contractual obligations simultaneously (e.g., a regulatory reporting obligation AND a financial milestone obligation AND an operational reporting obligation), while a single contractual obligation (e.g., 'Submit all required regulatory documents') can be satisfied by multiple deliverables. CROs actively manage this mapping as 'obligation fulfillment tracking' — a recognized compliance and audit process where each deliverable-obligation link carries its own fulfillment status, evidence, and completion date. This is not an analytical correlation; it is an operationally managed record created, updated, and closed by contract managers and compliance teams during study execution.

Determines applicable regulatory requirements and timelines. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|Health_Canada|TGA|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; PMDA; MHRA; Health Canada; TGA

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The clinical or disease area that the investigational product targets (e.g., oncology, cardiology, neurology, infectious disease, rare disease). Used for portfolio analytics and regulatory strategy segmentation.
attributes.references: MedDRA SOC Classification; ICH E8; FDA CDER/CBER Division

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this submission record was most recently modified in the system of record. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; Veeva Vault

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Technical validation outcome of the eCTD dossier package against agency-published validation criteria (e.g., FDA eCTD Validation Criteria, EMA eCTD Specification). Indicates whether the submission passed automated technical checks prior to or upon agency receipt.
attributes.references: FDA eCTD Validation Criteria; EMA eCTD Specification; ICH M8

attributes.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
attributes.description: The unique document identifier assigned by Veeva Vault (eTMF/Regulatory Submissions module) to the submission package or primary dossier document. Enables direct traceability to the source system of record.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault Regulatory Submissions Module; 21 CFR Part 11

products.name: application
products.description: Master record for regulatory applications (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, CTA, IMPD) filed with health authorities. Tracks application number, application type and subtype, therapeutic area, indication, sponsor reference, lead agency, application status (active, approved, withdrawn, refused), initial filing date, approval date, lifecycle phase, and type-specific attributes including IND number/type/annual report dates for investigational applications and PDUFA goal date/priority review/breakthrough therapy/orphan drug designations for marketing applications. Parent entity for all submissions, correspondence, approvals, and commitments under a given regulatory dossier. SSOT for the complete regulatory application lifecycle.
products.reference: IND/NDA/BLA/MAA/CTA Application (21 CFR Part 312/314, EU CTR 536/2014)

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the regulatory application record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for all downstream joins to submissions, correspondence, approvals, and commitments under this dossier.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: indication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to program.indication. Business justification: Regulatory applications are filed for specific indications. application.indication is a denormalized text field. Linking to program.indication enables indication-level application portfolio reporting
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: organization_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor entity that owns this regulatory application. Enables sponsor-level portfolio reporting across all applications.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5; 21 CFR Part 312.23

attributes.name: regulatory_contact_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: The regulatory affairs employee accountable for an application lifecycle (IND, NDA, MAA) is tracked for workload management, PDUFA deadline accountability, and inspection readiness. 'regulatory_contac
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: accelerated_approval
attributes.description: Indicates whether this application is approved or being reviewed under the FDA Accelerated Approval pathway, based on a surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. Requires post-approval confirmatory trials.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314 Subpart H; 21 CFR Part 601 Subpart E; FDA Accelerated Approval guidance

attributes.name: agency_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the health authority jurisdiction (e.g., USA, GBR, JPN, CAN, AUS). Supports multi-regional dossier tracking and jurisdiction-specific compliance reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH M4 CTD; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: agency_receipt_date
attributes.description: Date the health authority officially acknowledged receipt of the application. May differ from initial_filing_date if the agency issues a receipt acknowledgment letter after a validation check.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.23; FDA Acknowledgment Letter guidance; EMA validation procedures under EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: annual_report_last_submitted_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: IND Annual Report Last Submitted Date
attributes.description: Date the most recent IND Annual Report was submitted to FDA. Used to calculate the next due date and to confirm compliance with 21 CFR 312.33 annual reporting obligations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.33 (IND Annual Report); FDA IND Annual Report guidance

attributes.name: application_number
attributes.description: Externally assigned application number issued by the health authority (e.g., IND 123456, NDA 210001, BLA 761234, EMA/H/C/004321, CTA-2024-001). This is the official dossier identifier used in all agency correspondence and is the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this entity.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.23 (IND); 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); 21 CFR Part 601 (BLA); EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: application_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the regulatory application. 'active' = application is open and under review or in use; 'approved' = marketing authorization or IND in good standing with approval; 'withdrawn' = sponsor voluntarily withdrew; 'refused' = agency issued a refuse-to-file or complete response letter with no resubmission; 'on_clinical_hold' = FDA-issued clinical hold per 21 CFR 312.42; 'inactive' = IND placed in inactive status.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.42 (clinical hold); 21 CFR Part 314.110 (complete response); EU CTR 536/2014 Article 14; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: application_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory application by submission type. IND = Investigational New Drug; NDA = New Drug Application; BLA = Biologics License Application; MAA = Marketing Authorization Application; CTA = Clinical Trial Authorization; IMPD = Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); 21 CFR Part 601 (BLA); EU CTR 536/2014 (CTA/IMPD); ICH M4 CTD (MAA)

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the health authority granted marketing authorization or IND approval. Null for applications that have not yet been approved. Critical milestone for commercial launch planning and post-approval commitment tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.105 (NDA approval); 21 CFR Part 601.4 (BLA approval); EMA Decision date; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: breakthrough_therapy
attributes.description: Indicates whether FDA has granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) for this application, enabling intensive FDA guidance and rolling review. Granted when preliminary clinical evidence shows substantial improvement over available therapy for serious conditions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.300; FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation guidance; FDASIA Section 902

attributes.name: clinical_hold_date
attributes.description: Date on which the FDA issued the clinical hold order for this application. Null if no clinical hold has been imposed. Used to track hold duration and response timelines.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.42; FDA Clinical Hold guidance

attributes.name: clinical_hold_status
attributes.description: Current clinical hold status issued by FDA under 21 CFR 312.42. 'none' = no hold; 'partial' = hold on specific studies or patient populations; 'full' = all clinical investigations halted; 'lifted' = hold previously issued but now removed.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.42 (Clinical Hold); FDA Clinical Hold guidance; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this regulatory application record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ (Attributable Legible Contemporaneous Original Accurate); ICH E6(R2) Section 8

attributes.name: ctd_module
attributes.description: Indicates which CTD modules are included in this application. M1=Regional Administrative; M2=Summaries; M3=Quality; M4=Nonclinical; M5=Clinical. 'full' indicates all modules are present. Supports dossier completeness tracking.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; ICH M8 eCTD; FDA CTD guidance; EMA CTD guidance

attributes.name: dossier_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-2 three-letter language code of the primary language in which the regulatory dossier is submitted (e.g., ENG for English, JPN for Japanese, DEU for German). Relevant for multi-regional submissions requiring translation.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; EMA language requirements; PMDA submission guidelines; ISO 639-2

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date the application became legally effective and binding. For INDs, this is 30 days after FDA receipt unless a clinical hold is issued. For approved applications, this is the date the approval letter takes effect.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.40 (IND 30-day rule); 21 CFR Part 314.105; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 8

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the application or authorization expires, if applicable. Relevant for CTAs with fixed authorization periods and some national approvals. Null for open-ended authorizations such as US NDA/BLA approvals.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 14; ICH E6(R2); Health Canada CTA regulations

attributes.name: fast_track_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether FDA has granted Fast Track Designation for this application, facilitating development and expediting review of drugs to treat serious conditions and fill unmet medical needs. Enables rolling review and more frequent FDA interactions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.300; FDA Fast Track guidance; FDAMA Section 112

attributes.name: ind_annual_report_due_date
attributes.description: Next due date for the IND Annual Report submission to FDA, calculated as 60 days before the anniversary of the IND effective date. Tracks compliance with mandatory annual reporting obligations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.33 (IND Annual Report); FDA IND Annual Report guidance

attributes.name: ind_number
attributes.description: FDA-assigned IND serial number for investigational applications (e.g., IND 123456). Populated only for IND-type applications. Used in all FDA correspondence, annual reports, and safety reporting.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.23; FDA IND numbering system

attributes.name: ind_type
attributes.description: Subclassification of the IND by purpose. Commercial IND is sponsor-held for drug development; Research IND is investigator-initiated; Treatment IND allows expanded access; Emergency IND is for single-patient emergency use.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.310 (Treatment IND); 21 CFR Part 312.310(d) (Emergency IND); FDA IND guidance

attributes.name: initial_filing_date
attributes.description: Date the application was first submitted to the health authority. For INDs, this is the date the IND package was received by FDA. For NDAs/BLAs, this is the date of original submission. This is the principal BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this entity.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.23 (IND receipt); 21 CFR Part 314.101 (NDA filing); EU CTR 536/2014 Article 5

attributes.name: lead_agency
attributes.description: Primary regulatory health authority to which this application is filed. Determines the regulatory pathway, submission format, and review timelines applicable to this dossier. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|Health Canada|TGA|ANVISA|NMPA|Other — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Parts 312/314/601; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4 CTD; PMDA Pharmaceutical Affairs Law (Japan); MHRA UK Regulations

attributes.name: lifecycle_phase
attributes.description: Current development phase associated with this regulatory application. Tracks the application from pre-IND through post-approval lifecycle. Supports portfolio planning and regulatory strategy alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pre_ind|phase_1|phase_2|phase_3|nda_bla_maa|post_approval|discontinued — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Studies; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA PDUFA VI Commitment Letter

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional regulatory context, strategic notes, or agency-specific instructions not captured in structured fields. Used by regulatory affairs teams for internal documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault RIM notes field

attributes.name: orphan_drug_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the FDA Office of Orphan Products Development (OOPD) or EMA Committee for Orphan Medicinal Products (COMP) has granted Orphan Drug Designation for this application. Confers 7-year market exclusivity (FDA) or 10-year (EMA) and fee waivers.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 316 (Orphan Drug); Orphan Drug Act; EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000

attributes.name: pdufa_goal_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) Goal Date
attributes.description: FDA-assigned PDUFA action date by which the agency commits to completing its review of an NDA or BLA. Applicable only to marketing applications under PDUFA. Drives internal milestone planning and commercial readiness timelines.
attributes.references: PDUFA VI Commitment Letter; 21 CFR Part 314.101; FDA PDUFA performance goals

attributes.name: priority_review
attributes.description: Indicates whether the FDA has granted Priority Review designation to this NDA or BLA, reducing the standard review clock from 12 months to 6 months. Applicable to drugs offering major advances in treatment or providing treatment where no adequate therapy exists.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.510; FDA Priority Review guidance; PDUFA VI

attributes.name: product_name
attributes.description: Name of the drug, biologic, or device covered by this application. May be the INN (International Nonproprietary Name), proprietary brand name, or code name at the investigational stage.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; 21 CFR Part 312.23(a)(3); ICH M4Q CTD Quality Module

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investigational or approved product by modality. Determines the applicable regulatory pathway, CMC requirements, and review division assignment at the agency.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312 (drugs/biologics); 21 CFR Part 820 (devices); EU CTR 536/2014; ICH Q6A/Q6B

attributes.name: rolling_review
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority has granted rolling review, allowing submission and review of completed sections of the dossier before the full application is submitted. Applicable under FDA Fast Track and EMA PRIME/rolling review procedures.
attributes.references: FDA Fast Track Rolling Review guidance; EMA Rolling Review procedure; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: sponsor_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the sponsor's designated regulatory contact as listed on the application cover sheet (e.g., FDA Form 1571 for INDs). This individual is the official point of contact for agency communications.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.23(a)(1); FDA Form 1571; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.1

attributes.name: submission_format
attributes.description: Technical format used for dossier submission to the health authority. eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document) is the standard for FDA, EMA, PMDA; NeeS (Non-eCTD Electronic Submission) is a transitional format; paper submissions are legacy.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eCTD guidance; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: subtype
attributes.description: Further classification within the application type. Examples for IND: Commercial, Research, Treatment, Emergency; for NDA: 505(b)(1) Full, 505(b)(2), 505(j) ANDA; for BLA: Original, Supplement, Efficacy Supplement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Commercial|Research|Treatment|Emergency|505(b)(1)|505(b)(2)|505(j)|Original|Supplement|Efficacy Supplement — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.310 (Treatment IND); 21 CFR Part 314.50 (NDA subtypes); FDA PDUFA guidance

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Broad disease or medical specialty area covered by the application (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology, Infectious Disease, Immunology). Used for portfolio segmentation, resource allocation, and regulatory strategy reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MedDRA SOC classification; FDA CDER/CBER therapeutic area taxonomy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this regulatory application record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: veeva_vault_dossier_reference
attributes.description: Cross-reference identifier linking this application record to the corresponding eTMF/regulatory dossier in Veeva Vault (the system of record for regulatory submissions and document management). Enables traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the source system.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8

products.name: health_authority
products.description: Reference master for global health authority organizations (FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, Health Canada, TGA, ANVISA, NMPA, etc.). Stores agency code, full name, country/region, regulatory framework, submission portal URL, eCTD gateway identifier, contact division, applicable regulatory procedures, and fee schedules. Used as a foreign key lookup across all submission, application, correspondence, and authorization records in the regulatory domain.
products.reference: Health Authority Registry (ICH, WHO ICTRP)

attributes.name: health_authority_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the health authority record in the regulatory reference master. Primary key for all downstream FK references across submission, application, correspondence, and authorization records.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: acronym
attributes.description: Widely recognized abbreviation for the health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, TGA, HC). Used in reporting dashboards, regulatory tracking systems, and internal communications.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; WHO ICTRP

attributes.name: agency_code
attributes.description: Short, standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, HC, TGA, ANVISA, NMPA). Used as a business key in regulatory workflows, submission routing, and eCTD gateway configuration.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; FDA ESG; EMA eSubmission Gateway

attributes.name: agency_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the health authority record. Active indicates the agency is currently accepting submissions; inactive indicates it is no longer operational; merged indicates it has been absorbed into another agency; superseded indicates it has been replaced by a successor body.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault Regulatory

attributes.name: annual_safety_report_type
attributes.description: Type of periodic safety report required by this health authority for ongoing clinical trials (e.g., DSUR - Development Safety Update Report per ICH E2F for EMA/MHRA, IND Annual Report per 21 CFR 312.33 for FDA, PBRER for post-marketing). Drives safety reporting schedule configuration.
attributes.references: ICH E2F (DSUR); 21 CFR Part 312.33 (IND Annual Report); ICH E2C(R2) (PBRER)

attributes.name: authority_type
attributes.description: Classification of the health authority by its jurisdictional scope: national (single country, e.g., FDA, PMDA), supranational (multi-country, e.g., EMA), regional (sub-national or regional body), or reference_agency (recognized reference authority used by other agencies for reliance procedures).
attributes.references: WHO ICTRP; ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: clinical_trial_registry_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires mandatory registration of clinical trials in a public registry (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov for FDA, EU Clinical Trials Register for EMA, JAPIC for PMDA) as a condition of authorization or publication. Drives trial registration workflow in CTMS.
attributes.references: WHO ICTRP; ICMJE; 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 81; FDAAA 801

attributes.name: contact_division_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary regulatory division or office within the health authority responsible for receiving submissions and correspondence for the sponsor's therapeutic area (e.g., FDA CDER Office of New Drugs, EMA Human Medicines Division, PMDA New Drug Division). Used to address regulatory correspondence and meeting requests.
attributes.references: FDA CDER; EMA Human Medicines; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: contact_email
attributes.description: Official email address for regulatory correspondence with the health authority's primary contact division. Used for submission cover letter addressing, meeting request submissions, and regulatory query responses.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: contact_phone
attributes.description: Official telephone number for the health authority's primary regulatory contact division. Used for urgent regulatory communications, inspection notifications, and meeting coordination.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the jurisdiction in which the health authority operates (e.g., USA, GBR, JPN, AUS, CAN, BRA, CHN). Drives country-level regulatory strategy and submission planning.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; ICH M8 eCTD

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this health authority record was first created in the regulatory reference master. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles for regulatory data.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: ctd_format_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority mandates submission of dossiers in the ICH Common Technical Document (CTD) format. True for ICH member agencies (FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, Health Canada); may be false for non-ICH jurisdictions with proprietary submission formats.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; ICH M8 eCTD

attributes.name: data_privacy_framework
attributes.description: Primary data privacy legislation or framework applicable to clinical trial data collected under this health authority's jurisdiction (e.g., GDPR for EMA/MHRA, HIPAA for FDA, PIPEDA for Health Canada, APPI for PMDA). Governs patient data handling, consent requirements, and cross-border data transfer restrictions.
attributes.references: GDPR (EU 2016/679); HIPAA 45 CFR Parts 160/164; PIPEDA; APPI (Japan); OHRP 45 CFR Part 46

attributes.name: ectd_gateway_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Gateway Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned to the health authority's eCTD submission gateway endpoint (e.g., FDA ESG sender ID, EMA DUNS number for eSubmission). Required for configuring automated eCTD transmission via Veeva Vault and validating submission acknowledgement receipts.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; FDA ESG Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eSubmission Gateway Guidance

attributes.name: ectd_specification_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Specification Version
attributes.description: Version of the eCTD technical specification required by this health authority for electronic submissions (e.g., 3.2.2, 4.0). Governs the XML backbone structure, validation criteria, and submission package format for IND, NDA, BLA, and MAA applications.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; FDA eCTD Specification v3.2.2 / v4.0; EMA eCTD Specification

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Authority Record Effective From Date
attributes.description: Date from which this health authority record is considered valid and active for use in regulatory submissions and correspondence. Supports temporal validity tracking for agencies that have been established, reorganized, or renamed.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault Regulatory; ISO 8601

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Authority Record Effective To Date
attributes.description: Date after which this health authority record is no longer valid (e.g., due to agency merger, dissolution, or supersession). Null indicates the record is currently active with no planned end date. Supports historical regulatory record integrity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault Regulatory; ISO 8601

attributes.name: electronic_submission_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority mandates electronic submission (eCTD or equivalent) for regulatory applications. True for FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA; may be false for agencies still accepting paper or hybrid submissions. Governs Veeva Vault submission package configuration.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; FDA ESG; EMA eSubmission Gateway; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: fee_schedule_effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the current regulatory fee schedule for this health authority is effective. Fee schedules are typically updated annually (e.g., FDA PDUFA fees effective October 1 each fiscal year). Used to ensure correct fee amounts are applied in SAP S/4HANA budget planning.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA Fee Schedule; EMA Fee Regulation; PMDA Fee Schedule; ISO 8601

attributes.name: full_name
attributes.description: Complete official name of the health authority organization (e.g., U.S. Food and Drug Administration, European Medicines Agency, Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency). Used in regulatory correspondence, submission cover letters, and CTD/eCTD dossier headers.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: gcp_guideline_version
attributes.description: Version of the GCP guideline mandated or recognized by this health authority (e.g., ICH E6(R2), ICH E6(R3), EU CTR GCP Annex). Governs clinical trial conduct standards, monitoring requirements, and inspection readiness criteria applicable to studies submitted to this agency.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH E6(R3); EU CTR 536/2014; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: ich_member
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Member Status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority is a full member or observer of the International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH). ICH membership determines applicability of harmonized guidelines (CTD, eCTD, GCP, safety reporting) and mutual recognition procedures.
attributes.references: ICH Membership List; ICH M4 CTD; ICH M8 eCTD

attributes.name: ind_application_type
attributes.description: Local equivalent application type for initiating clinical trials under this health authority's jurisdiction (e.g., IND for FDA, CTA for EMA/MHRA/Health Canada, JIND for PMDA, CTN for TGA). Drives submission template selection and regulatory timeline planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|CTA|JIND|CTN|ANVISA_CTA|NMPA_IND — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312 (FDA IND); EU CTR 536/2014 (CTA); ICH E6(R2); TGA CTN Scheme

attributes.name: ind_review_clock_days
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational New Drug (IND) / Clinical Trial Authorization (CTA) Review Clock (Days)
attributes.description: Number of calendar days the health authority has to review and respond to a clinical trial authorization application before the sponsor may proceed (e.g., 30 days for FDA IND, 30 days for EMA CTA under EU CTR). Critical for study start-up timeline planning.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.40 (FDA); EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 8; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: ind_submission_fee_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Investigational New Drug (IND) / Clinical Trial Authorization (CTA) Submission Fee Amount
attributes.description: Standard regulatory fee amount charged by this health authority for an IND or CTA application in the currency specified by submission_fee_currency. May be zero for agencies that do not charge IND/CTA fees (e.g., FDA does not charge IND fees). Used for regulatory budget planning.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312 (FDA - no IND fee); EU CTR 536/2014; EMA Fee Regulation; PMDA Fee Schedule

attributes.name: inspection_authority
attributes.description: Indicates whether this health authority has the mandate and capability to conduct Good Clinical Practice (GCP) inspections of clinical trial sites, sponsors, and CROs. True for FDA, EMA (via national competent authorities), MHRA, PMDA. Drives inspection readiness program scope.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 78; MHRA GCP Inspection

attributes.name: local_language_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires submission documents (or portions thereof) to be translated into the local national language in addition to English. True for agencies such as PMDA (Japanese), NMPA (Chinese), ANVISA (Portuguese). Drives translation cost and timeline planning.
attributes.references: PMDA Submission Guidelines; NMPA Regulations; ANVISA RDC; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: mailing_address
attributes.description: Official mailing address of the health authority's primary contact division for paper-based regulatory correspondence, original document submissions, and formal notifications where electronic submission is not accepted.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: mutual_recognition_agreements
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of mutual recognition agreement frameworks in which this health authority participates (e.g., FDA-EMA Parallel Scientific Advice, MHRA-EMA MRA, ACSS - Australia-Canada-Singapore-Switzerland). Informs regulatory reliance strategy and submission optimization.
attributes.references: FDA-EMA Parallel Scientific Advice Program; MHRA MRA; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: nda_application_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: New Drug Application (NDA) / Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) Type
attributes.description: Local equivalent marketing authorization application type for this health authority (e.g., NDA/BLA for FDA, MAA for EMA, J-NDA for PMDA, ANDS for Health Canada). Used to configure submission workflows, fee schedules, and review clock tracking in Veeva Vault. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NDA|BLA|MAA|J-NDA|ANDS|ARTG — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); 21 CFR Part 601 (BLA); EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: nda_submission_fee_amount

attributes.description: Standard regulatory submission fee amount charged by this health authority for a full marketing authorization application (NDA/BLA/MAA) in the currency specified by submission_fee_currency. attributes.name: non_fatal_sadr_reporting_clock_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Non-Fatal Serious Adverse Drug Reaction (SADR) Expedited Reporting Clock (Hours)
attributes.description: Mandatory expedited safety reporting timeline in hours for non-fatal, non-life-threatening SUSARs to this health authority (e.g., 15 calendar days / 360 hours for FDA and EMA). Used alongside the fatal SUSAR clock to configure Oracle Argus Safety reporting deadlines.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for regulatory affairs teams to capture additional context, special submission requirements, known agency preferences, or recent regulatory guidance updates specific to this health authority that are not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: paper_submission_accepted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority still accepts paper-based regulatory submissions as an alternative or supplement to electronic submissions. Relevant for agencies in transition to full eCTD mandates or for specific submission types (e.g., original INDs, amendments).
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; FDA ESG Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eSubmission Policy

attributes.name: priority_review_clock_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days in the expedited or priority review clock for marketing authorization applications under this health authority (e.g., 180 days for FDA priority NDA review, 150 days for EMA accelerated assessment). Supports regulatory strategy planning for breakthrough and priority designations.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA VI; EMA Accelerated Assessment Guideline; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: region_name
attributes.description: Geopolitical or regulatory region associated with the health authority (e.g., North America, European Union, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, Middle East & Africa). Supports regional regulatory strategy grouping and multi-regional submission planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Primary regulatory framework or legislation governing the health authority's operations (e.g., 21 CFR Parts 312/314/601 for FDA, EU CTR 536/2014 for EMA, PMDA Act for Japan, Medicines Act for MHRA). Critical for determining applicable submission requirements and compliance obligations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); ISO 14155

attributes.name: review_procedure_type
attributes.description: Primary review procedure applicable under this health authority (e.g., Standard Review, Priority Review, Accelerated Assessment, Breakthrough Therapy, PRIME, Conditional Approval, Orphan Drug). Determines review timelines and regulatory strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|priority|accelerated|breakthrough|prime|conditional|orphan — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA; EMA PRIME; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: sadr_reporting_clock_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Serious Adverse Drug Reaction (SADR) / Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Expedited Reporting Clock (Hours)
attributes.description: Mandatory expedited safety reporting timeline in hours for fatal or life-threatening SUSARs to this health authority (e.g., 7 calendar days / 168 hours for FDA, 7 days for EMA). Drives automated deadline calculation in Oracle Argus Safety for SUSAR and ICSR submissions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.32 (FDA); EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 42; ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: standard_review_clock_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days in the standard regulatory review clock for marketing authorization applications under this health authority (e.g., 365 days for FDA standard NDA review, 210 days for EMA MAA). Used for regulatory milestone planning and submission timeline modeling.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA VI; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: submission_fee_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for regulatory submission fees charged by this health authority (e.g., USD for FDA PDUFA fees, EUR for EMA fees, JPY for PMDA fees). Used in SAP S/4HANA for regulatory fee budget planning and accounts payable processing.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; FDA PDUFA Fee Schedule; EMA Fee Regulation (EC) No 297/95; PMDA Fee Schedule

attributes.name: submission_language
attributes.description: ISO 639 language code(s) required for regulatory submissions to this health authority (e.g., en for English, ja for Japanese, zh for Chinese, de/fr/it for Switzerland). Governs translation requirements for CTD modules, labeling, and patient-facing documents.
attributes.references: ISO 639; ICH M4 CTD; EU CTR 536/2014; PMDA Submission Guidelines

attributes.name: submission_portal_url
attributes.description: Official URL of the health authority's electronic submission portal (e.g., FDA ESG gateway, EMA eSubmission portal, PMDA eCTD gateway). Used by regulatory affairs teams to route eCTD dossier submissions and track submission acknowledgements.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; FDA ESG Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eSubmission Gateway

attributes.name: trial_registry_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary public clinical trial registry mandated by this health authority for trial registration (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov for FDA, EU Clinical Trials Register for EMA, JAPIC CTI for PMDA, ANZCTR for TGA). Used to configure trial registration workflows in Oracle Siebel CTMS.
attributes.references: WHO ICTRP; FDAAA 801; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 81; ICMJE

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this health authority record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

products.name: submission_sequence
products.description: Tracks individual eCTD submission sequences within a regulatory application. Each sequence has a sequence number, submission type (original, amendment, supplement, response, withdrawal), sequence date, eCTD lifecycle operation (new, replace, append, delete), CTD module scope, submission reason, and validation status (eCTD technical validation result). Enables granular tracking of dossier evolution over time.
products.reference: eCTD Sequence (ICH M8, FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide)

attributes.name: submission_sequence_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each eCTD submission sequence record within the regulatory application dossier.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Specification; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent regulatory application (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, CTA) to which this submission sequence belongs.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: audit_id
