attributes.name: conditions_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of any conditions, restrictions, or obligations attached to the Clinical Trial Authorization by the national competent authority. Populated only when conditions_attached is True.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 8; EMA; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this Clinical Trial Authorization record was first created in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and ALCOA+ compliance requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: cta_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-assigned reference number issued by the national competent authority (NCA) or EU CTIS portal upon authorization of the clinical trial. This is the official business identifier used in all regulatory correspondence and submissions.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 8; EMA EU CTIS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: ctd_section_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the relevant Common Technical Document (CTD) or eCTD dossier section submitted in support of this CTA application (e.g., Module 5 clinical study reports). Supports regulatory dossier traceability.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; eCTD; EMA; FDA; PMDA

attributes.name: ctis_trial_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) Trial ID
attributes.description: Unique trial identifier assigned within the EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) under EU CTR 536/2014. Used for multi-country EU submissions and authorization tracking via the centralized CTIS portal.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; EMA CTIS Guidance

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the national competent authority issued its formal decision (authorization, conditional authorization, refusal, or withdrawal). Used for regulatory timeline KPI reporting and compliance tracking.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 8; EMA; MHRA; Health Canada

attributes.name: decision_outcome
attributes.description: Formal outcome of the national competent authority's review decision for this CTA application. Distinct from authorization_status in that it captures the point-in-time decision rather than the current lifecycle state.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 8; EMA; MHRA

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which the Clinical Trial Authorization is legally effective and trial activities may commence in the member state. May differ from authorization_date if conditions or a deferred start apply.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2) GCP; EMA

attributes.name: ethics_committee_opinion
attributes.description: Outcome of the ethics committee (IRB/IEC) review associated with this CTA in the member state. Tracks whether a favorable opinion was obtained, which is a prerequisite for trial commencement in most jurisdictions.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Chapter III; ICH E6(R2) Section 3; OHRP; FDA 21 CFR Part 56

attributes.name: ethics_opinion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the ethics committee (IRB/IEC) issued its opinion for this CTA in the member state. Used to confirm that ethics approval preceded trial commencement and to track parallel review timelines.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Chapter III; ICH E6(R2); OHRP

attributes.name: eudract_number
attributes.description: European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) number assigned to the trial, serving as the pan-European unique trial identifier. Used for cross-referencing across EU member states and EU CTIS.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; EudraCT Regulation (EC) No 536/2014; EMA

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization expires, after which trial activities in the member state are no longer authorized unless a renewal has been granted. Null for open-ended authorizations.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); EMA

attributes.name: gdpr_data_transfer_mechanism
attributes.description: Legal mechanism under GDPR used to authorize the transfer of personal data of EU trial subjects to non-EU countries in connection with this CTA. Required for EU-based trials involving cross-border data flows.
attributes.references: GDPR Articles 44-49; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA; EDPB

attributes.name: indication_meddra_code
attributes.description: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) code for the primary disease indication under investigation in this authorized trial. Enables standardized cross-study and cross-authority indication reporting.
attributes.references: MedDRA; ICH M1; EMA; FDA

attributes.name: inspection_readiness_status
attributes.description: Current inspection readiness status for this CTA record, indicating whether the regulatory documentation and evidence supporting this authorization is ready for NCA or GCP inspection. Supports proactive inspection readiness management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Inspection Guidance

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a separate Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) approval is required in addition to the NCA authorization in the member state. Relevant for countries with parallel ethics and regulatory review tracks.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; EU CTR 536/2014 Chapter III; OHRP; FDA 21 CFR Part 56

attributes.name: member_state_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code of the EU member state or non-EU country in which this Clinical Trial Authorization was granted by the national competent authority. Enables multi-country authorization tracking.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ISO 3166-1; EMA

attributes.name: modification_scope
attributes.description: Brief description of the scope of the substantial modification covered by this CTA record (e.g., protocol amendment, IMP change, new investigational site addition, safety update). Populated for substantial_modification authorization types.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Articles 15-19; EMA Guidance on Substantial Modifications

attributes.name: national_portal_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier assigned by the national regulatory portal (e.g., MHRA IRAS number, BfArM reference, ANSM reference, Health Canada CTD number) for this CTA. Complements the CTIS trial ID for country-specific tracking.
attributes.references: MHRA; BfArM; ANSM; Health Canada; TGA; PMDA

attributes.name: planned_subject_count
attributes.description: Number of trial subjects planned to be enrolled in the member state under this Clinical Trial Authorization, as declared in the approved protocol. Used for site capacity planning and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); EMA

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Primary regulatory framework under which this Clinical Trial Authorization was granted (e.g., EU CTR 536/2014, national regulation, ISO 14155 for medical devices). Determines applicable procedural and reporting requirements.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ISO 14155; ICH E6(R2); EMA

attributes.name: sponsor_protocol_number
attributes.description: Internal protocol identifier assigned by the sponsor or CRO to uniquely identify the study protocol associated with this CTA. Used to link the authorization to the study protocol design and development records.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ICH E8; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization application was formally submitted to the national competent authority. Used to calculate regulatory review timelines and track compliance with submission deadlines.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 5; EMA CTIS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: substantial_modification_number
attributes.description: Sequential identifier for substantial modifications to the original CTA, as assigned by the sponsor or NCA. Populated only for authorization_type = substantial_modification. Enables tracking of the amendment history chain.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Articles 15-19; EMA Guidance on Substantial Modifications; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: suspension_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization was suspended by the national competent authority or voluntarily by the sponsor. Null if the CTA has never been suspended. Triggers safety and compliance escalation workflows.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 77; ICH E6(R2); EMA

attributes.name: suspension_reason
attributes.description: Narrative reason for the suspension of the Clinical Trial Authorization, as communicated by the national competent authority or sponsor. Populated only when suspension_date is not null.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 77; ICH E6(R2); EMA

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area or disease indication covered by the clinical trial authorized under this CTA (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology, Infectious Disease). Used for portfolio analytics and regulatory reporting segmentation.
attributes.references: EMA; ICH E8; MedDRA; WHO-DD

attributes.name: trial_phase
attributes.description: Regulatory phase of the clinical trial covered by this authorization (Phase I through Phase IV), as defined by ICH E8 and applicable NCA guidelines. Determines applicable regulatory requirements, safety reporting thresholds, and monitoring intensity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Phase I|Phase I/II|Phase II|Phase IIa|Phase IIb|Phase III|Phase III/IV|Phase IV — promote to reference product]
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase I/II|Phase II|Phase IIa|Phase IIb|Phase III
attributes.references: ICH E8; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this Clinical Trial Authorization record was last modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail, change tracking, and ALCOA+ compliance requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: validation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the national competent authority confirmed the CTA application was formally valid and complete for review. Marks the start of the regulatory assessment clock under EU CTR 536/2014.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014 Article 6; EMA CTIS Guidance

attributes.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault (eTMF/regulatory submissions module) for the CTA authorization letter or dossier. Enables direct linkage from this master record to the source regulatory document in the eTMF system of record.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; EU CTR 536/2014; TMF Reference Model

attributes.name: withdrawal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization was formally withdrawn, either by the sponsor or by the national competent authority. Null if the CTA has not been withdrawn.
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); EMA

attributes.name: withdrawal_reason
attributes.description: Narrative reason for the withdrawal of the Clinical Trial Authorization. Populated only when withdrawal_date is not null. Required for regulatory reporting and inspection readiness.

attributes.name: is_unannounced

attributes.name: major_findings_count

attributes.references: EMA GCP Inspection Procedure; ICH E6(R2); FDA BIMO Program

attributes.name: minor_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of minor (other) findings identified during the inspection. Minor findings represent deviations from GCP or regulatory requirements that are unlikely to have a significant impact on subject safety or data integrity.
attributes.references: EMA GCP Inspection Procedure; ICH E6(R2); FDA BIMO Program

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: outcome

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Regulatory action items are often generated to fulfill specific regulatory obligations with agency-mandated deadlines. Linking action items to obligations enables obligation-driven action item managem
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: prior_action_item_regulatory_action_item_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the previous action item from which this one was derived (e.g., a re-opened or recurring item). Enables lineage tracking across action item generations. Nullable for original items.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.protocol_deviation. Business justification: Protocol deviations with regulatory reporting requirements generate regulatory action items. Linking action items to protocol deviations supports the deviation-to-regulatory-response workflow required
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: regulatory_correspondence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.correspondence. Business justification: Action items can arise from regulatory correspondence (Complete Response Letters, Information Requests, deficiency letters). The source_event_type field on regulatory_action_item can be 'correspondenc
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) to which this regulatory action item belongs. Links the action item to the relevant trial context for reporting and filtering.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IG

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific regulatory submission (e.g., a response sequence, amendment, or safety report) that triggered or is associated with this action item. Nullable when the action item originates from a meeting or inspection rather than a submission.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; ICH M4 CTD; Veeva Vault Submissions Module

attributes.name: tmf_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Regulatory action item responses (agency information requests, inspection findings responses) are filed as TMF documents. Linking action items to their response TMF documents enables inspection-ready
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: action_item_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the specific regulatory task, finding, or commitment that must be addressed. Captures the full context of what is required, including any agency-specified language from meeting minutes or inspection reports.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: action_item_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-known business identifier for the action item (e.g., RAI-2024-00123). Used in regulatory correspondence, meeting minutes, and inspection response packages to uniquely reference the task.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; Veeva Vault Action Item Module

attributes.name: action_item_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the regulatory action item. Drives operational dashboards, escalation logic, and compliance reporting. 'overdue' is system-set when due_date has passed without closure.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: action_item_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the nature of the action item. Drives workflow templates and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: commitment|information_request|capa|protocol_amendment|label_update|response_to_agency|internal_task|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; ICH E6(R2) GCP; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: agency_acknowledgement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the health authority formally acknowledged receipt of the response or deliverable. Used to confirm the regulatory clock was stopped and to document agency receipt for the eTMF.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: agency_mandated_due_date
attributes.description: The specific response deadline formally communicated by the health authority (e.g., FDA 30-day information request clock, EMA Day 120 response). Distinct from the internal due_date which may be set earlier to allow review time. Nullable when no formal agency deadline exists.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; PMDA; MHRA

attributes.name: agency_submission_date
attributes.description: The date on which the completed response or deliverable was formally submitted to the health authority. Distinct from completion_date (internal closure) — captures the actual agency-facing delivery date for regulatory clock tracking.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: assigned_owner_email
attributes.description: Email address of the individual responsible for completing this action item. Used for automated notifications, escalation alerts, and audit trail. Classified as confidential PII per GDPR and HIPAA.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: assigned_owner_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual (typically a Regulatory Affairs professional or CRA) responsible for completing this action item. Captured as a denormalized field for operational task management and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: assigned_team
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory affairs team or functional group responsible for this action item (e.g., 'Global Regulatory Strategy', 'Submissions Team', 'Safety Reporting'). Supports team-level workload reporting and capacity planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Veeva Vault

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: The date on which the action item was fully completed and closed. Nullable until the item reaches 'closed' status. Used to calculate cycle time and measure regulatory responsiveness KPIs.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when this regulatory action item record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the action item must be completed. May be agency-mandated (e.g., 30-day response clock from FDA information request) or internally set. Drives overdue status calculation and escalation triggers.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: The date on which this action item was escalated. Nullable when escalation_flag is False. Used to track escalation response time and management intervention patterns.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this action item has been escalated to senior regulatory leadership or executive management due to risk, overdue status, or strategic importance. True = escalated; False = not escalated.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: escalation_reason
attributes.description: Narrative explanation of why this action item was escalated (e.g., 'Approaching agency deadline with incomplete data package', 'Potential clinical hold risk identified'). Provides context for management review.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: finding_classification
attributes.description: GCP/GMP inspection finding classification when the action item originates from an inspection finding. Aligns with FDA and EMA inspection classification standards. Nullable for non-inspection-sourced action items.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Inspection Procedure; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, interim progress updates, or commentary on the action item that does not fit structured fields. Supports operational communication within the regulatory affairs team.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: open_date
attributes.description: The date on which this action item was formally opened and entered into the regulatory task register. Represents the business event timestamp for the creation of the obligation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault Action Item Module

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to the action item, reflecting urgency and regulatory risk. 'critical' typically indicates a potential clinical hold, safety signal, or imminent agency deadline. Used for resource allocation and escalation decisions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CTCAE; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: recurrence_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this action item represents a recurrence of a previously identified issue or finding. True = recurrence of a prior finding; False = new issue. Used in quality trend analysis and CAPA effectiveness assessments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ISO 9001 CAPA

attributes.name: regulatory_area
attributes.description: Functional regulatory domain to which this action item belongs (e.g., clinical, safety, CMC). Enables domain-specific filtering and assignment routing within the regulatory affairs team. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clinical|safety|cmc|regulatory_affairs|data_management|biostatistics|quality|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: regulatory_procedure_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific regulatory procedure, guideline, or regulation that this action item must satisfy (e.g., '21 CFR 312.32', 'EMA/CHMP/ICH/295148/2004', 'ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18'). Provides the regulatory basis for the required action.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; ICH E6(R2); EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: response_document_title
attributes.description: Title of the formal response document prepared to address this action item (e.g., 'Response to FDA Information Request Letter dated 2024-03-15'). Supports eTMF filing and regulatory correspondence tracking.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: review_cycle
attributes.description: Indicates the review cycle stage of this action item within an ongoing agency interaction (e.g., initial response, follow-up clarification, final closure). Supports multi-round agency dialogue tracking.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: source_event_reference
attributes.description: Free-text or structured reference identifier for the originating event (e.g., meeting number, inspection report number, correspondence reference number, or internal review ID). Provides traceability back to the source document or event record.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: source_event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the business event that originated this action item. Drives workflow routing and reporting dashboards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: agency_meeting|inspection_finding|regulatory_correspondence|internal_review|dsmb_recommendation|other — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: sponsor_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the sponsor representative responsible for oversight of this action item. Relevant when the CRO is acting on behalf of a pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor and the sponsor must approve the response.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Short, human-readable title summarizing the regulatory action item (e.g., 'Respond to FDA Information Request on CMC Data'). Used in dashboards, email notifications, and task lists.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when this regulatory action item record was last modified. Supports change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the associated document or record in Veeva Vault (eTMF or regulatory submissions module), such as the meeting minutes, inspection report, or correspondence document that originated this action item. Enables direct navigation to the source document.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault eTMF Module

products.name: country_registration
products.description: Tracks product registration status and requirements across individual countries and jurisdictions. Captures country, registration number, registration type (national, mutual recognition, decentralized, centralized), registration date, expiry date, renewal due date, local agent name, registered indication, registered dosage form, and current registration status. Supports global regulatory intelligence and market access planning.
products.reference: Product Registration / Marketing Authorization (EU CTR, ICH CTD, WHO Prequalification)

attributes.name: country_registration_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each country-level product registration record in the regulatory lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent regulatory application (IND/NDA/BLA/MAA) under which this country registration was granted.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: ethics_approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.ethics_approval. Business justification: Country registrations require local ethics approval in many jurisdictions as part of the authorization package. Linking country registration to ethics approval supports the complete country authorizat
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: health_authority_id
attributes.description: Reference to the health authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, Health Canada, TGA, etc.) that issued or oversees this country registration.
attributes.references: FDA; EMA; PMDA; MHRA; Health Canada; TGA

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Each country registration creates specific local regulatory obligations (annual reports, renewals, variations, local language labeling). Linking registrations to obligation records enables systematic
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.approval. Business justification: A country registration is the direct outcome of a regulatory approval in a specific country/jurisdiction. Linking country_registration to the approval that granted it provides the approval-to-registra
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: regulatory_contact_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: The employee managing country-level product registrations owns renewal deadlines and local agent coordination — a named regulatory operations process. 'regulatory_contact_name' is a denormalized workf
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Country registrations are initiated through regulatory submissions (initial marketing authorization applications, renewal submissions). Linking country_registration to the initiating submission provid
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: tmf_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Country registration certificates and approval letters are TMF Zone 1 essential documents. Regulatory teams must retrieve registration documentation during inspections and for renewal submissions; thi
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: annual_report_due_date
attributes.description: Next due date for the periodic safety update report (PSUR), development safety update report (DSUR), or annual product report required by the health authority in this country to maintain the registration.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) PSUR; 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA PSUR Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

attributes.name: conditional_approval
attributes.description: Indicates whether this registration was granted under conditional or accelerated approval, requiring post-marketing confirmatory studies or commitments. True if conditional approval conditions are still outstanding.
attributes.references: EMA Conditional Marketing Authorization Guideline; FDA Accelerated Approval 21 CFR Part 314 Subpart H; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code identifying the jurisdiction in which the product is registered (e.g., USA, GBR, JPN, CAN, AUS, DEU).
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH E2C(R2); GDPR Article 3

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this country registration record was first created in the regulatory data product. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; ALCOA+ (Attributable Legible Contemporaneous Original Accurate); ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: ctd_module_scope
attributes.description: Scope of the Common Technical Document (CTD) dossier submitted for this registration: full (complete Modules 1-5), abridged (generic/hybrid referencing originator data), hybrid (mixed), or bibliographic (literature-based). Determines the regulatory review pathway.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; EMA CTD Guideline; 21 CFR Part 314.50; PMDA CTD Requirements

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Pharmaceutical dosage form as registered in this country (e.g., tablet, capsule, solution for injection, lyophilized powder). Must match the approved product dossier. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|solution_for_injection|lyophilized_powder|oral_solution|patch|inhaler|cream|suppository|suspension — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q6A; EMA Guideline on Pharmaceutical Development; WHO Model List of Essential Medicines

attributes.name: dossier_format
attributes.description: Format of the regulatory dossier submitted for this registration: eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document), NeeS (Non-eCTD Electronic Submission), paper, or VNeeS (Veterinary NeeS). Determines submission and archival requirements.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD; 21 CFR Part 11; EMA eCTD Guideline; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current registration period expires and renewal is required to maintain marketing authorization. Null for registrations that do not expire (e.g., some FDA approvals).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Health Canada Food and Drug Regulations

attributes.name: indication
attributes.description: Approved therapeutic indication(s) for which the product is registered in this country, as stated in the approved product labeling or Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC). May be narrower than the global indication.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.57; EMA SmPC Guideline; ICH E3; MedDRA

attributes.name: inn_name
attributes.description: WHO-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) for the active substance, as recognized in the country registration. Provides a globally consistent scientific identifier independent of brand name.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; ICH Q6A; EMA Guideline on INN

attributes.name: inspection_readiness_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the regulatory file and documentation for this country registration are currently in a state of inspection readiness as assessed by the regulatory affairs team. True if ready for a health authority inspection.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Inspection Guideline; MasterControl

attributes.name: last_annual_report_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent annual product report, PSUR, or equivalent periodic safety report was submitted to the health authority for this country registration.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA PSUR Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

attributes.name: last_renewal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent registration renewal was granted by the health authority. Establishes the start of the current registration period for expiry and renewal due date calculations.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 14; 21 CFR Part 314.81; Health Canada

attributes.name: last_variation_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recently approved post-approval variation or amendment to this country registration. Used to track the currency of the approved dossier and labeling.
attributes.references: EMA Variation Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008; 21 CFR Part 314.70; ICH Q12

attributes.name: local_agent_contact
attributes.description: Primary contact details (phone, email, or address) for the local regulatory agent or marketing authorization holder in the registered country. Used for regulatory correspondence and inspection coordination.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 314.50

attributes.name: local_agent_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Local Agent / Marketing Authorization Holder Name
attributes.description: Name of the local regulatory agent, marketing authorization holder (MAH), or in-country representative responsible for maintaining the registration and liaising with the national health authority. Required in many jurisdictions for foreign sponsors.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 8; 21 CFR Part 314.50; Health Canada Food and Drug Regulations C.08.002

attributes.name: market_exclusivity_expiry
attributes.description: Date on which the data exclusivity or market exclusivity period expires in this country, after which generic or biosimilar applications may reference the originator dossier. Critical for lifecycle and competitive intelligence planning.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 14(11); 21 CFR Part 314.108 (Hatch-Waxman); TRIPS Agreement Article 39.3

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional regulatory context, authority-specific conditions, post-approval commitments, or operational notes relevant to this country registration that are not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: orphan_drug_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the product holds orphan drug designation in this country, conferring market exclusivity and regulatory incentives for rare disease treatments. True if orphan designation is active.
attributes.references: FDA Orphan Drug Act 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; PMDA Orphan Drug Designation

attributes.name: patent_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the primary product patent expires in this country. Used in conjunction with market exclusivity for lifecycle management and generic entry forecasting.
attributes.references: TRIPS Agreement; 21 CFR Part 314.53 (Orange Book); EMA Patent Linkage Guidance

attributes.name: product_name
attributes.description: Brand or trade name of the medicinal product as approved and registered in this specific country. May differ from the global brand name due to local naming requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201; EMA Guideline on the Acceptability of Names; WHO INN Programme

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the health authority formally granted or issued the product registration or marketing authorization. Represents the effective start of the registration.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: registration_number
attributes.description: Official registration or marketing authorization number assigned by the national health authority upon approval (e.g., NDA 123456, EU/1/20/1234, PMDA approval number). This is the externally-known business identifier for the registration.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: registration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the country registration: active (valid and in force), expired (past expiry date without renewal), suspended (temporarily halted by authority), withdrawn (voluntarily or involuntarily removed), pending (application submitted, awaiting decision), cancelled (application withdrawn before approval).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH Q10

attributes.name: registration_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory procedure used to obtain this registration: national (single-country), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralized (DCP), centralized (EMA), or bilateral agreement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: national|mutual_recognition|decentralized|centralized|bilateral|abridged|hybrid — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
attributes.references: EU CTR 536/2014; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: regulatory_procedure_number
attributes.description: Procedure number assigned by the health authority for the specific regulatory review procedure (e.g., EMA centralized procedure number EMEA/H/C/XXXXXX, MRP/DCP reference number). Distinct from the final registration number.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA EPAR database

attributes.name: reimbursement_status
attributes.description: Current reimbursement or health technology assessment (HTA) status of the registered product in this country. Indicates whether the product is covered by national health insurance or payer systems, supporting market access planning.
attributes.references: EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282; NICE Technology Appraisal; HAS (France); IQWIG (Germany); Health Canada CDR

attributes.name: renewal_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the renewal application must be submitted to the health authority to avoid lapse of the registration. May precede the expiry date by a regulatory-mandated lead time.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 14; 21 CFR Part 314.81; Health Canada

attributes.name: renewal_submission_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the renewal application was submitted to the health authority. Used to confirm timely submission relative to the renewal due date.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Approved route of administration as registered in this country (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical, inhalation). Must align with the approved product dossier. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|intrathecal|transdermal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q6A; 21 CFR Part 201.57; EMA SmPC Guideline; EDQM Standard Terms

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: Approved strength or concentration of the active substance as registered in this country (e.g., 10 mg, 100 mg/mL, 500 mg/5 mL). Expressed as a free-text string to accommodate varied unit formats across jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A; 21 CFR Part 201.56; EMA Guideline on Pharmaceutical Development

attributes.name: submission_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-1/639-2 language code of the primary language in which the registration dossier was submitted to the health authority (e.g., en, fr, de, ja). Relevant for translation management and local labeling compliance.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; EMA Language Policy; PMDA Submission Requirements; Health Canada Bilingual Requirements

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Broad therapeutic area classification for the registered product (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology, Infectious Disease). Used for portfolio reporting and market access analytics.
attributes.references: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC); ICH E3; EMA Product Classification

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this country registration record. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault (eTMF/Regulatory module) for the approved registration certificate, marketing authorization letter, or associated dossier. Enables direct traceability to the source regulatory document.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault Regulatory; 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

Used to classify submissions and plan timelines.

attributes.name: applicable_product_types

attributes.name: application_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory application to which this procedure applies (e.g., IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, ANDA, sNDA, sBLA, CTA). Each record links one health_authority to one clinical_program with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship and cannot reside on either master entity alone.. Conversely, each health authority oversees many clinical programs from many sponsors. The business actively manages this relationship as a named operational concept: a 'Regulatory Submission Strategy' or 'Program-Agency Engagement', with agency-specific data (submission dates, pathways, priority designations) that belongs to neither entity alone.

products.name: protocol_ethics_coverage
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory-compliance contract between an IND application and an ethics submission. It captures which specific protocol (by number and version) under a given IND application is covered by a given IRB/IEC ethics submission, including the IND serial number amendment referenced. Each record links one ind_application to one ethics_submission and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this protocol-level regulatory linkage — enabling sponsors and regulatory teams to answer 'which ethics submissions cover which IND protocols?' and 'which IND serial numbers are referenced by this ethics submission?'. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single IND application covers multiple protocols, each of which requires its own ethics submission to an IRB/IEC — so one IND application is associated with many ethics submissions. Conversely, a single ethics submission (particularly an amendment or continuing review) may reference multiple IND serial numbers or cover protocols under different IND applications, meaning one ethics submission can be associated with multiple IND applications. The business actively tracks which ethics submissions are linked to which IND protocols/serial numbers as part of regulatory compliance management, and this linkage carries its own data (protocol number, protocol version, IND serial number, submission date, ethics committee name).

It captures the regulatory act by which a health authority approves a specific labeling document version as the valid label for a product registration in a given country. Each record links one labeling_document to one country_registration and carries the country-specific approval status, effective dates, and health authority decision data that exist only in the context of this country-level label approval — not on the document or registration alone.. Conversely, a single country registration tracks multiple labeling document versions over its lifecycle as the label is updated through variations and renewals. The business actively manages which specific label version is approved in each country — this is a recognized operational process called 'label approval' or 'labeling registration' in global regulatory operations.

products.name: binder_document_inclusion
products.description: This association product represents the inclusion contract between a labeling_document and a regulatory_binder. It captures the operational act of assembling a regulatory submission binder by including specific labeling document versions, recording where each document is filed within the CTD structure, whether inclusion is mandatory, and any submission-specific handling requirements such as redaction. Each record links one labeling_document to one regulatory_binder with attributes that exist only in the context of this inclusion relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical regulatory operations, a labeling document (e.g., a USPI or SmPC) is genuinely included in multiple regulatory binders — the original NDA submission, subsequent supplements, annual reports, and amendments — while each binder contains multiple labeling documents covering different languages, CTD modules, and document types. This is an operationally managed relationship: regulatory affairs teams actively assemble binders by selecting and including specific labeling document versions, tracking which documents are mandatory, their CTD section placement, and whether redaction is required. The relationship is a recognized business concept in regulatory document management, commonly called a 'Binder Inclusion' or 'Document Inclusion'.

Conversely, a pivotal study's ethics approval (e.g., a Phase III trial) can be cited in both an original NDA and a subsequent supplemental NDA (sNDA) or even a related BLA, meaning one ethics approval supports multiple applications. The business actively manages this linkage as part of dossier assembly, tracking which ethics approvals are included in which CTD module and why.

products.name: substantial_modification_submission
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory submission event between a protocol_amendment and a clinical_trial_authorization. It captures the per-member-state, per-amendment submission workflow required under EU CTR 536/2014 and equivalent national frameworks, where each protocol amendment must be formally submitted to and approved by each national competent authority holding a CTA for the trial. Each record links one protocol_amendment to one clinical_trial_authorization and carries the country-specific submission date, approval date, decision outcome, and modification scope that exist only in the context of this specific amendment-to-authority submission.. Existence Justification: Under EU CTR 536/2014, every substantial protocol amendment must be submitted as a separate modification to each national competent authority's CTA in each member state where the trial is running. A single protocol amendment (e.g., AM-003) generates distinct CTA modification submissions to Germany, France, Spain, etc., each with its own submission date, approval date, decision outcome, and member-state-specific conditions. Conversely, a single CTA accumulates multiple substantial modifications over the trial lifecycle as successive protocol amendments are approved. This is a genuine operational M:N: the business actively creates, tracks, and queries each amendment-to-CTA submission as a named regulatory workflow record.

attributes.name: superseded_sop_number

attributes.name: superseded_version_number

attributes.references: MasterControl Document Control; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: title
