attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sop. Business justification: GCP delegation logs must reference the governing SOP under which task delegation is authorized. Regulatory inspectors verify that delegations comply with current SOPs. This link supports inspection re
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: primary_workforce_pi_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Principal Investigator (PI) who is delegating the trial-related duties. The PI retains overall responsibility per GCP.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.2; FDA 21 CFR 312.60

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this delegation of trial-related duties applies. Links the delegation log to the specific protocol and sponsor.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.3.25; CDISC SDTM

attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: employer_benefits_contribution
attributes.description: Employer-paid portion of employee benefits costs (health insurance, dental, vision, life insurance) for this pay period. Included in total workforce cost allocation to clinical studies.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; HIPAA; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: employer_retirement_contribution
attributes.description: Employer matching or defined contribution to the employee's retirement plan for this pay period (e.g., 401(k) match, pension contribution). Part of total compensation cost for study budget allocation.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; IRS Publication 560; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: employer_tax_contribution
attributes.description: Employer-side payroll tax contributions (e.g., employer FICA/Social Security, Medicare, unemployment insurance) associated with this payroll record. Required for total labor cost allocation to clinical studies.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; IRS Publication 15; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: employment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the employee's employment arrangement during this pay period. Determines applicable payroll rules, benefit eligibility, and tax treatment.
attributes.references: Workday HCM; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act)

attributes.name: gross_pay
attributes.description: Total gross compensation earned by the employee for the pay period before any deductions. Equals the sum of all pay components (base salary, overtime, bonus, allowances). Key figure for SOX financial reporting and workforce cost allocation.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; SOX Section 302/404; FLSA

attributes.name: hours_worked
attributes.description: Total regular hours worked by the employee during the pay period as recorded in Workday HCM time tracking. Used for hourly pay calculations and study resource utilization reporting.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Time Tracking; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act)

attributes.name: is_reversal
attributes.description: Indicates whether this payroll record represents a reversal of a previously processed payroll entry. True if this record corrects or voids a prior disbursement. Critical for SOX audit trail integrity.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: job_title
attributes.description: The employee's job title at the time of payroll processing (e.g., Clinical Research Associate, Biostatistician, Data Manager). Captured as a point-in-time snapshot for workforce cost analytics.
attributes.references: Workday HCM; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: net_pay
attributes.description: The actual amount disbursed to the employee after all deductions (taxes, benefits, retirement contributions) have been subtracted from gross pay. Represents the take-home pay amount.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: overtime_amount
attributes.description: Total overtime pay earned by the employee during this pay period, calculated per applicable labor law (e.g., FLSA 1.5x rate). Relevant for CRAs and site staff with variable field hours.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act)

attributes.name: overtime_hours
attributes.description: Total overtime hours worked by the employee during the pay period beyond the standard threshold (e.g., >40 hours/week under FLSA). Drives overtime_amount calculation.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Time Tracking; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act)

attributes.name: pay_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which the employee is paid within this pay group (e.g., biweekly, monthly). Determines the number of pay periods per year for annualization calculations.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act)

attributes.name: pay_group
attributes.description: The Workday HCM pay group to which the employee belongs, determining pay frequency and processing rules (e.g., US-Biweekly, EU-Monthly, APAC-Monthly). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US-Biweekly|US-Semimonthly|EU-Monthly|APAC-Monthly|CA-Biweekly|UK-Monthly — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module

attributes.name: pay_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last calendar date of the pay period covered by this payroll record. Defines the end of the compensation earning window.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act)

attributes.name: pay_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first calendar date of the pay period covered by this payroll record. Defines the beginning of the compensation earning window.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act)

attributes.name: payment_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the net pay was disbursed to the employee. Used for cash flow reporting and SOX financial controls.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: The method by which net pay was disbursed to the employee (e.g., direct deposit, check, wire transfer). Sourced from Workday HCM payment election settings.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; NACHA (ACH payment rules)

attributes.name: payroll_run_reference
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the payroll run batch in which this record was processed, as assigned by Workday HCM. Enables traceability of all records processed in a single payroll run cycle.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: payroll_run_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of the payroll run: regular scheduled run, off-cycle correction, supplemental bonus run, or final paycheck upon termination.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this payroll record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and SOX financial reporting controls.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this payroll record was last modified in the Databricks Silver Layer. Tracks data refresh cycles and supports SOX audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: retirement_deduction
attributes.description: Employee pre-tax or post-tax retirement contribution deducted from gross pay (e.g., 401(k), pension, RRSP). Supports benefits compliance and workforce total compensation reporting.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; IRS Publication 560; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: run_status
attributes.description: Current processing lifecycle status of this payroll record within the Workday HCM payroll run workflow. Supports SOX audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this payroll record was sourced. For this data product, the authoritative source is Workday HCM Payroll module.
attributes.references: Workday HCM; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: study_allocation_code
attributes.description: The clinical study or project code to which this payroll expense is allocated for workforce cost tracking. Enables direct linkage of labor costs to specific clinical trials for sponsor billing and budget management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Project Accounting; ICH E6(R2) GCP; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: tax_jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: The primary tax jurisdiction code applicable to this payroll record (e.g., US-CA for California, UK for United Kingdom). Determines which tax tables and rates are applied during payroll calculation.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; IRS; HMRC; local tax authority

attributes.name: tax_withholding_status
attributes.description: The employee's federal/national tax filing status as declared on their withholding form (e.g., W-4 in the US), which determines the applicable tax withholding rate for this pay period.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; IRS Form W-4; local tax authority

attributes.name: total_tax_deduction
attributes.description: Aggregate amount withheld from gross pay for all applicable taxes (federal, state/provincial, local income tax, social security, Medicare/national insurance) during this pay period.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module; IRS Publication 15; GDPR; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: work_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the employee performed work during this pay period. Determines applicable tax jurisdiction, labor law, and regulatory compliance requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; GDPR; HIPAA; local labor law

attributes.name: workday_worker_code
attributes.description: The native worker identifier assigned by Workday HCM for the employee. Used for system-of-record traceability back to the Workday Payroll module.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll Module

attributes.name: email_address

attributes.name: is_gcp_regulated

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp

products.name: program_team_member
products.description: This association product represents the Role-based assignment between an employee and a clinical_program. It captures the operational team membership record that the CRO actively manages for each employee-program pairing, including the employee's functional GCP role on the program, FTE allocation, delegation authority, GCP certification status at assignment time, and the full lifecycle of the assignment. Each record links one employee to one clinical_program with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific assignment relationship. This is the SSOT for program team composition and workforce allocation across the clinical development portfolio.. Existence Justification: In clinical research operations, employees (CRAs, Medical Monitors, Data Managers, etc.) are actively assigned to multiple clinical programs simultaneously, and each clinical program has a team of many employees in distinct functional roles. This is a core operational reality in CROs — a Medical Monitor may oversee 3 oncology programs concurrently, while a single program may have 15+ staff across CRA, CRC, biostatistics, and regulatory functions. The business actively manages these assignments with role designations, FTE allocations, delegation authority levels, and GCP certification status per assignment — this is not derivable from transactional data but is an explicitly managed operational record.

attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC Configuration; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this therapeutic area classification ceased to be valid (null for currently active entries). Enables temporal validity management of the taxonomy, ensuring historical program classifications remain traceable after taxonomy updates.
attributes.references: Sponsor Portfolio Governance SOP; CDISC Therapeutic Area Standards Versioning; MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this therapeutic area classification became effective and valid for use in program classification and regulatory submissions. Supports temporal validity tracking for the reference master taxonomy.
attributes.references: Sponsor Portfolio Governance SOP; CDISC Therapeutic Area Standards Versioning; MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: global_disease_burden_rank
attributes.description: Relative ranking of this therapeutic area by global disease burden (e.g., based on WHO Global Burden of Disease data). Used in portfolio prioritization, business development decisions, and sponsor pipeline strategy assessments.
attributes.references: WHO Global Burden of Disease Study; WHO ICTPR; FDA CDER Strategic Plan

attributes.name: governance_owner
attributes.description: Name or role of the business owner responsible for maintaining and governing this therapeutic area classification (e.g., VP Therapeutic Area Head, Chief Medical Officer). Accountable for taxonomy accuracy and alignment with sponsor portfolio strategy.
attributes.references: Sponsor Data Governance Policy; ICH E6(R2) GCP; MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth of this therapeutic area within the taxonomy hierarchy. Level 1 represents the broadest classification (e.g., Oncology); higher levels represent sub-specialties (e.g., Level 2: Solid Tumors; Level 3: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer). Enables hierarchical roll-up in portfolio analytics.
attributes.references: CDISC Therapeutic Area Standards; Sponsor Portfolio Governance SOP

attributes.name: hierarchy_path
attributes.description: Full delimited path from the root therapeutic area to this node (e.g., 'Oncology > Solid Tumors > Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer'). Facilitates breadcrumb navigation in portfolio governance tools and enables efficient subtree queries without recursive joins.
attributes.references: Sponsor Portfolio Governance SOP; CDISC Therapeutic Area Standards

attributes.name: icd11_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 11th Revision (ICD-11) Code
attributes.description: WHO ICD-11 classification code aligned to this therapeutic area. Supports global regulatory submissions, epidemiological benchmarking, and alignment with health authority disease classification frameworks (FDA, EMA, PMDA, Health Canada).
attributes.references: WHO ICD-11 (International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision); WHO ICTPR; EMA Scientific Guidelines

attributes.name: is_oncology
attributes.description: Indicates whether this therapeutic area is classified as oncology or hematology-oncology. Triggers specific regulatory considerations (FDA Oncology Center of Excellence, EMA oncology guidelines, CTCAE grading requirements) and specialized safety monitoring protocols.
attributes.references: FDA Oncology Center of Excellence; EMA Oncology Scientific Guidelines; CTCAE (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events) v5.0; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: is_rare_disease
attributes.description: Indicates whether this therapeutic area is classified as a rare disease area (orphan disease), triggering specific regulatory designations (FDA Orphan Drug, EMA Orphan Medicinal Product), expedited review pathways, and specialized patient recruitment strategies.
attributes.references: FDA Orphan Drug Act (21 CFR Part 316); EMA Orphan Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; OHRP; WHO Rare Disease Definition

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code that most closely aligns with this therapeutic area. Enables cross-referencing of therapeutic area classifications with adverse event coding, safety signal detection in Oracle Argus Safety, and regulatory submissions using MedDRA terminology.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) v26+; ICH M1; FDA and EMA MedDRA Requirements

attributes.name: meddra_soc_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Name
attributes.description: Human-readable MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) name corresponding to the meddra_soc_code (e.g., 'Neoplasms benign, malignant and unspecified', 'Nervous system disorders'). Supports safety reporting alignment and regulatory submission consistency.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) v26+; ICH M1; FDA and EMA MedDRA Requirements

attributes.name: patient_population_type
attributes.description: Primary patient population type targeted by clinical programs in this therapeutic area. Drives regulatory requirements (e.g., pediatric investigation plans under EMA PUMA, FDA PREA), protocol design, and IRB/IEC considerations.
attributes.references: FDA Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA); EMA Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006; ICH E11(R1); OHRP 45 CFR Part 46

attributes.name: portfolio_priority_tier
attributes.description: Sponsor-assigned portfolio priority tier for this therapeutic area, reflecting strategic investment level and resource allocation priority (e.g., Tier 1 = core franchise, Tier 2 = growth area, Tier 3 = exploratory). Used in portfolio governance reviews and budget planning.
attributes.references: Sponsor Portfolio Governance SOP; ICH E8(R1) Strategic Planning

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_type
attributes.description: Typical primary endpoint category used in clinical trials within this therapeutic area (e.g., Overall Survival for Oncology, ADAS-Cog for CNS/Alzheimer's, ACR20 for Rheumatology, LVEF for Cardiovascular). Informs Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) design and biostatistical methodology selection.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance for Industry — Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials in Small Populations; ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: primary_regulatory_agency
attributes.description: Primary health authority with jurisdiction over clinical development programs in this therapeutic area for the sponsor's primary market. Determines applicable regulatory frameworks, submission formats (eCTD), and GCP inspection standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|TGA|Health Canada|multi-agency — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA (21 CFR Parts 312, 314, 601); EMA (EU CTR 536/2014); PMDA; MHRA; TGA; Health Canada; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: primary_regulatory_pathway
attributes.description: Primary regulatory submission pathway most commonly associated with programs in this therapeutic area (e.g., NDA for small molecules, BLA for biologics, MAA for EU submissions). Guides regulatory strategy planning and submission resource allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NDA|BLA|MAA|IND|510k|PMA|other — promote to reference product if additional pathways are needed]
attributes.references: FDA IND/NDA/BLA Regulations (21 CFR Parts 312, 314, 601); EMA MAA Guidelines; ICH CTD (Common Technical Document); ICH M4

attributes.name: regulatory_classification
attributes.description: Regulatory classification or designation relevant to this therapeutic area from applicable health authorities (e.g., Orphan Drug designation eligibility for Rare Disease, Breakthrough Therapy eligibility for Oncology, Priority Review eligibility). Informs regulatory strategy and submission planning.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 316 (Orphan Drug); FDA Breakthrough Therapy Guidance; EMA Orphan Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: safety_system_ta_code
attributes.description: Therapeutic area code as configured in Oracle Argus Safety for adverse event case routing, signal detection configuration, and regulatory case submission (ICSRs). Ensures consistent therapeutic area classification across safety reporting workflows.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety Configuration; ICH E2B(R3) ICSR; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this therapeutic area classification was sourced or is mastered (e.g., Oracle Siebel CTMS, Veeva Vault). Supports data lineage tracking and cross-system reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.value_regex: Oracle Siebel CTMS|Veeva Vault|Manual Entry|SAP S/4HANA|other
attributes.references: Sponsor Data Governance Policy; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; CDISC Data Management Standards

attributes.name: sponsor_portfolio_category
attributes.description: Sponsor-defined portfolio category or franchise label aligned to this therapeutic area (e.g., Oncology Franchise, Rare Disease Unit, Immunoscience). Maps the standardized therapeutic area taxonomy to the sponsor's internal portfolio governance structure for cross-program analytics and budget allocation.
attributes.references: Sponsor Portfolio Governance SOP; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_code
attributes.description: Short, standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the therapeutic area within the sponsor portfolio (e.g., ONCO, IMMUNO, CNS, CARDIO, INFECT, RARE). Used as a business key in CTMS, EDC study builds, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC Therapeutic Area Standards; ICH E8(R1); FDA CDER Therapeutic Area Guidance

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the therapeutic area, including the disease scope, patient population, and key biological mechanisms addressed. Used in regulatory submissions, portfolio governance documents, and sponsor-facing communications.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA CDER Therapeutic Area Guidance; EMA Scientific Guidelines

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_name
attributes.description: Full human-readable name of the therapeutic area (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Central Nervous System, Cardiovascular, Infectious Disease, Rare Disease). Used as the primary display label across portfolio governance dashboards and regulatory documents.
attributes.references: CDISC Therapeutic Area Standards; ICH E8(R1); WHO ICD-11 Disease Classification

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the therapeutic area record within the reference master. 'active' indicates the area is in use for program classification; 'deprecated' indicates it has been superseded by a revised taxonomy entry; 'under_review' indicates pending governance approval for changes.
attributes.references: Sponsor Portfolio Governance SOP; MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: typical_trial_phase
attributes.description: Most common clinical trial phase(s) conducted within this therapeutic area, reflecting the maturity of the pipeline and typical development strategy (e.g., Phase III for established Oncology indications, Phase I/II for Rare Disease). Supports portfolio planning and resource forecasting.
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase II|Phase III|Phase IV|Phase I/II|Phase II/III
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU CTR 536/2014)

attributes.name: unmet_medical_need_level
attributes.description: Assessment of the level of unmet medical need in this therapeutic area, as evaluated by the sponsor's medical and regulatory teams. Influences regulatory designation eligibility (Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, PRIME), portfolio prioritization, and pricing strategy.
attributes.references: FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation Guidance; EMA PRIME Scheme; ICH E8(R1); WHO Essential Medicines List

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this therapeutic area record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the therapeutic area taxonomy entry (e.g., '1.0', '2.1'). Tracks changes to the classification definition over time, supporting audit trails required under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity principles (ALCOA+).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; MasterControl Document Control

products.description: Master record for the integrated development plan (IDP) or clinical development plan (CDP) associated with a clinical program. Captures plan version, plan type (initial, revised, approved), planning horizon (years), overall program strategy narrative, target product profile (TPP) reference, regulatory pathway (standard, accelerated, breakthrough, orphan), planned number of studies, planned total subjects, planned program budget envelope, plan approval date, and plan author. Tracks the strategic blueprint governing all program activities.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sponsor.master_agreement. Business justification: Program plans are executed under the commercial framework of a master agreement. Linking program_plan to master_agreement enables financial and scope compliance checks against contracted terms. No exi

attributes.name: organization_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor organization funding and overseeing this clinical development program. Links the plan to the sponsor master record for contractual and regulatory accountability.

attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this version of the Clinical Development Plan (CDP) received formal governance approval (e.g., from the Development Committee or Executive Sponsor). Marks the transition from draft/review to approved status.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; MasterControl Document Control; Veeva Vault Quality Management

attributes.name: approval_target_date
attributes.description: Planned date for receipt of regulatory approval (e.g., FDA approval, EMA CHMP positive opinion) for the primary indication. Used for commercial launch planning and portfolio milestone reporting.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA Review Timelines; EMA CHMP Review Procedures; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: breakthrough_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the investigational product has received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) or EMA PRIME (PRIority MEdicines) designation for the target indication. Enables more intensive FDA/EMA guidance and rolling review.
attributes.references: FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation (FDASIA 2012); EMA PRIME Scheme; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: budget_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the planned program budget (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Enables multi-currency portfolio reporting and financial consolidation.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA Finance; SOX Financial Reporting Controls

attributes.name: compound_code
attributes.description: The sponsor's internal compound or asset code for the investigational product covered by this development plan (e.g., 'XYZ-001', 'ABC-123'). Used as the primary asset identifier across portfolio management systems.
attributes.references: FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E8(R1); Oracle Siebel CTMS Asset Management

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this program plan record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: development_phase
attributes.description: The current or leading clinical development phase of the program at the time this plan was authored. Indicates the maturity of the asset and the scope of the CDP (e.g., phase_1 for first-in-human programs, phase_3 for pivotal programs). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: preclinical|phase_1|phase_1_2|phase_2|phase_2_3|phase_3|phase_4 — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Phases Guidance

attributes.name: dsmb_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) is required for the program based on the risk profile, study design, and regulatory requirements. Drives governance structure planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA DSMB Guidance (2006); ICH E9(R1); EMA Guideline on DMC

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this version of the Clinical Development Plan (CDP) is expected to conclude or be superseded. Null for open-ended plans. Used for planning horizon calculations and version lifecycle management.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: fih_target_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the first-in-human (FIH) dose administration for the program. A key program milestone used for portfolio milestone tracking and IND/CTA filing planning.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; EMA CTA Guidelines; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: go_no_go_criteria
attributes.description: Documented criteria that will be used to make go/no-go decisions at key program milestones (e.g., Phase II proof-of-concept readout, interim analysis results). Defines the evidence thresholds required to advance the program.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9(R1) Estimands; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

attributes.name: inn_name
attributes.description: The International Nonproprietary Name (INN) or proposed INN (pINN) for the investigational product, as assigned or applied for from the WHO INN Programme. Used in regulatory submissions and scientific publications.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; EMA INN Guidelines; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: key_assumptions
attributes.description: Documented key assumptions underpinning the plan (e.g., enrollment rate assumptions, regulatory review timelines, manufacturing readiness). Critical for plan risk assessment and scenario planning. Classified as confidential.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: lead_regulatory_agency
attributes.description: The primary regulatory authority for the lead market submission under this development plan (e.g., FDA for US, EMA for EU, PMDA for Japan). Determines the primary regulatory strategy and submission format (eCTD). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|TGA|Health_Canada|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314/601; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E8(R1); PMDA Guidelines

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: The drug modality or product class of the investigational compound (e.g., small_molecule, biologic, cell_therapy, gene_therapy). Drives regulatory strategy, manufacturing requirements, and safety monitoring approach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|cell_therapy|gene_therapy|oligonucleotide|vaccine|combination|radiopharmaceutical — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Guideline on Biologics; ICH Q6A/Q6B; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: nda_submission_target_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the primary regulatory submission (NDA/BLA/MAA) to the lead regulatory authority. A key program milestone driving backward planning for Phase III completion, Clinical Study Report (CSR) preparation, and eCTD assembly.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); FDA 21 CFR Part 601 (BLA); EMA MAA Guidelines; ICH CTD M4; ICH E3 CSR

attributes.name: orphan_drug_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the investigational product has received or is seeking Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) from FDA or EMA for the target indication. Orphan designation confers regulatory incentives including market exclusivity and fee waivers.
attributes.references: FDA Orphan Drug Act 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Orphan Regulation EC 141/2000; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: owner_role
attributes.description: The organizational role or function responsible for owning and maintaining this Clinical Development Plan (CDP) (e.g., 'Global Program Director', 'Clinical Development Lead', 'VP Clinical Development'). Supports governance accountability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ICH E8(R1); Workday HCM Organizational Structure

attributes.name: plan_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable identifier for the Clinical Development Plan (CDP) or Integrated Development Plan (IDP). Follows the organizational naming convention (e.g., CDP-ONCO001-2024-v1). Used in regulatory submissions and governance documents.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND Regulations 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the program plan record. Draft indicates work-in-progress; under_review indicates governance review in progress; approved indicates formal sign-off received; superseded indicates replaced by a newer version; retired indicates no longer active.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); MasterControl Document Control; Veeva Vault Quality Management

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Classification of the plan document indicating its stage in the approval lifecycle: initial (first draft), revised (updated after review), amended (post-approval change), approved (formally endorsed), or final (locked version submitted to regulatory authority).
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); Veeva Vault Document Lifecycle; MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: planned_budget_usd
attributes.description: The total approved budget envelope for the entire clinical development program as defined in this plan version, expressed in US Dollars (USD). Represents the high-level financial commitment approved by governance. Classified as confidential due to commercial sensitivity.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Project Accounting; SOX Financial Reporting Controls; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: planned_study_count
attributes.description: The total number of clinical studies (Phase I through Phase III/IV) planned under this development program as defined in the CDP. Used for portfolio capacity planning and milestone tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); Oracle Siebel CTMS Program Planning

attributes.name: planned_subject_count
attributes.description: The total number of subjects (patients or healthy volunteers) planned for enrollment across all studies within the program as defined in the CDP. Drives site selection, patient recruitment strategy, and budget planning.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9 Statistical Principles; FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: planning_horizon_years
attributes.description: The total number of years covered by this Clinical Development Plan (CDP), from first-in-human (FIH) or current phase through anticipated regulatory approval. Drives long-range resource planning and portfolio forecasting.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND Regulations 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: poa_target_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the proof-of-concept (POC) or proof-of-activity (POA) readout, typically at the end of Phase II. A critical go/no-go decision milestone for program continuation and investment decisions.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; Oracle Siebel CTMS Milestone Tracking

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_description
attributes.description: Description of the primary clinical endpoint(s) that the program is designed to demonstrate, as defined in the CDP. Aligns with the Target Product Profile (TPP) and regulatory agency expectations for the indication.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Estimands; ICH E8(R1); FDA Endpoint Guidance; EMA Guideline on Clinical Endpoints

attributes.name: regulatory_pathway
attributes.description: The regulatory development pathway designated for the program asset. Drives planning assumptions for review timelines and submission strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|accelerated|breakthrough|orphan|fast_track|priority_review|rolling_review — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation; EMA PRIME Scheme; ICH E8(R1); EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this version of the Clinical Development Plan (CDP) becomes effective and governs program activities. Corresponds to the plan approval date for approved versions.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: strategy_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the overall clinical development strategy for the program, including scientific rationale, competitive landscape considerations, regulatory strategy, and key decision points. Classified as confidential due to proprietary strategic content.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Scientific Advice Guidelines

attributes.name: submission_type
attributes.description: The anticipated regulatory submission type targeted by this development plan. IND (Investigational New Drug), NDA (New Drug Application), BLA (Biologics License Application), MAA (Marketing Authorization Application), sNDA (supplemental NDA), or sBLA (supplemental BLA). Governs the regulatory strategy and data package requirements.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); FDA 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); FDA 21 CFR Part 601 (BLA); EMA MAA Guidelines; ICH CTD M4

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Full descriptive title of the Clinical Development Plan (CDP) or Integrated Development Plan (IDP), including the therapeutic indication and compound name (e.g., 'Integrated Development Plan for Compound XYZ in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma').
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND Regulations 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: tpp_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier or version reference for the Target Product Profile (TPP) that defines the desired product characteristics (efficacy, safety, dosing) guiding the development plan. The TPP is the strategic anchor for all clinical and regulatory decisions.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Target Product Profile (2007); ICH E8(R1); EMA Guideline on TPP

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this program plan record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and Silver Layer incremental processing.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier of the Clinical Development Plan (CDP) following the organization's document versioning convention (e.g., 1.0, 2.1, 3.0). Incremented with each approved revision to maintain a complete audit trail of plan evolution.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; ICH E6(R2) GCP; MasterControl Document Control

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_date

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_required

attributes.name: superseded_date

attributes.name: timeline_impact_flag
