products.name: risk
products.description: Master record for program-level risks identified through risk management processes. Captures risk identifier, risk category (scientific, regulatory, operational, competitive, financial, safety), risk description, probability rating, impact rating, risk score, risk owner, mitigation strategy, contingency plan, risk status (open, mitigated, closed, accepted), identification date, and last review date. Supports proactive program risk management and portfolio governance reporting.
products.reference: Program Risk Register

attributes.name: risk_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the program-level risk record within the clinical development program risk register.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 14971 Risk Management

attributes.name: clinical_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical development program to which this risk belongs, enabling portfolio-level risk aggregation and governance reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: FK to workforce.employee

attributes.name: owner_id
attributes.description: FK to workforce.employee

attributes.name: risk_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the workforce member (typically a Program Director, Clinical Lead, or Regulatory Affairs Lead) accountable for monitoring and managing this risk to resolution. Aligns with RACI accountability frameworks in GCP-compliant program governance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: actual_resolution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk was actually resolved (mitigated, closed, or accepted). Null if the risk remains open. Used for cycle time analysis and governance performance reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: affected_studies
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of study protocol numbers or identifiers within the program that are impacted by this risk. Supports cross-study impact analysis and portfolio governance reporting. (Formal study-level linkage is established via the program_risk_study association product.)
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: capa_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier of any associated CAPA record in MasterControl or the quality management system, linking this risk to formal corrective and preventive action processes where applicable.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 820; MasterControl CAPA Module

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, reviewer notes, governance meeting minutes excerpts, or supplementary information related to the risk that does not fit structured fields. Supports audit trail completeness per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: contingency_plan
attributes.description: Documented fallback actions to be executed if the risk materializes despite mitigation efforts (e.g., 'If IND placed on clinical hold, initiate Type B meeting with FDA within 30 days'). Supports business continuity and regulatory response planning.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Clinical Holds

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail, ALCOA+ compliance, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk was formally escalated to a higher governance level (e.g., program steering committee, sponsor, DSMB/DMC). Null if escalation has not occurred.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9

attributes.name: escalation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk requires escalation to program leadership, the sponsor, DSMB/DMC, or a regulatory authority based on its risk score or category. Drives governance workflow routing.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_target
attributes.description: The governance body or individual to whom the risk has been escalated (e.g., Program Steering Committee, Sponsor Medical Monitor, DSMB, FDA). Supports audit trail and governance accountability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9

attributes.name: financial_exposure_usd
attributes.description: Estimated financial exposure or potential cost impact if the risk materializes, expressed in US dollars. Used for financial risk quantification, budget contingency planning, and sponsor reporting. Classified as confidential due to commercial sensitivity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); SAP S/4HANA Project Accounting; SOX Financial Reporting Controls

attributes.name: identified_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the risk was first formally identified and entered into the program risk register. Supports risk aging analysis and regulatory audit trails per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: identifier
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-known unique code assigned to this risk record within the program risk register (e.g., PRSK-ONC-000123). Used in governance reports, DSMB/DMC submissions, and sponsor communications.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 14971; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

attributes.name: impact_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the severity of consequences if the risk materializes, considering impact on program timeline, patient safety, regulatory approval, and financial outcomes.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: impact_score
attributes.description: Numeric value corresponding to the impact rating (e.g., 1=very low, 2=low, 3=medium, 4=high, 5=very high). Combined with probability_score to compute the composite risk score.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk was most recently reviewed and assessed by the risk owner or program governance committee. Supports overdue review identification and governance compliance tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: mitigation_status
attributes.description: Current implementation status of the mitigation strategy: not_started, in_progress, completed, or on_hold. Enables tracking of mitigation execution progress separate from the overall risk status.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: mitigation_strategy
attributes.description: Detailed description of the planned or implemented actions to reduce the probability or impact of the risk (e.g., 'Engage additional regulatory consultant for IND submission review', 'Activate backup sites to offset enrollment shortfall'). Core field for proactive risk management per ICH Q9.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2); FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ISO 14971

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the next formal review of this risk. Drives automated review reminders and governance calendar scheduling. Frequency is typically determined by risk priority (e.g., critical risks reviewed monthly).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9

attributes.name: patient_safety_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk has a direct or potential impact on patient safety, including SAE/SUSAR reporting obligations, DSMB/DMC review triggers, or clinical hold risk. Ensures safety risks receive mandatory expedited review.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Derived priority classification based on the risk score (e.g., critical: score 20–25, high: 12–19, medium: 6–11, low: 1–5). Used to drive escalation workflows, governance review frequency, and resource allocation decisions.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971

attributes.name: probability_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative likelihood rating that the risk event will materialize during the program lifecycle. Typically assessed on a 5-point scale (very low to very high) per the program's risk management framework. Used in risk scoring and prioritization.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; ISO 14971; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: probability_score
attributes.description: Numeric value corresponding to the probability rating (e.g., 1=very low, 2=low, 3=medium, 4=high, 5=very high). Used in quantitative risk score calculation and portfolio-level risk heat map generation.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971

attributes.name: regulatory_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk has a direct potential impact on regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, eCTD) or regulatory agency interactions (FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, TGA, Health Canada). Drives regulatory affairs team notification workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: residual_impact_rating
attributes.description: Reassessed impact rating after mitigation controls have been applied. Used alongside residual_probability_rating to compute the residual risk score and confirm risk acceptability.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971

attributes.name: residual_probability_rating
attributes.description: Reassessed probability rating after mitigation controls have been applied. Compared against the initial probability_rating to demonstrate risk reduction effectiveness.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971

attributes.name: residual_risk_score
attributes.description: Composite risk score after mitigation (residual probability score × residual impact score). Compared to the pre-mitigation risk_score to quantify risk reduction and determine if the residual risk is within acceptable tolerance.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the risk domain: scientific (e.g., efficacy uncertainty), regulatory (e.g., IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submission risk), operational (e.g., site activation delays), competitive (e.g., competitor trial results), financial (e.g., budget overrun), or safety (e.g., emerging SAE signal).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: risk_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the nature of the risk, its potential cause, and the business context in which it was identified. Supports risk review meetings, DSMB/DMC briefings, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9; ISO 14971

attributes.name: risk_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the risk record: open (active and unresolved), mitigated (controls applied and risk reduced), closed (risk no longer applicable or resolved), accepted (risk acknowledged and formally accepted by program leadership without further mitigation).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ISO 14971; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: score
attributes.description: Composite numeric risk score, typically calculated as probability_score × impact_score (range 1–25 on a 5×5 matrix). Drives risk prioritization, escalation thresholds, and portfolio risk heat map reporting.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: source_record_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the corresponding record in the originating source system (e.g., CTMS risk ID, Veeva Vault document ID, MasterControl CAPA ID). Supports data lineage tracing and reconciliation between the lakehouse and operational systems.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this risk record originated (e.g., Oracle Siebel CTMS for operational risks, Veeva Vault for regulatory/quality risks, MasterControl for CAPA-linked risks, or manual entry via governance process).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: subcategory
attributes.description: More granular classification within the risk category (e.g., within 'regulatory': IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, PMDA, EMA; within 'safety': SAE signal, SUSAR reporting, DSMB review). Supports detailed risk analytics and reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ind_approval|nda_submission|bla_submission|maa_submission|ema_review|pmda_review|sae_signal|susar_reporting|dsmb_review|site_activation|patient_recruitment|data_quality|supply_chain|budget|competitor_data|scientific_validity — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MedDRA SOC/PT hierarchy; ICH Q9

attributes.name: target_resolution_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the risk is expected to be mitigated, closed, or formally accepted. Used for milestone tracking and program governance reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ISO 14971

attributes.name: timeline_impact_days
attributes.description: Estimated number of calendar days by which the program or study timeline could be delayed if this risk materializes. Used for critical path analysis, milestone risk assessment, and sponsor portfolio reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Short, human-readable label summarizing the risk (e.g., 'Delayed IND approval due to CMC data gaps'). Used as the primary display name in risk dashboards and portfolio governance reports.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: tolerance_threshold
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable risk score defined by the program governance framework. Risks with residual_risk_score exceeding this threshold require escalation to senior leadership or the sponsor. Supports risk acceptance decision-making.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: trigger_criteria
attributes.description: Defined conditions or early warning indicators that signal the risk is materializing or escalating (e.g., 'Enrollment rate falls below 60% of target for two consecutive months'). Supports proactive risk monitoring and automated alerting.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this risk record, in ISO 8601 format. Supports change tracking, audit trail completeness, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: parent_risk_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on risk (parent_risk_id)

products.name: risk_mitigation
products.description: Transactional record capturing individual risk mitigation actions and their execution status for program-level risks. Captures mitigation action description, action owner, planned completion date, actual completion date, action status (planned, in-progress, completed, overdue), effectiveness assessment, and residual risk level after mitigation. Enables tracking of risk response execution and effectiveness evaluation within the program risk management framework.
products.reference: Risk Mitigation Action

attributes.name: risk_mitigation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each risk mitigation action record within the program risk management framework. Primary key for this entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; ISO 14971 Risk Management

attributes.name: clinical_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical development program to which this mitigation action belongs. Links the mitigation action to the overarching program risk management framework.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: compliance_capa_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Reference ID
attributes.description: Reference to an associated CAPA record in the quality management system (MasterControl) when this mitigation action is formally linked to a CAPA. Enables traceability between risk mitigation and quality event management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100; MasterControl CAPA tracking

attributes.name: primary_risk_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the individual (employee or contractor) accountable for executing and completing this mitigation action. Serves as the PARTY_REFERENCE category for this TRANSACTION_HEADER entity. Typically a Program Manager, Risk Manager, or functional lead.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GCP; Workday HCM workforce records

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_id
attributes.description: Reference to a protocol deviation record that triggered or is associated with this mitigation action. Supports traceability between compliance events and risk response actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; compliance.protocol_deviation

attributes.name: quaternary_risk_action_owner_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quaternary Risk Action Owner Employee Id
attributes.description: FK to workforce.employee

attributes.name: risk_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent program-level risk record that this mitigation action is designed to address. Establishes the parent-child relationship between a risk and its mitigation actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ISO 14971; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

attributes.name: tertiary_risk_effectiveness_reviewer_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the individual who conducted the formal effectiveness review of this mitigation action. Typically a QA lead, Program Manager, or independent reviewer per GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; MasterControl CAPA; GCP audit trail requirements

attributes.name: action_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the specific mitigation action to be taken, including the approach, scope, and expected mechanism by which the action reduces the identified risk.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.0; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.62; ISO 14971 Section 6

attributes.name: action_owner_role
attributes.description: Functional role or job title of the mitigation action owner at the time of assignment (e.g., Program Manager, Clinical Operations Lead, Biostatistics Lead). Supports accountability reporting and escalation routing.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GCP; Workday HCM

attributes.name: action_status
attributes.description: Current execution lifecycle state of the mitigation action. Drives risk dashboard reporting and escalation workflows. 'overdue' is set when planned_completion_date has passed without completion. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for this TRANSACTION_HEADER entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; MasterControl CAPA workflow standards

attributes.name: action_title
attributes.description: Short, human-readable title summarizing the mitigation action (e.g., 'Implement enhanced site monitoring protocol'). Used as the IDENTITY_LABEL in risk registers and dashboards.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: Classification of the mitigation action by its strategic intent: preventive (reduces likelihood), corrective (addresses root cause after occurrence), contingency (response plan if risk materializes), transfer (shifts risk to another party), or acceptance (formal acknowledgment of residual risk).
attributes.references: ISO 14971; ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: actual_completion_date
attributes.description: The date on which the mitigation action was fully executed and confirmed complete. Null if the action has not yet been completed. Used to calculate cycle time and assess timeliness of risk response.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; MasterControl CAPA tracking

attributes.name: actual_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which execution of the mitigation action actually commenced. Compared against planned_start_date to assess schedule adherence and identify systemic delays in risk response.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: closure_justification
attributes.description: Narrative justification for formally closing this mitigation action, documenting the evidence that the action was completed, verified, and the residual risk accepted. Required for regulatory inspection readiness and TMF documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; Veeva Vault eTMF; MasterControl CAPA closure

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this mitigation action record was first created in the system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for this TRANSACTION_HEADER entity. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: data_integrity_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the risk being mitigated has a direct or potential impact on clinical data integrity (ALCOA+ principles). True = data integrity is implicated; False = no direct data integrity impact. Relevant for EDC and CDISC compliance.
attributes.references: ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC SDTM/ADaM standards

attributes.name: due_date_revised
attributes.description: Updated target completion date if the original planned_completion_date was formally extended. Captures approved timeline changes and distinguishes legitimate extensions from overdue actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl CAPA; Oracle Siebel CTMS change management

attributes.name: effectiveness_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative from the effectiveness reviewer documenting the rationale for the effectiveness rating, evidence reviewed, and any observations about residual risk or further actions needed.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; MasterControl CAPA; ALCOA+

attributes.name: effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Post-execution assessment of how effectively the mitigation action reduced or eliminated the identified risk. Populated after action completion and formal effectiveness review. Drives decisions on whether additional mitigation is required.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; ISO 14971 Section 9; MasterControl CAPA effectiveness check

attributes.name: effectiveness_review_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal effectiveness assessment of the completed mitigation action was conducted. Required for CAPA closure and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; MasterControl CAPA tracking; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100

attributes.name: implementation_approach
attributes.description: Narrative description of the specific method, process, or procedure to be used in executing the mitigation action. May reference SOPs, work instructions, or system configurations (e.g., EDC edit checks, RTSM alerts).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GCP SOP standards; MasterControl document control

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this mitigation action record was most recently modified. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category for this TRANSACTION_HEADER entity. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: linked_milestone
attributes.description: Name or code of the program milestone (e.g., 'First Patient In', 'Database Lock', 'NDA Submission') to which this mitigation action is tied. Enables milestone-level risk tracking and critical path analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS milestone tracking; FDA IND/NDA submission timelines

attributes.name: mitigation_action_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the mitigation action, used in risk registers, audit trails, and regulatory submissions. Follows the pattern MIT-<PROGRAM_CODE>-<SEQUENCE>. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for this TRANSACTION_HEADER entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ISO 14971

attributes.name: mitigation_strategy
attributes.description: High-level strategic approach applied to manage the risk, aligned with ICH Q9 risk management principles. Distinguishes the overarching strategy from the specific action_type.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; ISO 14971 Section 6; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

attributes.name: planned_completion_date
attributes.description: The target date by which the mitigation action is expected to be fully executed and closed. Used to calculate overdue status and drive risk dashboard KPI reporting. Serves as the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date-precision) for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ISO 14971

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which execution of the mitigation action is planned to begin. Used for timeline planning, Gantt chart generation, and milestone tracking within the program risk management plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS milestone tracking

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to this mitigation action, reflecting the urgency of execution relative to the risk severity and program timeline. Drives resource allocation and escalation thresholds.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ISO 14971

attributes.name: recurrence_prevention_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes describing measures put in place to prevent recurrence of the risk after mitigation. Supports lessons-learned capture and cross-program knowledge transfer within the clinical development portfolio.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; MasterControl CAPA; FDA CAPA guidance; ISO 14971

attributes.name: regulatory_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this mitigation action has direct implications for regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA) or regulatory agency notifications. True = regulatory impact identified; False = no direct regulatory impact.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: residual_risk_acceptance_date
attributes.description: The date on which the residual risk was formally accepted by the authorized governance body. Null if residual risk has not yet been accepted or if further mitigation is required.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: residual_risk_accepted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the residual risk level after mitigation has been formally accepted by the program risk governance body (e.g., DSMB, DMC, or Sponsor). True = accepted; False = further mitigation required.
attributes.references: ICH Q9; ISO 14971 Section 7; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: residual_risk_level
attributes.description: The assessed level of risk remaining after the mitigation action has been fully implemented and its effectiveness confirmed. Used to determine whether the residual risk is acceptable or requires further mitigation per the program risk acceptance criteria.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; ISO 14971 Section 7; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: responsible_function
attributes.description: The organizational function or department accountable for executing this mitigation action (e.g., Clinical Operations, Data Management, Pharmacovigilance, Regulatory Affairs, Biostatistics). Supports cross-functional risk governance reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS organizational structure

attributes.name: risk_domain
attributes.description: The functional domain of the parent risk that this mitigation action addresses. Enables domain-specific risk reporting and cross-program benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: safety|regulatory|data_quality|operational|financial|supply_chain|site|subject_recruitment — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH Q9; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this mitigation action record originated (e.g., Oracle Siebel CTMS risk module, MasterControl CAPA module, Veeva Vault quality management). Supports data lineage and Silver Layer provenance tracking.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; Databricks data lineage standards

attributes.name: subject_safety_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the risk being mitigated has a direct or potential impact on subject safety. True = subject safety is implicated; False = no direct subject safety impact. Drives prioritization and DSMB/DMC notification requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP regulations

attributes.name: supporting_systems
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of operational systems involved in executing or monitoring this mitigation action (e.g., Medidata Rave, Oracle Argus Safety, Veeva Vault). Supports system-level impact analysis and integration planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC standards

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: The date on which implementation of the mitigation action was formally verified as complete and effective. Distinct from actual_completion_date (when the action was done) and effectiveness_review_date (when effectiveness was assessed).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GCP; ALCOA+; MasterControl audit management

attributes.name: verification_method
attributes.description: Description of the method used to verify that the mitigation action has been implemented as planned (e.g., site visit, SDV, EDC audit trail review, document review in Veeva Vault, monitoring report review). Supports GCP audit readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ALCOA+

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Incrementing version counter for this mitigation action record, supporting optimistic concurrency control and audit trail versioning in the Databricks Silver Layer. Incremented on each substantive update.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; Databricks Delta Lake versioning

attributes.name: escalated_risk_mitigation_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on risk_mitigation (escalated_risk_mitigation_id)

products.name: assumption
products.description: Master record for key planning assumptions underlying the clinical development plan and program timeline. Captures assumption description, assumption category (enrollment rate, regulatory timeline, safety profile, competitive landscape, manufacturing readiness), assumption owner, confidence level, sensitivity to program outcome (high/medium/low), validation status, validation date, and assumption review frequency. Tracks the dependency assumptions that, if invalidated, would trigger program plan revisions.
products.reference: Program Planning Assumption

attributes.name: assumption_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the program assumption record within the clinical development program planning framework.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies

attributes.name: assumption_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Workday HCM workforce record of the individual (typically a Program Director, Clinical Lead, or Regulatory Affairs Lead) accountable for maintaining, validating, and updating this assumption.
attributes.references: GCP ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; Workday HCM

attributes.name: assumption_validated_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Workday HCM workforce record of the individual who performed or approved the most recent validation of this assumption.
attributes.references: GCP ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: clinical_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical development program to which this assumption belongs. Links the assumption to its parent program for portfolio governance and milestone tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: FK to workforce.employee

attributes.name: owner_id
attributes.description: FK to workforce.employee

attributes.name: parent_assumption_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier linking this assumption to a higher-level parent assumption, enabling hierarchical assumption structures within the clinical development plan (e.g., a site-level enrollment assumption nested under a program-level enrollment assumption).
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: applicable_geography
attributes.description: Geographic scope to which this assumption applies, expressed as ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or regional designations (e.g., 'USA', 'GBR', 'JPN', 'Global'). Relevant for enrollment rate, regulatory timeline, and site activation assumptions.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ISO 3166-1; FDA; EMA; PMDA; Health Canada; TGA

attributes.name: applicable_phase
attributes.description: Clinical development phase(s) to which this assumption applies. Allows program planners to scope assumptions to specific phases of the development program (Phase 1 through Phase 4 or across all phases).
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: assumption_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the planning assumption type that drives program timeline and resource planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: enrollment_rate|regulatory_timeline|safety_profile|competitive_landscape|manufacturing_readiness|biomarker_prevalence|dropout_rate — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs; CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: assumption_code
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code assigned to this planning assumption for cross-referencing in clinical development plans, program governance documents, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); CDISC Study Design Model

attributes.name: assumption_description
attributes.description: Full narrative description of the planning assumption, including the basis for the assumption, supporting evidence, and its role in the clinical development plan timeline and resource projections.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: assumption_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the planning assumption within the program governance workflow. Drives whether the assumption is actively used in program planning or has been retired/replaced.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: assumption_value
attributes.description: The specific quantitative or qualitative value of the assumption (e.g., '2.5 patients/site/month', '18 months for FDA review', '15% screen failure rate'). Stored as STRING to accommodate diverse assumption types across categories.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); CDISC Protocol Representation Model; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the degree of certainty in the planning assumption, based on available evidence, historical data, and expert judgment. Drives risk-adjusted program timeline and resource planning.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: confidence_rationale
attributes.description: Narrative explanation supporting the assigned confidence level, including references to historical study data, literature, competitive intelligence, or expert opinion used to substantiate the assumption.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this program assumption record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for ALCOA+ audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Primary source of data or evidence underpinning this assumption (e.g., 'Medidata Rave enrollment metrics', 'Published literature – NEJM 2022', 'FDA precedent database', 'Internal historical study database', 'Competitive intelligence report').
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ALCOA+; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: dependency_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the program plan elements, milestones, studies, or other assumptions that are dependent on this assumption. Identifies what would need to be revised if this assumption is invalidated.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this assumption version is considered active and applicable to program planning. Supports temporal versioning of assumptions across the clinical development lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this assumption version ceases to be active. Null indicates the assumption is currently in effect. Supports historical tracking of assumption changes across program lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: invalidation_trigger
attributes.description: Specific, pre-defined condition or threshold that, if observed, would constitute invalidation of this assumption and trigger a program plan revision (e.g., 'Enrollment rate falls below 1.0 patients/site/month for 3 consecutive months').
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Guidance for Industry: Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: is_dependency_trigger
attributes.description: Indicates whether invalidation of this assumption would trigger a mandatory revision of dependent program plan elements, milestones, or other assumptions. True = this is a critical dependency assumption requiring escalation upon invalidation.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs; ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which this assumption was most recently formally reviewed by the program governance committee or assumption owner, regardless of whether the assumption value was changed.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); GCP ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: lower_bound_value
attributes.description: Pessimistic or minimum plausible value for the assumption used in downside scenario planning and sensitivity analysis (e.g., '1.5 patients/site/month' as the low-end enrollment rate estimate).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next formal review of this assumption by the program governance committee or assumption owner. Drives automated review reminders in the CTMS and program planning tools.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); GCP ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: regulatory_agency
attributes.description: Primary regulatory agency relevant to this assumption, particularly for regulatory timeline and submission assumptions. Drives agency-specific planning parameters in the clinical development plan. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|TGA|Health_Canada|WHO|Other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA; EMA; PMDA; MHRA; TGA; Health Canada; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: review_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency at which this assumption must be reviewed and revalidated by the assumption owner or program governance committee to ensure continued relevance to the clinical development plan.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: risk_mitigation_plan
attributes.description: Description of the contingency or mitigation actions to be executed if this assumption is invalidated, including fallback strategies, alternative approaches, and escalation paths within the program governance framework.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs

attributes.name: sensitivity_to_program
attributes.description: Assessment of the degree to which invalidation of this assumption would materially impact the program timeline, budget, or probability of success. High sensitivity assumptions trigger mandatory program plan revision if invalidated.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs; ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management

attributes.name: subcategory
attributes.description: Further granular classification within the assumption category (e.g., within 'enrollment_rate': 'screen_failure_rate', 'site_activation_rate'). Enables detailed segmentation for sensitivity analysis and program risk management.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: supporting_document_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier or URL to supporting documentation in Veeva Vault eTMF or document management system (e.g., Clinical Development Plan version, Feasibility Report, Regulatory Intelligence Report) that substantiates this assumption.
attributes.references: GCP ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area or disease indication to which this assumption applies (e.g., 'Oncology', 'Cardiovascular', 'Rare Disease', 'Neuroscience'). Enables cross-program benchmarking of assumptions within the same therapeutic area.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); MedDRA; WHO International Classification of Diseases (ICD)

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Concise, human-readable title summarizing the planning assumption (e.g., 'Phase 3 Enrollment Rate – North America Sites'). Used as the primary label in program governance dashboards and Clinical Development Plan (CDP) documents.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Development Programs

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this program assumption record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for ALCOA+ audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: upper_bound_value
attributes.description: Optimistic or maximum plausible value for the assumption used in upside scenario planning and sensitivity analysis (e.g., '4.0 patients/site/month' as the high-end enrollment rate estimate).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance for Industry: Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: validation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the assumption was most recently validated or invalidated by the assumption owner or program governance committee. Used to assess currency of assumptions in program planning.
attributes.references: GCP ICH E6(R2); ICH E8(R1); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: validation_method
attributes.description: Description of the method or evidence source used to validate the assumption (e.g., 'Historical enrollment data from Phase 2 study', 'FDA precedent review', 'DSMB interim analysis', 'Competitive intelligence report').
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); GCP ICH E6(R2); CDISC Protocol Representation Model

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Current validation state of the assumption, reflecting whether supporting evidence has been reviewed and confirmed. Validated assumptions are used as confirmed inputs to program planning; invalidated assumptions trigger plan revision workflows.
attributes.references: GCP ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: value_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the assumption value where applicable (e.g., 'patients/site/month', 'months', 'percentage', 'mg/kg'). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of quantitative assumptions in program planning models.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); CDISC Controlled Terminology; ISO 11240 Units of Measurement

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this assumption record, incremented each time the assumption value, confidence level, or validation status is formally revised. Supports audit trail and change history requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; GCP ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

attributes.name: version_rationale
attributes.description: Narrative explanation for why this version of the assumption was created, including the trigger event (e.g., 'Updated based on Phase 2 interim enrollment data', 'Revised following FDA Type B meeting feedback', 'Adjusted per DSMB recommendation').
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; GCP ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: revised_assumption_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on assumption (revised_assumption_id)

products.name: cross_study_dependency
products.description: Association entity capturing formal dependencies between studies within a program or across programs where one study's outcome, data, or completion gates another study's initiation or design. Captures dependency type (data dependency, safety dependency, regulatory dependency, supply dependency, sequential design), predecessor study reference, successor study reference, dependency description, dependency status (active, resolved, waived), and impact if dependency is not met. Critical for integrated program planning and risk management.
products.reference: Cross-Study Dependency

attributes.name: cross_study_dependency_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the cross-study dependency record within the clinical development program. Primary key for this association entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: primary_cross_clinical_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical development program under which this cross-study dependency is governed. Links the dependency to its overarching portfolio governance context.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND Regulations 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: primary_cross_predecessor_study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the study whose outcome, data, or completion gates the successor study. The predecessor study must reach a defined milestone or status before the successor can proceed.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); Oracle Siebel CTMS Study Object

attributes.name: program_milestone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific program or study milestone record in the CTMS that represents the gating event in the predecessor study. Enables direct linkage between dependency tracking and milestone management.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS Milestone Object; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: actual_resolution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the dependency was actually resolved, waived, or formally closed. Populated when dependency_status transitions to 'resolved' or 'waived'. Enables schedule variance analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, notes, or observations about this dependency that do not fit into structured fields. Used by program managers and clinical operations teams for ad hoc annotations.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this cross-study dependency record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and ALCOA+ compliance requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: cross_program_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dependency spans studies in different clinical development programs (True) or is contained within a single program (False). Cross-program dependencies require portfolio-level governance escalation.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); Oracle Siebel CTMS Portfolio Management

attributes.name: data_package_required
attributes.description: Description of the specific data package, dataset, or analysis output from the predecessor study required to satisfy this dependency (e.g., 'Interim PK/PD analysis dataset in CDISC ADaM format', 'DSMB safety summary report', 'Dose-response modeling results'). Relevant for data dependencies.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM; CDISC SDTM; SAS Drug Development; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: dependency_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for this dependency record, used in program planning documents, integrated development plans, and CTMS tracking. Format: DEP- followed by 4-12 alphanumeric characters.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E8(R1) Integrated Development Plan

attributes.name: dependency_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the nature, rationale, and conditions of the dependency between the predecessor and successor studies. Captures what specific data, outcome, or event from the predecessor is required and why.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA IND Regulations 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: dependency_direction
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dependency flows in one direction only (predecessor gates successor) or bidirectionally (studies mutually constrain each other, e.g., platform trials with shared safety data). Bidirectional dependencies require special governance handling.
attributes.references: FDA Platform Trial Guidance; ICH E8(R1) Adaptive Design

attributes.name: dependency_name
attributes.description: Short human-readable label for the dependency, used in program planning dashboards, integrated timelines, and governance reports (e.g., 'Phase 1 PK Data Required for Phase 2 Dose Selection').
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: dependency_owner
attributes.description: Name or role of the individual or team accountable for monitoring and resolving this dependency (e.g., Program Director, Clinical Operations Lead, Regulatory Affairs Lead). Supports accountability in program governance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: dependency_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the dependency. 'active' = dependency is in force and being tracked; 'resolved' = predecessor condition has been met and dependency is satisfied; 'waived' = dependency formally waived by program governance with documented rationale; 'on_hold' = dependency tracking paused pending external decision; 'pending_review' = dependency under governance review for waiver or modification.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: dependency_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the dependency between studies. 'data' = successor requires data outputs (e.g., PK/PD, biomarker) from predecessor; 'safety' = successor requires safety review or DSMB/DMC clearance from predecessor; 'regulatory' = successor requires regulatory milestone (IND, NDA, MAA) from predecessor; 'supply' = successor requires drug supply or manufacturing readiness from predecessor; 'sequential_design' = adaptive or platform trial design where predecessor results inform successor design; 'operational' = site, staff, or resource dependency.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Adaptive Trial Guidance; EMA Adaptive Design Scientific Advice

attributes.name: dsmb_review_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Review Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether resolution of this dependency requires a formal DSMB or DMC safety review of predecessor study data before the successor study may initiate. Particularly relevant for safety dependencies.
attributes.references: FDA DSMB Guidance; ICH E6(R2); EMA Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this dependency record is considered active and binding for program planning purposes. Supports temporal tracking of when dependencies were formally established.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); Oracle Siebel CTMS; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this dependency record ceases to be active (e.g., upon resolution, waiver, or supersession by a revised dependency). Null for currently active dependencies. Supports slowly changing dimension tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); Oracle Siebel CTMS; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: escalation_contact
attributes.description: Name or role of the senior stakeholder to whom this dependency is escalated if it is at risk of not being resolved by the planned resolution date. Supports risk escalation workflows in program governance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: gating_condition_detail
attributes.description: Precise, measurable condition or threshold that must be met in the predecessor study to release the successor (e.g., 'Minimum 80% of Phase 1 subjects must complete PK sampling', 'No Grade 3+ DLTs observed at target dose level'). Supports objective dependency resolution assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Adaptive Trial Guidance; DSMB Charter

attributes.name: gating_milestone
attributes.description: Specific milestone or event in the predecessor study that must be achieved to satisfy this dependency (e.g., 'Database Lock', 'DSMB Safety Review Completion', 'Regulatory Clearance of IND Amendment', 'Last Patient Last Visit'). Aligns with CTMS milestone tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: governance_review_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dependency requires formal review and sign-off by a program governance committee (e.g., Program Steering Committee, Joint Development Committee) before the successor study can proceed.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ICH E8(R1) Program Governance

attributes.name: impact_if_unmet
attributes.description: Narrative description of the business, regulatory, or patient safety impact if this dependency is not satisfied before the successor study proceeds. Used in risk management and program governance decision-making.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which this dependency record was most recently reviewed by the program governance team or dependency owner. Supports periodic dependency health checks in integrated program planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: mitigation_plan
attributes.description: Documented contingency or mitigation strategy to be executed if this dependency cannot be resolved by the planned date. Describes alternative approaches to allow the successor study to proceed with acceptable risk.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next formal review of this dependency by the program governance team. Drives governance calendar and ensures active dependencies are not overlooked.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: planned_resolution_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the dependency is expected to be resolved (i.e., the predecessor gating milestone is expected to be achieved). Used in integrated program timeline planning and critical path analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E8(R1) Integrated Development Plan

attributes.name: regulatory_agency_notification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether resolution or waiver of this dependency requires notification to or approval from a regulatory agency (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.) before the successor study proceeds. Drives regulatory submission planning.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the regulatory submission (IND amendment, CTA, protocol amendment) associated with the resolution or waiver of this dependency. Links to Veeva Vault regulatory submission records.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Assessed risk level associated with this dependency not being met on schedule. 'critical' = program-stopping impact; 'high' = significant delay or regulatory risk; 'medium' = manageable delay with mitigation; 'low' = minor impact with available workarounds. Supports integrated program risk management.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: schedule_impact_days
attributes.description: Estimated number of calendar days by which the successor study initiation would be delayed if this dependency is not resolved by the planned resolution date. Used in critical path and scenario planning.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); Oracle Siebel CTMS Program Planning

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this dependency record originated. 'CTMS' = Oracle Siebel CTMS automated extraction; 'CTMS_MANUAL' = manually entered in CTMS; 'IDP' = Integrated Development Plan document; 'PROGRAM_OFFICE' = Program Management Office planning tool.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; Veeva Vault; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: Native identifier of this dependency record in the originating operational system (e.g., Oracle Siebel CTMS dependency object ID). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail back to the system of record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Siebel CTMS; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: successor_earliest_start_date
attributes.description: Earliest permissible initiation date for the successor study, derived from the expected resolution of this dependency. Drives integrated program scheduling and site activation planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E8(R1)

attributes.name: supply_dependency_detail
attributes.description: Specific description of the drug supply, manufacturing batch, or IRT/RTSM configuration requirement from the predecessor study that must be fulfilled before the successor study can be supplied. Relevant for supply dependencies.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH Q7 GMP; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this cross-study dependency record was most recently modified. Supports change detection, incremental data loading, and audit trail for regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this dependency record, incremented each time the dependency definition, gating condition, or resolution criteria is formally revised. Supports change history and audit trail.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: waiver_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the dependency waiver was formally approved by the designated governance authority. Required for audit trail completeness when dependency_status = 'waived'.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: waiver_approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the governance body or senior authority (e.g., Program Steering Committee, Chief Medical Officer, DSMB) that approved the waiver of this dependency. Supports audit trail for regulatory inspection.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GCP Guideline

attributes.name: waiver_rationale
attributes.description: Documented justification for formally waiving this dependency, including the scientific, regulatory, or operational basis for proceeding without satisfying the original gating condition. Required when dependency_status = 'waived'.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline

attributes.name: predecessor_cross_study_dependency_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on cross_study_dependency (predecessor_cross_study_dependency_id)

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: mitigation_action

attributes.name: plan_code

attributes.name: plan_type

attributes.name: planning_granularity
